body: Refs #4621 (acceptance item 4). Item 4 asked that hosts launching senpi with fixed arguments, such as the desktop, can still turn TTSR off without `--ttsr-disabled`. That switch already exists: adding `"ttsr"` to `disabledBuiltinExtensions` in `settings.json` disables the whole builtin, including its detectors, user stream rules and `/ttsr`. It applies at session start and on settings reload, and removing it re-enables TTSR. This PR documents the switch in `docs/settings.md` and pins it with a regression. No runtime change. **Evidence** (faux provider, offline, no CLI flags): - `CI=1 vitest run --maxWorkers=1 test/suite/regressions/issue-4621-ttsr-settings.test.ts`: 1/1 on unchanged runtime code. With `ttsr` disabled the stream completes untouched; after removing it and reloading, TTSR correction triggers. - With `test/ttsr` and `ttsr-extension`: 361/361 across 22 files. --- ## Summary by cubic Documents the existing `disabledBuiltinExtensions: ["ttsr"]` setting so desktop and other hosts with fixed launch arguments can turn TTSR off without the `--ttsr-disabled` CLI flag. - Adds the setting to the settings reference in `docs/settings.md` and a changelog entry. - Adds a regression test covering disabling TTSR at session start and re-enabling it on configuration reload. - No runtime code changed. Written for commit ad35a39349f07f61badcdf259e6e51572c9bbd00. Summary will update on new commits.

author: flomaetschke
body:
Part of #507, #408, #401, #103 (wave 4, M3).

## branch (#507)
- `branch -m <old> <new>` onto a dangling symbolic ref overwrites it (t3200 16).
- Linked worktrees on a renamed branch follow under their `HEAD` lock; a locked `HEAD` gives git's errors ("HEAD of working tree <path> is not updated", "branch renamed to <new>, but HEAD is not updated", exit 128) and keeps the `branch.<name>` section (t3200 33, 34).
- An unborn branch checked out in another worktree can be renamed (`-c` says "no commit on branch") (t3200 39).
- `--set-upstream-to <remote> <branch>` suggests `--set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch>` when that remote-tracking ref exists (`advice.setUpstreamFailure`) (t3200 106, 109).
- A local branch that remotes' fetch refspecs map to is tracked through those remotes, so two of them are "ambiguous information" (t3200 127).

With every `branch` call except `--forked`, `--delete-merged`/`--dry-run` and `--recurse-submodules` routed to rgit, t3200 passes in fallback except 50 (checkout in a worktree of a bare repository with `core.bare` in `config.worktree`, unchanged by this PR).

## for-each-ref (#401)
- `%(is-base:<committish>)`: the listed ref whose first-parent history meets the first-parent history of `<committish>` earliest, ties to the earlier ref in listing order (before `--sort`); works as a sort key; `tag --format` computes it, `branch --format` leaves it empty like git. Refs pointing at mistyped tags are reported ("object ... is a commit, not a blob", "bad tag pointer to ... in ..."). t6600 (all is-base/ahead-behind cases) and t6300 418 pass.
- `%(ahead-behind:)`/`%(is-base:)` with an empty argument: "expected format"; a base that is not a commit: "error: object ... is a tree, not a commit" + "fatal: failed to find '...'".
- `%(ahead-behind)` over a history with a missing commit counts it, stops that line of history and reports "error: Could not read <oid>" (git repeats it depending on its walk; the counts match).

## refs verify (#103)
New `git refs verify [--strict] [--verbose]`: loose refs of the common directory and of each linked worktree (badRefName, badRefContent, refMissingNewline, trailingRefContent, badReferentName, symrefTargetIsNotARef, symlinkRef, badRefFiletype), root refs (`HEAD`, `ORIG_HEAD`, ...) of each worktree, and `packed-refs` (badRefFiletype, emptyPackedRefsFile, badPackedRefHeader, badPackedRefEntry, packedRefEntryNotTerminated, badRefName, packedRefUnsorted with the `sorted` trait). Levels from fsck-msgids and `fsck.<msg-id>` (shared with `mktag`), exit 255 on errors. t0602 passes completely (fallback). `--verbose` lists entries in name order; git follows readdir order.

## tag (#408)
`tag --contains`/`--no-contains` read commits through replace refs when there are any, and fail with "fatal: commit ancestry contains a cycle" when the replaced history loops (t7004 150).

## Tests
`tests/branch.rs` (2 new), `tests/for_each_ref_is_base.rs`, `tests/refs_verify.rs`. Conformance routing follows in rgit-conformance after merge.

author: thrudthebarbarian
body:
`tests/determinism.sh` compiles every fixture twice in separate processes and compares the assembly byte for byte. It is what keeps the fixpoint (stage 3 == stage 2) honest. It had rotted: it ran `bin/<host>/xcc`, a compiler the releases do not ship, at its default level and for arm64 only. No gate section ran it.

It now runs the shipped compiler, `bin/<host>/xcc-xc` (or `XCC=...`), at `-O2` (`-O` to change it), for each `-A` given (default arm64). A fixture counts as skipped where it does not compile for that target or is marked `skip`, rather than skipping every target-pinned fixture. Each target's first differing pair is kept at `/tmp/determinism-<target>-{a,b}.s`.

Run with it, every fixture at `-O2`, two separate processes each, on x86-64 Linux:

| Target | identical | differing | does not compile |
|---|---|---|---|
| arm64 | 797 | 0 | 183 |
| x86-64 | 856 | 0 | 124 |
| win64 | 856 | 0 | 124 |
| arm9 | 871 | 0 | 109 |
| atarist | 735 | 0 | 245 |
| wasm32 | 788 | 0 | 192 |
| xt6502 | 734 | 0 | 246 |

On arm64 macOS, 100 fixtures take 59 s, so about 9 minutes per target for all of them.

Test script only.

author: infinitedusky
body:
## What changes

- **Adding data to an endpoint** asks one thing, with one box: **This is real data** (ticked to begin with). Real data is always faked: the original stays on this computer and a faked version is made. Unticked, the file is used as it is.
- **"Use faked version" is on the endpoint**, beside its data, not on the place. It appears where the endpoint has a real response, ticked to begin with. Unticked, a person's own prototype and smoke test get that endpoint's real response. A reviewer always gets the faked one, and a sensitive endpoint has no switch.
- **A task starts from the app's answer** and may set its own for one endpoint, then put it back ("Follow the app").
- **A place** (prototype, smoke test, reviewer) now only says the real service or the mock. That stays per service because the app reads one address for a service.

## How

- `mock-serve.ts`: `served` reads each endpoint's answer (the task's own, else the app's) for a person's own run; `setEndpointFaked`.
- Migration **0053**: one added column, `task_service.faked`.
- The stored source `replay` is refused from now on, and read as the mock where it was already chosen.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter app test`: 767 pass.
- Engine: 712 pass, 2 fail in the full run (`github.test.ts` stacked PRs, as on main; one runner test that fails under full runs). `mock-data` and `mock-serve` tests rewritten for the endpoint switch and passing.

## ⚠️ Sonda desechable — F14 del spec 5.15 — **NUNCA MERGEAR**

Este PR existe únicamente para demostrar que el job `audit` de CI **bloquea** ante un lock con security advisories:

- Lock degradado a `laravel/framework v11.57.1` (los 5 PKSA del spec).
- `policy.advisories.block=false` en composer.json para que el step `composer install` del job pase y el ROJO provenga exactamente del step `composer audit --locked`.

**Resultado esperado:** job `audit` en rojo con `Found 5 security vulnerability advisories affecting 1 package`. Los jobs `tests`/`static-analysis` también fallarán (el stub `PreventRequestForgery` no existe en 11.x) — irrelevante, el sonda se cierra sin mergear en cuanto se captura la evidencia.

Se cerrará y su rama se borrará tras capturar el run. Evidencia final: PR #66 + spec §12.

Refs: .agents/spec-impl/spec-laravel13-advisories-fase5.md (F14)

body:
## Sprint y alcance
- Tarjeta Jira: [SIEP-237](https://unihumboldt-team-p0nfba0h.atlassian.net/browse/SIEP-237)
- Requisitos / reglas: RNF-06 (despliegue), SIEP-RNF-02 (IP del cliente detrás del proxy)
- Bloque / apps: despliegue (`psychosim/settings/production.py`, `Dockerfile`, CI, `docs/`)
- Reemplaza a #49 (primera versión para Azure; se cerró al renombrar la rama). Se pasó a Google Cloud porque la universidad no es elegible para Azure for Students.

## Qué cambia
Deja el repositorio listo para desplegar en **Google Cloud Run** con **Cloud SQL para PostgreSQL** (prueba gratuita de Google Cloud), con una sola imagen: Django sirve la API en `/api` y el build de Angular en el resto de rutas.

- **`Dockerfile` y `.dockerignore`**: imagen multietapa (Node 26 + Python 3.14, bases fijadas por resumen), usuario no root 10001, `migrate --noinput` antes de `exec gunicorn` (3 procesos × 4 hilos) en `$PORT`, bytecode precompilado y sin el socket de control de gunicorn 26. Parte del Dockerfile del proyecto anterior, adaptado a la raíz de este repo.
- **`production.py`**: reconoce Cloud Run por `K_SERVICE` y rechaza `SIEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=0`, como ya hacía en Railway. El dominio `*.run.app` se declara en `DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- **`.github/workflows/despliegue-gcp.yml`**: en los PR que tocan el despliegue construye la imagen y la prueba contra PostgreSQL como la arranca Cloud Run. En `main` (o a mano) la sube a Artifact Registry y la despliega en Cloud Run con Workload Identity Federation (sin llaves guardadas), y comprueba `/api/health`. El despliegue se salta mientras el repo no tenga la variable `GCP_PROJECT_ID`.
- **`docs/despliegue-gcp.md`**: arquitectura, costos, comandos `gcloud` paso a paso, secretos en Secret Manager sin escribirlos, primer administrador y medición de `SIEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES` con trabajos de Cloud Run, correo, Workload Identity Federation, logs, cómo cuidar el crédito y problemas comunes. Enlazada desde `README.md` y `.env.example`.

## Endpoints, modelos y migraciones
- [x] Sin cambios

## Cómo se probó
- `manage.py check` sin avisos (PostgreSQL 17 local).
- Lista de pruebas de la CI (`s3-s4.yml`) más las de settings de producción, correo, JWT, redirección a https e índice del SPA: **796 pasan, 4 fallan, 1 omitida**. Los 4 fallos ya ocurrían en `develop` y no tocan archivos de este PR: tres variantes `[raiz]` de `test_production_settings.py` y `test_spa_index.py::test_el_html_real_del_frontend_lleva_el_marcador_que_el_servidor_sustituye` buscan archivos con `parents[3]`, un nivel por encima del repo (herencia de `backend_django/`). Las 4 pruebas nuevas de Cloud Run pasan.
- `docker build` local y contenedor arrancado como lo haría Cloud Run (`PORT=8080`, `K_SERVICE`, `DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`) con `psychosim.settings.production` contra PostgreSQL 17:
  - migraciones aplicadas al arrancar; `/api/health` → 200 (`db: ok`), también por HTTP plano (exento de la redirección);
  - `/` sin `X-Forwarded-Proto` → 301 a https; con él → 200, `Cache-Control: no-store` y el nonce sustituido en `<app-root>` y en los `<script>`/`<style>`;
  - `Host` ajeno → 400; proceso con uid 10001;
  - con `K_SERVICE` y `SIEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=0`, la imagen no arranca y el error nombra la causa;
  - con `SIEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=1` y `X-Forwarded-For: 6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.7`, la auditoría registra `203.0.113.7`;
  - `create_admin` + inicio de sesión → 200 con `mustChangePassword`;
  - con 0,5 CPU y 1 GB, unos 9 s desde el arranque hasta la primera respuesta; 193 MiB en reposo.
- La URL de Cloud SQL por socket (`postgres://…@%2Fcloudsql%2F<conexión>/metafronesis`) se comprobó con `dj_database_url` y `base.py`: `HOST=/cloudsql/<conexión>` y `connect_timeout` intacto.
- El workflow todavía no ha corrido en GitHub: este PR es su primera ejecución (solo el trabajo de la imagen). El trabajo de despliegue no se ha probado contra Google Cloud.

Limitaciones declaradas:
- Aún no hay recursos en Google Cloud: la tarjeta pide desplegar solo con la aprobación del equipo.
- `SIEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=1` para Cloud Run se debe medir en el primer despliegue (guía, paso 8).
- La primera imagen se sube desde un equipo (guía, paso 4); después, el workflow publica y despliega desde `main`.

- [x] Los criterios de aceptación de la tarjeta están comprobados o sus faltantes están declarados
- [x] Pruebas de mi bloque pasan (los 4 fallos son previos y ajenos a este PR)

author: jr11ikhsan
body:
# Bounty 01, stage 2: grants — spend caps and recurring limits (#63)

Third of the per-stage PRs for the Programmable payments bounty, in the
program page's order. This is a standalone branch from pristine main
c2b8c47: its tree is byte-identical to the stacked branch
`bounty01-pr3-grants-caps` @ 751d50b, and its three commits above main
carry the trees of the stacked stages in order (commit 1 = stage 1a
standing payments + payout rules, commit 2 = stage 1b receive routes,
commit 3 = this stage, grants spend caps). The diff against main
therefore includes the stage 1a and 1b code as well as the grants code
below; the staging is preserved in the commit history, and stage 1a is
separately open as PR #155 (stage 1b as PR #171). The remaining grants
stages (time conditions; refunds and combination rules) follow in their
own PRs.

## What is added

- `consensus/grants.py` — conditional grants as a consensus book in the
  RetractableBook pattern. A grant entry is frozen; its id is the hash of
  its signed fields. At creation the funder's total is custodied by the
  book (it never sits in the beneficiary's own balance, so the caps
  below are the node's, not a wallet's promise). The beneficiary draws
  against a per-period release: `released(ts) = min(total, release x
  periods begun)`, counted from the grant's start anchor by its own
  calendar (daily/weekly fixed; monthly dates clamp and return — the
  31st releases on Feb 28/29 and again on Mar 31). Because the release
  is a pure function of the block timestamp, each period's allowance is
  counted exactly once by construction; unreleased funds are never
  spendable, and draws settle only up to released-minus-spent.
- A funder-level shared cap: one signed record per funder caps the
  total drawn across ALL of that funder's grants in a period. Every
  settled draw counts against the shared period total exactly once;
  replacing the cap is a next-version record with the same period shape
  (seconds + anchor), so the count survives replacement and cannot be
  reset by re-setting the cap. The 108-history check ships as a test
  against the real book.
- Engine wiring: `create_grant` custodies the total through the
  transfer seam with `escrow=True` (the funder's o5 is re-checked on
  the real beneficiary and amount, the fee is measured on the real
  inputs, and a fee-rejected create holds nothing and creates nothing);
  `draw_grant` is transfer-less — the credit is staged in-branch and
  can only ever land on the beneficiary; `set_grant_shared_cap` is
  funder-signed and transfer-less. Admission parity via the book's own
  verbs, the `getgrant` command, grant events in snapshot metadata and
  governance changes, and a governance meta-hash root that appears only
  once a grant or shared cap exists (grantless chains hash
  byte-identically to before). A draw carries the `grant_draw` credit
  class: a route on the beneficiary never splits a draw.

## Cases claimed by this PR (spend caps, recurring limits, shared cap)

| Case | Test |
|---|---|
| Per-period release is a pure function of time; each period counted exactly once, capped at the total | `test_released_by_is_a_pure_function_of_time` |

body:
## Summary

**F3:** the AB LED group, `Status_PanelAB` and Blynk V4 classified the **average** of panels A and B.

- A dead B next to a healthy A (6.8 V + 0 V → 3.4 V) showed only YELLOW.
- A heavily shaded B often stayed GREEN.

**Decision taken (recommended option):**
1. **Group = weakest panel.** `groupAB(a, b) = min(a, b)` drives the LEDs, `Status_PanelAB` and V4. Any failing member raises the group alarm, which is standard practice for group status.
2. **Additive per-panel detail.** `/api` appends `Status_PanelA` and `Status_PanelB` after the original six keys. `index.html` and UE blueprints that read named fields are unaffected. The v1 JSON Schema lists the new keys as optional; the UE reference poller colours A and B individually when they are present.

Not changed: Blynk pins (still V0–V5) and the web UI layout. The AB card simply reflects the new group rule.

> Behaviour change: an AB group that used to be GREEN or YELLOW because one panel compensated for the other will now show the weaker panel's colour.

author: isaacthoman
body:
The search agent's run of `apps/web/scripts/e2e-imports-providers.mjs` found that hearting an album not on the server didn't fill the heart in time, and the album's songs were neither fetched nor added to the library. I reproduced it on a local server with the mock provider.

## Cause
**The album page had two buttons named "Save to library" while a song was playing.** The player bar's heart, for the song still playing from the step before, had the same accessible name as the album header's heart. The script's `button('Save to library')` took the first, which was the song's. The server log for that step shows one `PUT /me/likes/track/…` and no album save. So the album was never saved, and nothing fetched it.

The server side was fine throughout. With the album's own heart, the save persists and the fetch is asked for. It's the same for screen-reader users, who had two identical "Save to library" buttons to pick from.

## Fix
- **Player hearts named after their song.** The player bar and Now Playing hearts are now "Save *Song* to library" / "Remove *Song* from library", as row hearts already were. The page's own heart is the only "Save to library".
- **The heart fills in the click's own frame.** Measured in Chromium, the optimistic heart took 8–16 ms to flip: one task, because TanStack Query hands cache changes to its observers on a `setTimeout(0)` scheduler. It now uses `queueMicrotask` (`notifyManager.setScheduler`, set once in `api/query-client.ts`), so an optimistic update reaches the screen before the browser paints. Changes in one task are still batched.
- **Reads already in flight can't undo the heart.** An album page re-reads itself while its songs arrive. An answer sent before the click could land after the optimistic patch and empty the heart until the next refetch. Before patching, the save now cancels in-flight reads that hold the entity, without reverting. It's built on #116's `applyChanges`, merged here, and leaves that flow as it is.

## Regression tests (web, `AlbumView.test.tsx`)
Each fails without its fix and passes with it:
- "has one Save to library while a song plays, the album's, and it saves the album": exactly one such button, and clicking it calls `like('album', id)` and never `like('track', …)`.
- "fills the heart before any timer runs after the click": only microtasks run between the click and the check.
- "keeps the heart filled when a read sent before the click answers after it": a held re-read answers with `liked: false` after the click.
- "empties a heart filled at once when the server refuses": the rollback still wins.

## The script
- **Failing provider (#119 and #97):** a provider that fails every job is an outage, not missing songs (`acquisition/health.ts`).
  - Playback pauses once, with "Can't load music right now".
  - The provider is reported failing.
  - No song is blamed, so there are no per-song notices and no grayed tracks.
  - The old "the track is gray after a refresh" check encoded the opposite, so it's replaced by a check that the provider is reported failing.
- **Wrong delivery:** a song the provider can't supply is skipped under one counting notice ("Skipped 3 songs — not available"). After five in a row, playback pauses with "Several songs in a row aren't available".
- **Search:** songs are found under the Songs filter (`type=track`) with #137's `resultRow`, because the mixed list shows only the top few songs. The row spinner, decorative since #117, is checked in the row's markup.
- **`e2e-playback.mjs`:** its likes step clicks the player's song-named heart.

## Checks
- `e2e-imports-providers.mjs` against a fresh local API with the mock provider: **59 of 59**, on the branch merged with current dev (#116, #137).
  - "the heart fills at once";
  - "the server fetches its songs behind it (4 of 4)";
  - "and it is in the library".
- `npm run build:packages && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` passes:
  - server: 1199;
  - web: 902;
  - mobile: 342;
  - client-core: 278;
  - contracts and adapters.
- `npm run docs:build` and `npm run docs:check` pass.
- **iOS, by hand in the Simulator** (Release build from this branch, local API, standalone mock provider): hearting the on-demand album *Amber* filled the heart at once and showed the notice. The album was in Library → Albums, and a `library` fetch job for it was queued. iOS needed no change.
- `e2e-playback.mjs`: the likes step passes with the new label. Its search and quick-search steps fail on current dev too: they still look for a `searchbox` and "Top result" headings from before #117's combobox. That's left to the search owner.

## Noticed, not changed
- **Mixed availability after an outage.** Some of the Aphex Twin tracks whose fetches failed read `none`, others `on_demand`. `health.ts` says a failing provider's streak misses are dropped, so they should all read the same. Flagging this for the acquisition owner.
- **Search album rows have no Save entry.** #117's album rows in search have their own row menu, without Save to library. They can't use `albumMenuEntries` until a row knows whether the album is saved.

## Screenshots
| Album page, unsaved | Hearted | Failing provider: one outage notice |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/IsaacThoman/e05e5143382921fa3df2d6af4116f38f/raw/album-on-demand-1440-light.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/IsaacThoman/e05e5143382921fa3df2d6af4116f38f/raw/album-added-1440-light.png) | ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/IsaacThoman/e05e5143382921fa3df2d6af4116f38f/raw/on-demand-failed-1440-light.png) |

author: hornof-claude
body:
Closes #173

## What to look at

No preview (a script and a hook). One check, about a minute, from the repo root on this branch:

```
python3 -m unittest scripts/test_consistency_check.py -k LooseFollowUp
```

Then read what the turn would be sent back with, on the real 2026-11-22 PRs: the `test_the_2026_11_22_merges_are_sent_back` test names PR #161 Note 2, PR #163 Note 6 and PR #164's advisor comment, each with its link.

## What changed

- **New case `loose-follow-up`** in `scripts/consistency-check.py`. When a turn hands over a merge, or says a PR is merged, it names each loose item and its link:
  - every **reviewer Note** on the PR (a numbered item, plain or bold, in the Notes section of a post of Claude's that isn't the advisor's), and
  - every **ask for a card** on the PR or on the cards it closes: "file a card" (or one, another, a new…), "want a card?", and "say so" next to "file" or "card".
- **What settles an item:**
  - a Note: it links a new card itself, or a later reply names it on one line with a new card or "no action": `Note 6: #181`, `Notes 3 to 5: no action`, `Notes 4 and 5: no action`.
  - an ask for a card: the line itself links a new card or says "no action", or a later reply links or quotes that comment (the same rule merge-with-open-request uses) and links a new card or says "no action".
  - "A new card" is a `#N` or an issues link other than the PR itself and the cards it closes. "PR #N", `#N` inside backticks, and `&#N;` don't count.
- **The query** now also reads the 5 most recently updated merged PRs (`merged:`), and the last 30 comments on each card a PR closes. Measured on hornof/apb: 13 points, up from about 9 (the playbook says so now).
- **`hooks/apb-stop.py`:** `noticed_merges()` finds the PRs the message says are merged ("PR #163 merged", "PRs #161, #163 and #164 merged", a link to the PR), outside quotes and plans, and not "isn't merged". The check gets them as `merged`, so a merge the turn notices is checked even when the ask block hands over something else. The send-back is once per turn, like the other cases (no check on a retry).
- **Playbook**, "Rules a script can check": the new case, with its incident, and the cost.

## Tests

- `scripts/test_consistency_check.py`:
  - `LooseFollowUp` is built from `scripts/test_consistency_check_2026_11_22.json`: PRs #161, #163 and #164, their comments and reviews, and the comments on #135, #162 and #136, all read with `gh` on 2026-11-22.
  - The incident is sent back, as a merge handed over and as a merge noticed. The same PRs pass with a card linked, with "no action" replied, and with the replies on the card instead of the PR.
  - Each rule is also tested on its own: own-card refs, earlier replies, one line per Note, bold items, which posts are Notes, request phrases and look-alikes ("the PR says so", "should say so in the hand-off").
- `LooseFollowUpProperties`: 300 random Notes posts and replies (cards in the Note, `Note k: #N`, `Note k: no action`, ranges, plus decoys: too early, the wrong number, no disposition, the PR's own card). They are checked against a bookkeeping of what each reply settles, written as the replies are made. Both directions: a settled Note is never named, and a loose one always is.
- `PlaybookListsEveryCase`: every case id in `CASES` is in the playbook.
- `FromGitHub`: merged PRs and card comments come through `from_answers`, and an answer without them reads as none.
- `hooks/test_apb_stop_checks.py` `MergeNoticed`: what `noticed_merges` reads, and the whole hook on "PR #163 merged." (sent back, naming Note 6 and its link). The same turn with the Notes settled goes through.
- Mutation check, in a scratch copy: 14 mutants of the new code, all killed. They covered no case, no-action ignored, replies at any time, no ranges, own cards counted, self-settling asks ignored, no bold items, asks inside Notes double-counted, request replies that don't address the comment, any reply line settling any Note, advisor Notes counted, a bare "say so", `merged` ignored, and refs in code spans.
- Run locally:
  - the two changed test files;
  - every test file that reads `docs/playbook.md`, `hooks/apb-stop.py` or `scripts/consistency-check.py`: `test_apb_stop`, `test_apb_popups`, `test_apb_folder`, `test_apb_events`, `test_apb_brief`, `test_apb_watch_start`, `test_apb_watch`, `test_card_times` and the `scripts/test_*_docs.py` files, `test_tests_workflow`, `test_ci_template`, `test_version_bump` and `test_product_guide`. All pass.
- **Test edits, flagged:** four older `MergeWithOpenRequest` fixtures (`scripts/test_consistency_check.py`, lines 423, 458, 466 and 471) had a reviewer post with `## Notes\n1. fine` and no card. Under the new case, that Note is loose, so those merges would also be sent back for it. Each such Note now links a card (`1. fine, filed #9`), so those tests still test only the Fix items and the advisor comment. No assertion changed.
- **Review fixes on this PR** (Fix post https://github.com/hornof/apb/pull/179#issuecomment-7088968493):
  - Fix 1, 6878d3c: a PR said to be merged is looked up only among merged PRs, so "PR #179 is ready to be merged." on an open PR isn't a merge noticed. New tests in both test files; both fail on the old lookup.
  - Fix 2, 6a6fdf5: only "no action" settles a follow-up, not "no card". **Test edit, flagged:** `Notes 2-3: no card, harmless.` moved from the replies that settle a Note to those that don't, with "Notes 2 and 6 still have no card." and "Note 2 has no card yet; filing after merge."; the dash range stays tested as `Notes 2-3: no action, harmless.`
  - Fix 3, 0675e58: the playbook bullet's first sentence, as the review wrote it.

## Not tested

- A real Stop on a real merge wake, end to end with GitHub: the hook test uses the real PR data through a stand-in for the GitHub read. I ran the new query against hornof/apb by hand: it is valid, costs 13 points, and on the 5 latest merged PRs (#178, #177, #176, #164, #168) it names 10 loose Notes and the #164 advisor comment.
- A merge noticed for a PR that isn't among the 5 most recently updated merged PRs isn't checked.
- A Note that mentions any other card in passing, such as "#165's second Done-when line…" (PR #177 Note 6), counts as linked. Only the PR itself and the cards it closes are excluded.

Projects: none. The change is in the plugin's own script and hook, which every project runs from the plugin; no project file changes.

## What this does

Two new pages, both in the menu under People & things. Each was a button on one person's card on Volunteers; those buttons stay.

**Families (`/families`)** — for whoever may link families (Admins and the Owner out of the box)

- Every family by its adults, with everybody in it; and everybody with an account who is in no family yet.
- A search box that narrows both lists as a name is typed.
- Opening somebody draws their family as a tree: parents above, the person beside their husband or wife, children below. Pressing an account in the tree draws it from them.
- Under the tree, the same box as the Volunteers dialog: link another account, or write in somebody not on the app.
- On a phone the children wrap onto more rows and the lines follow, so the whole tree is in sight without scrolling sideways.

**DBS Checks (`/dbs`)** — for whoever sees safeguarding details (the Owner alone out of the box)

- Everybody with where they stand, what wants doing first: to check, details not given, verified, no DBS.
- Counts on four tiles and on the filter; search by name.
- Each line has the certificate, how old it is, and who verified it.
- Pressing one opens the same check as the Volunteers button, including "Mark as verified".

## Database

Migration `0326_every_family_on_one_page.sql` — **already on production** (rehearsed in a rolled-back transaction as the Owner and as somebody without the right; then applied; version 326 and checksum confirmed).

`families()` returns every household of two or more with its members by name. No address, date of birth or school. The DBS page needs no database change.

## How each opens

Both open by one right and never by a page level: `people.family` and `people.compliance`. An Admin without the right is not shown the page, and nothing is asked of the database.

author: hadnutz
body: **Description** Add an optional `emulatorjs.cache.enabled` setting (default `true`). RomM sends it through the config API and turns off EmulatorJS's download cache before the browser player loads. Administrators can then bypass the cache when IndexedDB fails to initialize, without editing generated frontend HTML. ```yaml emulatorjs: cache: enabled: false limit: null ``` > [!WARNING] > `emulatorjs.cache_limit` moves to `emulatorjs.cache.limit`. The old key still works for now: RomM reads it, logs a deprecation warning, and writes it under the new key the next time it saves `config.yml`. When both are set, `cache.limit` wins. > > `config.yml` is also read more strictly. A block that should hold settings but holds a plain value (for example `netplay: true` or `cache: false`) now stops RomM at startup with exit code 3 and an `Invalid config.yml: must be a dictionary` message. Before, RomM ignored the block and used the defaults. An empty block (`netplay:`) still means defaults. **What changed** - **Cache switch.** RomM loads EmulatorJS 4.2.3 when netplay is off and the nightly build when it is on. Nightly reads `EJS_cacheConfig.enabled`, but 4.2.3 only reads `EJS_disableDatabases`, so the setting sets both. In both builds, the ROM, BIOS and core downloads skip IndexedDB while save states still use it. - **`cache.limit`.** 4.2.3 does not cache a file this size or larger (in bytes). Nightly reads `EJS_CacheLimit` as its total cache size in MB, so a limit under 1 MiB gave it a 0 MB cache. RomM now passes nightly its default 4096 MB size explicitly. - **Clear cache.** The "Clear EmulatorJS cache" dialog now also deletes `EmulatorJS-bios` (4.2.3) and `EmulatorJS-Cache` (nightly), which kept serving downloaded files after a clear. - **Strict config reads.** Every `config.yml` read goes through one reader in the config manager, which replaces the per-key `get_nested` calls. `get_nested` had no other callers, so it is removed from `utils/database.py`. **Reproduction and verification** - **Reproduced in the browser:** On RomM 5.5 beta using nightly FreeIntv, the browser console reports `Error creating cache database`, followed by `Error downloading core (freeintv-legacy-wasm.data)`. - **Owner-host functional test passed:** Turning off EmulatorJS's download cache before its loader started let the same Intellivision game run in a standalone EmulatorJS test and inside RomM with firmware installed. - **Checks run:** backend config loader and config endpoint tests, the player unit tests in Vitest, `vue-tsc`, mypy and Trunk all pass. `npm run generate` reproduces the `ConfigResponse` type in this PR exactly. - **Not run:** a RomM image build, and a browser run of 4.2.3 with the cache turned off. The 4.2.3 behaviour comes from its source: `EJS_disableDatabases` swaps the ROM, BIOS and core stores for dummy storage. **Checklist** - [x] I've tested the changes locally (unit tests and typecheck; no image build) - [x] I've updated relevant comments (example configuration) - [ ] I've assigned reviewers for this PR - [x] I've added unit tests that cover the changes #### Screenshots (if applicable) The original core-download error in RomM. The change adds configuration, not a UI feature, so there is no after screenshot. **AI assistance disclosure:** AI assisted with source review, code and test authoring, and the PR description. A maintainer then ran an AI-assisted review pass (Claude Code) that added the 4.2.3 cache switch, the `cache.limit` move, the strict config reader and the clear-cache fix. Testing and its limits are stated above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: benzatkulak-collab
body:
## Why
Ben's Vercel Hobby account is over its free limits (Active CPU 4h52m/4h, Functions Storage 10.3/10 GB). This PR moves Social Perks to a free host. **Not to be merged or deployed until Ben gives the go.** His steps are in [`docs/hosting-move.md`](../blob/claude/move-off-vercel-5109d0/docs/hosting-move.md).

## Host choice
**Northflank free Developer Sandbox, running the existing `Dockerfile` as one always-on container.**

- **Cloudflare Workers Free (tried first, built with OpenNext):**
  - The bundle fits (18.5 MiB of 64 MiB).
  - In a local Workers preview, warm page views took **30–60 ms** against the free plan's **10 ms CPU cap**.
  - The global Postgres pool also broke there: 9 of 10 concurrent DB requests failed.
  - Verdict: it needs Workers Paid ($5/mo) plus a DB change.
- **Netlify Free:** the site **pauses** when the 300 monthly credits run out, and its functions cold-start.
- **Render / Koyeb free:** both sleep when idle.
- **Northflank:** always-on with no sleeping, builds Dockerfiles, supports custom domains, and the app code is unchanged. Caveat: its docs say the free tier isn't meant for production, which is fine while pre-launch.

## Changes
| Vercel piece | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `vercel.json` crons (5) | `.github/workflows/cron.yml`: same UTC schedules, same `Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, no-op until `CRON_BASE_URL` is set |
| `@vercel/analytics` | Removed, along with its CSP hosts (PostHog unchanged) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build | Docker build args. Empty ones are unset so the `socialperks.app` fallback still applies |
| `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` | `GIT_COMMIT_SHA` build arg (old name still works as fallback) |
| `x-vercel-forwarded-for` | `cf-connecting-ip` preferred (Cloudflare proxy) |
| — | CI job **Docker image**: builds the image, boots it against Postgres, smoke-tests health/pages/cron |

These need no change:
- No edge runtime and no `next/image`.
- Prisma isn't used; the DB is Supabase through `postgres.js`.
- `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL` reads already fall back to `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, then `socialperks.app`.

## Verified locally
- `next build` passes.
- The standalone `node server.js` (the container's `CMD`), run against a scratch Postgres:
  - Migrations created 37 tables.
  - Health returned `durable:true`, and 20 of 20 concurrent DB requests returned 200.
  - Pages answered in 6–20 ms; memory was about 200 MB.
  - 4 of 5 cron routes returned 200.
- `tsc`, lint and `vitest` (2118 tests) all pass.
- `docker build` itself is checked by the new CI job (no Docker available locally).

## Known issue, already there before this PR
`onboarding-drip` sends `CRON_SECRET` as a fallback key, but `/api/v1/drip` doesn't accept it, so the cron gets a 401 unless `DRIP_API_KEY`/`INTERNAL_API_KEY` is set. Same on Vercel. Workaround is in the doc; the code fix is left for a follow-up.

## Not done (waits for Ben)
No merge, no deploy, no DNS change, no Vercel project changes, and no Northflank account.

author: lilianpe
body:
Fixes ORC-486

The daemon's mirror (ORC-479) fetched its branches without prune, as the old clone did: a branch deleted on GitHub stayed visible to `prepare`.

- `fetchOrigin` takes a `prune` option; `RepoMirrors.fetch` passes it for a mirror's branch fetches only. Fetches with explicit refspecs (the forge's `HEAD` read to `refs/factory/forge-head/<uuid>`, a merge sha) stay unpruned.
- Workspaces lose nothing: their objects are copied into their own `.git` (`agentRepository`). The test deletes the branch upstream, fetches, runs `git gc --prune=now` on the mirror, and still reads the workspace's commit, head and diff.
- A prune can leave `origin/HEAD` naming a deleted branch (default branch renamed on GitHub, old one deleted). `setHead` now checks that `origin/HEAD` resolves after each fetch, rather than trusting a once-set cache, and sets it again from the forge when it does not. Tested.
- Doc: `docs/projects-and-workspaces.md`.

Behaviour change to note: a ticket relaunched without a workspace whose branch was deleted on GitHub (merged PR, branch auto-deleted) now starts a fresh branch from the trunk instead of reusing the stale ref.

author: shkelqimbasha
body:
## Problem

`ProductVariantController` / `ProductVariantServiceImpl` (`/api/product-variants/**`) had **no authorization**: any authenticated user could create, update or delete variants of *any* product. The request body was also unvalidated (blank names, negative stock, values longer than the `VARCHAR(100)` columns all reached the database).

Found by the web-panel API audit (omnia-web `docs/api-audit-admin.md`, section 2.10 / gap #1).

## Fix

**Authorization** — create / update / delete now use the same rule as product images (`ProductImageServiceImpl`):

| Caller | Result |
|---|---|
| Platform admin (`ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN`) | allowed |
| OWNER or ADMIN of the product's organization, org active, category grant with `canUpdate` | allowed (`OrganizationAccessService.requireCanUpdateProduct`) |
| STAFF of the organization | 403 |
| Member of another organization / plain user | 403 |
| Product without organization or category | platform admin only |

Authorization is checked after the product/variant lookup and before any write, so a denied request changes nothing. `GET /api/product-variants/product/{productId}` is unchanged.

**Validation** (`ProductVariantRequest`):
- `variantName`, `variantValue`: `@NotBlank`, max 100 chars (column size); trimmed before saving
- `stock`: required, `0..1_000_000`
- `priceAdjustment`: optional, may be negative, must fit `DECIMAL(10,2)`; `null` is stored as `0.00` (matches the column default)

Invalid bodies return 400 through the existing `GlobalExceptionHandler`.

## Client impact

Neither the Android app nor the web uses variants, so no client changes are needed. Any future client must send `stock`.

## Tests

- `ProductVariantServiceImplTest` (25 tests) uses the **real** `OrganizationAccessService` and `CurrentUserService` with mocked repositories and a real `SecurityContext`, so the role rules are exercised for real: OWNER/ADMIN with grant → OK; STAFF → denied; stranger → denied; owner without grant / grant without `canUpdate` / inactive org → denied; platform admin → OK without membership lookups; org-less product → admin only; GET needs no auth.
- `ProductVariantControllerTest` (+10 tests): `AccessDeniedException` → HTTP 403 for POST/PUT/DELETE; blank/missing/too-long names, negative/missing stock and over-precise price → 400 without reaching the service.
- Full suite: `./mvnw test` → 1116 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS (incl. Testcontainers MySQL integration tests).

Not merged and not deployed.

author: sakobu
body:
Updates every dependency to its latest stable version, cleans up the repo setup, makes the `typescript` peer optional, and makes use-form require pipelines 0.2.

Merging this makes the release workflow open a Version Packages PR for **@railway-ts/pipelines 0.2.1** (patch) and **@railway-ts/use-form 0.2.0** (minor). Each commit passes `bun run check` on its own.

## Published changes (changesets)

- **Optional `typescript` peer (both packages, patch).** npm, pnpm and Yarn install required peers automatically, so JavaScript projects got TypeScript installed. The `>=5.0` floor is still checked where TypeScript is installed. The packed packages type-check in a strict ESM consumer (`skipLibCheck: false`) with TypeScript 5.0.4, 6.0.3 and 7.0.2.
- **use-form requires pipelines 0.2 (use-form, minor).** The peer range goes from `^0.1.27 || ^0.2.0` to `^0.2.0`. People on use-form 0.1.x stay on it and keep pipelines 0.1 support. The README's stale `^0.1.29` requirement is fixed.

## Dependencies

- `@eslint-react/eslint-plugin` 4 → 5. Its rules now match v5's `recommended` preset: two rules removed, four added. The current code passes all of them.
- use-form: happy-dom 21, jest-dom 8, react/react-dom 19.3, `@types/react`/`@types/react-dom` 19.3, zod 4.6, valibot 1.5, testing-library patches.
- New devDependencies: `semver` and `@types/semver`, for the peer-range check.
- Already at latest: oxlint, oxfmt, oxlint-tsgolint, tsdown, size-limit, changesets, publint, attw, `@types/bun`, Bun 1.4.5, and every GitHub Action.
- **TypeScript stays on 6.0.3.** TypeScript 7 no longer ships the JavaScript compiler API that `@eslint-react` loads (through typescript-eslint) inside oxlint, so with 7 installed oxlint fails with "Failed to load JS plugin". CONTRIBUTING.md documents this. Type-aware lint already runs on TypeScript 7 through oxlint-tsgolint.

## Setup

- CI and release run on **Node 26**, the active LTS.
- `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` move to `tsconfig.base.json`, and the dead `allowJs` and `*.js`/`*.d.ts` include globs are removed.
- **`check-peer-ranges.ts` now checks against npm.** A release that accepts fewer peer versions than the package's latest npm release must be a breaking release. This replaces "never narrow a workspace peer range" and covers every peer. It catches Changesets' own rewrite of an out-of-range peer, which Changesets ships as only a patch.
- **New `release-plan` CI job** runs `bun run ci:version` on every PR, so a missing changeset fails in the PR instead of in the release workflow.
- **`use-form-min-pipelines` job.** It gets the lowest supported pipelines from `scripts/lowest-pipelines.ts` and skips its checks when that is the workspace's own version, which the checks job already tests. **That's the case on this PR**, since 0.2.0 is still the workspace version. It tests against npm's 0.2.0 again once 0.2.1 is released.
- CONTRIBUTING.md has the new rule: a pipelines minor needs use-form's range moved to the new minor and a use-form minor changeset, in the same PR.

## Verification

Tested locally:
- `bun run check` passes after each commit. That covers build, attw/publint, typecheck, lint, format, 782 + 390 tests at 100% coverage, the package checks and size.
- Simulated on scratch copies:
  - `ci:version` produces pipelines 0.2.1 and use-form 0.2.0.
  - On that versioned state, the min-pipelines job installs pipelines 0.2.0 from npm, and use-form passes typecheck and all 390 tests.
  - Removing the use-form minor changeset makes `ci:version` fail with an explicit message.
  - The use-form-min-pipelines job passes against pipelines 0.1.27 before the range is narrowed.

author: olegg90
body:
Stage 6 of the roadmap: the UI refresh, after `docs/design/ui-refresh.md` and its Decisions, plus the changes agreed while building it.

## What changed
- **Theme:**
  - the "Classical" tokens: warm neutrals and one gold accent, used for strokes and text, in light, sepia and dark;
  - Cormorant Garamond and Lora, bundled from Fontsource (woff2, Latin and Cyrillic, about 100 KB), with their OFL licences in `public/licenses`;
  - theme swatches;
  - Lucide icons in one inline SVG sprite.
- **Reading chrome:**
  - a slim top bar: ← Library, Contents · title and author · Bookmark, Aa, mode, ⋯;
  - a bottom row: the chapter · a track with chapter ticks and a draggable knob · `p. 5 of 99 · 2%` (pages within the chapter);
  - the two bars come and go together, from the mouse at an edge or a tap in the middle;
  - on the phone, the bottom bar adds Contents / Appearance / Mode / More.
- **Aa and Settings:**
  - Aa is a pop-up in a book, a sheet on the phone;
  - Settings has one section at a time: Reading, Catalogs, System (library folder, offer to add books, file types, interface font, history length, clear history), Shortcuts, About;
  - `S` / `Ctrl+,`: Aa in a book; Settings in the library, and back to the page you left.
- **Library:**
  - Desktop: a WinUI 3-style navigation pane (Continue reading, Library, Catalogs, and Settings folding out to its sections), with the content beside it. The pane can be resized; its width is kept in WebView storage.
  - Phone: the same pages from a bottom navigation bar.
  - "Continue reading" (cover cards, 1–5 books, a setting) and all the books are separate pages.
  - A progress line under every cover, and a status switch with counts.
- **Contents drawer:** Contents | Bookmarks (n).
- **Offer bar:** the last choice first; "Never for this file" behind ⋯.
- **Catalogs:**
  - breadcrumbs named after the folders opened;
  - an In library tag;
  - outlined download buttons;
  - a renamed catalog shows its new name at once.
- **Shortcuts:** they work in any keyboard layout. Latin keys go by what they type; others (Ukrainian) by their place on the keyboard.
- **Backend:**
  - `recent_books` gives each history book's library cover (`cover_key`);
  - `library_cover` falls back to the cache before the first scan.
- **Dependencies:** reader-core 0.3.0 (`BookView.chapterPage`, `chapterStarts`).
- **Dev server:** Vite scans only `index.html` and ignores `src-tauri`, `docs` and `samples`. Before, the first page load in dev took 12–40 s (blank window).
- **Docs:** `docs/spec.md` (Reading, Android interaction, Library screen, Files outside the library, Catalog browsing, State, Technology, Keyboard) and the roadmap, with stage 6 done.

## Verification
- `tsc` is clean and vitest passes 27 tests, with new ones for the Aa panel, the settings page and its tabs, and layout-independent shortcuts.
- `cargo test` passes 68 tests and `cargo clippy` is clean.
- The Android CI build is signed and installs over the previous version.
- **Checked by hand on Windows (dev build):**
  - theme and fonts, the interface font setting;
  - reading chrome, Aa, Settings tabs;
  - the navigation pane, Continue reading cards;
  - the status switch, the Contents / Bookmarks drawer;
  - catalog breadcrumbs, shortcuts in a Ukrainian layout.
- **Checked by hand on the phone (signed APK):** reading chrome, the Aa sheet, Settings, the library's bottom navigation and pages.
- `/code-review` (standards and spec) and `/simplify` were run; their findings are fixed.

## Left for later (noted in review)
- `main.ts` grew. The library navigation and the reading chrome could each become their own module; that is a bigger refactor, so it is not in this PR.
- ⋯ → Shortcuts / About still open their side panels. They could open the Settings sections instead, but that changes behaviour, so it is left for now.

## Breaking changes
- None for data.
- Settings gain `historyLength` and `uiFont`, both with defaults.
- The Library / Catalogs tabs and the library window's top bar are gone, replaced by the pane and the bottom navigation.

author: davinerto9
body:
## Summary

HU-51: release notes for every published version and a record of which version runs in each
environment.

- **Deployment record.** New step `recordDeployment`. Every `deployK8s` and every rollback, success
  or failure, creates a GitHub Deployment for the environment (state, build link, environment URL)
  and appends a row to `docs/release-notes/registro-ambientes.md` on the `registro-despliegues`
  branch: date, environment, version, type, approver, result and build. `main` and `dev` are
  protected, so the log lives on its own branch and the pipeline pushes it without a PR (the first
  deploy creates it; retries if another build pushed first). The Helm revision description carries
  the same data (`helm history`).
- **Approver per deploy.** dev and stage from main: `automatic: merge by <author>`; RC on stage:
  `automatic: PR #N by <author>`; prod: `PROD_APPROVER`. The rollback job now captures the prod
  approver with `submitterParameter`; in dev and stage it records who started the job. A rollback
  that stops before `Roll back` did not touch the environment and is not recorded.
- **Release notes audit.** New job `circleguard-release-notes` (`jenkins/release-notes.Jenkinsfile`,
  declared in `casc.yaml`). It compares the GitHub Release of every `vX.Y.Z` tag with the notes
  `releaseNotes` generates (`OK`, `MISSING`, `DIFFERENT`) and, with `APPLY`, creates or replaces
  them. Today v0.1.0 has a release whose notes predate HU-22. `publishGithubRelease` gets
  `latest: false` so older versions do not take the *Latest* mark.
- A failure to record marks the build UNSTABLE; it never undoes a deploy.
- Docs: `docs/release-notes/trazabilidad.md`, plus links from `jenkins-pipeline.md`,
  `politica-cambios.md` and `rollback.md`.

## Related issues

CGR-161

## Type of change

feat

## Change category

- [ ] Standard
- [x] Normal
- [ ] Emergency

## Risk

Medium. It touches `deployK8s`, used by every deploy and by the rollback job. The record runs in a
`finally` after the rollout and smoke test and catches its own errors, so a GitHub outage leaves the
build UNSTABLE instead of failing a finished deploy. `helm upgrade` gets one new flag
(`--description`). The `github-pat` credential needs **Deployments: Read and write** if it is a
fine-grained token (classic `repo` already covers it).

## Test plan

- Groovy syntax of every `jenkins/vars/*.groovy` and of `Jenkinsfile`, `rollback.Jenkinsfile` and
  `release-notes.Jenkinsfile` with the same `CompilationUnit` check as `Validate shared library`: OK.
- Unit run of the `@NonCPS` helpers: table row (escapes `|`), Deployment and status payloads,
  audit report and `make_latest`: expected output.
- The log-branch shell against a local bare remote: creates the orphan branch, appends a second row,
  a concurrent push is rejected and the retry lands; history keeps the three rows in order.
- `casc.yaml` parses and declares the four jobs.
- Not run yet in Jenkins. After merge: run `circleguard-release-notes` without `APPLY` (v0.1.0
  should be `DIFFERENT`), then with `APPLY`, then without it again (all `OK`); run a rollback on
  stage and check GitHub → Deployments, the `registro-despliegues` branch and `helm history`.

## Rollback plan

Revert this PR. Deploys go back to the previous `deployK8s` behavior. The `registro-despliegues`
branch and the GitHub Deployments it created stay as history and need no cleanup.

## Size policy

About 450 added lines in source and configuration files, below the limits.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] No secrets or credentials added
- [x] Documentation updated if needed

## Summary

When the researcher agent was asked to message the tester agent, the message turned into a subagent nested under the researcher's chat. The tester agent showed (0) chats, and the sidebar never said which subagent was spun up.

The CLI change in inference-gateway/cli#1942 lets an agent message another agent's orchestrator. The recipient starts in a top-level chat of its own, and every session records `agent`, `label` and `sent_by`. This reads those fields from `infer conversations list`.

**Depends on inference-gateway/cli#1942.** Merge it after a CLI release that contains it, with `.cli-version` moved there (`gh workflow run bump-cli.yml`). Until then `agent-message.yaml` cannot pass.

## Changes

- **Filed under the agent** - a top-level chat the listing names an agent for is filed under that agent.
  - The sidebar store merges `listedAgentOf(conversations)` under its own `agentOf` assignments, so the count, opening the chat as that agent, the model bar and the chat's computer (`chatWorkspace`) all agree.
  - Only the user's own assignments are saved to `projects.yaml`.
  - Subagents and `main` chats are skipped.
- **Label badge** - a subagent row shows the label its orchestrator gave it as a badge before the title. The title and the `Delete conversation <title>` label are unchanged.
- **Row tooltip** - `chatOrigin` builds it: `invoked by orchestrator: <parent> as <label>`, `sent by <chat>` or `invoked by human`.
- **Message card** - the recipient's chat opens on `[Message from <sender>]`, which the transcript already shows as a **Message from** card.
- **Tests** - unit tests for `listedAgentOf` and `chatOrigin`. A new `e2e/tests/agent-message.yaml` with two mock scenarios: `e2e-sonnet` messages `e2e-docs-writer`, whose chat must appear under `e2e-docs-writer` and above `e2e-sonnet`.
- **Docs** - `docs/chat.md` (subagent labels, the row tooltip) and `docs/agents.md` (agents messaging each other).

The e2e tests were not run locally. The new test needs the CLI from inference-gateway/cli#1942 (`INFER_BIN`). The badge has no e2e check, because its text also shows in the prompt and the status bar.

author: fumingzhang
body:
## Summary

A built-in Agent without a Team could keep reporting identity `Provisioning` after the directory had verified its existing binding. The Operator only persisted the result before a Helm upgrade when a policy was attached.

Persist the transition to `AgentIdentityReady` before calling the Gateway or Helm, including for a no-Team Agent. Keep the existing policy checkpoint and optimistic concurrency checks. An already-ready ordinary Agent does not get an unconditional status write. The regression reads the stored Agent from inside the Helm call, before post-upgrade reconciliation can hide the bug.

For a no-policy Agent, this checkpoint writes only the verified identity and its condition. A running workload keeps its stored `Ready` phase while Helm upgrades it, so this identity update does not cause the Broker to reject its connection requests.

## Related issue

Fixes #637.

## Validation

**Checkpoint failure (`f66b84ba1`):** A transient Agent read failure after identity verification now invalidates only the prerequisite condition. The regression reproduced the premature workload and identity transitions on `a16eb56d8`; on this revision the other persisted status remains unchanged, the failed pass never calls Helm, and the retry upgrades once. `make check` and `make docs-check` passed. Before push, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -tags=envtest -count=1 -run '^(TestNoTeamIdentityCheckpointReadFailureInvalidatesOnlyPrerequisites|TestNoTeamAgentIdentityIsReadyDuringHelmUpgrade|TestAgentStatusPatchPreservesFutureFields)$' ./internal/controller` passed in the Operator module with local Kubernetes API-server assets. AKS was not rerun for this revision.

**Review follow-up (`a16eb56d8`):** `make check`, `make docs-check`, and `go test -count=1 ./internal/broker` (Broker module) passed. In the Operator module, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -tags=envtest -count=1 -run '^(TestAgentStatusPatchPreservesFutureFields|TestNoTeamAgentIdentityIsReadyDuringHelmUpgrade)$' ./internal/controller` passed. The local Kubernetes API-server test verified that unrelated workload state stays unchanged and a stale resource version conflicts. The AKS results below apply to the preceding revision (`7fcaf502a`); AKS was not rerun for this follow-up.

**Offline (Go 1.27.4, Helm 3.22.0):**

- From `app/cetirun-operator`, `go test -count=1 -run '^TestNoTeamAgentIdentityIsReadyDuringHelmUpgrade$' -v ./internal/controller` reproduced the bug on the unpatched controller. `go test -count=3 -run '^TestNoTeamAgentIdentityIsReadyDuringHelmUpgrade$' ./internal/controller` passed on the fix.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` in the Operator module, and `make -C app/cetirun-operator test` from the root: passed.
- `make check` passed lint and the CI helper suites, then stopped at `python-test` because system Python lacked `aiohttp`. After restoring the pinned test dependencies, `make python-test` passed (202 tests and 236 subtests). `python3 -B scripts/ci/validate.py go-test --component <component>` passed separately for `internal`, `portal`, `agent-broker`, `memory-context`, and `cetirun-connections-mcp`; the Operator result is above. `make portal-test memory-native-test openclaw-skills-test` passed with conditional skips. These were separate runs, not one uninterrupted `make check`.
- `make docs-check` passed with Hugo 0.164.0 extended (70 HTML pages checked). `git diff --check` passed.

**AKS integration:** Ran the original and patched reconcilers locally against a new AKS 1.36 cluster, with an active no-Team OpenClaw Agent for each case. The integration probe (`-test.run '^TestIssue637OnTaskAKS$' -test.timeout 8m -test.v`) paused the Helm client after the Kubernetes API stored revision 2. An independent client confirmed the release was `pending-upgrade` and read the persisted Agent before Helm could finish:

| Controller | Identity at generation 3 | Workload observed generation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original `0b8e4b22c` | `Provisioning` | 2 |
| Fix `7fcaf502a` | `Ready` | 2 |

Both upgrades then completed, acknowledged generation 3, and retained the original identity binding. Preliminary fixture setup attempts did not reach an upgrade and are not counted. The task and AKS node resource groups were verified absent after teardown; the temporary kubeconfig was removed.

**What this verifies:** real Kubernetes status writes and reads during a real Helm upgrade. The directory and AI Gateway used test adapters. This did not exercise live Entra provisioning, model inference, the Portal browser, or end-user runtime readiness.

## Compatibility and operational impact

Only the timing of an existing Operator status update changes. There are no API, CRD, AgentPolicy, Sandbox, storage, credential, or chart changes. The Agent's identity can correctly be ready before its runtime finishes updating.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and preserves unrelated work.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior, or I explained why no new test is necessary.
- [x] Documentation and examples match any public behavior changes.
- [x] Generated artifacts were updated from source, or none are affected.
- [x] Dependency changes include lockfiles, source attribution, and license information, or none are affected.
- [x] I examined the diff and attachments for secrets, private endpoints or identifiers, customer data, agent conversations, and internal information.
- [ ] I followed the applicable CLA instructions, or asked a maintainer about an unclear check.
- [x] I identified checks that must have credentials or a live environment and did not run them without authorization.

author: onlyonebyte
body:
Fixes #1125

## What does this PR do?

The API now gzips its JSON and CSV responses when the client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Before, every response went out uncompressed. Both proxy examples in `docs/deployment.md` also turn compression on.

- `backend/src/app.ts`: `compress()` from `hono/compress` on `/api/*`, as the first middleware, so error responses are compressed too. Hono's default content-type filter only compresses text-like types (JSON, CSV, XML), so photo thumbnails (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `application/pdf`) and the backup ZIP download (`application/zip`) are sent as they are. Hono also adds `Vary: Accept-Encoding` and skips `HEAD` and `206` responses.
- `docs/deployment.md`: `encode zstd gzip` in the Caddy example, and `gzip on;` plus `gzip_types` in the nginx example. Both proxies leave a response the backend already compressed alone, so these lines mainly cover the frontend's pages and assets. A short note under each example says so.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Test evidence

Sizes on a scratch DB (`db:init --seed`, then expenses copied up to 2 vehicles × 2,000), measured with `curl` against this branch. Main ignores `Accept-Encoding`, so its size is the first column.

| Endpoint | No Accept-Encoding (same as main) | Accept-Encoding: gzip (this PR) | Content-Encoding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /analytics/fuel-efficiency` | 74,274 B | 3,834 B | gzip |
| `GET /expenses?limit=100` | 52,528 B | 4,249 B | gzip |
| `GET /analytics/summary` (all time) | 57,447 B | 4,822 B | gzip |
| `GET /analytics/fuel-stats` (1 year) | 21,393 B | 2,279 B | gzip |
| `GET /analytics/fuel-efficiency?vehicleId=…` | 73,957 B | 3,760 B | gzip |
| `GET /expenses/export` (CSV) | 528,903 B | 17,866 B | gzip |
| `GET /sync/backups/download` (ZIP) | 115,823 B | 115,823 B | none |

New test `backend/src/__tests__/api-compression.test.ts`:
- a JSON list is gzipped when the client accepts gzip, carries `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, and decodes to the same data
- JSON is sent as it is without `Accept-Encoding`
- the backup ZIP download and a 4 KB PNG thumbnail come back with no `Content-Encoding`

The ZIP and thumbnail tests fail if the filter is swapped for one that compresses every type.

Local runs (backend):
- `bun test src/__tests__`: 53 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test src/api/sync src/api/photos src/api/expenses`: 968 pass, 0 fail
- `tsc --noEmit`, `check:musl` and `bun run build` are clean

## Scope
Notebooks 20–22 only. No global model inventory.

## Native fit()
- Reuse existing `fit()` of `PCAMultiTaskGP` (Notebook 20), `MixedPCAGP` and `MixedPLSGP` (Notebook 21).
- Explicitly opt 11 I-BNN / Spectral Mixture Exact GP variants in Notebook 22 into native MLL `fit()`; preserve existing `SpectralMixtureGP.fit()`, joint-encoder and DeepGP custom training methods.
- Replace direct `fit_gpytorch_mll()` invocations with `fit()` in all three notebooks. For Kronecker expressive GP examples use bounded optimizer options; preserve model-specific training losses.

## Educational visualization additions
- **20**: Keep task-specific latent intervals; add task-wise residual / posterior-SD comparison with slice RMSE and visualization of qLogEI proposals versus observations in public x0-x1 coordinates.

author: bsoneca
body:
Sign-out now drops every web-push subscription before it clears the cookie, so a signed-out account's notices no longer reach the next person on the browser.

**Problem.** A push subscription belongs to the browser, not the account. Sign-out left it behind, and apps that patched this per page missed pages.

**Change.**
- `signOut` in `shell.js` calls `revokePush()` (`signin.js`) first. Under the `omnishell:push` lock it unsubscribes every subscription of every service-worker registration of the origin. It always asks the browser, never a screen's last draw.
- If one will not go, it throws. The reader stays signed in, nothing is cleared, and a bubbling `omnishell:signout-failed` event (error on `event.error`) lets the page say so in its own words.
- `data-signing-out` on `<html>` is set while it runs and stays until reload. An app's opt-in that takes the same lock can check it and not re-subscribe. Failures and in-place sign-out clear it.

**Tests.** Two smokes in `login-smoke.js`: revokes under the lock before the cookie; a subscription that will not go leaves the reader signed in, fires the event and clears the bar. `login-smoke` and `signout-smoke` pass (37). The other smokes pass 163; 2 sync-shape cases fail in my checkout, which runs on a borrowed `vendor/` build, and this change does not touch them.

**Not changed.** No chrome copy for the failure (the event carries it) and no app wiring.

author: jun025
body:
## 무엇을
MIDP 이벤트 스레드가 빈 큐를 1 ms 마다 다시 보는 폴의 마감을 «그 스레드가 도는 step 이 시작한 때 + 1 ms»로 되돌립니다(`System::poll` · `Executor::step_started` — 잠금 밖 `AtomicU64`).

#603 은 실행기의 sleep 마감을 «부른 때부터»로 옮기면서 이 내부 폴까지 같이 옮겼습니다. 그래서 그리기를 막 끝낸 이벤트 스레드가 «그리기 끝 + 1 ms»까지 큐를 보지 않았고, 잠 없이 `repaint(); yield();` 로 그리기 완료를 기다리는 게임 스레드가 장마다 최대 1 ms 를 헛돌았습니다(게이트② 검수가 변이로 확정한 원인 줄).

게스트 `Thread.sleep` 의 의미(부른 때부터 센다)는 건드리지 않았습니다. pacing API(`tick_for` · `wants_cpu` · `TICK_BUDGET_MS` · `sleep_toward`)의 서명과 기본값도 그대로입니다.

## 잰 것(전 `e843ce009` · 후 = main `8fcd668c5` · 고친 뒤 — 세 프로세스를 같은 순간에)
- **범위**: 그 꼴은 지원 목록 SKT 82행 중 1행(`b42e4242866b`) · KTF 표본 80행 중 0 · LGT 표본 40행 중 0.
- **그 행**: #603 의 손실은 첫 화면 −11 ~ −13% · 게임 안 장면 둘 −32 ~ −36% · −8 ~ −10%. 고친 뒤 ÷ 후 는 +26 ~ +33% · +64 ~ +75% · +45 ~ +49%.
- **#603 전 수준으로 정확히 돌아옵니다**: #603 병합 `b52f6c46f` 에 이 diff 만 얹은 판 ÷ 전 = +0.4% · +0.9% · −0.5% · −0.0%. 지금 main 위에서 «전»보다 빠른 몫은 #605 의 것입니다.
- **#603 이 «요청한 속도로 돌려놓은» 행은 다시 빨라지지 않습니다**: SKT 7행 · KTF 3행 재측에서 고친 뒤 = 후.
- **유휴 화면의 CPU 는 늘지 않습니다**(60 Hz 로 쉬어 가는 스크래치 호스트 · 30초): 고친 뒤 − 후 가 −0.10 ~ +0.07초(4행 · 부호가 한쪽으로 서지 않음). 첫 판(step 시작 시각을 실행기 잠금 안에 적음)은 +3 ~ 4% 였고 그 측정이 잡아 원자 변수로 옮겼습니다.
- `test_pacing` 의 수는 main 과 한 칸도 다르지 않습니다(720 틱 · 그리기 200 · `redraw_cross_tick` 0 · `sleep_late_p95` 2 · `starved_ticks` 0).
- 전/후/고친 뒤의 `result` 가 다른 행: SKT 0/82 · KTF 0/80 · LGT 0/40.

## 시험 · 개악
새 시험 `a_repaint_handed_over_in_the_step_of_a_paint_is_looked_at_in_the_next_step`(멈춘 시계 · 결정적). main 의 꼴로 되돌리면 이 시험만 red(`left: 3, right: 103`)이고 `event_queue` 의 나머지 12개와 `test_pacing` 은 green 입니다 — 이 꼴을 보던 시험이 없었습니다.

## 같이 싣는 것
- 이용자 고지 1건 `docs/player-updates/2026-11-23-one-skt-game-back-to-its-speed.json`(`titles: []`).
- 0573 §9 「영향 범위 — 정적」 과 그 worklog `summary` 에 «0579 가 정정했다» 한 줄(검수 F2).
- `docs/report/0581`(표 전부 · 한계) · worklog(제안 0).

## 한계
측정 호스트가 다른 레인의 부하로 굶었습니다(load1 7 ~ 236). 판정은 같은 순간의 세 판 사이의 비와 계수(그리기 지연 p50 · yield 수 · sleep 수)로 했고 ±3% 밖 행은 전부 25초로 다시 쟀습니다. 훑기 202행은 첫 판으로 잰 것이고, 커밋한 판은 핵심 행 · 장면 둘 · 유휴 화면을 다시 쟀습니다. 브라우저(wasm)와 KTF 189행 · LGT 38행은 재지 않았습니다.

author: alexandre-afonso-silva-virgens
body:
## O que tem neste PR

Item (d) do enunciado: definição dos nós da AST e testes.

- `src/ast_nodes.py`: uma classe (dataclass) por construção da EBNF de `docs/gramatica.md`:
  `Programa`, `Bloco`, `Atribuicao`, `Print`, `If`, `While`, `For`, `BinOp`, `Num`, `Bool`, `Var`.
  - `While(condicao, corpo)` e `For(inicializacao, condicao, atualizacao, corpo)`, com os nomes do item (d).
  - Todo nó guarda `linha` e `coluna`, para o interpretador reportar erros semânticos com posição (`ErroSemantico`).
  - `linha`/`coluna` não entram na comparação (`==`), então os testes comparam só a estrutura.
  - Parênteses não geram nó: o agrupamento fica na forma da árvore.
  - `formatar(no)` imprime a árvore como texto indentado (para o relatório e o vídeo).
- `tests/validos/test_ast.py`: 6 testes, incluindo a AST de `1 + 2 * 3` e a de um `for` com as três cláusulas.

## Como testar

author: artur-t-96
body:
## Co i dlaczego

Router jednej skrzynki wsparcie@ (`support_mail_route.is_settlements_mail`) oddawał czytnikowi rozliczeń tylko maile **z załącznikiem**. Klient bez własnego systemu (PKO, BIK) akceptuje godziny odpowiedzią w wątku z TS, zwykle bez załącznika („łączna liczba godzin: 112, październik 2026”). Taki mail stawał się sprawą, a `proof.accept_has_hours` nie miał czego sprawdzić. W próbie IX–X 2026 dało to fałszywe uwagi i wyłączoną regułę u kilku klientów.

Teraz mail **bez załącznika** idzie do czytnika rozliczeń, gdy:
- adres rozliczeń (`CONSULTANT_PORTAL_SETTLEMENTS_ADDRESSES`) jest w „Do” albo „DW”,
- domena nadawcy jest **dokładnie** domeną klienta z regułą akceptacji mailowej (`support_mail_route.acceptance_clients`, reguły bieżącego i poprzedniego miesiąca):
  - `proof.excel_with_mail` włączona → jej parametr „domena”;
  - `proof.accept_has_hours` włączona → domena z `proof.excel_with_mail`, a bez niej domeny kontaktów klienta (PKO ma na produkcji tę regułę bez domeny);
  - `cl.client_acceptance` włączona → domena jej adresu (odpowiedź Banku Pocztowego na paczkę KCP; `_store_client_reply` istniał, ale na wspólnej skrzynce router go nie dopuszczał).

Czytnik rozliczeń (`_store_client_acceptance`) zapisuje mail jako `.eml` (`report`) u osoby z tematu wątku. Osobę szuka tylko wśród kontraktów klientów z tej domeny (`identity.resolve_named_for_clients`): imię pełne albo inicjał, np. „Akceptacja godzin wrzesień 2026 - P. Nowak”. Gdy nie ma jednej osoby, powstaje karta do przypisania (`internal`/`all`), a w pilotażu mail jest pomijany. Maile z załącznikiem i ścieżka T4T (`is_time_report_mail`) bez zmian. Wspólny zapis `.eml` wydzielony do `_store_eml` (używa go też `_store_mail_body`).

Reguła: `docs/claude/finanse-insights/rozliczenia-akceptacja-w-tresci-maila.md`, router w `docs/claude/ludzie/jedna-skrzynka-wsparcie.md`.

## Skala (archiwum rozliczenia@ 01.09–31.10.2026, reguły z produkcji 23.11)

**24 maile** bez załącznika na rozliczenia@ od domen klientów z regułą akceptacji trafiłyby teraz do rozliczeń zamiast do spraw: PKO 11, BIK 10, Plus, KIR i BNP po 1. **18** z nich ma osobę w temacie (BIK 10, PKO 8), reszta to karty do przypisania. Jeden (BNP) to pytanie o fakturę, nie akceptacja. Tak wygląda skutek uboczny reguły: pytanie pracownika takiego klienta bez załącznika na rozliczenia@ to karta, nie sprawa.

## Testy

- `tests/test_support_mail_acceptance_db.py` (z bazą), 3 testy: domeny tylko od klientów z regułą (w tym domena z kontaktu przy samej `proof.accept_has_hours`); czytnik spraw oddaje akceptację rozliczeniom, a mail bez reguły i mail bez adresu rozliczeń zostają sprawą; czytnik rozliczeń zapisuje `.eml` u osoby z tematu z okresem z tematu, a od klienta bez reguły nic.
  Na `main` wszystkie 3 padają (brak `acceptance_clients`, `routed_settlements` 0, `created` 0), na gałęzi przechodzą.
- `tests/test_support_mail_route.py`: brzegi routera bez bazy (poddomena, brak adresu rozliczeń, obca domena, pusty nadawca).
- Lokalnie na zmigrowanej bazie: router, czytnik spraw, czytnik rozliczeń (`internal`), KCP, KEŚU, PKO/Velo, T4T z maila, dokumenty portalu: 165 passed; potem jeszcze 72 passed po dopisaniu domeny z kontaktów.

Bez migracji. Wchodzi w życie dopiero przy działającym czytniku rozliczeń na wspólnej skrzynce (dziś czytniki wyłączone).

author: jag3773
body:
Closes #114

## What it does

**Appearance › Accent colour**, and `accent colour` in the palette, put an accent of your own over any theme.

- **Theme's** (the default), eight preset swatches (red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink), or any `#rrggbb` / `#rgb` typed in the field under them.
- Saved as `accent=#rrggbb` in `settings` (absent: the theme's own). `#rgb` and a missing `#` are accepted and written back long; a broken line keeps the theme's accent.
- One accent for every theme: it survives a theme change.
- The palette previews each choice as you browse, as `theme` does. `Esc` takes it back.

## How it keeps every theme readable

The typed colour replaces the theme's accent in `Theme::of` **before** the existing derivations (selection share, `accent_read`, pills, ground, code colours), so the 4.5:1 rules apply unchanged. Two cases the built-in accents never hit needed handling:

1. **A colour close to the page** (a pale yellow on Bref Light) is first taken to 3:1 on it. Otherwise the selection and the open pill, which are tints of the accent, would not show.
2. **Tints that look alike.** The selection, the open row and the commented passage are all shares of one colour, and for some typed colours two of them landed on the same shade (e.g. `#ffff99` on One Dark: selection vs open row 1.000). `Theme::of` now uses the nearest lightness of the same hue that keeps them apart. If no lightness works, it tries slightly less saturation: orange and red on Solarized Dark's teal needed that.

A grey accent gets some saturation for the code colours, so strings and numbers still differ from the text and from each other.

When the colour shown differs from the one typed, the row shows both and says why, as the issue proposed.

## The issue's open questions

I took the proposed defaults:
- **One accent for all themes**, not one per theme.
- **Presets are hues spread evenly**, mid-light so the legibility rules move them little on light or dark pages.
- **Diagrams, highlights and callouts keep their fixed hues.**

## Tests

- `logic/prefs.rs`: parsing and writing `accent=` (short form, case, missing `#`, refused values, broken line).
- `ui/theme.rs`: the contrast tests (`every_pair_reads`, `every_theme_reads`, ground, translucent ground, open row vs selection, commented passages, board columns, hover) now run over **every theme × (its own accent + 8 presets + 6 extreme accents)**: `#ffff99`, `#111111`, `#ffffff`, `#000000`, `#808080`, `#ff0000`. Plus a test that the accent replaces the theme's, survives a theme change and keeps its hue.
- Journey in `src/shell/tests/settings_page.rs`: click a preset, type `#f80` (kept as `#ff8800`), type a word (refused and said), `Esc`, a pale yellow shown darker and said, back to the theme's from the keys, and the palette with preview and `Esc`.

`cargo test --locked`: 580 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `shell::tests::link_preview::ctrl_over_a_link_previews_the_note`, and it fails the same way on `develop` without this branch (macOS 27, locally). I built with `--features gpui/runtime_shaders` because this machine has no Metal compiler; nothing in the repo changes for that.

## Not done

- **Design captures**: I have not looked at the result in a running window or taken screenshots of themes with a custom accent. That check from the issue is still open.

## Docs

`book/src/settings.md` (new Accent colour section, settings keys table, palette and keys mentions), README feature line and guide table, `docs/index.html` feature card.

## Overlap

This does not touch the files of #129 (PDF search), except one line each in README and `docs/index.html`, in different places. No new dependency; `Cargo.lock` is untouched.
