## Summary Stacked on #314. Adds a bot-first chat page at `/bot-chat`, laid out like the Devin Bots app: a bot list on the left, one continuous thread per bot in the center, and a closable bot profile on the right. Each turn runs on the existing cloud worker. - **Bot list:** each entry shows an avatar, the bot's name, a preview of the last message and an unread dot. - **Profile:** the 动态 tab shows upcoming scheduled tasks (read-only here) and sandbox status; the 文件库 tab lists the bot's artifacts. - **Admin opt-in:** in 系统设置 → 云端常驻机器人, each bot gets a separate **网页对话** switch, independent of scheduling. Only the bot's assigned, eligible employee can use it or read its history, and admins cannot read transcripts through the generic task endpoints. - **Long context:** `0053_runtime_chat.sql` and `0054_runtime_chat_threads.sql` give each (bot, owner) pair one thread and merge legacy duplicate conversations. Older turns stay browsable and are compacted into a stored rolling memory; the worker's prompt is that memory plus recent turns, so the active context is bounded. Chat replies are stored up to 16,000 runes; non-chat summaries keep their existing truncation. - **Notifications:** web turns do not notify Feishu. - **UI:** zh/en i18n. The bot list refreshes when the page opens and when the user clicks refresh. Tests: Go tests pass for `internal/api`, `internal/store` and `internal/runtime` (isolation, idempotency, thread merge, rolling memory, long replies, artifacts). The e2e tests `42-bot-chat-refresh` and `43-bot-chat-workspace` pass, as does `tsc && vite build`. ---

Product Engineer opened this PR for Hcsk
Implemented in session Build multi-bot chat web page in dsh-ee
Review with Devin · Open in Devin Desktop


--- ## Handoff 1: full screen, motion, whale avatars, generated files in the 文件库 (08bf4e8f) **Bug: files the bot wrote didn't reach the 文件库.** Storage, the profile query and the web refresh were all fine; the files never made it into the collected directory. DSH ran with `/tmp` as its working directory; its shell tool runs under bwrap with a per-command tmpfs over `/tmp` and binds back only the workspace root, relative saves (`明日待办.md`) landed outside `/tmp/dsh-ee-output`, and the collector silently dropped anything in a subdirectory. I couldn't reproduce on a real sandbox (no credentials here), so this is the most likely cause rather than a confirmed one. Changes: - DSH runs with `/tmp/dsh-ee-output` as its working directory (its sandbox workspace root); both the chat and task prompts say so. - Files up to two subdirectories deep are collected and named by relative path (`reports/周报.md`); hidden files and directories are skipped; every skipped file logs `跳过云任务产物` with a reason. Downloads use the base name. - Scheduled-task files keep appearing in the same library, labelled 定时任务; chat files are labelled 对话. Only the bot's owner can list or download them. **/bot-chat UI** - Full screen: a header button covers the system sidebar and top bar, keeping the bot list, chat, input box and right panel. Persisted per account on this device, works on narrow screens; Esc closes an open overlay first, then exits. - Whale avatars: an abstract whale built on the dsh-ee mark, one of eight colours per bot; while replying it bobs, spouts and gets a pulsing ring. - Motion: messages rise in, replies fade between queued/running/done, the chat fades on bot switch, the profile panel slides open and closed. All of it is off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. - 文件库: click a file to preview it in the page (Markdown formatted or source, text, images, PDF via a typed blob URL); download stays one click away. zh and en strings; `docs/dev/cloud-runtime.md` updated and generated docs rebuilt. **Testing (local, macOS)** - New: `TestRuntimeChatFilesReachLibrary` (fake sandbox that resolves relative paths against the command's cwd: chat files appear in the library with the right sizes and download content; another employee and an admin get 404 on the library and the downloads; a scheduled run's file appears as `task`) and `TestRuntimeArtifactName`. The test caught a hidden top-level `.dsh/` directory leaking through, now fixed. - All `Runtime|CloudRuntime|RouteAgentCoverage` tests in `internal/api`, `internal/store`, `internal/runtime` pass. `gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, the Windows cross-build, `tsc`, `pnpm build` and the docs check pass. - e2e `42-bot-chat-refresh` and `43-bot-chat-workspace` pass; 43 now also covers file preview and full screen (wide and 390px). - Database tests ran against MySQL 8, not TiDB: local TiDB containers were repeatedly OOM-killed. In the full `go test ./...` run, `TestEphemeralStateReplaceAcrossInstances` and `TestEmbedSessionExpiry` fail on the unmodified branch too under the same setup; `TestBetaRateLimit` and `TestMigrateLockSerializes` failed only under load and pass in isolation; `internal/api` hit the 110-minute timeout on this machine. CI on TiDB is the source of truth. **Pending:** the Chinese screen recording with real model replies needs OpenSandbox and model credentials that weren't available here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Authored by Claude (claude-opus-5-5).

## What

A whole-crate cargo-mutants run over `lsr-wal`, using lsr-wal's own tests. Every survivor is resolved: 4 by simplifying code, 3 by tests, and 6 as equivalent with an escape line.

## Totals

| Run | Commit | Mutants | Caught | Missed | Unviable | Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo mutants -p lsr-wal --test-package lsr-wal --test-tool nextest --jobs 4 --timeout 240` | `d5d92c8` | 170 | 112 | 13 | 45 | 0 |
| The same, after the fixes | branch | 157 | 112 | 0 | 45 | 0 |

## Survivors

| Where | Mutants | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.rs`: `generation_unchanged`, `commit_follows`, `verified_before`, `checksum_before` | 4 (`<` becomes `>` on a short read) | **Simplified.** Five call sites compared `read_at`'s count with their buffer, and only `read_page`'s was tested at that boundary. At the others a short read leaves zeros that fail the next checksum anyway. One helper, `read_full`, now makes the comparison for all five. |
| `scan.rs` `read_at` | 1 (the `Interrupted` retry becomes an error) | **Test:** `open_retries_an_interrupted_read`. |
| `header.rs` `WalHeader::checkpoint_seq` | 1 | **Assertion extended:** `header_decodes_every_field` decodes a header with sequence 7, not only 0. |

| `testing.rs` `page` | 6 | **Equivalent:** the mixing steps of the test-data generator. A weaker mixer still gives deterministic, distinct pages, and changing it would change every recorded simulator history. One escape line, plus a row in `docs/mutants.md`. The rest of `testing.rs` (the WAL builder the simulator uses) stays mutated. |

Classes: a rule stated five times (the short-read check), and behaviour no test asked for.

## Size

Production code: +11 / −5 in `scan.rs`. Tests: +39, as one new test and two extended assertions in an existing test. The `docs/mutants.md` section is at the end of the file, so it can't conflict with #189's section.

Owner ruling on #57: every sport mirrors NFL.

## What it adds
`models/cfb/cfb_shared_sim.py` runs one drive-level Monte Carlo per game:

Challenger only. The frozen sha-pinned CFB model is untouched. Props need per-player usage-mean inputs before they can price real games (`NO_FORECAST` until then).

body:
**Unknown codes.** Until now, a code that no family uses quietly started an empty family, so a typo looked like every player was gone.
- `GET /api/family` now returns `exists`. Families made before settings existed still count, because they have a players list.
- `PUT /api/family` on an unknown code is refused unless the body has `create: true`.
- Logging in with an unknown code opens a popup, "No family found with this code", with **Create new family** and **Try again**. Nothing is saved or remembered until the grown-up picks Create new family, which goes straight to adding the first player.

**Changing the family code**
- New `POST /api/family/move` with `{ newCode }`, called with the current code. It copies every player's stars, the settings and the players list to the new code, writing the players list last, then deletes everything under the old code.
- It refuses a short code, the same code, and a code another family already uses (409).
- In the grown-up corner, once unlocked with the current code, there is now "Change family code" (the new code is typed twice). This device is then logged out with a note.
- Any other device still holding the old code is logged out with a note the next time it loads.

**Checks**
- API tests: 14 of 14 pass. They cover `exists`, create being refused without the flag, nothing written for a typo, move validation, conflicts, stars and settings moving across, and nothing left under the old code.
- Playwright end-to-end with the real function logic behind a mocked `/api`: 15 of 15 pass, with no page errors. They cover the popup, Try again, Create new family, logging straight in with an existing code, change code being locked until unlocked, mismatched new codes, the device logging out, the old code showing the popup, the new code bringing Max and his stars, and the second device being logged out.

body:
## Why

A generation task can reuse all Quint typechecks and still spend CPU comparing the same types many times. Reuse those comparisons during a model's generation.

## Change

Remember successful typedef lookups and structural shapes within each module's type environment. Keep exact-name lookup before the existing base-name fallback. Keep ambiguity checks and diagnostics in their original order.

## Evidence

Change types: non-ui, performance

Test results: `41bf3fc17c1866807ba4dd57fb15b47cb183eef0` passed root typecheck, changed-file ESLint, diff checking and the three existing native selftests for invalid types, imported machine types and generated enum and record code. The two positive cases exercised Dafny proofs. A real pack contained 111 files. Main verify and the three selftest shards passed on the exact head. [Hosted run](https://github.com/lalalune/vibestack/actions/runs/45091536688)

Proof of change: Generated all 439 models from the Eliza tree at `22ca5f6bc610caefd7f8c9edd4e01ccc7cfcf401` in both arms with its installed toolchain and 439 warm Quint action receipts. The 3,829 generated files and every action receipt were byte-identical. A separate run compared all 433 complete proof inputs, including four annotated source units. Every input matched, with aggregate digest `7d8669cab0ad31fadc0b96695699c75a28c2ce324a5679ebb2b515d171cfb5aa`.

Runtime logs: The three focused cases passed, including identical record-shape rejection, a proof over a named import, and execution of the emitted enum and record operations. Each measured generation reported zero Quint typecheck subprocesses.

Benchmarks: On macOS arm64 with Node 26.13.0, pnpm 10.24.0 and Quint 0.33.1, run `node vibestack/spec.ts gen` from a private Eliza source archive. Keep the same verified action receipts and start each arm with no generated output. One preload counted child processes. Alternate the original file and this patch after one warmup per arm. In five matched pairs, median child-inclusive CPU was **13.01 s → 10.71 s** (11.84–13.70 s and 9.90–11.44 s). Median wall time was 9.98 s → 7.84 s (9.37–11.01 s and 7.46–8.15 s). Peak memory ranges overlapped. This measures warm generation and excludes proof solving.

author: nethalo
body:
Refs #3081. Does not close it: the follower still learns a table's newer cut from a statement (see "Seen and not done").

## What changes for a user

On a PostgreSQL source in fresh mode, the keeper writes recent changes to disk far fewer times, and a snapshot update no longer makes the first statement that reads a table pay for rewriting its whole tail. Answers do not change. MySQL and MariaDB sources behave as before.

## What it does

1. **A prune keeps the chain.** Pending changes are written first, then the keys the newer cut holds leave memory, and only the leading files wholly below the cut are retired. Invariant: a key dropped from memory has its last change in the chain (`PGTail.PruneKeepingChain` refuses otherwise).
2. **Only across cuts of one read of the source.** A newer full read can lack a row that a TRUNCATE removed with no row event, so a kept row could come back. Any other case, or one that cannot be told, takes the existing path.
3. **At eight files, merge the newest ones** instead of writing the tail whole: the run ending at the newest file that costs the fewest rows per file removed. A merge never takes in a file from before a prune.

The fix of the skipped change that an earlier version of this branch carried went to main on its own in #3206. This branch takes main's.

## Every shared line (`internal/console/tail_keeper.go`)

No line of `tail_follow.go` or `reconstruct/tail.go` changes.

```diff
@@ type tailEntry struct
+	segHigh map[string]pgSegment
+	pgPruned int
@@ func (k *tailKeeper) pruneTo
+	if k.pgPruneKeepingChain(e, t, cut, to) {
+		return true
+	}
@@ func (k *tailKeeper) write
+	if merged, err := k.pgMergeNewest(e, path); merged {
+		return err
+	}
@@ after the delta write
+		k.pgNoteSegment(e, path, n)
@@ after the whole write
+	k.pgNoteSegment(e, path, n)
```

Plus their comments. For a MySQL source: the two new fields stay at zero, and each of the three calls returns at its first type check (`pgChainSource`, or `pgChainTail` for `pgNoteSegment`). `TestPGTailChain_onlyPostgresDeclaresIt` fails if the MySQL source or tail ever declares either.

## Measurement

Synthetic, on the real keeper and real Parquet files, on the test machine. Not a TPROC-C run and not the live board: the load is one table, with no capture, index or other process competing for the machine, so read the ratios and not the absolute times.

**At scale** (`BT_TAIL_COST=scale go test ./internal/console -run '^TestPGTailChainCostAtScale$'`): 1,200,000 changes over 1,000,000 keys, 600 update cycles, a newer cut every 300; the tail peaks at 718,001 keys.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Rows written per captured change | 23.52 | 5.62 |
| Largest single write (rows) | 712,001 | 322,001 |
| Whole writes (first / prune / eight files / ratio) | 1 / 2 / 74 / 0 | 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Time under the keeper's lock, total | 142 s | 51 s |
| Longest single update | 3.7 s | 1.6 s |
| Updates of 3 s or more | 7 | 0 |
| Files a statement reads, on average | 4.5 | 6.9 |
| A statement reading the table, average | 33 ms | 39 ms |
| A statement reading the table, worst | 55 ms | 67 ms |

**Small** (`BT_TAIL_COST=1`, 240,000 changes over 50,000 keys): 9.89 to 5.53 rows per change, 12.2 s to 8.6 s under the lock, longest update unchanged (225 ms to 224 ms).

The cost of this change is the read: about 50 % more files and 20 % more time per statement in this load. The read was timed over a very small base file, so it isolates the chain and does not predict a real query's total. Keeping the chain alone moved nothing (9.89 to 10.09 rows per change in the small load): the eight-file rewrite was the cost, which is why the merge is in this PR.

## Tests

Edge cases and a model of random histories of writes, merges and prunes, each step compared with a tail rebuilt from the cut (`TestPGTailKeepChain_randomHistories`, 40 seeds).

Mutations, each caught by a test and none committed: prune with keys unwritten; retire a file that is not a prefix; merge ignoring event ids; no flush before the prune; `fileCut` left old; merge across a prune; keep the chain over any read; over an unknown read; an empty file blocking retirement.

Run on the test machine after merging main: the model and the keeper tests with `-race`; `internal/console` with `-race` (the only failures are the 4 known tests that fail as root); `consoleapp` with `-race`; the console's PostgreSQL tail integration tests; and `scripts/pg-console-tests.sh` (no test failed; 1 skipped there for want of a TLS setup, which CI runs). MySQL and MariaDB integration run in this PR's CI.

## Seen and not done

- **The follower does not prune on its own.** A prune still happens when a statement first reads the table after an update; it now costs a delta write instead of a whole one. Left out because it is not small: the follower would have to list the tables as a statement does (`buildViewsInput`), a fixed cost every second, or the two name one cut differently and the tail is rebuilt; a statement that listed its tables just before a publish would then find its cut gone and wait; and it adds lines to the shared `tail_follow.go`, which this PR does not touch.
- **#3084** (a table carried unchanged, or a quiet source) is not addressed here.
- Not measured on a live TPROC-C board.
- A statement reads more files on average (table above).
- The whole `PGTail.WriteFile` path is unchanged for the first write and when the rows on disk pass the ratio.

## What changed
- Where a route matched and the method has no handler, the answer is 405 with `Allow` listing the route's methods (`HEAD` with `GET`; `OPTIONS` not added).

author: thearnica
body:
Part of #1764

## Problem

Every `ask` loaded the readers only some questions use: the reader of the last run's report, and the image library behind it, the claim reader and the watcher reader. A question about names never reads any of them, but on Kibana each such call paid for loading them.

## Solution

`ask` loads the report reader, the claim reader and the watcher reader where a question reads them, as `bin.ts` already loads each command. The load test now fails if a name question loads the image library.

## Blocks

| Mark | Block | Change | Pinned by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Upgrade | `ask` command | The report, claim and watcher readers load at their use sites; answers are unchanged | the `ask` tests, unchanged; answers to `symbol` for `Button`, `useState` and `EuiButton` and to `search` for `recalculation` are byte-identical on Kibana |
| Upgrade | Load test | `ask symbol`, `ask uses` and `ask search` share one case, which also refuses `raster` | `loads only what a name question calls for` failed before the change with `raster` in the loaded list |

Measured on Kibana (warm cache, ten runs each, one process at a time): `ask symbol --name Button` 430 → 411 ms, `ask search --query recalculation` 423 → 403 ms.

## Assumptions

- The issue's narrow-entry-point change (taking `ask` off the `mcp/tools` and `help/tools` barrels) is not made here: the help package and `ask`'s tool lists are built on that barrel's helpers, so it is a change of its own.
- Deferring the distiller was measured at about 5 ms inside the call, within the noise, and needed a `require`; it was dropped.
- `report` (~6 ms) and `vantage` (~2 ms) still load: other tools in the barrel load `report`, and `ask`'s question table reads vantage's variable.
- The issue's estimates overstated the saving; the figures above are the measured ones. Kibana's catalogue is still version 3.

## Findings set aside

- Occam's case for no change: a measured ~20 ms per name question, and speed outranks scope on this path.
- The issue's Done-when list names `mcp`, `report`, `vantage` and `yaml` for the load test (alignment C, Codex P2). The test refuses only what this change stops loading; the rest waits on the barrel change, so this PR is part of #1764 and leaves it open.
- The load test pins `raster` only, not the claim and watcher deferrals, which load no package of their own.
- Alignment A (the distiller's `require`) and B (the vantage deferral) were reviewed on an earlier diff; both were reverted.

author: goguzgungor
body:
When a Model has adapters, the controller adds a `loader` container that downloads them. Since #482 that container gets the Model's `spec.env`, but it does not get the `spec.files` mounts, which only go to the `server` container. A Model that loads adapters from an S3 endpoint with a private CA sets `AWS_CA_BUNDLE` in `spec.env`, the loader receives the variable, and the file it names is not there. Every adapter load then fails with `SSL validation failed ... [Errno 2] No such file or directory` (#801).

This change mounts the Model's files into the `loader` container as well, read-only and at the same paths as in `server`. A CA bundle can then be delivered per Model through `spec.files`, next to the env var that points at it. The mount list moves into a small `modelFileVolumeMounts` helper that both containers use. Models without adapters are unchanged, and so is the `server` container.

The issue lists four options. I took the fourth (mount `spec.files` in the loader) for two reasons:

- the first, copying the `server` container's mounts to the loader, would not pick up mounts that `modelServerPods.jsonPatches` adds, because the patches are applied after the loader is appended;
- the second and third add new configuration surface.

The `Files` field is documented as "Files to be mounted in the model Pods", and the loader is part of those Pods.

## Testing

- New integration test `TestModelFilesInAdapterLoader`: a Model with one file, `AWS_CA_BUNDLE` pointing at it, and an `s3://` adapter. It checks that both the `server` and `loader` containers mount the file. It fails on `main`, where the loader has only the `adapters` and credentials mounts, and passes on this branch.
- `make test-unit` and `make test-integration` (envtest, Kubernetes 1.37.0) pass.
- `make lint` already reports findings on `main`; `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=main` (v2.14.0) reports none for this change.

I did not run an e2e with a real S3 endpoint and a private CA.

Fixes #801

#### What's new

Systematic’s project-connection research now flags when one checkout pins a dependency at a different version from another, making cross-project version drift easier to spot. It also reads user configuration from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` when that variable is set, matching OpenCode’s configuration lookup behavior. ### [`v0.147.0`](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/releases/tag/v0.147.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/compare/v0.146.0...v0.147.0)

#### What's new

<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Run tracing is now available in the Action when you provide `trace-endpoint`; `trace-headers` can supply collector credentials. The Action forwards each turn's trace through a loopback relay, keeping the collector credential out of the agent server's environment, and tracing remains off when the endpoint is unset.

Tracing is best-effort: invalid settings produce a warning without exposing their values, and relay or collector failures do not fail the run. The documentation explains what trace data contains, how credentials are handled with and without `isolate-agent`, and the privacy implications of sending prompts and tool activity to your chosen collector. [#​2285](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2285), [#​2292](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2292), [#​2315](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2315)

Supplying provider credentials without choosing a model now makes the default explicit: the Action reports that it will use `opencode/big-pickle` and warns when supplied credentials will go unused. If configuration disables that model's provider, the run now fails at startup with the cause and remedy instead of failing on its first turn. [#​2278](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2278)

The repository now runs Systematic's `ce:connect` sweep daily, with manual dispatch also available. Its report issue, ledger cache, and run artifacts stay in this repository; configure the documented repository variables before the first run. [#​2317](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2317)

CI checks no longer rely on a short-circuiting `grep -q` pipeline to inspect logs or a tarball listing. Reading the output first and matching it without a pipe avoids broken-pipe errors under `pipefail`, including false reports that a required plugin notice file is missing. [#​2304](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2304), [#​2312](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2312)

body:
## Integration outcome — 2026-11-23

- [x] Reviewed exact `.gitignore`-only diff and confirmed no tracked env files or affected build inputs.
- [x] No Actions checks triggered by the metadata-only path; none claimed as passed. Normal GitHub merge eligibility was clean and no rulesets are currently configured on the public repository.
- [x] Squash-merged as [`09216fbd`](https://github.com/MikeDanton/myengine-asset-pipeline/commit/09216fbdd638ea585c19443c4f52df39c3c0451b). Re-fetched `main`, verified `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example` and retained Python-cache patterns. The source branch was automatically deleted.

---

## Scope

The optional live image provider reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment. The public repository has no `.env` ignore rule, creating a preventable accidental-commit risk if a contributor stores local credentials in an environment file.

- Ignore `.env` and `.env.*` at any depth.
- Explicitly keep `.env.example` eligible for version control (future sanitized examples).
- Retain all existing ignore patterns; no tracked `.env` files currently exist.

## Validation and limits

- Reviewed the provider source and main tree; verified the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment dependency and absence of tracked `.env` files.
- Single-file `.gitignore` change; no API calls, token values, secrets, generation behavior, workflow permissions or releases changed.
- CI workflows are path-filtered and generally will not run for `.gitignore` only; do **not** report skipped checks as passed.
- This prevents *new accidental git-adds* but cannot protect credentials committed in history or supplied directly to an application; use standard credential management and key revocation if a secret was previously exposed.
- Inspect exact diff and merge eligibility before squash merge. Verify integrated rule and automatic branch retirement afterward.

body:
## What this changes

The signed-in app's full-screen "You're offline" / "Can't reach Navigate Wealth" state was the last takeover still in the old look: a rounded purple card with a generic cloud icon over a grey wash. It is now in the Navigator design, the same family as the site-wide loader (#536): paper and chart grid, the sail mark, a serif title, violet only on the action. The owner reviewed it as a live before/after preview and approved it.

What users notice:

- **Reads as "searching for a signal", not "loading".** The sail mark sits in compass range rings with a violet ping going out from it; the ping quickens while a manual check runs.
- **Two things to check, matched to the failure.** No network: Wi-Fi or mobile data, and flight mode. Network up but we can't be reached: the router's internet light (or a restart), and switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
- **Fairer wording for `unreachable`.** That state is inferred from *our* backend not answering while the browser says it is online, so the body no longer pins it on the user's router outright.
- **One status line:** amber while reconnecting, violet while checking, red with a time when a check fails ("Still no connection at 02:13. We'll keep trying."), so a second failed tap visibly did something.
- **"Your work is safe" footer.** The page underneath was always kept mounted with anything typed; it now says so, and asks the user to keep the tab open.

Unchanged behaviour: the 1.5 s delay, `inert` on `#root`, focus landing on Try again, the portal, the "You're back online" toast, and the `enabled` prop (signed-in only).

Tokens: the screen renders in the portal and the admin, which never carry `.nw-site`, so it borrows the loader's palette, type stacks and mark colours through a new `.nwl-tokens` class in `brand-loader.css` rather than copying them a third time. Values only it needs live under `--nwo-` in `offline-screen.css`. All motion is transforms and opacity; reduced motion holds the ring still and lets it breathe.

## How it was verified

Every gate run locally on Node 22, on the final tree.

- [x] `npm run format:check`
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 problems
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run typecheck:middleware`
- [x] `npm run typecheck:deno` — no error codes at all (0); this change touches no server code
- [x] `npm run depcruise` — no violations
- [x] `npm test -- --coverage` — 962 files, 14,946 tests passed, thresholds met
- [x] `npm run test:coverage:server` — 238 files, 6,296 tests passed, backend floors met
- [x] `npm run bundle:check` — every metric inside tolerance
- [x] `npm audit` — 0 high, 0 critical
- [x] `npm run build`

Also rendered in Chromium at phone and laptop widths for each state (unreachable, offline, checking, still down), with no horizontal overflow.

## Ratchets

- [x] No baseline in `quality/baselines/` moved
- [x] None had to rise

## Documentation

- [x] `docs/STATUS.md` notes the offline screen beside the loader, and the `.nwl-tokens` hook it uses
- [x] No files moved or deleted
- [x] The token-sharing arrangement is documented at the top of `offline-screen.css` and beside `.nwl-tokens` in `brand-loader.css`

## Risk

Presentation only; the connectivity logic and the hook it reads are untouched. The first symptom of a problem would be visual: the screen unstyled or the mark unfilled if `brand-loader.css` failed to load. It is imported directly by the component, so it ships in the same chunk. Rollback is a revert of this one commit.

author: jamiej5926
body:
## What

ACP sessions now wait for in-flight background model discovery before they build their model options. The wait is `session.modelRegistry.awaitBackgroundRefresh()` in `#registerPreparedSession` (`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/acp/acp-agent.ts:1961`). Every path that registers a session reaches it: `session/new` (`acp-agent.ts:1839`), the fork request `unstable_session/fork` (`unstable_forkSession` at `acp-agent.ts:1154`, `#forkManagedSession` at `:1912`), and a stored session opened by `session/load` or `session/resume` (`#openStoredSession`, `acp-agent.ts:1935`). A `session/load` or `session/resume` for a session that is already open returns the existing record without waiting (`acp-agent.ts:1844-1847` and `:1856-1859`).

The model options are built after that wait, in `#buildConfigOptions` (`acp-agent.ts:2448`), which reads `session.getAvailableModels()` at `:2466`. The responses that carry them are `session/new` (`acp-agent.ts:1107`), load (`:1119`), resume (`:1147`) and fork (`:1159`). A client can select a discovery-backed model as soon as `session/new` returns, for example `github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol-1m`, and `session/set_config_option` accepts it (`#setModelById` reads the list at `acp-agent.ts:2519`).

## Why

Fixes #19127. Before this change nothing in `acp-agent.ts` awaited the background refresh (`git grep awaitBackgroundRefresh origin/main -- packages/coding-agent/src/modes/acp/acp-agent.ts` prints nothing), so the option list could be read while `main.ts` was still running the discovery it starts after session creation (`main.ts:2502`). The 1M sibling was missing from the picker, and selecting it failed with `Unknown ACP model`.

`awaitBackgroundRefresh()` returns at once when no refresh is in flight (`packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts:1121-1126`). ACP sessions are non-interactive: `isInteractive` is false whenever `--mode` is set (`main.ts:1982`). `main.ts:2502` starts a background refresh after each non-interactive session creation, and the ACP session factory creates its sessions through that same `createSession` (`main.ts:2528`). So in practice the wait is usually real: `session/new` waits for that refresh to finish. How long the wait lasts is not measured.

Upper bounds on the wait, stated only where the code enforces them:
- Built-in providers: each model-manager fetch is capped at 15 s (`RUNTIME_DYNAMIC_MODEL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-provider-discovery.ts:38`, applied at `packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts:3345`).
- Extension `fetchDynamicModels` providers: each fetch is capped at 15 s (`packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-registry.ts:4607`).
- Configured discovery providers: the `discovery.timeoutMs` setting when set. Otherwise LiteLLM and proxy discovery use 10 s (`packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-discovery.ts:1443`, `:1520`), and a non-loopback local-engine host uses the 10 s `REMOTE_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (`model-discovery.ts:107`, `:133`). Loopback local engines use the shorter 150 or 250 ms caps passed to `discoveryProbeTimeoutMs` (`model-discovery.ts:120-133`).
- The body does not state an overall bound on the whole wait. The caps above apply per fetch or per request.

## Testing

Regression test: `lists and accepts a discovery-backed model selected while the catalog refresh is pending` in `packages/coding-agent/test/acp-agent.test.ts`.

- Before the fix (origin/main source, new test): `bun test test/acp-agent.test.ts -t "lists and accepts a discovery-backed model"` fails with `Expected to contain: "openai/gpt-5.4-1m"`.
- After the fix: the same command passes; `bun test test/acp-agent.test.ts` passes 109 of 109; `bun test` over all `test/*acp*` files passes 351 of 351.
- `bun run check:ts` exits 0. The Rust check (`check:rs`) was not run: no Rust file changed.

The two test fakes in `acp-event-mapper.test.ts` and `acp-lazy-startup.test.ts` gained the `awaitBackgroundRefresh` method the real `ModelRegistry` has.

author: ullbergm
body:
marquee and episodic showed each other's pictures: 101 Dalmatians in marquee had the poster of a series from episodic.

Both apps' claims are the same NFS export, and each app kept its poster cache in the chart's default folder, `.covers`, at the top of its claim. That is one folder for both. The cache files are named by each app's own title number (`54/poster.jpg`), so a movie and a series with the same number overwrite each other.

This sets the cache folder per app: `marquee/covers` and `episodic/covers`. The cache is only downloaded pictures, so each app fills its new folder again by itself; nothing in the library is touched. The old `.covers` folder is left behind and can be deleted afterwards.

author: zdiemer
body:
Closes #40.

45 of 47 corpus games use In-Fusio's shared SMS library. Before this, every send failed ('problem when sending the SMS'); now a mock server answers like the real one.

## Protocol (`docs/re/SMS.md`)
- **gensimu's link:** TCP to a separate In-Fusio PC tool. The outgoing message is a 140-byte "EXEN" frame with a checksum; incoming SMS are queued 500 ms and dispatched by block id, with block 0x60's contents going to `onSmsReceived`.
- **Per use case:**
  - score → `MT_RANKING` (a 993-bit record copied into the game's context; layout confirmed on GhostHunter's ranking pages);
  - opinion vote → results block 24;
  - pay-per-use 25 → no reply (success alone grants the continue);
  - unlock 1 → granted bitmap 2;
  - restore 8 → 9;
  - download 6 → 7.
- Includes a per-game table of block ids for all 44 games that send.

## Mock (`src/core/smsserver.c`)
- **Modes:** `server` (default), `delivered` (success, no reply; the simulator with its link off), `offline` (the old behaviour). API: `exen_sms_set_mode/set_log/set_date`.
- **Replies:** built only from what the player sent (their own scores and votes), delivered through `Bootstrap.smsReceived` 2 s later on the VM clock, after a host callback, never re-entrantly.
- **Save states:** an optional `SMSV` chunk holds the server's records and any reply in flight (older states load with an idle server); `exen_state_max_size` includes it.
- **Frontends:** SDL `--sms` (dates rankings with today's date); `exen-run --sms`, `--sms-log`; libretro option `exen_sms` (fixed default date, so runs stay deterministic).

## Results
- **Before/after (offline vs server):** GhostHunter continue ('Sorry, there has been a problem…' → level restarts), score → 'Ranking 1', opinion → results screen; FootballFans unlock → 'L'extension a été reçue'; MutantAlert unlock → 'Ok you've got it!'; 007 Q-lab download.
- **Corpus:** 47 games × 3000 ticks in server and offline mode, no halts; 20 games sent SMS on their own and every reply was delivered.
- **Save states:** `--selftest-state` passes with a reply in flight and after delivery.
- **Tests:** new `sms` unit test; locally 12/12 CTest; the libretro test passes with the option.

**Open:** IFRacing2's ghost/challenge blocks (27, 116, 117) get no reply, because another player's racing line can't be invented. A restore on an empty server clears the local score table, as the real service would.

author: ben-kaufman
body:
# Never place a held list without its single-use marks

A payer wallet holds a payee's Private Payment List when that payee app's `payment_lists` record is deleted or doesn't read. The record carried the marks of single-use endpoints already paid, and a list written afresh would let one of them be paid again. Several paths still allowed that:

- `place_held_list_without_marks` let the host place the list after showing the user the risk.
- Once the service forgot a delete the wallet had seen, the key read as absent and the held list, or the same list sent again, was written there with no marks. This followed a restore into a fresh store, a restore from a backup taken after the delete was seen but before any list was held, and an in-place restore from a backup taken before the hold.

Spec 6 says that "listing, restart, backup and restore do not turn that known deletion into absence", and wire 4.13 that a held list "keeps waiting, also across restart, backup and restore". Wire Section 5 ("Put back over a delete", "A visible delete without a copy") says only a protective put-back replaces the hold. No spec change is needed.

## Changes

- `Paykit::place_held_list_without_marks` is removed, with the divergent-write refusal only it used.
- The wallet marks a `payment_lists` record lost (`lgone/<record key>`) in the commit in which it sees the record deleted, from the feed or a read, and when it holds a list over a record that doesn't read. The mark is never cleared. A restore keeps the installation's own marks beside the backup's, as it keeps the installation's block floor hold.
- While a record is marked lost, an absence of it keeps the list held: when held lists are placed and when a list arrives. A list held for another reason, such as a first list whose write was refused, is still placed on the absent key once a write of it lands.
- A held list's placement is a record write with no local write in its batch, so a batch that settles late can't drop a newer hold. The hold goes in a commit of its own at a later pass, once the record holds the list.
- The docs say what the code does. A held list is placed only onto a readable write that keeps the marks this app saw. After a delete it has seen, an SDK app keeps that payee app's private lists held, even one that holds every mark, because no SDK path writes this record over a delete: this revision withholds the put-back (wire Section 5, "Incomplete protected-record contract"). The payee's public endpoints, or a list it shares from another app, remain the user's way to pay.

## Limit

A restore from a backup taken before the app ever saw the delete, after the service forgot it, still reads the key as absent: nothing the app holds records the delete. Closing it needs the service to keep the cursor for `payment_lists` deletes. A delete written by another installation of the same app is not observed as a delete (the client hands a protocol only other apps' deletes); the mark then comes when a list is held over it or its placement finds it gone. No SDK path deletes these records.

## Protocol and API impact

- Removed public SDK call: `Paykit::place_held_list_without_marks`. No binding or wire changes.
- New local state key family `lgone/`, restored with its binding checked.
- Touches none of `paykit-sdk/src/error.rs`, `paykit-ffi/src/review.rs` or `docs/paykit-host-guide.md`.

## Tests

- `unrequested::test_unrequested_list_after_a_delete_stays_held_and_its_single_use_endpoint_unpaid`: after another own app deletes the record, both the same version and a newer list stay held, across receives and a reload, with `WaitingForList` and nothing written over the delete. A write over the delete that drops the mark is refused, and one that keeps it places the list with the mark.
- `unrequested::test_unrequested_list_held_over_a_forgotten_delete_stays_held_after_a_fresh_restore`: after the service forgets the delete, a restore into a fresh store keeps the list held, a newer list is held too, and the paid single-use endpoint is never paid again. The user can still pay the payee's public endpoint.
- `unrequested::test_unrequested_delete_seen_before_any_list_survives_a_restore_and_a_forget`: the backup is taken after the wallet saw the delete and before any list came, then the service forgets the delete; restored fresh and in place, the list sent again stays held and the endpoint unpaid.
- `unrequested::test_unrequested_hold_over_a_delete_survives_an_in_place_restore_from_before_it`: an in-place restore from a backup taken before the delete keeps the installation's mark.
- `unrequested::test_unrequested_placement_settling_late_keeps_a_newer_hold`: a placement whose answer is lost settles after the record was deleted again and a newer list held; the newer hold stays and the endpoint stays unpaid.
- `unrequested::test_unrequested_list_held_for_a_refused_write_stays_held_over_a_later_delete`: a list held because its write was refused, then a delete, a forget and a restore: still held.
- `stored::test_stored_refused_first_list_placed_once_a_write_lands`: a first list whose write was refused, with no record ever written, is placed once a write lands, so the hold over an absent record never keeps a list that wasn't lost.
- Each new guard was removed in turn (the delete's observation, the restore's carry of the installation's marks, the batch without local writes, the marks at placement) and a test fails without it.
- The certificate, local-state and epoch-key tests no longer call the removed function. The local-state test asserts the exact error when a held list sits under another app's key.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo +1.100.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` and `cargo +1.91.1 check --locked --workspace --all-features`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features` with the Switch PostgreSQL backend: 2,655 passed, 0 failed.

M75 "Big worlds", version 0.35.0.

- **LOD**: automatic LOD chains from our own deterministic simplifier on import, `LodGroup` by distance or screen size with dithered cross-fade and hysteresis, octahedral impostors (`model.bake_impostor`), HLOD proxies for groups and for far streamed cells (`world.bake_hlod`, `world.bake_cell_hlods`).
- **Occlusion**: CPU `Occluder`s rasterised on the job system, areas and portals for interiors (`Camera.areaCulling`), GPU Hi-Z depth pyramid where the backend can (`SceneSettings.occlusionMode`), `render.occlusion` stats.
- **Streaming**: `StreamedWorld` cells of 3D scenes and 2D tilemaps loaded and unloaded around anchors on background threads (`world.split_cells`, `world.merge_cells`, `world.stream_status`, `tilemap.split_cells`), the editor's Cells panel.
- **Floating origin**: the world, physics, audio and renderer follow a rebase (`world.rebase`, `world.origin`, `world.absolute_position`).
- **Terrain**: heightmaps with GPU LOD, splat layers, holes, heightfield collider, `terrain.*` commands and the editor's Terrain tool.
- **Foliage**: instanced grass, trees and rocks with chunk culling, fade, LOD and wind; `foliage.scatter` / `paint` / `clear` and the editor's foliage brush.
- Polish packages per area (stream, render, terrain, editor, docs) and four doc pages split before they reached 60 KB.

Checked on macOS (Apple Silicon): Debug build of every target, the Debug suite (85 tests; the 8 that open a window did not run because the displays were asleep, so only CI runs them), the 47 example game tests in Release, `scripts/ci-preflight.sh --lint-only`. Not run on this host: MSVC/D3D11, GCC/Clang on Linux, GLES3/WebGL2, x86 (the foliage and terrain golden hashes and the streaming checksums were computed on ARM).

author: hardmax71
body:
Adds fix task B10044. [B025](https://github.com/betterlite-ai/betterlite/blob/main/.development/tasks/B025-azure-provider.yaml)'s review found that Provider::from_slug builds the Azure composition from the process environment on every request, so the litellm_settings globals never reach an Azure call in the server. The fix needs a new config section and the five server callers of Provider::from_deployment, all outside B025's scope, so B025 keeps the environment read and this task replaces it.

B10044 resolves the litellm_settings globals and the Azure variables at config load, builds the composition once in a server state slot, and passes it to the provider. A check makes sure the provider crate no longer calls process_environment. It depends on B025.

LiteLLM reads the call's value first, then the litellm global, then the environment: [main.py L1367-L1388](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/d665dc1a6315847fcad6cc2c1264ceb47c06abce/litellm/main.py#L1367-L1388). The proxy sets each litellm_settings key as a global: [proxy_server.py L6594](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/d665dc1a6315847fcad6cc2c1264ceb47c06abce/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6594).

author: felixgeelhaar
body:
## What

Taint now follows a controller into the service it is injected with.

- **Receiver types** (`core/callgraph/receivers.go`): a call on a field, parameter or variable binds through the type the file declares it with:
  - Spring constructor injection: `private final StaffService directory;`
  - NestJS parameter properties: `constructor(private readonly svc: FetchService)`
  - a Python attribute assigned a constructed instance: `self.repo = UserRepository()`

  It binds to that type's method in the one file declaring the type, or, for an interface or abstract type, to its one subtype with the method. A name declared with two types, a type two files declare, or two implementations bind to nothing. Declarations are read with comments and strings masked. The declared type is tried before the qualifier is read as a file stem.
- **Java enhanced for** (`extract_java.go`): `for (T x : items)` is read as `x = items`, conditional, so a service call in the header is a call of the method. Before, the header was skipped as structure.

## Why

On the dev split, most misses where a parameter reaches a sink were services called from a controller in another file through an injected field. The call graph left a method on a value of unknown type unresolved (ADR 0007, decision 1), so the cross-file pass never saw the call. This is the plan's "route entry points as sources across files" task. Request parameters were already sources; what was missing was the edge from the route handler to the service.

## Measured

RealVuln dev split. The 25 repos that changed were rescanned with both binaries (0d8af04 and this branch) at low load:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| F3 | 16.5 | 17.0 |
| Java | 8.0 | 8.8 |
| JS/TS | 23.0 | 23.6 |
| Python | 23.1 | 23.1 |

- **Labelled:** +28 (LDAP, XPath, SSRF, path traversal, code injection, SQL in services), none lost.
- **Unlabelled:** +38. Most are existing sink matches that taint now reaches through services, for example a class's own `exec(...)` method read as a shell and `AsyncManager.me().execute(...)` read as SQL. A few look like real unlabelled bugs, such as `path.join(DIR, `${profileName}.json`)`. The sink matches are follow-ups, not part of this change.
- **Unlabelled removed:** 1. A wrong edge where a field typed `PortalAuditService auditService` had bound to another module's `AuditService.java` by its stem.

## Tests

- `TestSourceReceiverTypes`: Java field, interface to its one implementation, TypeScript parameter property, Python attribute. Negative cases: two implementations, two types for one name, a declaration inside a comment. Each guard was falsified by disabling it.
- `TestJavaForEachHeader` and `TestJavaForEachCarriesTaint`. The classic-for guard was falsified with a ternary initialiser.
- `TestScan_CrossFileTaint`: Spring controller to injected service, and NestJS controller to injected service, end to end. Both fail with the binding removed.
- `go test ./...` and golangci-lint pass.

## Found on the way (not fixed here)

The tree-sitter parse budget is wall-clock (`DefaultBudget`, 5 s base). Under heavy load (load average above 100) a parse timed out, the scan fell back silently to the line reader, and the findings changed: damn-vulnerable-flask-application lost two XSS findings in one run and not in the next. No limitation was recorded. That breaks the determinism constraint and needs its own fix: either a budget that doesn't depend on the clock, or recording the fallback as a limitation.

author: bennyjo
body:
## What Changed

- Adds a speaker check to the gateway. A new `walkie-gateway enroll` command records six read-aloud parts from a Mac audio input and saves one voiceprint, with the speaker model's checksum, in the private state folder. `enroll --remove` deletes the voiceprint. `fetch-models.sh` now downloads the pinned 3D-Speaker CAM++ model.
- The turn detector scores each message's audio against the voiceprint while it transcribes. The conversation compares that score to a threshold set by how much speech the message holds (0.35, 0.42, and 0.50 by default). Prompts, read-back yeses, "type it", and "go" while listening are checked. Stop and decline words, wake words while paused, and switches are not. By default the check runs in shadow mode, which logs one `speaker` line per message and refuses nothing. With `--enforce-speaker` (and optional `--speaker-thresholds`), a failing message is dropped with the warning tone and "Didn't catch your voice. Say it again." With no voiceprint, the check is off, and `--enforce-speaker` refuses to start.
- Adds `gateway/tools/speaker_scores.py`, which summarizes the logged scores by speech length so the owner can pick thresholds. Also adds tests for the speaker check and for the new turn detector callback, and documents enrollment, what's checked, reading scores, and enforcing in the usage, setup, security, and develop docs and the README.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The speaker check is off without a voiceprint and only logs in its default shadow mode, the decision order in _turn_finished matches the intent's checked and unchecked kinds, the _switch refactor keeps its old behavior, and the fixer commits (2 s wording, log-line note, non-pausing recorder) are correct and limited to what they claim.

## Testing

I built a scratch state folder and models folder. The speech models are symlinked from the local install, and the speaker model was downloaded and its sha256 checked. In that setup I drove the real product live: a full enroll on a real Mac audio input, recorder timing on two real inputs, serve start-up in four speaker modes, and a paired stand-in phone sending voice clips through serve in shadow mode and enforcing. A small stand-in session took the orders the gateway sent. Every scenario passed, and the targeted speaker-check and turn-detection unit tests also passed. I stopped a conversation unit test run that went past its timeout myself, so its exit code 144 is not a failure. The change has no visual UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts and gateway logs.

| The voiceprint is saved privately with the model's sha256, and the recordings are not kept | ✅ pass | live | The state folder held only voiceprint.json, mode 0600, with model_sha256 98daf9bc...88bb5 and a 512-value vector. Enroll printed that the recordings were kept only in memory. |
| Serve logs at start whether the check is off (no voiceprint), in shadow mode (the default once enrolled), or enforcing with the owner's own thresholds, and --enforce-speaker without a voiceprint refus… | ✅ pass | live | r4-serve-start.txt |
| Shadow mode: the owner's prompt passes, and a stranger's prompt and lone yes are logged as would-refuse but still reach the session | ✅ pass | live | r4-phone-shadow-enforce.txt shadow section: owner 0.93 pass; stranger prompt 0.165 and yes 0.088 would-refuse; the session received all three |

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"davitf"} -->
_Requested by **davi** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DbMk7aw1GQgNkBfBSYo2X2?thread=cmsg_01DbMk7aw1GQgNkBfBSYo2X2Ukt7Gsn9ET8KfC8AvNwGMK)_

## For dummies

A DMG is the disk image macOS apps ship in. Until now the tests checked archivey's DMG reader against one other program, 7-Zip, plus the hashes macOS itself recorded for a few test images. This PR adds two more independent readers as test oracles: dpp-py (written in Rust) and Joachim Metz's libyal libraries (written in C). Every test image is read by all of them, and where they can read a file, its bytes must match archivey's. Nobody using archivey notices anything. The change is test-only, and the two packages are dev-only test dependencies.

## What changes

- `tests/dmg_oracle_dump.py`: runs one reader (`dpp` or `libyal`) over one image in a subprocess and prints its entries as JSON (file sha256, directories, symlink targets). Both readers are native code, so a crash or abort can't take pytest down, and the GIL question on free-threaded builds stays out of the test process.
- `tests/test_dmg_oracles.py`: 35 images × 2 readers.
  - The images: the `hdiutil` fixtures (HFS+ and APFS with zlib, bzip2, LZFSE, xz, raw and ADC runs), the HFS+ builder images (GPT, APM and no partition map, × 6 codecs) and the APFS builder images (hashed and plain keys, × 3 layouts).
  - The check runs both ways. Every file, symlink and directory archivey lists must be listed the same way by the other reader, and the other reader may list nothing archivey doesn't, apart from the HFS+ private folders a mount hides.
  - The other readers' known gaps are pinned in four tables: whole images refused, members read wrong, an image whose directories list but no file reads, and an image that lists nothing. If a reader stops getting a pinned gap wrong, the test fails and asks for the pin to be removed.
- `dev-docs/formats/dmg.md` §8: one row for the new check.
- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`: `dpp-py`, `libmodi-python`, `libfshfs-python` and `libfsapfs-python` in the dev group, CPython below 3.15 only, which is where their wheels exist. The tests skip elsewhere through `requires(...)`.

## Why

davi asked for this after the comparison of archivey's DMG reader with the Python DMG packages (tracked internally). Neither package is good enough to be a backend: dpp returns silently empty hard links and aborts the whole process on a declared huge partition. Both are still useful second opinions on the bytes. libyal is right on hard links, APM images and plain-key APFS. The run found more dpp gaps, now pinned: plain-key APFS volumes list nothing, the builder's sparse APFS file reads wrong, and decmpfs type 12 is an error.

## Risk

Tier: standard (pyproject.toml, uv.lock). Public API: none. Security: yes. The template's rule is "adds a call into native code". The calls are to test-only native readers, run in a subprocess with a timeout, on committed fixtures and builder images only. Library code is unchanged. Merge: an agent merges once the Opus pass approves and CI is green.

If the wheels go missing on some leg, `uv sync` there would try to build from source. The markers keep to CPython 3.11 to 3.14, which have wheels on Linux x86-64/aarch64, macOS and Windows x64.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/test_dmg_oracles.py`: 53 passed, 17 skipped (the pinned refusals and empty listings). A pin made deliberately stale fails with "now reads … drop it".
- `pytest tests/test_dmg.py tests/test_dmg_apfs.py`: green.
- `./scripts/check.sh --fix`: every gate passes except one script test, `test_prepare_holds_history_up_to_head_only` in the review-eval script. It reads this branch's git history and doesn't touch these files.
- The full suite runs on CI, per the repository's long-run rule.

## Checklist

- [x] The change follows CONTRIBUTING.md: its coding and testing rules and its gates.
- [x] A bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix. (No fix here.)
- [x] The DMG handbook names the new check. User docs and specs are unaffected.
- [x] No CHANGELOG line (test-only).
- [x] No behaviour change, so no `needs-minor`.

## Summary

AIRI scheduled Compact from UTF-8 bytes. That size is not the token count of the request that goes to the provider. This PR measures that projected request at each model step and names the count source. Compact still edits only the provider projection. Stored history and exact tool receipts stay in place.

This PR stands on `main`. It does not include the later Computer Use changes.

## Context

- Request: Add one independent token-budget change. Measure the request that the provider receives. Name the source as a provider count, a local tokenizer count, an estimate, or unavailable. Recalculate the budget when the model or provider changes. Keep the current Compact projection, background summary, prefix check, and tool-receipt retention. Refuse a request when the retained floor cannot fit the model window. Do not drop execution evidence to keep running.
- Scenario: Agent context compaction before further Computer Use work. Byte estimates drift for Chinese text, tool JSON, reasoning, images, and mixed providers.
- Scope: `computer_verify` evidence, concurrent operation-budget admission, and unconfirmed side effects after a crash stay in later PRs. No new global lock. No second dashboard. No new tokenizer package. Community PR [moeru-ai/airi#3387](https://github.com/moeru-ai/airi/pull/3387) stays unmerged. Its tests were a reference for budget behavior.
- Source: The phase-1 boundary for AIRI Agent and Computer Use. Baseline commits on `main` include #3473, #3496, and #3557.

## Change map

| Module | Before | After | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core Agent metering | UTF-8 byte size of the projected request | `ContextTokenUsage` for that same request | The source field stops an estimate from looking like a provider count |
| Compact scheduling | Byte pressure against `softLimitBytes` | Token soft limit when the model window is known and the count is available | Byte scheduling remains when the count source is unavailable |
| Request admission | The provider rejects an oversized request after send | AIRI refuses the retained floor before send when the count says it cannot fit | Receipts stay in history |
| Stage UI chat | Compact uses the session byte budget | Each resolved model step measures the projected request for that model and provider | A model switch does not reuse the previous count |
| Context Inspector | Reported input tokens | Measured, reported, and estimated rows in the same inspector | The ring uses reported input when it exists |

## Architecture and behavior

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Chat
  participant Compact
  participant Meter
  participant Provider

  Chat->>Chat: resolve model and provider
  Chat->>Meter: estimate projected request
  alt near the Compact threshold and a counter exists
    Meter->>Provider: count tokens
    alt count succeeds
      Provider-->>Meter: input tokens
    else count fails
      Meter-->>Chat: estimate
    end
  else below the threshold
    Meter-->>Chat: estimate or local tokenizer
  end
  Chat->>Compact: schedule from that count
  Compact-->>Chat: provider projection
  Chat->>Meter: measure retained floor
  alt floor exceeds the admission limit
    Chat-->>Chat: refuse and keep receipts
  else floor fits
    Chat->>Provider: send the projection
  end
```

Admission limits:

- A provider count or a local tokenizer count refuses the request when input tokens exceed the window minus the output reserve.
- An estimate refuses the request only when input tokens exceed the full window.
- Source `unavailable` does not refuse the request.

The official count runs only when the local estimate is at least 80 percent of the input budget, or when the input budget is zero and the estimate is positive. An exact cache hit is reused for the same payload, model, provider, and counter capability. The cache holds 32 entries.

OpenAI Responses uses `POST /v1/responses/input_tokens` when the projection has `input`. Anthropic uses `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`. Gemini uses `models.countTokens`. OpenAI-compatible chat providers do not receive the OpenAI counter. A body that cannot represent an image or a tool call is not sent. The source stays `estimated`.

## Boundaries and risks

| Invariant or boundary | Failure mode | Protection | Evidence or gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The measured object is the projected provider request | A history array hides tool schemas | `readProjectedRequest` includes messages or Responses input, plus tools | Unit tests count tool schema text. No live provider comparison in this PR |
| A model switch cannot reuse the previous count | A cached count from another model schedules Compact too late | The cache key includes provider, model, and capability | Test calls the counter again for another model |
| Compact does not delete receipts | A summary replaces tool text | `retainedFloor` and the existing Compact projection keep tool identity and text receipts | Compact test checks `noNewDispatch` and the user goal |
| An oversized retained floor is refused | AIRI drops receipts and continues | `assertRetainedContextFits` throws `ContextAdmissionError` and names the source | Unit tests for estimate, provider count, and unavailable |
| A cancelled count stops the request | A swallowed abort continues Compact | An aborted signal rethrows the counter error | Unit test |
| A provider that cannot count still uses Compact | A missing counter blocks the request | Counter failure and an unmappable body keep the estimate | Unit tests |
| Hidden protocol and image processing can differ from the count | The count looks exact | The source stays named. The provider still accepts or refuses the sent request | No live comparison against provider usage in this PR |
| Inspector labels match the three readings | A reader treats an estimate as a provider count | Separate measured, reported, and estimated rows | Unit tests. The Electron window was not captured |

## Verification

- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/core-agent typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/core-agent exec vitest run` passed: 46 files.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-ui typecheck` passed.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-tamagotchi typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck --concurrency=1 -F='./packages/*' -F='./apps/*' -F='./server/**' -F='./services/*'` passed: 66 tasks.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-ui exec vitest run src/stores/devtools/context-projection.test.ts src/stores/chat/context-token-request.test.ts` passed: 18 tests.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-ui exec vitest run src/stores/devtools/context-prompt-projection.browser.test.ts` passed: 1 test.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-ui exec vitest run` failed one existing test: `routes cancellation from a follower window to the leader runtime`. `navigator.locks` is missing on Node 22.23.4 in this environment. The test does not call the new token path. CI uses Node 26.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-tamagotchi exec vitest run` passed: 139 files, 0 failures.
- `pnpm -F @proj-airi/i18n test:run` passed in the affected run.
- `pnpm i18n:check` found no errors.
- `pnpm lint` finished with 0 errors and 695 existing warnings. None of the warnings are in this diff.

## Visual changes

The desktop Context Inspector adds measured, reported, and estimated rows. This run did not open the Electron window, so there is no before and after capture. The row text is in the English and zh-Hans locale files. The numbers come from `describeContextTokenReadings`.

body:
Finishes the Wave 4 package moves that were skipped because package `__init__.py` files eagerly re-exported their siblings (circular imports). One commit for the import rewrite, then one commit per group.

## What changed

1. **Re-exports removed** (`0a059088e`). The 33 `control/src/vonk_control/<pkg>/__init__.py` files that re-exported submodule names are docstring-only. A script rewrote every importer (about 1,000 files, including imports inside subprocess source strings, relative imports, `from pkg import module` reads such as `models.Job`, and dotted patch strings) to import from the defining submodule. A leftover scan finds no `from vonk_control.<pkg> import <Name>` for a re-exported name outside intentional fixtures. Three explicit exceptions, all deliberate:
   - `models/__init__.py` keeps module imports (no names) so any `vonk_control.models.*` import registers every mapped table; startup drops tables the metadata lacks, and `test_orm_mapping_guard` pins this.
   - (Removed after review) `api` and `db` no longer carry lazy shims; the lane programs and the stable-surface table name `api.production` and `db.connections`.
   - Guard helpers that recognised model imports by a trailing `models` module now accept `models.<submodule>` (`optimistic_boundaries`, `lifecycle_writer_boundaries`); one pinned function AST hash covering a changed function-local import was updated.
2. **Moves**, each `git mv` plus import, dotted-string, path-literal, registry and docs rewrite:
   - F2 `agent_upgrades` (2 modules), F4 `recipe_update_batches` (2), F6 `run_switch_contract` (4), F7 `model_cache` (6), F8 `artifact_jobs` (6), F9 `recipe_image_availability` (6), F10 `fleet_profiles` (8), F11 `recipe_operations` (9).
3. `30448a484` fixes two tests that read a name through a package object (found by the full control suite).

## Not done
- F9 `availability_production`: already a package (earlier S4a); its `build_observation.py` would clash with the existing module of that name.
- F10 `profile_capacity.py`, `profile_stop_authority.py`: inside `fleet_profiles` they fall under `test_fleet_profile_package_boundaries` (canonical enums, no untyped `Mapping`) and violate it (19 string literals, 1 `Mapping[str, object]`). Left flat; fixing is a separate change.
- S4b: not a clean mechanical extraction. `service` is a late-bound cell the closures capture and then pass into its own constructor, and `builder` is a 550-line closure with nested closures; needs a dependency dataclass and judgement.

## Proof (local, head `e6273e56a` (review fixes: submodule `build_cancellation` binding restored, NAS-coverage scan kept for the six moved model_cache modules, shims deleted))
- Import: 717 modules import in one process and each in a fresh interpreter, 0 failures. `api.__main__` and `worker.__main__` import without starting.
- Collection: `control/tests` 10114 and `tests` 3163 before and after (equal; only path-parametrised ids differ).
- `git diff -M origin/main...HEAD | scripts/check-added-lines -`: exit 0, no findings.

## 做了什么

#124 阶段三的**进行中** PR（骨架已落地，细节在补）：

1. **【真 bug】用户可配变量去掉 `DSH_` 前缀**：dsh 的 app-boot 里
   `BOOTSTRAP_PREFIXES = ['DSH_', 'XDG_', 'DYLD_', 'BASH_FUNC_']` ⇒ **任何 `.env` 文件里写 `DSH_*`
   都会让 dsh 拒绝启动**（`dsh: …/.env sets "DSH_BASE_URL", which only the launching environment may set`）。
   而 dsh 会读**启动目录**的 `.env`（`backend/ai/.env` 正是那个位置），我们的 `.env.example` 又教用户写
   `DSH_BASE_URL` ⇒ 照着配就炸。⇒ 我们**用户可配**的变量改名 `AI_DSH_*`
   （`runner.ts` 的 `dshRunnerConfig` + 插件侧的 `DSH_AI_*` → `AI_DSH_*`）。
   dsh 自己认的名字（`DSH_HOME` 等）仍按原名传进**子进程环境**（进程环境是合法的，只有 `.env` 文件被禁）。
2. D3 验收脚本入库（无 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` ⇒ 打印跳过、exit 0）
3. 静态守卫：入库的 `.env` 模板里不许出现 `DSH_` 开头的键

Closes #<issue 号>

## 怎么验

```bash
cd backend/ai && npx vitest run
node scripts/e2e/dsh-official-route.cjs      # 无 key ⇒ 跳过
node scripts/e2e/dsh-env-names.static.cjs    # 静态守卫
```

## 高风险

⚠️ 高风险：AI 闸门口径 —— 本次**只改环境变量名**，闸门口径零改动；但 `runner.ts` 是闸门接线点，PM 请过目。

author: crzyc98
body:
## What changes

When `PLANALIGN_API_TOKEN` is set, Studio now signs in through a screen instead of a build-time variable.

- **API:** `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE /api/auth/session`. `POST` checks the token and sets an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie (`planalign_session`, 12 hours, `PLANALIGN_API_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`). Sessions live in memory, so a restart signs everyone out.
- **Protected routes** accept the cookie or the existing `Authorization: Bearer` / `X-API-Token` header. A cookie request that changes data must also carry an `Origin` from `PLANALIGN_API_CORS_ORIGINS`. Header requests are unchanged.
- **WebSockets** accept the cookie or a Bearer header. The `?token=` parameter is no longer accepted.
- **Studio:** a sign-in screen appears when a token is required, and again when a session expires. "Sign out" is in the settings menu. `VITE_PLANALIGN_API_TOKEN` is gone.
- **CLI:** `planalign studio` no longer passes the token to the frontend. It sets `PLANALIGN_API_CORS_ORIGINS` to the addresses it serves Studio from, unless the variable is already set.
- `SECURITY.md` describes the new flow.

With no token set (the loopback default), nothing changes and no sign-in screen appears.

## Effect on results

None. No engine or simulation code changes.

## Risk

Medium, limited to deployments that set a token.

- Scripts that opened a WebSocket with `?token=` must send a Bearer header.
- A deployment that serves Studio from an address not in `PLANALIGN_API_CORS_ORIGINS` gets a 403 at sign-in with a message naming the variable. Starting through `planalign studio` sets it automatically.
- The cookie is marked `Secure` only when the request arrived over HTTPS or carries `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`.

## Testing

- `tests/api/test_auth_sessions.py`, `test_api_auth.py`, `test_route_auth_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/cli`, the OpenAPI contract and theme contract tests: pass.
- Fast suite before review edits: 5301 passed; the only failures were the 17 `dbt_packages` manifest tests of a fresh worktree and one component-count fixture, since updated.
- Studio `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`: 61 files, 728 tests pass.
- Live check against a temporary API with curl: status, wrong token (401), missing or foreign Origin (403), sign-in, cookie GET (200), cookie POST with allowed Origin (201), Bearer header (200), docs with cookie (200), sign-out, then 401.
- Not done: the sign-in screen has not been looked at in a browser.

## How to revert

Revert this PR. Deployments would need `VITE_PLANALIGN_API_TOKEN` again.

author: churichard
body:
An IMAP server that refuses a SELECT with a bare `NO`, or with a temporary response code such as `UNAVAILABLE`, now gets one more SELECT on the same connection before the operation fails. A refusal with any other code, such as `NONEXISTENT` or `TRYCREATE`, still fails right away. A failure after the folder opens is never retried, and neither is a caller-owned connection that was closed when the folder was refused. A folder search that lists folders again after a refusal selects the folder at most three times in all.

Failures now also record the reply's RFC 5530 response code in `ProviderFailure.responseCode`, from a fixed list (`FAILURE_RESPONSE_CODES`), or `other` for any other code. Self-hosted telemetry sends it as `response_code`. The server's text is never kept.

## Why

FLU-392: one Fluxmail Cloud user with two AOL mailboxes hit `provider_unavailable` (`select`/`server_no`) three times in two days, in `list_emails` and `list_emails_batch`. Each time, AOL took 14.7 to 15.7 seconds to answer the SELECT and then refused it. That mailbox normally opens a folder in 0.3 to 3 seconds, and the next call, seconds later, opened the same folders normally. Every failure was the first call after a quiet period. Fluxmail has no 15-second timer on this path, so the refusal is AOL's. Other clients report Yahoo-hosted servers, which include AOL, answering `NO ... Server error - Please try again later` when the backend is slow.

The server's reply text isn't recorded anywhere, so its exact response code is unconfirmed. If the retry doesn't clear it, the new `responseCode` field will show the code on the next occurrence.

## Changes

- `@fluxmail/core`: add `FAILURE_RESPONSE_CODES` and the optional `ProviderFailure.responseCode`.
- `provider-imap`: `mapImapError` records the allowlisted `serverResponseCode`, or `other`. `withMailbox` selects once more after a bare or temporary `NO`, including on a caller-owned search connection that is still usable, and never reconnects for a refusal. The connection keeps its folder listing when the second SELECT works. The stale-listing retry in `listMessagesWithClient` doesn't select twice again.
- `server`: telemetry sends `response_code`; `docs/telemetry.md` and the public telemetry page list it.
- Tests: a scripted IMAP server covers a bare `NO` and an `[UNAVAILABLE]` refusal that clear on the next SELECT, a refusal that persists (two SELECTs, then the error with its code), `[NONEXISTENT]` and `[TRYCREATE]` (no retry), a reused folder listing after a refusal clears, a caller connection closed on refusal (one SELECT), and the three-SELECT cap after listing folders again. Error-mapping and telemetry tests cover kept and dropped codes.

## Verification

The new selection tests fail on `main` and pass on this branch. Docs generation and check, lint, format, typecheck, contract check and the full test suite pass. AOL's behaviour itself can't be reproduced without a real AOL account, so the retry is verified only against the synthetic server.

## Cloud

Cloud gets the retry with the next `@fluxmail/core` bump. Reporting `provider_response_code` in Cloud telemetry is a small follow-up after that bump. No MCP tool, schema or scope changes.

author: wilfight
body:
## Objetivo

Mostrar, com código que roda, que o ciclo de vida montado em scripts npm na atividade de build é o mesmo que o **Maven** e o **Gradle** trazem prontos. Uma regra real do sistema, a idade do doador (número inteiro de 16 a 69 anos), é construída pelas três ferramentas com os mesmos casos de teste.

**Comece por aqui:** [`comparativo-maven-gradle/README.md`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle/README.md), com a tabela que liga cada script npm a uma fase do Maven e a uma tarefa do Gradle.

## O que entrou

- **Regra em Java:** [`ElegibilidadeDoador.java`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle/src/main/java/br/ufam/bancodesangue/elegibilidade/ElegibilidadeDoador.java), espelho de [`src/lib/donor-eligibility.ts`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/src/lib/donor-eligibility.ts).
- **Os mesmos testes em JUnit:** [`ElegibilidadeDoadorTest.java`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle/src/test/java/br/ufam/bancodesangue/elegibilidade/ElegibilidadeDoadorTest.java), espelho de [`tests/donor-eligibility.test.ts`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/tests/donor-eligibility.test.ts).
- **Maven:** [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle/pom.xml), com plugins de versão fixa e o `maven-enforcer-plugin` na fase validate, que exige Java 21 e Maven 3.9, o equivalente ao `engines`.
- **Gradle:** [`build.gradle.kts`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle/build.gradle.kts), com toolchain Java 21 e JUnit Platform.
- **Workflow separado:** [`comparativo-maven-gradle.yaml`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/.github/workflows/comparativo-maven-gradle.yaml), com os jobs `npm test`, `mvn verify` e `gradle build` lado a lado. Os dois `.jar` ficam como artifacts.

## O que não muda

- O sistema continua usando só a regra em TypeScript; o módulo Java não entra no build da aplicação.
- O pipeline principal ([`homologacao.yaml`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/blob/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/.github/workflows/homologacao.yaml)) e o check obrigatório do `master` não mudam.
- O workflow novo só roda quando a pasta [`comparativo-maven-gradle/`](https://github.com/AugustoAzev/banco-de-sangue/tree/b55f35afb603b0695d329125d198581bfc16941b/comparativo-maven-gradle), a regra ou os testes dela mudam, ou manualmente em **Actions → Comparativo npm, Maven e Gradle → Run workflow**.

## Verificação

- Java, Maven e Gradle não estão instalados na máquina da equipe. A verificação é o próprio workflow deste PR, rodando no GitHub.
- `pom.xml` conferido como XML válido e o workflow conferido como YAML válido antes do envio.

## Limitação conhecida

O repositório não traz os wrappers (`mvnw` e `gradlew`). No CI, o Gradle está fixado na versão 9.9.2, e o Maven é o da imagem do GitHub, com a versão mínima conferida pelo enforcer.

## Summary

The second part of FR-206, after #87: a staging copy of a WordPress site now uses its own database copy and its own address.

Before this change, a staging copy of a WordPress site kept the database settings of the live site in `wp-config.php`. Thus the copy changed the live database, and it sent each visitor to the live address.

- **Database copy.** In the job `CreateWebsite` of the copy, the agent sets `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER` and `DB_PASSWORD` of the database copy in `wp-config.php`. The website user of the copy writes the file, and the password goes on standard input. When the agent cannot set the three values, the job fails before the copy starts. Thus the copy never connects to the live database.
- **New job `StageWordPress`.** When the copy runs, the agent replaces the live address with the address of the copy (`wp search-replace`, `WP_HOME` and `WP_SITEURL`). It sets `blog_public` to 0 and `WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE` to `staging`, then reads the versions again.
- **Own WordPress record.** The copy gets its own record with the status `copying` until the job is complete. Its automatic updates are off.
- **Member address.** The staging copy no longer gets the member address of the source, because that address is unique.
- **Panel, CLI, OpenAPI and docs.** They show the WordPress copy. The docs are architecture, security, status and screenshots.
