author: angelmunoz
body:
## Summary

Stack **6 of 6** for `FunGoo.Metro` (stacked on `metro/05-render-scenes`). This PR adds `MetroFlipView`, the first control of the planned set, and the public test seam that the next PRs use.

### What's included

- **`MetroFlipViewCell` (`FunGoo.Metro/MetroFlipView.fsi/.fs`):** shows one item at a time.
  - A slide moves the outgoing item and the incoming item on one paint-bound translation. The slide shows the direction of the step and runs without cell rebuilds.
  - A timer ends each slide after the track animation settles. The wait is at most one more slide duration, so a window that stops rendering still settles.
  - Previous and next edge buttons (40 px) at the vertical center. The button at an end is disabled.
  - Indicator dots (8 px, the active dot 10 px, each inside a 24 px target).
  - A horizontal swipe (48 px, the same threshold as Pivot) and the `Left`, `Right`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home`, and `End` keys.
  - Reduced motion and a host window that is not open snap into place. `ShowNavigation` and `ShowIndicators` hide the buttons and the dots.
- **Public view seam:** `MetroFlipView.buildView`, and `View`, `State`, and `Handle` on the cell. A test can build the real tree and raise its events through the public API.
- **Tests (`tests/FunGoo.Metro.Tests/FlipViewTests.fs`, `TestSupport.fs`):** two tests, with no reflection. They cover the tree contract, navigation events, the keys, indicator dots, hidden chrome, the slide start in both directions, swipe rules, canceled gestures, reduced motion, an unknown identifier, and the timer-driven slide end.
- **Gallery:** a `flip view` tab (`samples/MetroGallery/FlipViewTab.fs`) and a `flip-view` scene for `goo render`.
- **Plan and changelog:** PR 6 row, a new hard fact, and the FlipView in the `**Metro:**` entry.

### Design decisions from the Metro skill

| Point | Metrino | This PR | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Keyboard | No key handler | `Left`, `Right`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home`, `End` | Keep the platform convention of the Windows FlipView |
| Edge buttons | Hidden until hover or focus | Always visible when `ShowNavigation` is on | The button that has keyboard focus must be visible |
| Slide | Content track, 333 ms | Outgoing and incoming item on one translation, 333 ms decelerate | Same reading of direction, with one mounted item at rest |
| Dot target | 8 px button | 8 px dot in a 24 px target | Touch targets must be generous |
| Swipe | 15 % of width | 48 px | One swipe threshold in the library, shared with Pivot |

### Images

`goo render samples/MetroGallery/MetroGallery.fsproj --scene flip-view --theme dark --size 1200x800`

![FlipView gallery tab, dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3be0d169-09fd-426f-81fe-a9824399a912)

`goo render samples/MetroGallery/MetroGallery.fsproj --scene flip-view --theme light --size 1200x800`

![FlipView gallery tab, light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd5032dc-4eaf-436d-a05d-83538f1fb1de)

`goo render` does not advance app animations, so each frame shows the rest state on the first item. The previous button is dimmed because it is disabled on the first item.

### Verification

- `dotnet fantomas --check` passes on the six changed F# files. Every `.fs` file in `FunGoo.Metro/` has a paired `.fsi` file, with XML doc comments in the `.fsi` files only.
- `dotnet build FunGoo.slnx` (Debug and Release): 0 errors. A full rebuild shows the 3 existing `FS0046` warnings in the generated `FunGoo/Widgets/Setters.g` files on `main`. This PR does not change those files.
- `dotnet test tests/FunGoo.Metro.Tests/FunGoo.Metro.Tests.fsproj` (Debug and Release): 37/37 passed (35 before this PR).
- `dotnet run --project samples/MetroGallery/MetroGallery.fsproj -- --check` (Debug and Release): `MetroGallery checks passed.`
- `goo render samples/MetroGallery/MetroGallery.fsproj --list` prints `controls`, `flip-view`, `motion`, `overview`, `typography`.

### Skill audit

**`goo-fsharp`**

| Checklist item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Function field in a props, input, or store record | None. `MetroFlipViewInput`, `MetroFlipViewItem`, and `MetroFlipViewState` hold data and state handles only. Events travel as one DU over one callback |
| Curried view or `create` function with no partial application | None. `buildView`, `defaults`, `indexOf`, and `mount` take tupled arguments |
| Delegate created inside `Build` for a mounted widget input | None. The FlipView mounts no widget. The cell factory is created once outside `Build` |
| `Rebuild()` on the cell that authored the handler | The gallery tab calls `Rebuild()` from `onSelect`. The FlipView cell owns that callback, so the tab must rebuild itself |
| Tree read, write, or `Rebuild()` on a background thread | None. The slide timer runs on the UI thread |
| I/O inside `Build` | None |
| Keyed and unkeyed children mixed | Fixed in the gallery tab. Each parent now has keyed children only or unkeyed children only |
| F# list hand-converted for `Children` | None |
| Formatting pipeline per row | None |
| Cell holding a sibling cell | None |

**`goo-widgets-fsharp`:** This PR mounts no `Goo.Widgets` input. `MaterialIcons.Create` is composed as a child Blob, as the tiles do. All items are not applicable.

**`metro-design-system`**

| Audit | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome | The edge buttons and the dots each have one function. The content has no border and no shadow |
| Typography | The active item carries a 26 px light title and a secondary caption |
| Motion | The slide shows direction. Reduced motion removes it |
| Form factor | Desktop: edge buttons and keys. Touch: swipe. `ShowNavigation` gives a swipe-only layout |
| Ergonomics | 40 px edge buttons, 24 px dot targets |
| Glanceability | One item at a time, with its position shown by the dots |

**Rules from `AGENTS.md` and the plan:** No reflection in library code or in the new tests. No `Action` or `Func` wrapper was needed in the new code.

### Constraint found during this PR

A headless `EmbeddedWindowHost` with no presentation target does not advance animations. `Window.PumpEmbedded` sets `frameAllowed` to `false` when `windowTarget` is `nil`, and `Window.Pump` uses the same gate. For that reason the tests assert the start of each slide and the timer-driven end, and they do not assert animation progress. The plan records this as hard fact 12.

author: nahuel11500
body:
Fixes #912.

*Sync* on an Application (its page, the Argo CD page's row menu, the Argo CD panel) reads the Application, then opens a dialog: its resources out of sync, all ticked (untick some to sync only those left; hooks run only when all are synced, past 200 the whole app syncs), *Prune* naming exactly what it deletes (out of sync and no longer in git, of the resources ticked), and *Dry run*, whose result is read back from `status.operationState` when Argo CD ends it (up to 30 s). The `kubectl patch` shown follows the choices. *Terminate* (while an operation runs, also on an Application being deleted, whose deletion a stuck sync holds) sets `status.operationState.phase: Terminating`, as `argocd app terminate-op` does, and is retried on a conflict as argocd-server does. *Roll back…* on each past deployment (and *Roll back to the previous deployment* in the row menu) writes the sync argocd-server's Rollback writes: that deployment's revision(s) and source(s), apply strategy, the app's syncOptions, no prune. The deployment the dialog names is pinned by its id, so one landing while the dialog is open changes nothing. It is disabled with auto-sync on and refused then.

The checks argocd-server makes are made on the Application read right before the write (`k8s::argo::ops`): nothing starts while another operation runs or the Application is being deleted (Terminate excepted), no rollback with auto-sync on or without a recorded source, no resource the app doesn't have; the patch carries the `resourceVersion` read, so a change meanwhile is refused. The window's writes go through its client (WriteGate, write mode, the hub's protection, and now Run as on the Argo CD page and panel too).

Agents: `gitops` gets `sync` with `resources`, `prune` and `dry_run`, `terminate` and `rollback` (`deployment_id`, or the previous one), authorized as `patch` and rechecked before the write; the approval banner names what a prune deletes (read only when the user will be asked) and, for a rollback without `deployment_id`, the deployment it goes to, which is then sent by its id. A sync with prune, from the dialog or an approved call, is refused if it would delete more than the list shown. A `gitops` dry run still counts under Activity's Writes: it writes the Application's operation. Options given to an action that doesn't take them are refused, not ignored. `gitops` now takes `dry_run` (docs/agents.md and the `my_permissions` test updated).

Tests:
- `k8s::argo::ops`: the default sync is today's patch; options, resources, resourceVersion; rollback of one source and of several; terminate; refusals (operation running, auto-sync on, being deleted but Terminate allowed, unknown resource, no source); a rollback pinned to the deployment shown; prune refused past the list shown; prune limited to the resources picked (proptest); a dry run's result read only once it ended.
- `mcp::preview`: the sync preview with resources named, prune and dry run.
- `mcp::server::write_tools`: the approval detail pins the rollback sent and bounds the prune approved; `call_writes` keeps a `gitops` dry run under Writes.
- `details::argo`: the kubectl shown; the dialog's choice gives the whole sync when all are ticked and exactly the ticked ones otherwise (proptest).
- e2e on kind: installs the Application CRD (no status subresource, like Argo CD's) and plays the controller. An agent without a patch rule writes nothing; a sync of two resources with prune writes them and names what is pruned; a second sync while it runs is refused; terminate sets Terminating; a rollback writes deployment 1's revision and source; a rollback with auto-sync on is refused; a dry run returns the result the controller wrote; with write mode off the window's client refuses a sync.

Reconciled with #882: the banner's sync preview takes the sync's options (only the resources named, prune shown as deleted or, in a dry run, would be, and the dry run itself), and reuses the Application read for the prune list rather than reading it twice.

forge-cli 0.39.0 changes two rules the SDK copies:

author: derektu
body:
Part of #344（第 1 區：知識庫管理）

## 系統現在的樣子

- **匯入分兩階段**：先把要寫入的檔案全部解開到 Vault 裡的暫存資料夾，再逐一改名放到位。準備階段失敗時 Vault 不變；放到位階段失敗時，匯入對話框顯示部分內容已更新、匯入前備份的路徑與「顯示位置」，以完全取代匯入備份即可還原。開啟 Vault 時刪掉留下的暫存資料夾。
- **從匯出檔建立**：解開到目標旁的暫存資料夾後改名；程式中途停止時留下的資料夾由使用者刪除。
- **操作鎖**：同一時間一個操作，期間拒絕寫入；讀取不受影響。
- **格式版本**：Vault 與匯出檔共用常數 1；拒絕較新的版本，讀得了較舊的；新增來源類型時加 1（有測試把關）。
- **匯出檔讀取**：路徑安全與每檔 SHA-256。

## 拿掉的機制

匯入 journal 與自動恢復、等待中取消（`POST /api/vault/cancel`）、讀取升級、磁碟空間預檢、套用前重新比對、不屬於知識庫的檔案計數、64 MiB／大小寫重複／項目數上限、plugin 各自的格式版本與標記檔升版、巢狀位置檢查、匯入後索引失敗的重建備援（`searchRebuildNeeded`）。

## 測試

一個行為只在一層測：規則在 domain 以表格測，route 只測接線，runtime 只測切換，主要流程交給 E2E。產品程式 +282／−785，測試 +819／−2399。

## 驗證

- `npm run verify`：通過
- 全部回歸流程 `flows run --jobs 3 --issue 344 --label merge`（Web＋Desktop 背景模式）：21／21 通過
- 真引擎匯入→索引測試：通過

## 共用檔

`docs/storage-and-search.md`、`docs/architecture.md`、`README.md`、`skills/xr-collector-agent/SKILL.md`、verify skill（`features/vault-transfer.md`、`flows/vault-transfer.mjs`、`flows/app-update.mjs`）、`shared/vault/vault-types.ts`（`partiallyApplied`）、`shared/api/api-routes.ts`、IPC `revealExport` → `revealTransferFile`。

author: juliusmarminge
body:
## Problem

Every existing scenario starts a server on an empty database with one tiny git repo. Real servers carry months of threads, sit at 1–1.5 GB RSS, and run git on real-size trees, and that's where they stall. This adds an opt-in `busy` scenario (`--only busy`) that measures that server.

Expected: the benchmark measures a server shaped like a real one (a large database, real repositories and background git work), so costs that scale with data or with server memory, such as git's fork cost, show up before release.

## Change

- **Seeding.** The checkout's own `migrate-dev-db` copies the developer's `~/.t3/userdata/statev2.sqlite` read-only and drops scheduled tasks, pending work, auth sessions and environment links, once per checkout per invocation. `--seed-dir` reuses a base dir seeded once (`vp run migrate-dev-db --base-dir <dir>`). Seeding the full 14 GB source takes 2–5 min. Set `TMPDIR` to a real disk.
- **No real paths.** Each server gets a copy of the seed. In every non-transcript text column, each occurrence of the real home prefix or an original project root, mid-string too, is moved to a path under the run's temp dir that does not exist. This reaches thread and run worktree paths, provider session and checkpoint scope `cwd`, and provider-thread native paths. `tracked_folders_json` and `favicon_path` are cleared, and `task_folders` and the durable `workflow_*` tables are emptied. Only then is each project pointed at a `git clone --shared` of the checkout. The run **fails** if any such column still names a real path. Paths are matched in every spelling a database holds (as written, JSON-escaped with doubled backslashes, and with forward slashes), and each prefix is rewritten to a marker first, so a rewritten value is never rewritten again. Transcript text (events, messages, turn items, titles) keeps its words; the server never acts on it.
- **No resumed work, on every path.** `migrate-dev-db` drops families for every startup recovery kind (`unread-steers` and `restart-continuations` were missing; the list is now a `satisfies Record<ProjectionRecoveryKind, true>`), through one `resumableThreadIds()` built on the server's `getRecoveryThreadIds`. It also gains `--drop-resumable <db>`, which removes those families in place (keeping provider sessions a kept thread still binds) and fails if any remain. It refuses a target whose canonical path is the live database, including through a symlink, and one a running server holds. The benchmark runs this checkout's copy of it on each server's own database, so a seed from an older checkout passed via `--seed-dir` is made safe too, and the server refuses to start if it fails. After the rest window, busy asserts that no run started and the fake API saw no request. Proved with a seed holding a planted pending steer: dropped, no run, no API request, and the only `claude` process was the scenario's own git traffic, after the window.
- A failed git-traffic turn fails the scenario: the git window races the traffic loop, which only ends by failing.
- **Measured:** `busy.readyMs`; a 30 s rest window (CPU, wakeups, RSS, heap, ELD, GC) 30 s after ready; the HTTP shell snapshot a client loads first (`GET /api/orchestration/shell?omitIdleSubagents=1&omitOlderSettled=1` with a CLI-issued bearer session), 5 loads timed to the last byte, plus its size; and a 30 s `git` window of back-to-back short turns in a clone, each ending in a checkpoint of the whole tree, with ELD p99 as the headline. That window also saves a CPU/allocation profile (`busyGit`).
- **Ballast.** Seeded data alone keeps the server at ~0.5 GB RSS (heap ~185 MB, even with 1,726 threads), because a long-lived server's RSS comes from what it accumulates, not from the database. Fork cost scales with mapped memory, so `--busy-ballast-mb` (default 768) makes the server retain that many touched, off-heap MB through the inspector. That brings RSS to ~1.3 GB without adding GC work, so heap metrics stay real. It's recorded, not compared. With no ballast, the git window's ELD p99 was 13.8 ms; with it, 47–80 ms.
- Results hold numbers only, never thread content. The `migrate-dev-db` output that names projects is not printed.

## Scope

Maintainer tooling, not a product change, so no issue: requested by Julius (maintainer) in the T3 Code thread that investigated the 0.1.11 slowdown, to widen the server benchmark from #41159 (`scripts/server-metrics.ts`). It also runs in the maintainers' daily performance task. Part of a stack: #41252 → #41280 → #41281 → #41282. Outside `scripts/`, only the dev tool `apps/server/scripts/migrate-dev-db.ts` (and its test) changes, so dev seeds stop keeping work a server would resume.

## Verification

- `TMPDIR=~/.cache/t3tmp vp run check:changed` passes. Also ran the default seeding path (no `--seed-dir`) end to end.
- Not checked: macOS and Windows. The no-agent-scope #31488 A/B (only agent scope was run). Archived threads, which the seed tool doesn't keep. The 768 MB ballast (`--busy-ballast-mb`) is synthetic and is not compared between runs.

### Numbers on cups (1,726 threads in 9 projects, 3.5 GB DB, one run each)

| | agent scope | no agent scope |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| readyMs | 7,500 | 7,568 |
| rest CPU % / wakeups/s | 5.5 / 26.7 | 5.6 / 26.1 |
| rest RSS / heap MB | 1,297 / 181 | 1,293 / 181 |
| rest ELD p99 / max ms | 2.0 / 279 | 2.2 / 214 |
| rest GC count / pause ms | 18 / 114 | 18 / 83 |
| shell snapshot median / p90 ms (1,031 KB) | 193 / 1,196 | 195 / 1,468 |
| git window CPU % | 44.2 | 41.4 |
| **git window ELD p99 / max ms** | **68.9 / 225** | **80.4 / 196** |

In the git window's CPU profile, `spawn` is the top frame: 3.1 s of a 20 s profile, ahead of the garbage collector at 0.6 s.

### #31488 A/B (the scenario this was built to show)

`ab` of origin/main (0356d68) against #31488's head merged onto it locally (conflicts resolved to main's side plus the launcher wiring; main already carries the `layerWithSpawn` patch). `--only busy --seed-dir … --rounds 3`, agent scope:

author: temotxt
body:
Adds an opt-in force term for a time-varying solar gravitational parameter. It is off by default, and with it off nothing changes numerically.

## Convention (inferred, not documented by JPL)
GM_sun(t) = GMS · (1 + rate · (t − t0) / Julian year), rate = DE440 header `GMSDOT` (−9e-14), t0 = J2000.0 TDB. No public JPL document states the formula, the unit or the reference epoch. The convention rests on the fit against `de440.bsp`, on JPL IOM 335N-20-01 ("(dMS/dt)/MS, from J2000", lunar-ranging software) and on the non-zero `GMSDOT` in DE440's "used for integration" comment block. Decision record: #70 items 9 and 11. OI-04 is amended and stays open.

## What is added
- `ferroastro_forces::SolarGmRate`, `SolarGmVariation`; `ForceTerm::time_origin` (default `None`); `ferroastro_propagate::de440_inferred_solar_gm_rate`.
- Only the Sun's Newtonian pull uses GM(t). WHFast refuses the term; the scenario runner never adds it.
- PHY-023 as `draft`; vectors `tests/vectors/solar-gm-rate.toml`, registered in af2b547 before the implementation.

## Measured (353 bodies, 10 yr against de440.bsp, rustc 1.99.0)
| Check | Bound | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Mercury, option on | ≤ 1.0 m | 0.705 m |
| Venus, option on | ≤ 5.0 m | 2.999 m |
| Mercury, option off | 85.79 ± 15 m | 85.788 m |
| Two-body adiabatic a·GM | ≤ 1e-11 | 5.8e-15 |

The data bounds were set with the scratch measurements known, so the data test is a reproduction check, not a blind prediction.

## Known limits
- Mars's along-track residual grows from +14 m to +52 m with the term on. The shift is consistent with the term (same sign as Mercury and Venus, scaling with orbital speed); it exposes a separate Mars error whose cause is not measured.
- Generic `Ias15`/`Abm`/`Irk16` drivers started at t0 ≠ 0 are not guarded against a wrong time origin (documented; `NBodyPropagator` refuses with FA-E0500).
- No scenario or CLI switch yet.

## Review
Independent referee approved the code at 59737e7 and re-ran the data test. The documentation commit 4ab45ac followed and was not refereed.

Refs #42, #70

author: blackhole1
body:
`brew audit` rejects an explicit `version` that only repeats what brew scans from the url, so _Formula/dockswipe.rb_ failed audit on its own. That kept CI red even after #2, and the next dockswipe release would have died at the bump's audit step. The formula now has no `version` line and carries the version in its two urls, and _bump-dockswipe.yml_ rewrites it there, with the already-current check and the asserts following suit.

Running the workflow's own rewrite script from a fake older version up to 0.1.0 reproduced this formula byte for byte, and the result passes `brew style` and `brew audit --formula --online --strict` locally on Homebrew 7.0.15. Both arch urls scan to the same version. With the casks already current, CI here should be fully green.

- **Vérifié sans impact** : `.default({})` sur des objets sans défauts internes, `z.record` à clés libres, uuid (randomUUID v4), pas d'`.email()`/`.ip()`, aucun texte d'erreur zod attendu par les tests ou l'interface (les messages affichés changent seulement de formulation).
- **osv-scanner** : exceptions zod 3 (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) et vitest 3 / tinypool retirées, devenues inutiles (vérifié : « unused ignores », aucune vulnérabilité non exemptée).

## What
Adds Flux (hosted by fal.ai) as a second option for the ideal-partner illustration, alongside Gemini.

Gemini's image model returned HTTP 429 ("You exceeded your current quota") in production — its image generation needs billing enabled on the Google account, which many free-tier Gemini setups don't have. fal.ai's Flux Schnell is pay-per-image with no monthly minimum (roughly $0.003/image) and needs no special billing setup beyond adding some credit to a fal.ai account.

body:
Writer fix in the csv/tsv cause cluster of markup-carve/carve#6424 and markup-carve/carve#6425.

## The two ticket repros

carve-php next2 (da993a03) already writes both unchanged, before and after this PR, so neither carve-php line is ticked by it. The PR adds both shapes as regression rows.

markup-carve/carve#6424, input and output (the ticket's Expected section):

````
{table footer-rows=1}
```csv
h
 a
c
```
````

markup-carve/carve#6425, input and output (the ticket's Expected section):

````
{table body-rows=0}
```csv
""
```
````

## The gap this PR fixes

The variant sweep for those tickets found one carve-php writer gap: a body's leading header rows (`body-header-rows`, C2-B-230) forced the pipe form. `TableWriter::allowsDelimited` wanted non-header cells in every body row. The pipe form cannot spell a padded or multiline cell, so fmt refused the table, or wrote it as a pipe table and dropped its recorded `csv` form (C2-W-066). The leading all-header rows of each body now pass the check, as carve-rs `delimited_row` does. carve-js and carve-rs next2 already write these shapes in the delimited form.

Input:

````
{table body-rows=1 body-header-rows=1}
```csv
h
 b
c
```
````

Before:

```
carve[writer-refused]: field-unspellable: Carve source cannot spell the value field of a text node here at /children/0/children/1/children/0/children/0/children/0/children/0/value
```

After (the input unchanged, as carve-js and carve-rs write it):

````
{table body-rows=1 body-header-rows=1}
```csv
h
 b
c
```
````

Input with no padded cell:

````
{table header-rows=0 body-rows=0 body-header-rows=1}
```csv
a
```
````

Before (same tree, csv form lost):

```
{body-rows=0 body-header-rows=1}
| a |
```

After:

````
{table body-rows=0 body-header-rows=1 header-rows=0}
```csv
a
```
````

## Variant sweep

2,400 generated csv/tsv tables (two seeds; padded, multiline and quoted cells, empty cells, one to three bodies, `header-rows`, `footer-rows`, `body-header-rows`, `body-header-cols`). For every case: carve-php fmt output parses back to the same tree, fmt is idempotent, the table stays delimited, and the render matches carve-rs next2 (5ecd18ac). fmt output matches carve-rs except for attribute order in the `{table ...}` line (328 cases, parse-equal). Before this PR: 3 refusals and 1 lost csv form, all `body-header-rows` shapes. After: 0.

## Timing

`fmt` per call through the CLI, opcache on, minus startup, best of 7, fixtures of csv tables with a foot:

| size | this PR | next2 | 0.1.17 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2k | 5.2 ms | 4.5 ms | 19.7 ms |
| 8k | 28.0 ms | 27.3 ms | 76.4 ms |
| 32k | 119.4 ms | 121.5 ms | 350.9 ms |

codex review (medium): "The change makes delimited-table eligibility consistent with the existing body-header row counts, and the targeted tests pass. I found no actionable regression."

body:
## What and why

Closes #2685

The Files add-on hid every folder that is its own git repository whenever the workspace's `.gitignore` named it. A workspace of several repositories (Pilatus: `dlh_*/` in the outer `.gitignore`) showed only `.claude`, `.github` and `docs`; the person's real work was missing.

Now, like git: a folder holding a `.git` folder or file (repository, worktree, submodule) is always listed, and outer ignore rules stop there. Its own `.gitignore` files still hold, `.git` itself stays out (program folder), links are still never followed, and the person's leave-out list still wins.

**Round 2 (owner sent back: "add a tickbox or something to show gitignore or not"):** a switch "Also show what .gitignore leaves out" in the page's What is included menu. Off by default, kept per computer in `.orch/addons/files/state.json`; when on, the walk skips `.gitignore` (program folders such as node_modules, .git, build stay out either way). POST `/api/act` op `show_ignored`; status reports `show_ignored` and `ignored_shown` (the setting the last pass used) so the page checks every 1.5 s (at most 20 times) until the list matches. The background check no longer drops a wake that comes within 2 s of the last pass; it waits out the gap.

## Rules (AGENTS.md)

- Rules touched: R2 (ticket ORCH-1730), R4.5, R6 (kit switch and check-row only)
- New noun the user must learn? no
- Crosses the machine boundary (relay, publish, phone)? no
- Breaks a rule? no
- Decision log entry needed (docs/decisions.md)? no
- UI change: master library + gallery + mockup updated? Master: none (existing `.switch` + `.check-row`). Mockup: updated `workspace-addons/dashboard/mockup/files/files.html`
- Dashboard: a new action or page brings its click-through? n/a
- UI change: UX checklist: 61 items, 30 n.a., all others yes (L3: '.gitignore' kept, it is the owner's own word); screenshots at 1280, 1920 and 390 on the ticket (before, switch off, switch on); owner review card q2 on ORCH-1730

## Evidence

- Reproduced in a temp folder with the Pilatus layout: before, the walk listed only `.gitignore` and `docs/r.md`; after, `dlh_metabricks/src/a.py` too.
- New test `test_inner_repositories_show_even_when_the_outer_gitignore_names_them` (repo folder, worktree `.git` file, inner `.gitignore`, plain ignored folder, link, leave-out list).
- New tests `test_show_ignored_switch` (server) and `test_show_ignored_lists_what_gitignore_names_but_not_program_folders` (walk).
- `pytest tests/test_index.py tests/test_cli.py tests/test_server.py` (isolated home): 44 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. brand wording, style-lint and banned-word tests: 31 passed.
- Real page on a sample workspace (headless, keychain-safe): 14 files with the switch off, 17 on; flipping takes 1.5-3 s; no page errors.
- Outside review of the diff (subagent; Codex not installed, API credit keys missing today): fixed a stale switch when the click lands during a check, capped the fast checks, 500 on a failed save. Dismissed: extra passes when several tabs open (not a correctness issue).

body:
A `verity_contract` fallback could not be declared payable. The syntax took no `payable`, and the parser never set `isPayable`, so every macro fallback got the callvalue guard. That differs from Solidity's `fallback() external payable`: a proxy that forwards value to its implementation had to patch `isPayable` onto the compiled spec.

`CompilationModel` already supports a payable fallback, so this only adds the surface syntax `fallback payable := ...`. It composes with the reentrancy disposition and local obligations (#2787) in the same way as the plain `fallback`. `receive` stays always payable.

- `Verity/Macro/Syntax.lean` and `Verity/Macro/Translate/Parsing.lean`: the new `fallback payable` form, mapped to `specialEntrypointDecl "fallback" true ...`.
- `Contracts/Smoke/Declarations.lean`: `PayableFallbackSmoke`. `Compiler/CompilationModelFeatureTest.lean` checks that its spec has `isPayable` set, and that the plain fallback's does not.
- `test/PayableFallbackSmoke.t.sol`: runs the compiled bytecode.
  - A payable fallback accepts value on an unknown selector and on empty calldata, and reads it as `msgValue`.
  - A plain fallback reverts on value and runs on zero value.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: documents the form.

Evidence on `d8ef9d94c` plus these two commits:
- All of these exit 0:
  - a full `lake build` of every module, plus `Assurance` and `PrintAxioms`;
  - `compiler-main-test` (flags, compile, gates, mechanics);
  - the `PrintAxioms` check;
  - `check_proof_length.py`;
  - the Lean warning baseline (3 observed);
  - `make check`.
- `forge test --ffi --match-path test/PayableFallbackSmoke.t.sol`: 6 tests pass, 3 of them fuzz tests.

The rebase onto `25b756f18` only adds that scripts-only commit.

author: dexto-worker-box[bot]
body:
Linear: [DEXTO-3487](https://linear.app/truffleai/issue/DEXTO-3487)

## Why

The account MCP has `dexto_functions_list`, `dexto_function_get` and `dexto_function_invoke` (Cloud `apps/cloud/src/mcp/function-operations.ts`). The CLI could reach them only through generic `dexto workspace call`, which the parity inventory counts as debt, not coverage. `dexto cloud functions` is a different thing: the Cloud project `/v1` API.

## What changes

- New `dexto workspace functions` commands (`packages/cli/src/cli/cloud/commands/workspace-functions.ts`), registered in `host.ts`:
  - `list [--limit N]` → `dexto_functions_list`. Prints `{data: [...]}` with each Function's interfaces, operations and invoke availability. Needs `functions:read`.
  - `get <function_id> [--deployments N]` → `dexto_function_get` (`projectId`, `deploymentLimit`). Prints the tool's result unchanged. Needs `functions:read`.
  - `invoke <function_id> <operation> [--data JSON | --file PATH] [--deployment ID] [--timeout MS] [--yes]` → `dexto_function_invoke` (`projectId`, `operation`, `arguments`, `deploymentId`, `timeoutMs`). Needs `functions:invoke`. The tool is level `act`, so it asks first, as `workspace call` does: without `--yes` and no one to ask, it exits 4 before calling. A `response` result prints as is (`{kind, status, body, ...}`). An `error` result (the proxy didn't reach the Function) fails the command: `not_found` exits 5, `forbidden` 3, `invalid_request` 2, the rest 1.
- Inputs keep the MCP contract. Omitted options are left out, so Cloud's defaults apply. The CLI checks only the bounds Cloud itself sets (`limit` and `deploymentLimit` 1–50, `timeoutMs` 100–30000, arguments must be a JSON object). Everything else, such as an id that isn't a UUID, is refused by the operation and comes back as `invalid_input` (exit 2). Scope and not-found refusals map through the existing `queryWorkspaceTool` handling.
- `functions:invoke` joins `CLI_LOGIN_SCOPES`, so `requireLoginScopes` can name it and print `dexto login --scope functions:invoke`. Cloud already grants it to `dexto-cli`: it is a default scope in Cloud's MCP OAuth metadata. Cloud's drift test ("grants every scope the Dexto CLI asks for") picks it up on the next package bump.
- Parity: the three tools move from `passthroughOnly` to `commands` in both CLI copies of `cli-mcp-parity.json`, and leave the pinned `approvedPassthroughOnly` list. A paired dexto-cloudflare PR makes the same inventory change there.
- Agent audit baseline, the CLI overview doc and a changeset (`dexto` minor, `@dexto/agent-management` patch).

No new Cloud route or contract, and no change to permissions or proxy authorization.

## Tests

- New `workspace-functions.test.ts`, written first and red before the commands existed. It covers argument mapping and JSON output for all three commands, a Function that can't be read (not found, exit 5), an inaccessible Function and a provider-unavailable result on invoke, the confirmation gate, local and server refusals of unsupported input, and missing scopes both before the call and from a server refusal.
- `vitest run packages/cli/src/cli/cloud packages/agent-management/src/auth` (maxWorkers 2): 442 passed, including `cli-mcp-parity.test.ts`.
- Whole `packages/cli` unit run: 1265 passed. The one failure, `secret-path-policy.test.ts`, asserts that the checkout isn't shallow; the box clone is shallow. It is unrelated to this change.
- `tsc` typecheck and eslint for `dexto` and `@dexto/agent-management`: clean. `node scripts/check-cli-audit.mjs` matches the updated baseline.

body:
PR 2/19 for the review of #363. This PR does not touch the files of PR 1/19: #423.

## 1. Estimate columns filled by position

**Review comments:** [r4544927101](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4544927101), [r4553271356](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4553271356)

**Implementation:** `.model_compare_estimates_table()` (`R/model_compare.R`) subsets each model's `estimates` by name to the measures that all models share. The row order follows the first model. This applies only with `bare_names = TRUE`, which is the `pred_measure` path. Classic loo/waic/kfold objects keep the match by position, so their output does not change.

**Tests:** The test from the review checks that mse and mae are not in the output. The old code gave m1 a mae column with m1's mse value. A new test uses a different measure order and a different number of measures. It checks the m1 row, which the old code filled wrong. The second case gives the omitted-measures warning and no longer crashes.

## 2. Default model names assigned after sorting

**Review comment:** [r4544947628](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4544947628)

**Implementation:** `compare_pred_measure()` sets `names(loos) <- find_model_names(loos)` before the sort, as the classic path does.

**Test:** unnamed inputs where the second model is best give `c("model2", "model1")`, as `loo_compare()` does.

## 3. `identical()` on `se_diff_fun` closures

**Review comment:** [r4544950797](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4544950797)

**Decision:** `ignore.environment = TRUE`. It stays an error, not a warning, because a real difference (for example in `loss`) still means the models disagree. Limit: two closures with the same code but different captured values look equal.

**Test:** the same custom measure made in a helper function, and after `saveRDS()`/`readRDS()`, compares without an error. A different `loss` still errors.

## 4. `grep("elpd")` matches custom measures

**Review comment:** [r4545391902](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4545391902)

**Implementation:** `.is_elpd_measure()` matches `elpd`, `elpd_loo`, `elpd_kfold` and `elpd_test` exactly.

**Test:** a custom measure named `elpd_custom` gets its `_diff` and `_se_diff` columns. With the old function, both columns were missing.

## 5. Tolerance scaled twice

**Review comment:** [r4545429584](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4545429584)

**Implementation:** `.check_declared_aggregation()` uses a relative tolerance, `sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)`, scaled by the larger of the two values. `all.equal()` used an absolute difference for values below 1.5e-8.

**Test:** a measure declared `"mean"` whose estimate is 1.5 times the mean, with values around 3e11, now gives the warning. The old tolerance was about 4300, so it missed this. Values scaled by 1e-8 with a correct declaration give no warning. The old tolerance warned there. A wrong declaration with values scaled by 1e-8 now gives the warning.

## 6. Fallback returns `NULL` again

**Review comment:** [r4545434713](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4545434713)

**Implementation:** the fallback in `.measure_se_diff_fun()` is removed. `.measure_info()` already copies `se_diff_fun` from `.measure_spec`.

## 7. `compare_reference` not set for subsampling

**Review comments:** [r4544874307](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4544874307), [r4545558077](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4545558077), [r4544910468](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/363#discussion_r4544910468)

**Implementation:** `model_compare.psis_loo_ss_list()` sets `compare_reference` as the classic path does. The fallback in `.measure_ref_model()` and its doc sentence are removed.

**Test:** in `test_loo_subsampling.R`, a subsampling comparison has `compare_reference`.

## Test runs

`test_compare.R`, `test_print.R` and `test_loo_subsampling.R` pass. The 3 warnings in `test_compare.R` that are not caught were there before and will be addressed by a later PR.


This PR was assisted by use of LLM.

Closes #544

## What

Four text fields showed their label as a separate `Text` above an `OutlinedTextField` with no name of its own, so TalkBack read each as an unnamed "Edit box". Each field now carries its label as its accessible name, `Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = label }`, taken from the label's own string resource. That's the pattern the sign-in fields (`AuthScreen`) and the quest form (`QuestTextFields`) already use.

| Field | Screen | Name |
|---|---|---|
| Party code | `JoinPartyScreen` | `join_party_code_label` |
| Proof answer | `CompletionScreen` | `completion_answer` |
| Rejection note | `RejectProofSheet` | `reject_proof_note_label` |
| Display name | `ProfileSetupScreen` | `profile_setup_name` |

The issue lists the first three. A scan of every `OutlinedTextField` found the fourth, the profile's display name (setup and editing), with the same problem; it gets the same one-line fix. Every other text field already has a name.

## Review focus

- The label is read once into a `val` and used for both the visible `Text` and the field's name, so they can't drift apart.

## How to test

- One Compose test per field (`JoinPartyScreenTest`, `CompletionScreenTest`, `RejectProofSheetTest`, `ProfileSetupScreenTest`) finds the editable node by its accessible name, as TalkBack identifies it, and checks it's the field. With the fixes removed, all four fail.
- On a device (Samsung A55), the accessibility tree read with `uiautomator dump`, the data TalkBack reads, shows the party code and display name fields carrying their label as their name, inside the focusable edit box, and the display name keeping its typed value. The proof answer and rejection note weren't reached on the device; they're built the same way and covered by their tests.
- `./gradlew ktfmtCheck check compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` passes locally.

- [x] Acceptance criteria of the linked issue are met, except listening to TalkBack itself (see How to test)

author: fjarnskaggl
body:
Part of #7

## What
`src/textures/index.js` adds six original, procedural textures for print-then-cut: **wood planks, tiles, brick, striped wallpaper, sprig wallpaper and book spines**. It's a pure module with no DOM and no dependencies.

- **Sizing:** pattern sizes are real-world centimetres divided by the kit scale. A 12 cm plank prints at 10 mm on a 1:12 kit and 20 mm on a 1:6 kit.
- **Seeded:** the same seed gives the same file, so re-exports don't change.
- **`textureShapes(id, {width, height, scale, seed, params})`:** structured shapes in mm. The first shape is always a full background.
- **`textureSVG(id, …)`:** a standalone SVG with `width`/`height` in mm, clipped to its box. Clip and symbol ids are unique per texture, so several can share one print page.
- **Overrides:** `params` changes things like `colors`, `plankWidth`, `tileSize` + `checker`, `brickLength`/`brickHeight`/`mortar`, `stripeWidth` and `repeat`.
- **File size:** a 30 × 30 cm area stays under 400 KB for every texture. Sprig motifs are drawn once and placed with `<use>`.

Nothing uses this yet. The texture picker and applying textures in the 3D viewer are the next #7 item. T3's print sheets will use it through the interface I proposed on #4, and I'll follow whatever format T3 decides.

### Also in this PR: fix for intermittent e2e failures on main
`test/e2e/shells.e2e.cjs` (T2) and `test/e2e/t6.e2e.cjs` both started their test server on port **5198**. `node --test` runs e2e files in parallel, so whichever file finished first killed the server the other was still using (`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`). body:
## Linked issue

No issue: defect found during regtest phone validation of develop, requesting `no-issue-needed`.

Targets `develop` (01c5e373d, verified 2026-11-23).

## Problem

Paying a Lightning invoice that has less than about 20 minutes left before expiry shows "Failed to create swap". Boltz refuses the submarine swap with HTTP 400 `{"error":"invoice expiry too short"}` (it requires twice the funding chain's block time before expiry for a non-zero-conf lockup), but the app maps every Boltz rejection to the generic message, so the user cannot tell that a fresh invoice would work.

## Changes

- `packages/swaps`: `BoltzApiException.isInvoiceExpiryTooShort` recognises that rejection from the HTTP 400 JSON body, and `classifySwapCreationFailure` returns the new `SwapsInvoiceExpiryTooShortFailure` (a `SwapsBoltzRejectedFailure`).
- Send maps it to `SendInvoiceExpiryTooShortFailure`, shown as "This invoice expires too soon. Ask the recipient for a new invoice." The raw Boltz message never reaches the UI.

## Non-goals

No early client-side expiry check before contacting Boltz, and no change to other swap errors.

## Risk and security

UI message only; swap creation, funds and keys are untouched.

## Tests

Red → Green: the swaps test classifies the exact Boltz 400 response as `SwapsInvoiceExpiryTooShortFailure` and other 400 bodies as generic rejections; the Send localization test resolves the new message. Reproduced on a phone against the regtest stack: an invoice with 941 s left failed with the generic message before the fix, and an invoice with an hour left created the swap.

## Review guide

**Source — read**: `ddc22e199` fix(send): explain when lightning invoices expire too soon — 32 files, +91/−26, of which 27 are the localization catalogues (one key each).

**Tests — skim**: `d97c76969` test(send): cover the boltz invoice expiry rejection — 2 files, +55.

author: xiaoarnav
body:
## Summary of Step 7: Scientifically Correct AQI

### Objectives
This pull request implements **Step 7 of Avir's 24-step roadmap: Scientifically Correct AQI**. It upgrades all AQI calculations throughout the platform to align strictly with official regulatory standards, codifying the US EPA 2024 Revised PM2.5 Breakpoints (40 CFR Part 58, Appendix G, 89 FR 16202) and the Indian CPCB National Air Quality Index (NAQI) statutory 8-pollutant standard (CPCB 2014 Report).

### Key Scientific Standards & Mathematical Enhancements
1. **US EPA 2024 Revised PM2.5 Breakpoints**:
   - Replaced obsolete pre-2024 breakpoints (0–12.0 Good) with the codified May 6, 2024 standard (0–9.0 Good).
   - .0\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ now computes to AQI 56 (Moderate) rather than obsolete AQI 50 (Good).
   - Unhealthy range tightened to .5 - 125.4\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$; Very Unhealthy tightened to .5 - 225.4\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$.
   - Enforced concentration truncation to zsh.1\,\mu\text{g/m}^3$ per 40 CFR Part 58 Appendix G before linear interpolation.
2. **Indian CPCB NAQI (8 Criteria Pollutants)**:
   - Full support for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb.
   - Enforced CO unit validation ($\text{mg/m}^3$) with automatic division by 1000 when input is provided in $\mu\text{g/m}^3$.
   - Enforced statutory data sufficiency rules: requires $\ge 3$ pollutants with mandatory PM2.5 or PM10 presence.
   - Enforced pollutant-specific averaging intervals (24h for PM/NO2/SO2/NH3/Pb; 8h for CO/O3).
   - Prevented missing data from defaulting to 'Good' category (returns 'Unavailable' when input is null).
3. **Scientific Provenance Architecture**:
   - Introduced `AqiMethod` and `AqiEvidence` metadata distinguishing provider-reported indices, locally derived PM2.5 sub-indices, statutory-eligible calculations, and officially published government bulletins.
   - Local calculations never falsely claim official publication or statutory orders.
4. **UI Presentation Integrity**:
   - Updated `AtmosphereHero` and `MultiSourceInspectorModal` with truthful scientific labels ("US AQI (Modeled)", "PM2.5 AQI Sub-Index", "CPCB NAQI").
   - Added transparent evidence badges displaying standard versions and formulas.

### Verification & Test Coverage
- **Golden-Reference Test Suite** (`tests/integration/step7-scientific-aqi.test.ts`): **80/80 passed**.
- **Full Project Regression Suite**: **33/33 test files passed, 800/800 tests passed**.
- **TypeScript Checking** (`npx tsc --noEmit`): **0 errors**.
- **Next.js Production Build** (`npm run build`): **Clean build, static generation 7/7 pages green**.

### Technical Debt Register (Preserved)
- Step 4: CPCB official API key requirement for live CCR portal ingestion.
- Step 5: Testing on physical hardware microcontrollers.
- Step 6: World telemetry batch model query optimization for edge regions.

Documentation: `docs/improvements/STEP_07_SCIENTIFIC_AQI.md`

they type (e.g. `Bob@Example.COM` matches stored `bob@example.com`).

No custom `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` is configured, so Django's default
`ModelBackend` looks up `USERNAME_FIELD` (email) case-sensitively. Emails were
already stored lower-cased on creation, but typing a different case at login was

author: aburra16
body:
Clears the high and critical advisories in the production dependencies and moves the image cache to nginx's November 18 stable release.

- `body-parser` 1.20.5 → 1.20.9 (CVE-2026-111181, high). Trailing bytes after a compressed request body could tie up the parser. The API reads JSON bodies with `express.json()`, which inflates gzip and deflate by default, so this one reached the public API.
- `proxy-addr` 2.0.7 → 2.0.8 (CVE-2026-90711, critical). The spoofing needs a `trust proxy` subnet, and the API sets none, so it never applied here.
- `nanoid` 3.3.12 → 3.3.20 and 5.1.11 → 5.1.16 (CVE-2026-67214, high). The loop needs a negative size, which nothing here passes.
- The image cache runs `nginx:1.30.7-alpine` instead of `1.30.6-alpine`. nginx 1.30.7 fixes ten CVEs, led by memory corruption in HTTP/2 (CVE-2026-123007). The cache listens on plain HTTP inside the compose network behind Caddy, and its config uses none of the affected modules, so none of the ten reached it. The pin moves to the patched release.

All three packages change through a lockfile refresh, within the ranges their dependents already allow, and no `package.json` changes. The refresh adds `qs` 6.16.2, which body-parser 1.20.9 requires.

Checked on Node 24: `pnpm -r typecheck` passes, `pnpm -r test` passes (the API alone: 1046 passed, 13 skipped), and `pnpm audit --prod` reports 8 moderate, as before, and no high or critical.

author: gbotha13
body:
Stacked on #451 (equipment hire M). Merge that first; this PR's base then becomes `main`.

## Why
The hire register only knew tagged gear (one row and one QR per thing). FFSA also owns things that are counted, not tagged: 60 glasses, 10 black tablecloths, tealights. This adds those, lets the inventory manager add items in the Hub, and lets anyone signed in ask to borrow items for a school or ministry.

## What's in it
- **Three kinds of item** (`equipment_products.tracking`):
  - **tagged**: as before.
  - **counted**: a quantity that is lent and returned.
  - **consumable**: a quantity that is handed out. Never lent and never on the store; a constraint enforces this.
- **Counts have a history.** `stock_quantity` changes only through `equipment_stock_moves`: opening, bought, found, handed out, lost, damaged, and recount (manager only). A trigger applies each move and refuses anything that would go below zero.
- **Add item** at `/bookings/equipment/gear/new`, inventory manager only.
  - Tagged items get units numbered on from the prefix (`AUD-0015`, …).
  - Counted and consumable items get an opening count.
- **Item page:**
  - Count, free today, "Record a change" and the history.
  - Details (name, category, where it's kept, borrowable) can be edited.
  - Jack's listing editor sits underneath; consumables don't have one.
- **Register:**
  - Lists counted and consumable items with their counts.
  - Flags "Reorder" and "No description yet".
  - Has Add item.
- **Borrow equipment** at `/bookings/borrow`, plus a card on the Bookings hub:
  - Any signed-in user picks dates, items and quantities (free counts for those dates), then a school or ministry and what it's for.
  - Internal rate, no deposit. It lands in Orders as `requested` and the manager approves it with the existing flow and emails.
  - Personal hires still go through `/hire` at the public price.
- **Count out / count back** on an order's page for counted lines:
  - Back + damaged + missing must equal what went out, and losses need a note.
  - Damaged and missing come off the stock as moves tied to the order.
  - An order made only of counted lines moves to `out` and then `returned` by itself. Orders with tagged lines still wait for stage N's scan flow.
- **383** imports the first inventory list (Google Doc): 41 items, 29 counted (204 things) and 12 consumable (253).
  - Judgement calls are listed in the migration header and kept in each opening move's note. For example, the two "beige tablecloth" lines became one item with 2, and "100-150 ish" forks became 100.
  - The Doc had no descriptions, prices, photos or locations, so those are blank.
- **Permission names** in Users & Roles now read as Inventory. The keys are unchanged:
  - `equipment.manage` = inventory manager
  - `equipment.operate` = count and record stock
  - `equipment.view` = read only

## Access (382)
- Signed-in users can read products marked `is_requestable` and their photos, and that's all. They can't see stock history or other items.
- Requests are placed by the API with the service role, the same way checkout does.
- Stock moves: the warehouse can record bought, found, handed out, lost and damaged. Opening counts and recounts are the manager's. There is no update or delete; history is append-only.
- `equipment_count_line` checks `can_operate_equipment()` and treats NULL as no.

## Checked
- `tsc` and ESLint are clean on every file this touches.
- 15 new rule tests (`inventory.test.ts`) and 3 register-filter tests.
- All equipment tests pass on every run. The full vitest run (3,132 tests) passed apart from a few timing-based "round trip" tests in access and consent code. Those fail at random when the machine is under load (load average was about 120) and pass when run alone; this PR doesn't touch them.
- **Migrations, on PGlite** (Postgres in WebAssembly):
  - Ran 255, 257, 285, 380, 381, 382 and 383 over stand-ins for the Supabase pieces, then 381–383 a second time. They are safe to repeat.
  - 31 checks passed:
    - seed counts and no doubled opening moves
    - tagged availability unchanged
    - consumables never lendable
    - stock can't go negative
    - a request holds stock on its dates
    - `equipment_place_order` refuses over-booking
    - count out / back rules and status moves
    - losses come off the stock
    - RLS as a signed-in user with no permissions, and as the warehouse

## Not yet checked
- [ ] Apply **380, 381, 382, 383** in order in the Supabase SQL editor, before deploying this code. The order pages read `school:programs(...)`, which needs 381.
- [ ] Click through on a phone: Add item, record a change, borrow request, approve it, count it out and back.
- [ ] The slugs in 383 assume no existing product already uses them (e.g. `glasses`). If one does, 383 stops with a unique-slug error.
- [ ] Fill in descriptions, locations and photos for the 41 imported items, and recount the beige tablecloths.

author: devtomtom
body:
JIRA: CPOUI5FOUNDATION-1386
JIRA: CPOUI5FOUNDATION-1396

 ## Summary

  A build task's output can depend on the version of an external tool it loads to
  transform content. That version is an input to the build, but the cache never tracked
  it: upgrading a tool without a new `@ui5/builder` release left every signature
  unchanged, so the build served a cache hit with stale output.

  This change makes the cache aware of the tools a task loads. A main-thread
  module-resolution hook observes which tool files each stage resolves while it runs, and
  their content is hashed into a new `tool-content` component of the stage signature. No
  per-task declaration and no version strings.

## 概要

`validate_plugin_quality.py` の metrics-vocab 検査（計測ストアの語彙の足し忘れ）は warning として exit 0 で出る。このため `machine-layer.sh` の品質検査の段と `.githooks/pre-commit` が出力を捨てており、Stop hook にも pre-commit にも表示されなかった。

## 変更

- `.claude-plugin/scripts/machine-layer.sh`: 品質検査が exit 0 で終わった回も、出力から `[metrics-vocab]` の行だけを拾って検出に載せる（exit 1 になる）。`[run-tests:leak]` と同じ扱い。exit 1 の回は出力を丸ごと載せているので、拾い直さない
- `.githooks/pre-commit`: 同じ行を表示する。commit は止めない（語彙は計測ストアで足すもので、この repo の commit を止めても直らない）
- 拾うのは `[metrics-vocab]` の行だけで、要対応の warning の節は丸ごとは拾わない（2026-11-23 決定）。ほかの要対応 warning（今は 0 件）まで出し続けると「⚠️ が出たときだけ行動する」契約を崩しうるため

- `code-review/references/orchestration-measurement.md` の `## 18` には「Stop hook と pre-commit は warning を表示しない」と書いてあったので、書き直した（code-review 2.169.3）

body:
Refs #180

## 계획

- 계획: `docs/exec-plans/active/20261121-q10-confirm/` · 계획 수정(F16). step1 시작 전에 step1의 문구 지시를 고친다
- 요약: PR #188(step0) 구현 판정의 지적 F16(P1) 대응이다. 계획 폴더의 파일 둘(`plan.md`, `step1.md`)만 바꾼다. 코드·설정·다른 문서는 바꾸지 않는다. 계획 검증(G1)을 받으려고 올린다.

### 무엇이 충돌했나

- 2026-11-23에 제작자의 Windows PC에서 절차가 통과했다(`win32-x64: 통과`). 결과 파일은 남기지 않았다.
  - 계획의 "검증 방법과 결과"에 그렇게 적혀 있다.
  - 이 실행은 확정 근거가 아니다(출처를 확인할 수 없다).
- 그런데 step1은 ADR-0007의 "알려진 한계"와 TD-14에 "제작자의 Windows PC에서는 아직 재지 않았다"고 쓰게 하고, `confirmed.test.ts`가 그 문구를 요구했다.
- #188은 계획이 main에 없는 첫 PR이었다. 게다가 제작자가 올린 워크플로 파일이 있어 계획만 남긴 상태로 되돌릴 수 없었다. 그래서 #188에서는 고치지 않았다. 대신 step1.md의 "읽어야 할 파일"과 status `blocked`로 step1이 시작되지 않게 막아 두었다. F16은 `fixed`로 닫혔다.

### 바뀐 것

1. **step1 작업 3**(`confirmed.test.ts`의 기준):
   - ADR-0007:
     - 문서에 "아직 재지 않았다"와 `TD-14`가 없다.
     - "알려진 한계"에 `CI`·`Windows PC`·`결과 파일`이 함께 든 줄이 있다(바뀌기 전 기준은 `TD-14`와 `Windows PC`가 든 줄).
   - 설계서 Q10 행과 `lab/q10-db/README.md`에 `TD-14`가 없다.
   - TD-14 행에 `lab/q10-db`와 `ADR-0007`이 없다(바뀌기 전 기준은 "확정 조건은 채워졌다"가 있는 것).
2. **step1 작업 4**(문서 문구):
   - ADR "알려진 한계"에 두 가지를 따로 적는다.
     - Windows의 확정 근거는 CI `windows-latest` 러너의 산출물이다(`verify-artifacts.ts`로 출처 확인).
     - 제작자의 PC에서도 절차가 통과했으나 결과 파일을 남기지 않아 확정 근거로 쓰지 않는다.
   - ADR "확정 조건" 절과 README에서 앞으로 할 일로 적힌 줄(TD-14를 가리키는 줄)을 지금 상태로 고친다.
   - TD-14 행에서 `lab/q10-db` 항목을 뺀다.
3. **plan.md**:
   - 수용 기준 4(남은 한계, TD-14)와 비범위(PC 재실측 → PC 결과 파일을 리포에 더하는 것)를 위와 맞췄다.
   - status를 `blocked`에서 `active`로 되돌렸다.
   - step1.md의 "먼저 읽는다(F16)" 항목을 지우고, 그 자리를 "검증 방법과 결과"의 2026-11-23 줄을 가리키는 것으로 바꿨다.
   - 진행 로그와 의사결정 로그를 보탰다.

### 원장의 지적 (계획 검증 1회차, head `499d46c`)

Claude 승인, Codex 수정 요청(P1 2). 둘 다 수용했다.

- F1 (P1, codex) Windows 확정 근거를 뒤바꿔도 문서 테스트가 통과한다 → 수용.
  - 원인: 한 줄에 `CI`·`Windows PC`·`결과 파일`이 있는지만 보면, PC의 결과를 확정 근거로 삼았다고 적어도 통과한다.
  - 고친 것: step1 작업 4에 "알려진 한계"에 넣을 두 문장을 글자 그대로 정했다.
    - `Windows 네이티브의 확정 근거는 CI의 Windows 러너에서 받은 산출물이다.`
    - `제작자의 Windows PC에서는 2026-11-23에 절차가 통과했으나 결과 파일을 남기지 않아 확정 근거로 쓰지 않는다.`
  - `confirmed.test.ts`가 두 문장을 각각 본다.
- F2 (P1, codex) ADR의 결과 절에 잠정 상태를 남겨도 수용 기준을 통과한다 → 수용.
  - 고친 것: 작업 4에 `## 결과` 절의 Q10 줄을 확정에 맞게 고치는 것을 넣었다.
    - 설계서 18절의 Q10이 확정 결정으로 바뀐다.
    - 19절에서 Q10이 빠진다.
    - Q13은 그때 19절의 상태대로 적는다.
  - 테스트가 보는 것:
    - ADR 문서 전체에 `잠정`이 없다.
    - "결과" 절의 `Q10` 줄마다 `확정`이 있다.

### 판단한 것(의사결정 로그 "결정(F16 계획 수정)")

TD-14의 `lab/q10-db` 항목은 남기지 않고 닫는다.

- 그 PC 재실측의 목적은 러너가 재지 못하는 PC의 차이(경로, 사용자 이름, 보안 프로그램)를 보는 것이었다. 11-23 실행으로 그 목적이 채워졌다.
- 다시 돌려 결과 파일을 남겨도 출처를 확인할 수단이 없어 확정 근거가 늘지 않는다.
- 다시 잴 일(패키지 버전·설치 정책을 바꿀 때)은 워크플로 `q10-trial`이 맡는다.
- 버린 대안: "출처를 남기는 PC 재실측"으로 TD-14에 남기기.

### 왜 이 브랜치인가

- 절차서 4.1절 "실행 중인 step의 계획 수정"을 따랐다. 완료된 step0의 번호로 `docs/20261121-q10-confirm-s0`을 만들었다(step0의 PR #188 브랜치 `chore/…-s0`과 접두어가 다르다).
- 로컬 `plan-gate --mode pr`의 출력(1회차 대응 커밋 `ab1c5c3`):
  - `참고: step1의 작업·Acceptance Criteria가 바뀌었다: 계획 수정(G1 재검증 대상)`
  - `참고: G1: 계획 핵심 섹션이 base와 다르다(해시 827ef23ec69d). 병합하려면 계획만 담은 커밋에서 검증자 승인을 받아야 한다(CI가 원장으로 확인한다)`
  - `plan-gate: 통과`
- 해시는 `49fa50ae8ba1`(main)에서 `827ef23ec69d`로 바뀐다. 첫 커밋(`499d46c`)의 해시는 `f1b2b49e44fd`였다.
- step0 파일과 step1의 금지사항은 바꾸지 않았다. step1의 AC는 명령 블록을 그대로 두고, 그 아래 설명 한 줄에만 "결과"를 더했다(테스트가 ADR의 "결과" 절도 본다는 것, F2).
- 계획의 risk가 high라 병합에는 제작자 head 승인이 필요하다(risk-gate).

## 검증

- AC 명령과 결과: 해당 없음(계획만 바꿨다). `fmt --check`, `doc-lint` 통과.
- `node scripts/harness.ts check`: 통과(이 Windows PC)

body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution.
     Make sure you read the contributing guide and fill this template. -->
This PR introduces a new attribute `uip` to `Sort` declarations.

It makes it possible to write the following:
```rocq
#[universes(polymorphic=no), uip] Sort foo.

Inductive seq {A : Type} (x : A) : A -> SProp := srefl : seq x x.

Definition transport {A : Type} {x y : A} {P : A -> Univ@{foo;_}} (e : seq x y) (u : P x) : P y := 
  match e with srefl _ => u end.
```
This can be used to have a sort of strict sets, on which UIP should hold definitionally.

This type of definitional UIP is upwards closed, i.e., if we have `foo -> Prop`, then we can write:
```rocq
Definition transport' {A : Type} {x y : A} {P : A -> Prop} (e : seq x y) (u : P x) : P y :=
    match e with srefl _ => u end.
```
This means that if `foo` has definitional UIP and `foo -> Prop`, one can deduce `x = y` from `seq x y`.

Currently, this does not appear when the typing flags are printed but maybe we'd want to print it?

author: wrongsahil
body:
## What

Code the AI writes into a rule is saved only after **the user** accepts it in their MCP host (MCP elicitation, the same mechanism as #23 for deletes). The model can't answer the prompt.

Fixes **RQ-3011** (reopened by Security on 6 Nov: `confirmActivation` came from the model) and **RQ-3021**. These also close the chains **RQ-3033** and **RQ-3039**, plus **RQ-3005**.

## When the user is asked (decided 23 Nov)

| Call by the model | Prompt? | Dialog shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create a Script / Request / Response rule that has code | Yes | name, type, URL match, the status it gets, the full code |
| Change the code of such a rule (on or off) | Yes | the new code and the saved code it replaces |
| Turn a rule on or off, rename, change the URL match | No | |
| Rules without code (Redirect, Headers…) | No | |

"Code" = Script values (inline or URL) plus tag attributes (`onload` is code), and Request/Response bodies, code or static.

## How

- `src/codeApproval.ts` (new): finds the code in a rule's pairs, works out which code is new compared with the saved rule, and asks with `askHumanToApprove` (from #23).
  - **Where the code is shown.** Claude Code 2.1.330 shows at most 3 lines of an elicitation message, each cut at the terminal width, and they can't be expanded; the first hands-on test showed "… (+6 more lines)" where the code should have been. So the prompt is kept to at most 3 short lines (tested: each line is 120 characters or fewer, and the model-supplied name is JSON-quoted and cut to 40 characters).
    - Code that is one line of plain printable ASCII, 60 characters or fewer, with no tag attributes, is shown in the prompt (`Code: …`; on an update, `New: …` and `Was: …`).
    - Anything else is written to `~/.requestly-mcp/review/<nonce>.txt` (directory `0700`, file `0600`, created with `O_EXCL`, symlinked directories refused). The file **opens in the default text editor** when the prompt appears (`open` / `xdg-open` / `explorer.exe`, detached, stdio ignored), and the prompt names its absolute path; a `file://` link wasn't clickable in Claude Code. `REQUESTLY_MCP_OPEN_REVIEW_FILE=0` turns the auto-open off.
    - **The user may edit the code in the file** (decided 23 Nov). Whatever it holds when they click Accept is saved: each item is read back between nonce-marked lines and put back where it came from (script value, tag attributes, or body). The model is told the code was edited. A file that is gone, or whose marker lines were removed, saves nothing. On an update, the saved code it replaces is shown below the code for reference; edits there are ignored. The file is always deleted.
    - Code containing invisible or text-direction characters (Trojan Source) is never shown inline, and the prompt warns about it.
    - Residual risk, accepted: since edits are allowed, nothing detects a background process rewriting the file after the user has read it. In Claude Code the model could only start one through a Bash call, which needs the user's approval in default mode.
- `create_rule`: asks before saving a rule with code. After Accept it saves the status the model asked for (default Inactive). Decline, cancel, timeout, error, a cancelled call, or a host without elicitation → nothing is saved.
- `update_rule`: GETs the saved rule first and keeps any field the model left out. api2's PUT replaces the whole rule, so before this a missing `name` renamed the rule to "API: Script Rule <time>" and a missing `status` became `Active`. It asks only when new code appears, and refuses a rule-type change. `confirmActivation` is removed; `pairs` and `status` are optional.
- README: new "Code in rules" section.

## Evidence

- **Repro on main** (live api2, benign payloads): the model turned a Script rule on with its own `confirmActivation: true`, then swapped the code of the live rule, with no prompt. A wrong `ruleType` is refused by api2 (405), so it isn't a bypass.
- **Failing first:** the new `codeApproval.test.ts` fails 49 of 51 on main. The 2 that pass are guards for rules without code.
- **This branch:** 208/208 tests pass on Node 22.23.4 and 24.22.1 after a clean `npm ci`; `build/index.js` sha256 `82df570f…c2626` is the same on both. `tsc --noEmit` shows the same 4 errors main already has, none in changed files.
- **Live e2e against api2** (build `82df570f`): 12/12 scenarios pass. They cover create, update, turning a rule on and off, rename, a wrong rule type, a Response body, long code reviewed in the file, long code edited in the file (the edit is saved), keeping the group, and a host without elicitation.
- **Hands-on test in Claude Code:** the first round found the 3-line limit and that the link wasn't clickable; both are fixed. Rerun pending.

## Not in this PR

- Body size caps → RQ-3041.
- Turning a group on restarts the live rules in it. Decided: leave as is (it only runs code a person has seen or written).

author: igor-muse
body:
Developer: read span endpoints as measure windows close (wave 3, PR9a).

## Purpose

Wave 3 moves evaluation from the whole document to measure windows, so that a window's nodes can be released when it closes (PR15). The spans context provider (slurs, ties, beams, wedges, lyric extends, part-groups and the rest) read every node of the document in `Finish`. After this change, under the internal `windowed` strategy, it reads a window's nodes when the window closes and never again: `Finish` associates the endpoints from what the windows kept. `buffered`, the default strategy, is unchanged.

This is the first half of PR9. The endpoints themselves still live until `Finish`, as they do in `buffered`; PR9b removes them when the spans projection is not selected.

## Changes

- **`spanCollector`** (`validation/context_spans_runtime.go`). The provider's per-node pass is now `spanCollector.visit`. The buffered provider calls it for the whole document in `Finish`, in the same order of operations and charges as before.
- **Window read** (`validation/spans_window.go`, `evaluateWindowSpans`, called from `closeWindow` after the performance provider). It reads the window's nodes against the speculative timeline service and publishes into a stash. Each endpoint keeps what the passes of `Finish` used to read from its node (`spanCaptured`): the origins when the spans projection is selected, a beam's fan and whether it states one, whether a tie's note states the attack or release, the two tremolo recommendations.
- **Local gaps.** A window's endpoints meet the gaps of their own notes, frames and metronomes, and of their notes' lyrics, when the window closes; lyric identities and scopes live for one window.
- **Extend without a type.** Its role depends on the root's `version`, and the root is bound only in `Finish`. The endpoint is marked, its local gaps are kept (`spanDeferredRole`), and the role, what follows from it and those gaps are applied in `Finish` in the buffered order.
- **Domains.** A window answers "which part does this node belong to" from the timeline facts of its own nodes; `Finish` answers for the nodes outside windows from all facts, without reading a window's nodes.
- **`Finish`** (`adoptWindowSpans`). If every closed window was read, no read failed, node identities follow document order and the timeline was not rebuilt, the provider reads the nodes outside windows, charges the provisional context facts once, moves the stashed results into the report in document order, and runs the unchanged document-wide passes over the endpoints. Gaps of shared domains are folded in document order. Otherwise everything provisional is dropped, its charge released, and the buffered path runs.
- **No window node is read in `Finish`** on the accepted path: the provider's reader is sealed, and a read of a window's node is a contract error.
- **Accounting.** `windowSpans.retained` counts what the windows' work alone holds; shared attribute tables, interned strings and the speculation's journal are excluded. Charges for values read only to publish a fact are released right after publishing. At adoption the carrying lists and the captures are released; the endpoints stay charged with the provider, as the buffered provider's do.
- **Ends of the work other than adoption**, each reported to a test observer: `speculation` (no speculation, stopped, or rejected in `Finish`), `excursions` (a unit excursion is pending), `rebuilt`, `unbound` (a window closed unread), `domain` (a read could not answer from its window), `unordered` (node identities out of document order), `unsettled` (the phases never ran). An unread window, a stopped speculation and a pending excursion end the work at once and release its charge; the others are found in `Finish`.

## Compatibility

No public API change. `buffered` reports, rule steps and charges are unchanged: on MozartTrio ×16 the buffered rule-step totals are equal to `origin/main` to the step (331,058,094 without projection, 383,747,229 with all families). Under `windowed`, rule steps grow by 0.7–0.9 % on that score.

## Claims and evidence

| Claim | Test | Fails without it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reports of both strategies are byte-identical on the 154 corpus files, every entry point, with and without projection | `TestWindowedStrategyMatchesBuffered` with `MUSICXML_WINDOWED_FULL=1` | Yes: any captured field, order or deferred step |
| The same on 30 documents where a later fact decides an earlier window or the work cannot be adopted | `TestWindowSpansRiskCases` | Yes, per case |
| The work is adopted on 147 of 154 corpus documents (4.5 % not adopted, bound 5 %) | `TestWindowSpansDegradationOnCorpus` (`MUSICXML_WINDOWED_FULL=1`) | Yes |
| What windows keep is charged before `Finish` | `TestWindowSpansChargeCoversTheHeap`, `TestWindowSpansCaptureIsCharged` | Yes |
| Nodes without endpoints leave nothing behind: 3,200 lyrics and 1,600 time modifications hold no live memory and 4 KB of charge between windows | `TestWindowSpansKeepNothingForNodesWithoutEndpoints` | Yes: without the release after publishing the charge is megabytes |
| A drop releases all the windows' work charged and nothing else | `TestWindowSpansDropReleasesItsCharge` (three selections, with and without performance windows), `TestWindowSpansDropOnce` | Yes |
| Ownership of charges: tables, interned strings, journal and stashed results are not the windows' | `TestWindowSpansChargeOwnership` | Yes, per term |
| Adoption releases the lists and captures and nothing else | `TestWindowSpansAdoptionReleasesItsLists` | Yes |
| The report's lease covers the projection under `windowed` | `TestWindowSpansLeaseCoversTheProjection` | Yes |
| Context facts are charged once; both strategies complete or stop alike under every quota | `TestWindowSpansUnderContextFactQuotas` | Yes |
| The work's own defects end the run with a contract error | `TestWindowSpansReportsItsOwnDefects` | Yes |
| Confirmation, gap order, deferred extend order, window and outside domains, range order, ordered state outside windows | `validation/spans_window_test.go` | Yes |

Mutations: 80 on the final code (one more after the last review fix is covered by a unit test), 76 killed. The four survivors change no result:

- publishing the facts of nodes outside windows directly instead of through the stash (differs only if a publishing node outside windows followed a window, which the schema does not allow);
- climbing past an unchanged ancestor when a window indexes its domains (more steps, same index);
- not releasing the charge of values read for an endpoint's local facts (a few hundred bytes of over-charge per endpoint until `Finish`; the same release is tested at its two other call sites);
- not ending the work at a window whose rules were not evaluated (it then ends in `Finish` with the same reason).

Two independent review passes by a separate agent found no violation of the invariants. Pass 1 (on an earlier head): reports identical on 50 hand-built cases, 1,020 random documents and 1,822 prefix cuts; its findings were cost (windows read after the work could no longer be adopted), dead code and test gaps, all addressed. Pass 2: no blocker or major finding; its one minor finding (the order check covered adjacent windows only) is fixed.

## Measurements

MozartTrio, live heap at the end of `Finish`, `origin/main` → this branch:

| Input | Line | `buffered` | `windowed` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ×16 | 2 source | 68.5 → 67.9 MB | 27.9 → 27.9 MB |
| ×16 | 2 semantics | 118.6 → 118.8 MB | 56.8 → 56.8 MB |
| ×16 | 3 model | 71.7 → 71.7 MB | 53.3 → 53.3 MB |
| ×110 | 2 source | 465.6 → 465.7 MB | 193.8 → 193.7 MB |
| ×110 | 2 semantics | 820.4 → 820.4 MB | 396.1 → 396.6 MB |
| ×110 | 3 model | 497.9 → 497.9 MB | 367.1 → 367.1 MB |

Memory is unchanged, as intended: this change removes a reader of window nodes; the nodes are released in PR15. The `windowed` charge at ×110 falls from 1,470.3 to 1,457.8 MB (semantics) and from

**Shared code changed:**
- `packages/i18n` (en and pt-BR):
  - Removes `composer.attach.cancel`, which nothing uses now that the attach chooser is a menu.
  - Adds `settings.signOut.body.mobile`, because the old sign-out text said "This browser loses access" on a phone.
  - In pt-BR, `settings.signOut` and `settings.signOut.title` now read "Sair deste dispositivo" and "Sair deste dispositivo?".
- `packages/design-tokens`: fixes the `control-thumb` doc comment only. No values change.
- The empty-room keys `empty.quiet.room` and `empty.quiet.roomAnyHost` come from #150 and are reused here as they are.

This is the Android half of the Pips QA pass, on the Pixel 8 and the unfolded Pixel 9 Pro Fold emulators. #150 was the web and desktop half. I walked the flows in light and dark and in en and pt-BR, plus one pass under reduced motion. The server was the every-surface scripted one.

Before/after screenshots are in a [secret gist](https://gist.github.com/JPSAUD501/d87d920313b6bdbd8838eebb90f0b517).

## Findings and fixes

| # | Screen | Platform | What was wrong | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every confirmation: start fresh, delete, discard edits, sign out, revoke a device, stop a room, leave or change server | Android | Shown in the system `Alert`: Material buttons, system font, nothing from Pips | ugly | `confirm.tsx`: the app's own short dialog, a `surface` panel over the scrim that pops in on `pop` from slightly smaller and leaves on `out`. TalkBack starts at the dialog's title, so the question is heard before the answers, and Keep is the first answer. Back or a tap outside also means keep.
