author: francoisblavoet
body:
## Summary

Work around nondeterministic equal-time Handler callback dispatch in Layoutlib, using Paparazzi's existing compatibility-patch infrastructure.

`HandlerMessageQueue` keeps a time-sorted list per Handler in a `WeakHashMap`. When two lists have the same earliest timestamp, extraction keeps whichever Handler map traversal encounters first. That preserves FIFO within one Handler but not across Handlers, so object/hash allocation and test initialization order can change the rendered frame.

For example, posting `A1`, `B1`, `A2` for the same timestamp can dispatch `B1, A1, A2` instead of `A1, B1, A2`. The integration regression uses colliding Handler hashes to exercise this without relying on incidental allocation order.

## Changes

- Add a weak-owner callback queue ordered by `(due timestamp, session-wide posting sequence)` and a thin `HandlerMessageQueue` adapter.
- Install it at `SessionInteractiveData` construction, before any callbacks are posted. Refuse to replace a nonempty queue rather than silently lose or reorder pending initialization work.
- Extend the existing name/descriptor-checked transformer to match constructors. Preserve the preloaded-class retransformation support already on master.
- Keep Handler ownership weak, synchronize queue operations, and retain independent queues across sessions/configuration changes.
- Extend the fresh-JVM preloaded-target regression to cover the session constructor and assert that its queue is patched.

This uses Layoutlib's existing timestamp-only queue interface; it does not attempt to add Android sync-barrier/front-of-queue semantics that interface does not expose. No frame clock, dispatcher, deadlines, frame count, test order, comparison tolerance, dependency versions, coordinates, release configuration, or goldens are changed.

## Verification

Against current master (`afe2cad39`, Layoutlib 16.2.4):

```shell
./gradlew :paparazzi:check :paparazzi:apiCheck -PRELEASE_SIGNING_ENABLED=false --max-workers=4
./gradlew :paparazzi:spotlessCheck -PRELEASE_SIGNING_ENABLED=false --max-workers=4
```

- **145 tests: 140 passed, 5 skipped, no failures/errors**, including queue/session regressions and the isolated preloaded-target test.
- API compatibility, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Queue coverage includes colliding hashes, FIFO ties across owners, earlier/future timestamps, posts during drain, duplicate Runnable posts, negative/zero times, clearing/reuse, weak-owner collection, and concurrent posting.
- The full Gradle-plugin integration matrix has not been run locally on this upstream branch; CI is pending.

The same runtime fix was also exercised downstream: 12 navigation movies were pixel-identical across three class orders and a repeat (3,768 frames), where the unpatched renderer produced order-dependent frames. Two animation baselines changed consistently; no downstream code or baseline files are included here.

## Draft scope

Proposing this as a Paparazzi-side workaround pending a Layoutlib-side fix. Kept separate from the main-dispatcher and frame-clock work: those address different issues and did not remove this reproducer's nondeterminism.

body:
## Problem

`Deezer.Test(failures)` was empty, so saving or testing the Deezer download client always passed. A mistyped path, or a Docker volume that wasn't mounted, only surfaced on the first grab, after Deezer had already been asked for the album.

## Change

- `Deezer.Test` now runs Lidarr's `DownloadClientBase.TestFolder` on `DownloadPath`. A failure is reported against the Download Path field as "Folder does not exist" or "Unable to write to folder", with Lidarr's usual permissions hint naming the account Lidarr runs as.
- The ARL is still not checked here; it belongs to the indexer and `ArlCheck` reports it.

### Behavior change

During a download the plugin creates the album folder with `Directory.CreateDirectory`, which also creates a missing download path. A path that doesn't exist yet used to work and now fails the test on save. Users relying on that need to create the folder first.

## Testing

- 3 `DownloadClientTests` cases with a mocked `IDiskProvider`: writable path passes, missing path fails on `DownloadPath`, read-only path fails.
- Adds Moq 4.18.4 to the test project only (the version Lidarr's own tests pin). It is not shipped with the plugin.
- Local run (net8.0): 72 passed, 0 failed. The net10.0 build runs in CI only.

body:
## Summary

Monthly code audit (seven independent reviewers, areas 1–7 of the `samaudit-code-audit` procedure, now with the two guides WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH and DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE), plus re-verification of the six open candidates from the stopped run on 23.11. Every finding below was reproduced and re-checked by me before fixing. Every fix has a test in `tests/test_code_audit_2611.py`, `tests/test_update_sh.py` or `tests/smoke.py`, and that test fails on `main`; counter-checks were run.

## Security
| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| `update.sh` installed a newer `docker-compose.yml` from the image without consent; a crafted image could grant itself `privileged`/host mounts. Rollback kept the new file | saved as `docker-compose.yml.neu`, installed only after `ask_strict` (never `-y`, never without TTY); rollback and abort restore `.alt` |
| `security-update.yml` built `main` HEAD: merged but unpublished code could ship as `<version>-s1` before the owner says "publish" | new `published` step: skip unless tag `v<app>` exists and `app/`, `run.py`, `entrypoint.sh` are unchanged since the last `v<app>[-sN]` (docs excluded) |
| `/connection/reset` skipped the AD re-check; `account_locked` did not revoke sessions | `recheck()` added; `account_locked` in `ACCOUNT_GONE` |
| Before the first scan, any enterprise-CA server certificate `*.domain` was adopted silently for a new DC address | only domain name or `DC_HOSTS` entry; every adoption logged (`act_cert_pinned`) |
| Unauthenticated audit-log flood (`invalid_user` released from lockout, lock logging per username) | `invalid_user`/`account_locked` counted; locked IP logged once; bounded map |
| Diagnostics leaks: CertError object, names outside `_WORD`, `DOMAIN\\user`, escaped DN commas, IPv4 at sentence end; `--log` read as root | all pseudonymised and caught by `check_leaks`; `--log` read after `_drop_root`; clear message without a DB |
| `userPassword`/`unixUserPassword` values were read | presence filter only |
| `trivy.sh` ran a pre-existing binary without checksum | always a fresh folder |

## Correct results
- GPO precedence: enforced links win (higher container last); GPOs with disabled computer settings (`flags & 2`) skipped (`Ctx.gpo_guids`, `effective_dc_registry`)
- SYSVOL read errors other than ENOENT mark the GPO unreadable; A-GPPPassword / A-ScriptPasswords give `na_sysvol_partial` instead of "passed" when SYSVOL is incomplete
- `base_entry(strict=True)` in collect sections (AdminSDHolder, dsHeuristics, recycle bin, schema, PKI, DC OU), so the section fails → "not checkable"; `is_root` from naming contexts; P-SchemaEnterpriseAdmins `na_child_domain`
- AD bind sub-codes (`data 775/533/532/701/773`) evaluated before `invalidCredentials` (`_bind_error`)
- `_AUTOLOGON` and gPLink regexes are linear (were quadratic: 64 KB → 1 s, 2 MB extrapolated to minutes while holding the GIL)

## Operation
- backups older than the shorter retention period deleted (`datastate.prune_by_age`, janitor)
- unusual certificate files → `certerr_format` instead of 500; broken `./certs` file → self-signed instead of start failure
- `--cleanup` keeps old version folders containing keys, `.env*`, override, `*.bak`, backups
- healthcheck parses `TLS_ENABLED` like the program; blank/lower-case `LOG_LEVEL`; cert links in `./certs`; bytes CSRF compare (non-ASCII → no 500, logout works); oversized scan ids → 404; recheck technical errors → allowed as documented; re-login ends the old session

## Documentation updated in this PR
README.md / README.de.md (auditor group `SAMAUDIT-Users`, lockout 5/15, cookie SameSite, compose handling, backups, `LDAP_ALLOW_PLAIN`, `EGRESS_ALLOW` ports), handbook/manual (group, DC pinning, compose, diag `update` section), DATENSCHUTZ.md, `/privacy` (update cookie, backups), `.env.example` (empty `ALLOWED_GROUPS`), news.json, CHANGELOG(.de).md. No visible UI change, so no new screenshots.

## Deliberately left open (owner decision / on-site / hardening)
- Samba/self-signed multi-DC: a new address of a pinned name is still trusted on first contact (documented trade-off; stricter = manual approval)
- SMB to SYSVOL uses NTLM without server binding to the LDAPS pin – needs on-site check (DC event 4624)
- abort path of `update.sh` restarts the old version without DB rollback (existing "no silent decision" design, test-covered)
- script-password heuristics, "all"-scope settings, DC-OU block inheritance, root SID via GC in child domains
- CI hardening: release-age cooldown, Dependabot cooldown, `docker logout`, arm64 daily scan, release environment protection, `imagetools inspect` error handling
- upload > 1 MB shows "session expired"

## Version
2.5.1

## Tests
ruff, mypy, `unittest discover` (OK), `tests/smoke.py` (0 errors). New: 31 tests in `tests/test_code_audit_2611.py`, 5 in `tests/test_update_sh.py` (incl. pseudo-terminal answers), 3 smoke checks for pinning.

The local Docker SHA tags were consuming valuable disk space on our VPS infrastructure. By removing them immediately after successful push operations, we can reduce disk bloat and improve overall system performance.

No explicit testing was performed as this is a cleanup operation that doesn't affect functionality. The change simply removes an unnecessary step in the Docker build process.

This change only affects the local Docker image management and does not impact the actual image pushing or deployment process.

body:

_Requested by **Q** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01H6Z4chGUzwtPJUAVgdhQFg?thread=cmsg_01H6Z4chGUzwtPJUAVgdhQFg9fsMqjYowR9NJV9nXtv1vE)_

## What and why

PR 2 of 4 for #725 (LW-03) and #726 (LW-04), following plan `governance/plans/impl-725-plan.md` (branch governance), which D-903 approved. On its own it closes nothing (refs #725, refs #726): PR 3 closes #725 and PR 4 closes #726.
Feature IDs: LW-03, LW-04. Lanes: `lane:app`, `lane:cli`. It builds on #762 (output) and on #724 as merged. I checked #764 against plan section 2.4 and found no difference that touches this PR.

- **Chapter numbers come from the book (plan 4.1, D-903).** In printed order, a chapter's number (file name, track tag, fingerprint) is its place among the book's chapters that have something to say, counted with `app.script.speakable`. That function cuts the utterances of chapters that were not chosen, without speaking them. The count is the number of those chapters. With a custom order (#119), numbers stay among the chosen chapters, as today, and the record says `"order": "chosen"`. The app now always passes both `numbers` and `count` to output (review note N2 on #762).
- **The settings key leaves out the chapter choice**, so a job that adds chapters runs under the same settings. Chapter record version 2 (`app/playable.py`) adds:
  - `order`;
  - `made`, the settings the key is the hash of;
  - each chapter's `spoken` (the SHA-256 of `spoken/<index>.json`, its list of chunks);
  - `built`, the whole-book files with the fingerprints of the chapters they hold.

  Version 1 records still read, so #724's `read_record` users are unchanged.
- **Adding chapters (#726, in `run_audio_job`):**
  - Chosen chapters beyond those already made are added. The job plans the union in printed order, reuses the made chapters the way #723's resume reuses them, and speaks only the new ones.
  - A finished audiobook with nothing new is refused, as before (D-163).
  - Under other settings, the job raises `SettingsChangedError(OutputExistsError)` before any speech. The error carries the old and new settings and names what differs (`speed: 1.0, now 1.2`).
  - `keep_settings=True` rebuilds the settings from `made`. Only the chapter choice and the output folder are this job's own. Plugins are left out when the kept settings had them off.
  - With `keep_settings`, a difference that keeping cannot bring back (the voice's version) is an `OutputExistsError` naming it, not a settings-changed error.
  - A record of another book in the same working folder adds nothing: that book's files are checked like any other files, as before.
  - A custom-order project, a version 1 record, or a mix of book order and custom order asks for `overwrite`.
- **Building on request (#725), new `app/book.py`:** `build_book(work, out_folder, kind, *, partial_ok, progress, cancel, ffmpeg) -> BuiltBook`.
  - It runs under the working folder's lock and builds from each chapter's `spoken/<index>.json` and the chunk cache through output's `write_book_file`. No text step and no voice runs.
  - Missing chapters, and chapters whose chunks were cleaned out of the cache, raise `MissingChaptersError` unless `partial_ok`. With `partial_ok`, the file is named `<book> (partial).<kind>`.
  - A recorded file whose chapters are still the same is reused.
  - A file of that name that the record does not vouch for is refused. The file is vouched in the record before the rename, then recorded in `built`.
  - Progress is the share of audio fed to ffmpeg. Cancel stops the feed and leaves no file.
- `JobRunner.run_audio(..., keep_settings=)` and `JobRunner.run_book(...)`; new names exported from `sci2audio.app`.
- **CLI:** `convert --keep-settings`. On a settings change, exit 7 says ` (add --keep-settings or --overwrite)`. `--chapters` on a project with chapters made adds the missing ones. Nothing else in the CLI output changes, and the CLI still writes the M4B in the job.
- `docs/baseline.md`: a row for building the whole book.

## Round 1 answer (plans/review-pr765-round1.md)

The round has one fix commit, adeba28. Each new test was shown to fail on the code before it, and passes with it.

- **B1** (incomplete-fix), fixed. Whose book a chapter record belongs to is now decided before anything else, in `_same_book` (`app/audio.py`). For a version 2 record it compares the title and authors from `made`. A version 1 record keeps no book details, so it is matched by its files' names (`<book> - NN …`, `<book>.readalong.json`, `<book>.m4b`). `_adding` only ever sees this book's record, so another book's version 1 record is neither refused nor touched.
  - Test: `tests/unit/test_app_add_chapters.py::test_another_books_version_1_record_neither_refuses_nor_lends_its_settings[plain]`. It fails on 9e160c0.
- **S1** (correctness), fixed. The settings are kept only after the document is read, and only when the record is this book's. Another book's settings are never taken.
  - If the kept language differs from the one given, the file is read again, because the layout follows the language.
  - A language change without `--keep-settings` is now a settings change of this book (`SettingsChangedError`), not another book.
  - Tests: `tests/unit/test_app_add_chapters.py::test_keep_settings_never_takes_another_books_settings` and `::test_another_books_version_1_record_neither_refuses_nor_lends_its_settings[keep-settings]`. Both fail on 9e160c0.
- **S2** (missing-test), fixed.
  - `tests/unit/test_app_book.py::test_a_book_whose_subtitles_were_removed_is_built_again`: the M4B is built again and both subtitle files are back.
  - `tests/unit/test_app_book.py::test_a_book_whose_subtitles_were_edited_is_not_taken_as_current`: an edited `.srt` is no longer the project's, so the build is refused and the edit kept (D-163), rather than rebuilt over it.
  - Both fail with the `_pair_current` clause removed.
- **N1**: no change, as noted.
- **N2**: Issue #766 opened for `--with-script --keep-settings`.

Checks: ruff, format, lint-imports, deptry; the app, CLI and web player tests: 901 passed, 2 skipped.

## Golden files changed (plan 4.1, D-903)

- `tests/unit/__snapshots__/test_cli_convert.ambr` (`test_convert_writes_the_same_files_as_before_chapters_became_playable_early`): the `--chapters 1,3` run now names the third chapter `three - 03 Part C.mp3` (was `02`), with matching `.srt`/`.vtt` names, and its track tags become `1/3` and `3/3` (were `1/2` and `2/2`). This is the change 4.1 predicts for a chosen subset with a gap: a chapter keeps its book number, so it never has to be renamed when the chapter between is added later. A full-book run stays byte-identical (every other snapshot in that file is unchanged).
- `tests/unit/__snapshots__/test_app_audio_chapters.ambr` (`test_the_records_snapshot_of_a_chapters_only_job`): `chapters.json` is version 2, with `order`, `made`, `built` and each chapter's `spoken` hash (the test masks the hash like the others). The files, numbers and read-along file are unchanged.

author: fleetd-on-forge[bot]
body:
Heavy runs (a repo's full check, a whole test suite, a full build) now wait their turn for a small number of machine-wide slots, for any repo, not only fleetd's.

**What happens today.** Check slots shipped on Nov 22, but only fleetd's own `scripts/check.sh` used them. Other repos' checks, such as fleetd-cloud's `bun run check`, and agents' long test loops took no slot. On Nov 23 the devbox reached load ~47 and ~30k sockets in TIME_WAIT, with 4 fleetd checks holding slots while those other runs went alongside them unqueued (seen in `ps` on the devbox today).

**What changes.**
- The slot is now a generic heavy-run slot. Agents' PATH has `fleetd-heavy <command>`, which takes one of the machine's slots while the command runs. With every slot in use, it prints one line saying it is waiting and why (`fleetd: waiting for a heavy-run slot (1 run ahead; 4 slots on this machine, all in use, so it can't overload it)…`) and starts by itself once a slot frees. It uses the same flock queue as before, first come first served.
- Sizing is unchanged: one slot per 8 cores, at least 2 (4 on the 32-core devbox). The only setting is node.json's per-machine `heavySlots`, with `0` meaning off. The old `checkSlots` key is still read when `heavySlots` is absent.
- Built-in prompts: the worker's This machine note now tells agents to run the repo's full pre-push check and any other whole suite or full build as `fleetd-heavy <command>` (e.g. `fleetd-heavy bun run check`), with Bash's longest timeout or in the background with Monitor. The writer brief points full checks to it as well.
- `scripts/check.sh` wraps itself in `fleetd-heavy`. `--background` drops the slot env var for its detached run, so that run takes a slot of its own.
- Compatibility for branches and nodes from before this change: the old `fleetd-check-slot` wrapper and `check-slot` command still work, and the held marker `FLEETD_CHECK_SLOT` is set too. Without it, an older branch's check.sh would re-wrap itself in a loop. check.sh falls back to `fleetd-check-slot` on an older node. This PR's own check ran on the live, older devbox node and queued correctly that way.
- Docs: machines (fair share), config-and-files (`heavySlots`, plus a one-line snippet for a repo's check to take a slot itself), and what-agents-are-told.

**Proof.** `bun test test/node/heavy_slots.test.ts`: 13 pass. The new test "N+1 heavy runs at once" starts 4 runs through the installed `fleetd-heavy` wrapper with 3 slots. Three start, the 4th prints that it is waiting and does not start, and it starts once one of the three ends. Other tests cover first come first served, a crashed or killed run freeing its slot, a killed waiter leaving the queue, nested runs (under both held variables) not taking a second slot, the wrapper being written under both names, and check.sh wrapping through either name. `scripts/check.sh`: pushable 803f7be (it waited for a slot first).

Done-when 1 (load on the devbox) is checked once this is live; it can't be shown in the PR.

Unsure: an agent can still skip `fleetd-heavy` and run a full suite directly, because this relies on the prompt and on repos' own check scripts rather than intercepting commands. Also unsure whether one slot per 8 cores leaves enough headroom for agents' unslotted partial runs; the devbox will show this once it's live.

author: constantin-jais
body:
Door: two-way
Origin: proposal
Not-added: schema, workflow, hosted-service, telemetry

## Summary

Lot L7 of the open-code-review drill (2026-11-23, owner decision in chat: « L7 méthodes de gate »), part A: the git commands a skill prescribes in prose are now replayed in a trapped repository.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What runs a skill's commands | nothing: T1-T4 read form, routing, cascade, risky text | `check:skills-commands` (T5), link of `bun run check` |
| Extraction | — | every `git …` in fenced blocks and inline code spans of `skills/**/*.md` |
| Classes (sum to extracted, per skill) | — | replay (read-only subcommand, every word literal) / write (any other subcommand, unknown included: never run) / not-executable (placeholder, expansion, redirection, glob, global option other than `--no-pager`, option naming a program or an outside file) |
| Traps | — | `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, `GIT_PAGER`, `core.pager`, `diff.trap.textconv`, `filter.trap.clean`/`smudge` (witness file each), `color.ui=always` (escape sequence in output) |
| State | — | status, refs, HEAD, local config, worktrees compared before/after |
| Channels | — | pipe and pseudo-terminal: git starts no pager without a terminal, so a pager trap run through pipes alone can never fire. No terminal = named failure |
| Child environment | — | `PATH` only; `HOME`, `TMPDIR` in the fixture; `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` |

Files:

- `tools/skills/check-skills-commands.ts` — gate (new)
- `tools/skills/check-skills-commands.test.ts` — 49 tests (new)
- `package.json` — `check:skills-commands`, wired after `check:skills-security`
- `docs/method/SKILLS-ANATOMY.md` — section « Les commandes git d'une skill sont rejouées »
- `skills/context-conformity/SKILL.md` — `git log -1 --format=…` → `git --no-pager log -1 --format=…` (pages under a terminal)
- `skills/wizard/SKILL.md` — provenance sentence named `git check-ignore` alone (git exits 128 without a path); now `git check-ignore -q .env`

Current corpus (local run): `commands=15 (replayed 5)`; context-conformity 1 = 1 + 0 + 0; deploy-clever 1 = 1 + 0 + 0; pr-body 11 = 1 + 4 + 6; wizard 2 = 2 + 0 + 0.

## Evidence

Red before the module existed:

```text
$ bun test tools/skills/check-skills-commands.test.ts
error: Cannot find module './check-skills-commands'
 0 pass
 1 fail
```

Green after:

```text
$ bun test tools/skills/check-skills-commands.test.ts
 49 pass
 0 fail
```

Gate on the base skills (pipe channel), before the two skill edits:

```text
Skills commands (T5): wizard/SKILL.md:53 `git check-ignore` (pipe): git refused it on the fixture (exit 128): the replay proved nothing
```

Neutralisation (each decisive expression replaced by a `false &&` no-op, test file rerun, original restored from the index):

| Mutant | Tests red |
| --- | --- |
| witness detection | 5 (external diff, textconv ×2, filter, gate process) |
| colour detection | 1 |
| state comparison | 2 (ref moved, file written) |
| read-only classification | 6 |
| refused options | 5 |
| fatal exit (128/129) | 1 |
| blocked word (placeholder, expansion…) | 9 |

Test questions (gate-integrity §5):

1. What makes them red: the no-ops above; the trap tests also need git to actually run the trap programs (`git diff` → external diff, `git log -p` → textconv, `git cat-file --filters` → smudge, `git log --oneline` → colour).
2. Would an equivalent refactor or a better result turn them red? The expected values come from git's documented behaviour (pager only on a terminal, textconv on by default for `diff` and `log`, `--output` writes a file), not from the gate's output, except the wording of the problem strings, which is the gate's contract with its reader.

**Terminal channel not exercised locally.** The agent sandbox refuses `openpty` (`script: openpty: Operation not permitted`; Bun: `Failed to open PTY`). Locally the gate therefore fails with `terminal channel: no pseudo-terminal (Failed to open PTY)`, and the terminal test takes its « unavailable, named » branch. The pager branch (`git log --format=%h %s` fires `GIT_PAGER`) runs first in CI on `ubuntu-latest`: this PR's CI run is its first execution.

Aggregate, each link of `check:full` run separately after `git add`, on this branch and on a worktree of the base, both under the pinned Bun `1.4.0-canary.1+57f349f63`, in the agent sandbox:

| Link | Base | Branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check:attestation` | fail (sandbox: bare `mktemp` refused) | fail, same |
| `test` | fail, 55 tests (sandbox: `mktemp`, git fixtures) | fail, the same 55 (sorted lists compared byte for byte); 0 failure in `tools/skills` |
| `check:reuse` | fail (sandbox: `SC_SEM_NSEMS_MAX` refused to Python multiprocessing) | fail, same |
| `check:skills-commands` | — | fail: terminal channel unavailable (above) |
| every other link (41 of the 44 links of the base) | pass | pass |

`check:reuse` could not run here: the new files fall under the `tools/**` annotation of `REUSE.toml` (inferred, not measured). CI is the first full verdict.

## Blast radius

`project-governance` only: one more link in `bun run check` (CI job « Bun quality »). Any sandbox that refuses pseudo-terminals now fails this link locally. A skill that prescribes `git diff`, `git log -p` or any pager-eligible command without `--no-pager` will fail the aggregate until written hermetically.

Commits:

- `8e11280` Constantin Jais / Constantin Jais — Replay the git commands of skills in a trapped repository (T5)

author: lieranderl
body:
## What changed

On production, a visitor wrote "male pedicure zara 11:00 on 27 November". Instead of looking it up, the chat showed a **Book Male pedicure with Zara** button, and the guard withheld its unchecked reply as "I can only confirm free times…". Only the next message, "check the time", got the lookup, which found Fri 27/11 · 11:00.

The prompt had two competing rules:
- rule 7: "To suggest booking times, call find_free_slots…"
- rule 8: "When the visitor wants to book, call offer_booking…"

Naming the appointment you want reads as "wants to book", and nothing said that a time the visitor names must be checked first.

The new rules (`internal/assistant/prompt.go`):
- **Rule 7:** "Whenever the visitor names a day, a date or a time for a treatment, as a question or as the appointment they want ("Zara, 11:00 on the 27th"), call find_free_slots before you answer…", passing from/to date and time.
- **Rule 8:** "When the visitor wants to book but names no day or time, call offer_booking…"

`TestThePromptKeepsTimesAndCareAdviceHonest` pins both phrases.

## Checked with the real model (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `eu`)

I captured the exact request with Male pedicure bookable with Zara and sent it with three histories: on its own, after a booking request, and after two withheld turns.
- **Before the change:** 9 of 9 runs called `find_free_slots` correctly, so the production miss didn't reproduce outside that real conversation, which isn't logged.
- **After the change:** 9 of 9 runs again called `find_free_slots` with Zara, 2026-11-27 and 11:00–11:00.
- **"I want to book a male pedicure with Zara"** with no time: 1 run called `offer_booking` and 2 called `find_free_slots`. Both show a Book button.

So this makes the rule explicit rather than fixing a reproduced failure.

## Verification

- `make ci` passes.

author: georgejieh
body:
## What

A test that passes on base and fails on head in the repository's own checks is now always reported, whatever the models answered and also when the model review fails.

- The result carries `check_regressions` with source `repository_check`, a count and up to 16 tests. It is not a model finding and is labelled as such.
- It appears in JSON, text, Markdown and SARIF (as error notifications and a run property), for single reviews and review sets.
- `ci_disposition` becomes `blocked`. Exit code is 4 under `default`, `findings` and `strict`; `always-zero` still returns 0.
- When the model review failed, the output says the regressions come from the repository's tests alone.
- The model contract is unchanged. Lint diagnostics stay hints.

## Why

In a seeded-defect evaluation the sandbox proved a regression in 3 of 21 cases where the review reported no finding.

## Tests

`localreview`, `runtimeconfig` and `evaluation` passed locally. An end-to-end test runs a real checkout through the sandbox with a stub model that returns no candidates, then an invalid answer, alone and in a review set. Two local full runs of `cmd/trestle` each failed one different unrelated test that passes alone; CI decides.

## Not in this change

- The failing test's output line is not shown; the checks do not keep it.
- SARIF consumers that list only results will not show regressions.

author: risi-10
body:
Completes phase 1 of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The Fastify server now also serves the page, and the page picks its mode from how it was opened. There is no setting.

- **Opened from the server** (`http://…`): files are sent to `POST /api/clean`, and the intro text says they go to the server and aren't stored.
- **Opened as a file** (`dist/list-cleaner.html`): files are cleaned in the browser and never leave the computer, as before.

Both modes use `src/core/`. **The cleaning rules are unchanged**: `git diff main -- src/core` is empty.

**Changes**
- `server/routes/web.js` (new): serves `/` and exactly the files the page loads (its CSS and JS, `core/*.js`, SheetJS), from a fixed list. Nothing else in the project can be fetched.
- `server/clean.js`: the response also returns `roles`, `separator` and `files` (row count per file). The page uses these to rename columns and build downloads without another request. Existing fields are unchanged.
- `src/web/app.js`: the mode is chosen from `location.protocol`. Cleaning is split into `cleanInBrowser` (today's code) and `cleanOnServer`. In server mode, a file the server rejects is left out and the rest are retried, so one bad file doesn't block the others, as offline. File-list changes run in order, so a slow response can't overwrite a newer one.
- `src/web/index.html`: `id="lead"` on the intro text.
- README, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md updated.

**Verified**
- `npm test`: 73 pass (4 new). `web.test.js` checks that every script and stylesheet the page links to loads, and that `/package.json`, `/.env`, `/samples/…` and `/core/../package.json` return 404.
- `npm run build` works.
- Loaded the page in jsdom in both modes and ran: drop the sample → add a good and a bad file together → English column names → remove a file → start over. Both modes gave identical summaries, file lists and errors.
- **Not checked:** a click-through in a real browser (drag-and-drop and the download buttons).

author: nadethepup
body:
## Summary

Reworks Settings > Trash: every trashed video in a paginated list with search, filters, sorts, the size of each video and the total size of the trash (and of the current filter), plus bulk restore and bulk permanent delete.

## Changes

- List: thumbnail, storage path and relative path, size, duration, resolution, codec, trashed date, purge date (retention, or the scheduled duplicate deletion when earlier) with a countdown, badges "Duplicate" (not kept when its duplicate group was resolved, from existing data), "Kept on disk" (read-only storage path), "File missing" (last missing-file check).
- Search on title and path (debounced), filters (storage path, size, duration, trashed date, resolution, codec, source), five sorts; page, page size, sort and filters in the URL.
- Header strip with count and size of the whole trash and of the current filter.
- Bulk bar: select page / select all results (up to 500), restore, delete permanently. Permanent delete always goes through a modal with the count, the total size and an explicit "files are deleted from disk" acknowledgement; it reuses the existing permanent-delete path.
- Tests: repository integration (filters, sorts, totals, purge date, ids, facets), service and handler tests, `trashFilters` bun tests.

## API

- `GET /api/v1/admin/trash` with `page, limit, sort, order, q, storage_path_id, min_size, max_size, min_duration, max_duration, trashed_from, trashed_to, resolution, codec, source` -> items + `pagination` + `totals {filtered, all}` (`{count, size}`); the previous fields are kept.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/trash/ids` (same filters, max 500) and `GET /api/v1/admin/trash/facets`.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/trash/restore-bulk` and `POST /api/v1/admin/trash/delete-bulk` with `{"scene_ids": [...]}` (max 500) -> `{succeeded, failed: [{scene_id, error}], size}`.

## Migrations

None (the partial index on `scenes.trashed_at` covers the queries).

## What
`golive_next` could filter the next-step plan only by `--owner`, but the M1 phone plan compares exact catalogue stage IDs (roadmap M1, contract C1).

## Change
- `campaign_tool/records/golive_next.py`: new `--stage` option, `choices=golive_catalog.STAGES`, so an unknown ID (including a case-changed `a2`) is an argparse usage error (exit 2) before any report/evidence path is loaded.

## Tests (owner: `tests/records/test_golive_next.py`)
Extends the existing CLI tests/fixtures; each assertion names the bug it catches:
- unfiltered `--json` equals `plan(...)` unchanged: a default stage filter, or changed row shape/order;
- exact `17b` and `A2` selections (text and `--stage X --owner O --json`): numeric coercion, lost suffix, filtering JSON only, or owner-only matching returning other stages;
- `--stage A2 --owner operator` gives empty/no-pending: OR semantics or ignoring `--owner`;
- LIVE stage `1` returns `[]` / no-pending text: a live stage reappearing when requested explicitly;
- invalid `a2` / `99`: usage error, case-normalisation, unknown-as-empty; `--stage A2` with a bad report still fails full validation (exit 2).

## Qué cambia
Dos reglas de juego que decidió Ander el 23 nov. La tercera, dar por hecha una sesión desde el 70 %, quedó en «no» y no se aplica.

**Sin edad, el pulso pasa a watts**
- `Ent.normalizarBloques` convierte un bloque `fcpct` que no tiene pulso de referencia a watts con `pctFtpDeFcpct`. La conversión es por tramos: el 60–70 % de la reserva (zona 2) equivale a 56–75 % del FTP, el 80 % a 90 % y el 90 % a 105 %.
- Antes ese bloque quedaba con `metrica: ''`, es decir, «Libre».
- `bloquesEnWatts` conserva el comportamiento anterior con `wattsSinFc: false`.
- En vivo, el texto de la meta añade «con tu edad sería por pulso».

**Días suaves del plan**
- `J.esSuaveDelPlan(s)` es verdadero cuando la fecha es igual o posterior a `SUAVE_SIN_ZONAS_DESDE` (2026-11-24), la sesión tiene `delPrograma` y su `tipoPlan` no es intenso. En ese caso `gananciaSesion` no suma Fuerza por zona 4 ni Agilidad por VO₂. Las sesiones anteriores no cambian.
- `TIPOS_INTENSOS` se define ahora en `juego.js` y `consejos.INTENSOS` lo reutiliza.
- `C.enVivo` recibe `delPlan` (de `xpCtx.delPlanSemana`) y `ahora`. Si vas por encima del rango, el reto pasa a «Baja a X–Y W» con `aviso: true`, que se pinta en ámbar en `#atr-reto` y `#mr-atr`.

author: easyindustry
body:
Los nodos pasan a seguir la simbología de siempre, para que cualquiera que lea diagramas de flujo los entienda. La base es ISO 5807; la espera toma el círculo de borde doble de BPMN, porque la norma clásica no tiene símbolo para «esperar a que pase algo».

- **Evento** reemplaza a Disparador y Estado, con tres variantes: inicio y fin (óvalo de terminador) y espera (círculo de borde doble, con una salida por cada evento que escucha).
- La caja de la espera es invisible y abarca el círculo y el nombre, así ocupa su lugar real al acomodar.
- **Acomodar** ahora le pasa a elkjs los puntos de conexión de cada nodo: las flechas se alinean con los puntos y no con el centro de la caja, y las ramas salen en el orden de sus puntos.
- **Subflujo** lleva la doble barra del «proceso predefinido».
- La geometría de las salidas sobre el rombo y el círculo quedó en `geometria.ts`, sin React.
- El README suma la tabla de simbología.

Apilado sobre #2. Probado: chequeo de tipos, test de límites, la geometría y el acomodo con puntos de conexión corridos en Node. Falta el QA visual.

author: ckokolog-ship-it
body:
## Τι αλλάζει

Ένα πολυγλωσσικό **μοντέλο embeddings μέσα στη βάση** κάνει κάθε περιγραφή κίνησης ένα `VECTOR` 384 αριθμών. Έτσι μια ερώτηση με δικά σου λόγια βρίσκει τις κινήσεις που σημαίνουν το ίδιο, ακόμα και χωρίς κοινή λέξη. Όλα γίνονται στη βάση, χωρίς εξωτερική υπηρεσία. Αναλυτικά: `docs/ODIGIES_AI.md`, ενότητα 6.

| Ερώτηση | Βρίσκει |
|---|---|
| φαγητό έξω | Ψητοπωλείο Το Κάρβουνο, εστιατόριο, Ταβέρνα Ο Μπάμπης |
| βενζινάδικο, fuel | SHELL πρατήριο Ρίου, EKO βενζίνη, BP πρατήριο καυσίμων, AVIN καύσιμα |
| ρεύμα και νερό | ΔΕΗ, ΕΥΔΑΠ |
| ταινίες | Netflix συνδρομή ταινιών |

**Το μοντέλο (`ai/`)**
- Το `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` (άδεια MIT) γίνεται ένα αρχείο ONNX με τον SentencePiece tokenizer μέσα, όπως το θέλει το `DBMS_VECTOR.LOAD_ONNX_MODEL`.
- Το `build_embed.py` ελέγχει ότι δίνει τα ίδια vectors με το αρχικό μοντέλο.
- Το `mk_embed_model.sh` το φτιάχνει σε δικό του venv. Το μοντέλο κατεβαίνει από το Hugging Face και δεν μπαίνει στο repo (`.gitignore`).
- Δοκίμασα και τα e5-base και paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet: ήταν χειρότερα σε αυτά τα κείμενα και τριπλάσια σε μέγεθος.

**Βάση (`db/BK_VECTOR.sql`)**
- `bk_ai_phrase`: κάθε κείμενο μία φορά (69 για 9.000 κινήσεις), με `VECTOR(384, FLOAT32)` και **vector index** (IVF, cosine).
- `bk_vec.search`: `VECTOR_EMBEDDING` για την ερώτηση και `VECTOR_DISTANCE ... FETCH APPROX FIRST`. Κρατά τα κοντινά κείμενα με βάση ένα περιθώριο και την κατηγορία της ερώτησης· σε έναν λογαριασμό, μόνο τα δικά του.
- **Κατηγορίες:** 15, με την πιο κοντινή στο νόημα. Οι τόκοι, οι προμήθειες και οι αντιλογισμοί κατατάσσονται από το είδος της κίνησης.
- `bk_ai_spend12_v`: τα έξοδα του λογαριασμού στους τελευταίους 12 μήνες, ανά κατηγορία.
- Το `close_day` ενημερώνει τις νέες κινήσεις (`bk_vec.refresh`).
- `LOAD_EMBED.sql`: το INSTALL το τρέχει στο τέλος. Χωρίς μοντέλο, η υπόλοιπη τράπεζα δουλεύει κανονικά.
- `GRANT_AI.sql`: δημιουργεί και το directory `BK_MODELS` (διαδρομή ως παράμετρος).

**Demo:** οι αγορές με κάρτα έχουν πλέον έμπορο και τύπο, και οι λογαριασμοί με μισθό πληρώνουν κάθε μήνα ΔΕΗ, ΕΥΔΑΠ, κινητό, internet, Netflix και Spotify. Η σειρά των τυχαίων αριθμών του demo μένει η ίδια, και το demo του Βήματος 1 βγάζει ακόμα 6 ειδοποιήσεις.

**Οθόνες**
- Φόρμα `BK_SEARCH`.
- Σελίδα «Αναζήτηση με το νόημα».
- Καρτέλα «Έξοδα ανά κατηγορία» στον λογαριασμό.
- REST `GET /api/ai/search`, `GET /api/ai/spending`.

**Tests:** `tests/test_vector.py` (3) και ένα test σε καθένα από τα `test_forms` και `test_api`. Χωρίς το μοντέλο στη βάση, παραλείπονται.

## Στο forms1

```bash
sudo -iu oracle git -C bank pull
# 1. το μοντέλο: Hugging Face -> ai/models/bk_embed.onnx (~450 MB, λίγα λεπτά· Python 3.9+)
sudo -iu oracle ~oracle/bank/ai/mk_embed_model.sh
# 2. το directory BK_MODELS και τα δικαιώματα (ζητά τον κωδικό του SYSTEM)
sudo -iu oracle bash -c 'cd ~/bank/db && sqlplus system@localhost:1521/FREEPDB1 @GRANT_AI.sql'
# 3. από την αρχή με demo (οι νέοι έμποροι και οι λογαριασμοί σπιτιού)· στο τέλος φορτώνει το μοντέλο
sudo -iu oracle bash -c 'cd ~/bank/db && export NLS_LANG=GREEK_GREECE.AL32UTF8 && sqlplus bank@localhost:1521/FREEPDB1 @UNINSTALL.sql'
sudo -iu oracle bash -c 'cd ~/bank/db && export NLS_LANG=GREEK_GREECE.AL32UTF8 && sqlplus bank@localhost:1521/FREEPDB1 @INSTALL.sql demo'
sudo ~oracle/bank/api/install_service.sh
su - oracle
cd ~/bank/forms && ./build_forms.sh
```

Στο τέλος το INSTALL πρέπει να γράφει `== BK_EMBED loaded: 69 texts of the movements with their vector`. Αν η βάση δεν βλέπει τη διαδρομή `/home/oracle/bank/ai/models`, δώσε άλλη: `@GRANT_AI.sql /διαδρομή` (ODIGIES_AI.md).

Closes #10

User story dans Cockpit : https://cockpit.dorianvidal.com/projects/leurio/stories/fd2d1481-d19d-4e5b-ac54-51be6d7c818d
Maquette validée : https://claude.ai/artifact/GdeceYRVaWh4kKHVCniHfj (fichier `docs/maquettes/us-10-video-tierce-consentement.html`)

PLAN §7, §9 bis, §11.

## Ce qui est construit
- **VideoPlayer** (`src/app/shared/video-player/`) : sous la boucle courte de l'US 9, une rubrique « Vidéo complète » joue la première vidéo tierce de `videos`.
  - Sans réponse au consentement : « Cette vidéo est hébergée par <plateforme>. La charger ? », avec les boutons « Non merci » et « Charger la vidéo ».
  - Avec le consentement accepté : le lecteur officiel en iframe, calé sur `start` (`www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed`, `player.vimeo.com/video`, `geo.dailymotion.com/player.html`).
  - Après un refus : la rubrique disparaît, la boucle reste.
- **Crédit** « Vidéo : <auteur> » : il apparaît sous le lecteur. Avec `lienAuteur`, le nom est un lien qui ouvre la chaîne hors de l'app (`target=_blank`, `rel=noopener noreferrer`, icône de lien externe de la maquette). Sans `lienAuteur`, le crédit est en texte simple. Sans auteur, il n'y a pas de ligne.
- **Sécurité** : les URL du lecteur sont construites depuis trois hôtes fixes, avec l'id encodé. Seule l'URL construite passe par `bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl`. Aucune requête ne part vers une plateforme avant le consentement (vérifié en e2e).
- **Modèle du consentement (décision du propriétaire, option A)** : `users/{uid}.consentements.video` vaut `true | false | null`.
  - `null` (ou absent) signifie « pas encore répondu » : la question est posée.
  - `false` vaut refus, y compris pour les comptes existants.
  - Les nouveaux comptes sont créés avec `null`.
  - Compte › Consentements affiche `null` comme « non ».
  - `ConsentementsService.reponseVideo()` expose ces trois états.
- **Isolation par compte** (trouvé en revue) :
  - Les consentements sont remis à zéro à la suppression du compte (`oublier()`) et quand le compte change.
  - Une lecture tardive d'un ancien compte est ignorée.
  - Le lecteur attend sa propre lecture du consentement avant d'afficher quoi que ce soit.
- **Schéma** : `lienAuteur` doit commencer par `https://`.

## Tests
- Acceptation : `animation.page.us10.spec.ts` (16 tests, au moins un par critère), `e2e/animation-video-tierce.spec.ts` (4), plus des tests du service, du compte et du lecteur (changement de compte, lecture en attente, adresses des lecteurs).
- Tests modifiés sur décision du propriétaire : un compte neuf a maintenant `video: null` au lieu de `false` (`compte.service.spec.ts`, `user-doc.spec.ts`, `e2e/compte-anonyme.spec.ts`).
- Résultats sur 83e9152 :
  - `npm run lint` : OK
  - `npm run typecheck` : OK
  - `npm test` : 1285/1285
  - `npm run validate-data` : OK
  - `npm run test:acceptance` : 325/325
  - `npm run test:e2e` : 130/130

## À vérifier par le propriétaire
- **YouTube dans l'app Capacitor iOS** : pas vérifié sur un appareil. YouTube peut refuser l'intégration quand l'origine de la page est `capacitor://localhost` (erreur 153). La PWA dans Safari n'est pas concernée.
- **Contenu** : trois vidéos YouTube de `techniques.json` ont `"auteur": "À vérifier"`, et aucune n'a de `lienAuteur`. Le crédit affichera « Vidéo : À vérifier » tant que ce contenu n'est pas corrigé.
- **PLAN §7** : la description de `consentements.video` (booléen) est à mettre à jour (`boolean | null`). Le plan n'a pas été modifié dans cette PR.

author: nantoniazzi
body:
## What

This repository publishes an npm package from GitHub Actions: the `release` workflow (started by hand) builds the package and runs semantic-release with the `NPM_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` secrets. This PR hardens those workflows against a compromised third-party action or dependency, without changing what they do:

- **Every action is pinned to a commit SHA** instead of a tag, with the version kept in a comment (e.g. `actions/checkout@fbc6f39… # v5.1.0`). Each SHA is the commit the current tag already points to, so behavior is identical.
- **The release job no longer leaves the GitHub token in `.git/config` and skips dependency install scripts** (`persist-credentials: false` on checkout, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`). The build still runs explicitly, and semantic-release authenticates through the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable, as its documentation recommends.

## Why

CodinGame received a sales email from a CI/CD security vendor pointing at this pattern across our public repositories. An outsider cannot trigger these release workflows: they only run on `workflow_dispatch` or on pushes by people with write access, and pull requests from forks run without secrets. The remaining risk is indirect, the same one behind the tj-actions (March 2025) and Shai-Hulud (2025) incidents:

- a tag of a third-party action can be moved to malicious code, which would then run with the release secrets;
- a compromised npm dependency can run an install script in the release job, read the token left in `.git/config` by `actions/checkout`, or tamper with `node_modules` before semantic-release runs with `NPM_TOKEN`.

## Notable decisions

- **Same major versions, no upgrades.** Pinning only freezes what already runs, so the PR carries no functional change to review. Dependabot (or Renovate) can keep the SHAs up to date from the version comments.
- **`--ignore-scripts` only in the release job.** I checked `package-lock.json`: no dependency used on Linux needs an install script here (`fsevents` is macOS only; esbuild 0.19, where present, gets its binary from an optional dependency and works without its script). The PR check job keeps a plain `npm ci`, since a pull request from a fork never sees the secrets anyway.
- **`NPM_TOKEN` is still used.** The next step is npm trusted publishing (OIDC, no long-lived token), which needs the package to be configured on npmjs.com first; it will come in a follow-up PR.
- The release workflow only runs when someone starts it, so this PR's CI does not exercise the release job. The next manual release is the real test: if `--ignore-scripts` or the missing persisted credentials break something, the job fails before publishing anything, and reverting this commit restores the previous behavior.

## Evidence

- **Pins are behavior-neutral**: for each action, `git ls-remote --tags` showed the moving tag (`v5`, `v4`…) and the pinned exact tag resolve to the same commit.
- **Static scan**: [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor) (offline) reports no high-severity finding on these workflows after the change (before: unpinned actions, plus credential persistence in the release job). The remaining medium findings concern the PR check jobs, which never receive secrets from forks.
- **YAML parses** for every changed workflow file.

author: oscarfersan
body:
## Why

CodeRabbit's and Codex's reviews are optional in practice. Requiring all three approvals hid **Finish** on PRs that a teammate had already approved and that were ready to close.

## What changed

- New `src/finish/ready.ts` (`finishReadiness`):
  - a teammate's approval is required;
  - a teammate asking for changes, or a draft, blocks it;
  - the bots are optional unless the new team setting `finish.requireBots` is `true`.
- **Menu**: `Finish without CodeRabbit, Codex` (or `CodeRabbit (changes)` when it asked for changes). The full detail is in the tooltip. With every approval the label is unchanged.
- **`gh wpr finish`** applies the same rule and prints which optional reviews it is going ahead without.
- README and the example configs document `requireBots`.

## Testing

- `pnpm test`: 198 pass, with 4 new ones for readiness and the menu. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.
- Ran `finish --dry-run` on a real PR approved only by a teammate: it found the rebase needed, the merge, and its card in Notion. Nothing was changed.

author: paulpham157
body:
Fixes #248

## Problem

A retried or re-sent OTLP export stores the same span or log again under a new row id. #214 (PR #218) de-duplicates Claude/Grok `api_request` logs, and OpenCode/Pi count a span once by trace + span id, but:

- Copilot: `copilotTokens` summed every `chat` span (or top-level `invoke_agent` span) with no trace + span id de-duplication. Duration unions intervals, so time was not doubled, but tokens and the `nano_aiu` note were.
- Gemini: `geminiTokens` summed every `gemini_cli.api_response` log, so the logs fallback doubled.

## Dedup keys and why

- **Copilot: trace id + span id**, through the existing `spanKey` helper that OpenCode/Pi use. Span ids are only unique within a trace, so the trace id is part of the key, and a row missing either id is never merged. The check is in `copilotSpans`, so `chat` usage, the `invoke_agent` fallback (`copilotTopLevel`), the AIU note, and duration all see each span once. The first copy is kept. Copilot emits a span once, at its end, so a second copy is a re-send.
- **Gemini: an exact copy** (`geminiResponseKey`): session id + log record time + body + every attribute (`freeze`, the canonical map encoding `reduce` uses). I checked `tests/samples/gemini_logs.json` and the existing tests. `api_response` carries `session.id`, `prompt_id`, `event.timestamp`, `model`, `duration_ms`, `status_code`, counts, `finish_reasons`, `role`, and `auth_type`, but **no response or request id**. `prompt_id` is shared by every response of one prompt (all three sample responses share `sample-gemini-1########1`), and two responses can have the same model and counts. So any key looser than an exact copy could merge real responses. Like `apiRequestKey`, the key is empty, and the record is never merged, when the log has neither `event.timestamp` nor a log time.
- **Gemini metrics are unchanged.** `gemini_cli.token.usage` is cumulative, so `reduce` takes the latest point of each run, and a re-sent point does not add up. Feeding the whole Gemini sample twice gives the same metric totals. Duplicated *delta* points for any tool are the existing generic limit already listed in docs/gaps.md ("Retried delta exports can be double-counted"). That limit is not Gemini-specific and is not in scope here.

## Fix

- `internal/summary/copilot.go`: `copilotSpans` de-duplicates by `spanKey`. The method strings say a span stored twice counts once.
- `internal/summary/summary.go` (`geminiTokens` area only): skip `api_response` logs whose `geminiResponseKey` was already seen. Adds `geminiResponseDedupMethod` to the method string.
- Docs: `docs/summary.md` (precedence), `docs/agents.md` (Copilot tokens, Gemini table), `docs/gaps.md` (limits).

## Tests (written first), `internal/summary/copilot_gemini_dedup_test.go`

- `TestCopilotResentTracesCountChatTokensOnce`: the Copilot sample sent twice has the same tokens, duration, and 1.9 AIU as once.
- `TestCopilotDistinctChatSpansWithSameCountsBothCount`: three chat spans with equal counts (another span id, or the same span id in another trace) are all counted, once or re-sent.
- `TestCopilotResentInvokeAgentFallbackCountsOnce`: covers the `invoke_agent` fallback and AIU.
- `TestGeminiResentAPIResponseLogCountsOnce` and `TestGeminiResentSampleLogsCountOnce`: synthetic logs and `gemini_logs.json`, each sent twice.
- `TestGeminiDistinctAPIResponsesWithSameCountsBothCount`: same `prompt_id`, model, and counts at another time, or the same log time with another `event.timestamp`, are all counted. Undated logs are never merged.

Fail before (main a8236f8, new tests only):
```
--- FAIL: TestCopilotResentTracesCountChatTokensOnce: tokens[input_tokens]=127200 after a re-sent export, want 63600
--- FAIL: TestCopilotDistinctChatSpansWithSameCountsBothCount: re-sent: tokens map[input_tokens:600 output_tokens:42], want three chat spans
--- FAIL: TestCopilotResentInvokeAgentFallbackCountsOnce: tokens map[input_tokens:3600 output_tokens:160], want each top-level span once
--- FAIL: TestGeminiResentAPIResponseLogCountsOnce: re-sent: tokens map[input_token_count:5400 output_token_count:200 ...]
--- FAIL: TestGeminiResentSampleLogsCountOnce: tokens[input_token_count]=54708 after a re-sent export, want 27354
```
(`TestGeminiDistinctAPIResponsesWithSameCountsBothCount` passed before, as expected: it guards against over-merging.)

Pass after: all seven tests pass, and so do the existing Copilot, Gemini, and #214 tests.

## Checks

- `gofmt -l .`: empty
- `go vet ./...`: ok
- `go test ./...`: ok
- `go test -race ./...`: ok
- `go run honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@v0.8.2 -tags e2e ./...`: ok
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o sdf ./cmd/sdf && SDF_BIN=$(pwd)/sdf go test -tags e2e -count=1 -timeout 5m ./tests/e2e`: ok (6 tests pass)

## Not changed (follow-ups if wanted)

- Re-sent `execute_tool` spans and `gemini_cli.tool_call` logs still list each tool call twice (Copilot sample: 5 calls become 10; Gemini: 3 become 6). Those are tool-call paths, not tokens.
- Qwen Code `qwen-code.api_response` sums the same way as Gemini did and is not de-duplicated here.
- No overlap with `internal/pricing` (#246), `internal/decision`, `internal/cli`, `internal/ui`, or README. #231 edits other parts of `summary.go` (Grok/Claude pricing), not `geminiTokens`.

author: dizys
body: ## What this is A wheel zoom into the iOS kit's Control Center board made the GPU engine trap ("RuntimeError: unreachable"). It then dropped to the CPU worker, in both T4 modes. This PR fixes the cause and adds a regression test. I found it while replaying Figma's G2 gesture in the file bench (Control Center, 15% → 254% in 14 wheel steps), to compare like with like. That bench code is not in this PR. ## The bug A panic hook in a diagnostic build gave the message and the stack: - **Message:** `panicked at vello_common-0.4.0/src/clip.rs:307:45: clip stack underflowed` - **Stack:** `render_gpu → render_whole → render_reader_halo → run_halo_tier → capture_clamp_strips → draw_whole_pass → draw_split_resumable → Scene::pop_clip` `abort_isolated` started the parent's scene afresh, but didn't put back the clips still open round the scope. The walk's `open` list still marked those clips as on the scene, so the next pop found Vello's clip stack empty, and Vello panicked. Aborting runs on error unwind, and when a walk stops early inside a scope. The reduced reader-halo frame stops early: it captures exact edge strips for clamp-mode clip frames, and each strip walk stops as soon as it meets its reader. On Control Center that reader sits inside an isolated scope under a clip, so every such frame trapped. The error-unwind path had the same flaw, but it was only reachable on errors. ## The fix `Backend::abort_isolated` now takes the parent's `open` list, and both backends (GPU and CPU) replay its clips on the fresh scene, as `pop_isolated` and `pop_composited` already do. All 14 call sites already restored `self.open` to the parent's list before aborting, and now pass it. ## Tests - **New regression test:** `a_scope_stopped_early_under_a_clip_keeps_the_clip_on_the_scene` (CPU backend). It has a clipped frame whose child has a layer blend, drawn by a backend that stops early once the scope is open. On main it panics with the same "clip stack underflowed"; with the fix it passes. - **Rust:** `cargo fmt --check`, and clippy with `-D warnings` on host, gpu, compute and webgl, are clean. 268 tests passed across 17 binaries, including fuzz. - **JS:** `pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm lint` is clean apart from the existing CSS warnings. - **Units:** @drawpane/editor 970 passed in both passes, @drawpane/web 373, @drawpane/engine 45. - **WASM gzipped sizes are unchanged:** webgl 1,398 KB (budget 1,400), browser 692, compute 942, worker 378. - **On the T4, G2 replayed with this fix:** the engine stays on webgl2 through the gesture and its settle, with nothing in the console. Without the fix it trapped every time, in four runs across both modes. - **T4 parity:** 30/30 passed (`parity/engine.spec.ts`, webgpu mode, `ENGINE_PARITY_BACKENDS=auto`). - **T4 GPU e2e** (engine-zoom-blur, glass-atlas, glass-zoom, tiles-gpu, idle, page-open), main and this PR in one run: | Mode | main (a0ab295e) | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | gpu | 59 passed, 2 failed | 60 passed, 1 failed | | webgpu | 59 passed, 2 failed | 59 passed, 2 failed | Every failure on this PR is "real2880-100pct-r250 must run reader-halo (plan 4)". That test is stale since #314 and is fixed in #327. Main also failed "a dense page presents its first content before the full display list is built" (a timing check) once in gpu mode. ## Not in this PR With the trap gone, G2's end view still never becomes exact. It settles on the reduced reader-halo frame, drawn whole in one long call, and that frame never counts as exact. I'll report that separately with the G2 measurements. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: albertcbrown
body:
Closes #219

The proposal's Delivery section now matches what's being deployed:

- Jenkins `ard-ci` builds every same-repository branch and PR, `worker/*` included, but never forks. That's the head-filter change in the deployment repository.
- `main` requires `continuous-integration/jenkins/pr-merge` as well as Actions `test`. Jenkins stops reporting to a PR it has seen close, so a PR that merged before `ard-ci` finished kept a `pending` status for good (#201, #202, #207). A fork PR gets no Jenkins build, so a maintainer pushes it to a same-repository branch to merge it.

The ruleset change itself is made on GitHub after `worker/*` PRs get a Jenkins status. `deploy/test-repo.sh` passes.

author: retrogamedeveloper
body:
gcc 2.7.2's expand_end_loop rolls a conditional exit at the top of a loop to the bottom; its scan stops at a CALL_INSN, a CODE_LABEL or a NOTE_INSN_BLOCK_BEG. m2c declares every local at the top of the function, so `for (;;) { if (done) break; ... }` is always rolled, where the game's code keeps the test at the loop label. The family moves the declaration of a plain local used only inside the loop to the top of the body (one child per local, at most 4). Measured on a table-search loop of a 392-instruction function: 4402 -> 3312 (each of its four loop-only locals gives it). The rule is read from stmt.c, not measured on other compilers. Tests: local moved, outside use / no top exit / volatile left alone. No version bump, no tag.

author: sky9662
body:
Phone screens leave limited room for thumb movement. Acceleration lets slow swipes remain precise while fast swipes move the pointer or turn the camera farther, reducing repeated thumb lifts.

This proposal could make PC games played with touch controls feel closer to native mobile games. It could also help mobile players adapt faster to BCD's virtual joystick and camera controls. The reference is the familiar default feel of the Steam Link app's touchpad mouse and touch camera controls in Call of Duty: Mobile.

This adds:

- Separate Trackpad acceleration and Mouse-look acceleration switches, both off by default.
- Trackpad acceleration on the Duo lower touchpad, plus a per-game acceleration option for Aim mode's mouse output.
- Faster swipes receive a larger movement multiplier, up to 2.5× the existing sensitivity. Hardware mouse movement and gamepad-stick output keep their existing behavior.

Testing: I built an unsigned IPA and tested the touch controls on my device. The acceleration works as expected.

Automated tests confirm that turning acceleration off preserves the original movement calculations. They also check that the same swipe speed produces the same gain at different touch-event rates, and that invalid input falls back to the normal 1× gain.

Screenshot: the Pointer settings show the two independent switches.

![Pointer settings showing Trackpad acceleration and Mouse-look acceleration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sky9662/bcd-games/0015e1eaa77c78b85f799dca24b30edf5d60e41b/docs/images/touch-acceleration-settings.jpg)

author: laurajoyhutchins
body: Source-derived mathematical experiment stacked on [PR #27](https://github.com/laurajoyhutchins/riemann-hypothesis-lean/pull/27), independent of the unchanged final RH statements. A new `core_ineq_bounded_tail` reuses the original local polynomial inequalities `T1` through `TU` in `SubThreeMulLogTwoLe.lean`, but takes a bounded rational tail `tail ≤ spread` instead of `log(1+X) * spread`. Its proposed conclusion improves the **sum-form window power** from `yD*yL*y^3*E` to `yD*yL*y^2*E` under the same coefficient and size constraints. The proof of the coefficient improvement is explicit; no claim is made about the separate max-form `CErr7` exponent or about final RH. This experiment temporarily copies the source's common finite inequalities to test the new tail; they should be factored after verification rather than maintained in duplicate. **Lean CI pending, do not claim the theorem checked yet.**

author: viviencabannes
body:
## Summary

Proves 4 wanted statements of the wiki's task list in one area, each moved out of `WantedExt` with its full name and statement unchanged, with its own tests and bookkeeping.

### Prove that positive solutions of D(C(n)) = C(D(n)) are odd

Proves `MetaMathlibExt.odd_of_arithmeticDerivative_collatz_comm`: every positive integer n with D(C(n)) = C(D(n)), where D is the arithmetic derivative and C the accelerated Collatz map, is odd. The theorem keeps its name, statement and docstring, including its citation of Bradshaw's article in the Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.1.8. It moves from `WantedExt/NumberTheory/CollatzArithmeticDerivativeWanted.lean` to `MathlibExt/NumberTheory/CollatzArithmeticDerivative.lean`, which already holds the accelerated Collatz map, sits in the same wiki folder and is publicly imported by the wanted module; the host now also publicly imports `MathlibExt.NumberTheory.ArithmeticDerivative`. The proof writes an even n as 2m and uses the Leibniz rule and D(2) = 1 to reduce the equation to D(m) = C(m + 2D(m)), which fails for both parities of m when m > 0. New tests in `MathlibExtTest/NumberTheory/CollatzArithmeticDerivative.lean` check that 71 · 1609 is an odd solution (both sides equal 840), that n = 0 solves the equation but is even, so the positivity hypothesis is needed, and that no positive even number is a solution; the provenance rows of both modules are re-recorded and no wiki or taxonomy file changes.

Task: wiki article `af_674a30a8af74dda57e1171ca` (Positive solutions of the Collatz arithmetic differential equation are odd), declaration `MetaMathlibExt.odd_of_arithmeticDerivative_collatz_comm`, ready to prove in the wiki's task list.

### Prove the layer-index identity for quasi-arithmetical compact sets

If n/ρ^p lies in layer v of a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module μ, the integer pμ − v depends only on the numerator n for that set, module, and ratio. The proof in MathlibExt.Topology.ArithmeticalSelfSimilarCompactSet uses Arias de Reyna’s layer-scaling argument to compare both fractions at a common denominator. The wanted module now imports this module, which also holds its previously completed definitions and theorems. Tests cover an invariant of −2, the isolated point of a singleton, and the gauge of the empty set.

Task: wiki article `af_f192ec29f67f1f736083ce00` (The layer index of a quasi-arithmetical compact set is well defined (Proposition 5)), declaration `MetaMathlibExt.isQuasiArithmeticalCompactSet_layer_index`, ready to prove in the wiki's task list.

### Prove the piecewise lower bound for integer complexity

Prove that every expression for a positive integer n using ones, addition and multiplication contains at least g(n) ones, following Juan Arias de Reyna’s Complexity of Natural Numbers. The theorem now lives beside its definitions in MathlibExt.NumberTheory.IntegerComplexityBounds and is available through the original wanted module’s public import. Tests establish the exact complexity of two and check the lower bound at the three interval endpoints 9, 12 and 18.

Task: wiki article `af_575a459c912218389d5e02fa` (The function $g$ bounds integer complexity from below), declaration `MathlibExt.NumberTheory.IntegerComplexityWanted.complexityLowerBoundG_le`, ready to prove in the wiki's task list.

### Prove the repeating-decimal ratio count

Prove the repeating-decimal ratio count attributed to Sela Fried in MathlibExt.Combinatorics.Enumerative.RepeatingDecimalRatio. Writing x = 10^n + t identifies the solutions with residues satisfying t(t + 1) = 0 modulo 10^n − 1. Each prime-power component has two roots, and the Chinese remainder theorem combines the choices independently. The wanted module re-exports the theorem under its original name. Tests identify the exact solution set for n = 1 and verify the count for n = 2.

Task: wiki article `af_127707d32f7ee163637bec3e` (Counting solutions of a repeating-decimal ratio equation), declaration `MetaMathlibExt.ncard_repeating_decimal_ratio_eq_two_pow_omega`, ready to prove in the wiki's task list.

author: lukerandall
body:
At origin/main bc4203d the repository has no ui/flare app and no comment routes or schema. The owner answered question 20261123T1700Z-cpui with option a, "Split it" (answer 20261123T1700Z-cpui). This change therefore builds only:

- ui/headless: the framework-free core, test-first. comments/thread.ts holds the thread types, which allow one level of replies, and `withPosted`. comments/composer.ts holds the composer store. comments/a11y.ts holds the words of mockup v1795398322-8ae4 and the keyboard rule.
- ui/react: `useComposer` and `useThread`, which turn the core's state into React props and render nothing.
- A pnpm workspace in ui/, a root .node-version, and one CI job, `ui`, that installs, lints, type-checks, runs knip and runs the tests of both packages.

A later change builds the comments section in ui/flare (src/comments/*.tsx and src/api/comments.ts) once the reading-view change has created ui/flare and feature 16 has added the comment routes and their schema to crates/flare-contract. This change adds no route, no server code and no ui/flare file.

Later slices after that, each its own change: the anchored comment card on highlighted text (Markdown only); re-anchoring and the outdated state; polling feature 17's cursor fetch; drafts kept across a reload, and editing or deleting one's own comment.

Module diagram (+ marks new):

```
ui/flare  (later change; imports both packages through the workspace)
        |
ui/react +      useComposer.ts, useThread.ts: state as React props
        |
ui/headless +   comments/thread.ts, composer.ts, a11y.ts; no DOM, fetch or React
```

The core does no input or output and takes a `send` function (BASE-7). The composer state is one discriminated union of idle, composing, sending, failed (with failure no-answer or refused) and sent (BASE-22). `send` resolves with a result union whose members are sent and refused, and rejects when the server gave no answer (BASE-23). Each draft gets an idempotency key at its first keystroke and keeps it through edits and retries until it is sent. headless/tsconfig.json has no DOM lib and no global types, so the core cannot reach the document, the window or fetch. Both packages are private at version 0.0.0 (answer 20261123T0142Z-b468) and adopt typescript-standards' base profile with the toolchain /evals/typescript-standards-baseline pinned.

## Why

A Flare deployment brings its own front end, so Flare ships each interactive part's state, logic and accessibility with no styling, and Flare's own UI is the first user (decision 20261123T0050Z-headless-ui-own-auth-and-fe). The owner chose a framework-free TypeScript core and a thin React binding in the flare repository (answer 20261123T0049Z-2d8b), and each feature ships its simplest useful version first (decision 20261123T0112Z-utility-order-and-iterate). The GitHub repository is crumbkit/flare, and the board mount keeps the path /repos/hangar.

## Out of scope

The comments section in ui/flare and its API module. The comment store and routes of feature 16. The reading view, livery, Mermaid and Shiki. Publishing to npm. Mentions and notifications.

## What the tests prove

- Each composer action moves the state as the failure table says, in Vitest under Node with no DOM.
- A retry reuses the draft's key, and a refusal offers no retry.
- A type test shows that a reply has no replies and cannot name a reply as its parent.
- The binding's props render each state of artboards 01 to 07 with the right roles, names, aria-disabled, aria-busy, aria-describedby and live-region text, found by role in jsdom.
- Tab visits the reply fields and buttons, then the page field and Comment, in artboard 07's order.

## What the tests do not prove

- How a screen reader speaks a sent reply; jsdom checks attributes only.
- That the key prevents a duplicate on the real server; feature 16's change tests that.
- That a front end without React can use the core; none exists yet.
- The styled page in light and dark, and axe on a real browser; the ui/flare change adds the Playwright journey.

- No test run is attached to this change.

## Dependencies and CI

- The packages add no runtime dependency. `@flare/react` names React 19.3.1 as a peer, which the importing app supplies. The development tools are the versions that typescript-standards' baseline pins and /evals/typescript-standards-baseline tested: TypeScript 7.0.2, Biome 2.6.3, knip 6.43.0, Vitest 5.0.5, jsdom 30.1.3 and Testing Library. None runs an install script, so `allowBuilds` stays empty.
- A new `ui` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml installs the workspace with `--frozen-lockfile`, then runs lint, typecheck, knip and test from ui/. It catches a broken core or binding, which the Rust jobs never build. It takes about a minute, within its ten-minute timeout.
- ui/typescript-standards.toml records two exceptions with corrections: no job runs `pnpm audit` yet (BASE-17), and .github/dependabot.yml does not yet move the npm pins (BASE-13).

## Evidence

- `/changes/flare-s-comment-parts-run-on-a-headless-typescript-core-with`: the change
- `/changes/flare-s-comment-parts-run-on-a-headless-typescript-core-with/plans/20261123T170019969135Z.md`: the plan
- `/projects/artifact-server/answers/20261123T0142Z-7143`: plans/answer/v1
- `/projects/artifact-server/answers/20261123T0142Z-b468`: plans/answer/v1
- `/projects/artifact-server/decisions/20261123T1120Z-comments-mockup-and-plan`: plans/decision/v1
- `/projects/artifact-server/answers/20261123T1700Z-cpui`: plans/answer/v1

author: nicoloboschi
body:
Refs #6792 (does not close it).

**What I found**
- Seen once, locally, on 23 Nov. Never in CI: the 5 failed `test-system` jobs since 10 Nov are all breakage on work-in-progress branches.
- No repro in ~900 searches of the exact scenario: alone, with 4 other banks being created, filled and deleted alongside, and with a second test run on the same database at the same time.
- The failing result (`[1..5]`, no Step 0) only fits one case: both meaning searches returned nothing, keyword search found Step 3, and its window grew to 1–5. If any meaning search returns a row, the whole document joins the candidates and Step 0 always comes back.
- Ruled out: the stub's vectors (deterministic), ingest returning before vectors are saved (it waits), the query embedding failing quietly (it raises), reranking or the budget dropping Step 0 (no such path), pgvector version (0.8.1).
- Likely trigger: the original run overlapped other agents' system-test runs on the shared pg0 instance, the same setup behind #6432. #6824 added a lock that now stops that. Not proven.

**This PR:** the story searches with `trace=True` and puts which searches found which passages, the scores and the budget steps into each assertion message. The next failure will show whether the meaning searches really came back empty.

author: janisfox
body:
Fixes the red CI on main after #108 and #109 merged.

## Cause
#109 added a roundtrip check that no generic `for` falls back to a pass-through call, detected by the substring `(function(...)`. #108 added `tests/multiple_values.nyk`, which decompiles to legitimate inline vararg functions (e.g. `two(...)` becomes `(function(...) ... end)(1, 2)`). Each PR passed on its own, but together the check fails on all three platforms.

## Fix
- Replace the `PASS_THROUGH` substring with `has_pass_through`, which matches only the fallback's exact shape: a vararg function whose body is just `return ...`.
- Add `test_has_pass_through_sees_the_fallback`, which prints the exact expression `lift.rs` builds at several indent depths, so the check can't quietly stop detecting real regressions.

No decompiler behaviour changes.

## Checks
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`: all pass locally.

body:
## Stack (1/4)
1. **This PR**: Binary `LKW1` guest wire protocol, dead bindgen metadata stripping, deferred region evaluation, and compact Tailwind parsing/flags
2. `refactor/perf-element-and-layout` (stacked on this PR)
3. `refactor/perf-wasm-host-and-measurement` (stacked on #2)
4. `refactor/perf-web-and-delivery` (stacked on #3)

## Summary
- **Binary guest→host wire protocol (`LKW1`)**: Replaced per-node JSON + `#[serde(flatten)]` + `Vec<u8>` allocations with direct binary encoding into a reused `wire_arena` (zero `NativeProps::clone()`), while retaining single-pass `FlatWireNode` JSON decoding for legacy/JS/raw guests.
- **Native guest `.wasm` size (-45% to -52% raw, -29% to -35% brotli)**: Added `strip_guest_metadata` before `wasm-opt -Oz` in `leptoskit_cli::wasm::optimize_guest` to strip dead `__wasm_bindgen_unstable`, `name`, and `producers` custom sections and unreachable `__wbindgen_*` / `__wbg_*` browser glue exports.

author: extimsu
body:
## What

This adds an official Helm chart in `charts/urlchecker`, published to `oci://ghcr.io/extimsu/charts/urlchecker`. It has two modes:

- **`Deployment`** (the default) checks endpoints from the pod network.
- **`DaemonSet`** runs one pod per node, usually with `hostNetwork: true`, to measure packet loss between nodes.

### Best practices applied

- **Secure by default.**
  - The container runs as UID 65532 with every capability dropped, a read-only root filesystem, seccomp `RuntimeDefault` and no ServiceAccount token.
  - ICMP on the pod network uses the safe sysctl `net.ipv4.ping_group_range`, scoped to the pod's own group. The Deployment therefore passes the `restricted` Pod Security Standard, and CI checks that.
  - `icmp.rawSocket` switches to UID 0 with only `NET_RAW`. That's only for `hostNetwork`, where pod sysctls can't reach the node's network namespace.
- **Validation.**
  - `values.schema.json` checks the workload kind, target syntax, durations and ports.
  - The templates fail early on settings that can't work: no targets, a ServiceMonitor without a Service, or `icmp://` targets on the host network without `rawSocket`.
- **Standard structure.**
  - Recommended `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels and `fullnameOverride`/`nameOverride`.
  - Image `registry`/`repository`/`tag`/`digest`, with the tag defaulting to `appVersion`.
  - A checksum annotation restarts the pods when the targets change.
  - Optional ServiceMonitor and PodDisruptionBudget, scheduling knobs, `extraArgs`/`extraEnv`/`extraVolumes`, and `NOTES.txt`.
- **Tests.**
  - A `helm unittest` suite with 12 tests.
  - A `helm test` pod that reads `/metrics`.
  - `ci/*-values.yaml` for install tests.
