author: yansfil
body:
Related: mission-75 (Hide-to-Hide connection over iroh), PRD device-connect-iroh D-74, B10, B20; follows #2892.

## Summary

### Problem

On candidate 5 the operator showed the Mac mini's screen in this Mac's window and closed a terminal this Mac had started there.
After the confirm, the page jumped to the Overview and the terminal stayed open: the Mac mini refused the close (`event.refused guest_pane_close not_here client Remote`, five times in its log).
The close was allowed only from the Mac mini's own window, and the page moved away without hearing the answer.
The same evening, Settings opened over the Windows PC's screen still read `이 Mac 설정`.
Both were reproduced on two isolated candidate-5 apps.
The second came from the gear at the foot of the rail: it belongs to this Mac's window, stays beside the other computer's screen, and opened this Mac's own Settings, while ⌘, already opened the shown computer's.

### Before → After

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What the user gets | Close from another computer's screen is refused; the page jumps to the Overview | The terminal closes after the confirm; the page shows the next tab of that work, else its project |
| Screen | ![Before: after the close, the Overview, 일 1 still listed](https://github.com/yansfil/pr-assets/blob/main/hide/m75-remote-screen-fixes/0d8aae8/pr-before-c1.png?raw=true) | ![After: the next tab of that work](https://github.com/yansfil/pr-assets/blob/main/hide/m75-remote-screen-fixes/0d8aae8/new-c1-3-after.png?raw=true) |
| What the user gets | The rail's gear over the Mac mini's screen opens `이 Mac 설정` | It opens `Mac mini 설정` on that screen, as ⌘, does |
| Screen | ![Before: this Mac's Settings](https://github.com/yansfil/pr-assets/blob/main/hide/m75-remote-screen-fixes/0d8aae8/rc5-c2-rail-gear-opens-this-mac.png?raw=true) | ![After: the Mac mini's Settings](https://github.com/yansfil/pr-assets/blob/main/hide/m75-remote-screen-fixes/0d8aae8/new-c2-1-rail-gear.png?raw=true) |
| Flow | Show Mac mini → open its terminal → 닫기… → 닫기 → **Overview, terminal still open** | Show Mac mini → open its terminal → 닫기… → 닫기 → **next tab (or its project), terminal closed** |

Look at the center of each capture; the real computer's name in the first Before is masked.

- **Why the access class changes:** `guest_pane_close` moves from `OwnWindow` to `Window`, so the screen another machine shows of this one may send it.
  That screen is drawn only for a machine holding an open grant to this one, and it can already type into the same terminal, so closing gives it nothing new (operator decision on this node).
  The other D-74 items are unchanged: split, new tab, rename and start agent stay dimmed with `<machine>에서 할 수 있어요`, and pairing, sharing, phones and external tools stay refused to a remote screen (`a_remote_screen_works_but_lets_nothing_in`).
- **A close counts only once it reached the computer's node**: when that node is not connected or the write to it fails, the daemon answers `node_unavailable` instead of `ok`, because the terminal still runs.
- **A close that did not go** keeps the page and says why in one corner line (`닫지 못했어요. 이 터미널은 이제 여기 없어요`, `… 연결이 끊겼어요. 다시 해 보세요`, `… 이 컴퓨터의 Hide는 여기서 닫을 수 없어요` for an older build, else `이 터미널을 닫지 못했어요. 다시 해 보세요`).
- **The name a remote screen is told** is now kept by its preload from the start, so a page that listens after it was told still names the machine (Settings title and machine group, the screen's own title, its language).

## Decide

- With another computer's screen in front, the rail's gear now opens that computer's Settings, as ⌘, does; this Mac's own Settings open once its own tile is in front again. Is that the gear you expect, or should the rail's gear always stay this Mac's?
- Failure copy: the four one-line reasons above.

## Hard to undo

- `guest_pane_close` changes shape on the wire (`{request_id, call: {pane_id}}`, answered by a new `guest_pane_close_result` frame). A page loaded before its machine updated stays open in a window and still sends `{pane_id}` alone; the daemon keeps closing that form and answers it as before (nothing on a close, an error frame on a refusal), so an old page's close still ends the pane.

## Not verified

- A refused or failed close was not produced live: it needs a pane that leaves the list between the confirm and the answer, or an older build that still connects. It is held by the window tests and by the daemon test's `pane_unavailable` answer.
- Windows and Linux were not run live; the change has no platform-specific part (one access class, one page action, one preload).
- Locally, 11 hided tests failed for this Mac's state (a `tailscale status` that timed out, start waits under the full suite's load), none in the code this changes; CI runs them clean.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **Verified**: two isolated candidate apps on this Mac (own HOME, state folder and desktop profile each; only their own windows captured), paired as MacBook Pro (A) and Mac mini (B), A starting three terminals in B's project.
  - Candidate 5 (1.2.11-main.2688ce27): from B's screen in A, 닫기 → the page went to the Overview, the three terminals stayed, and B logged `event.refused guest_pane_close not_here client Remote`. The rail's gear opened `이 Mac 설정`; ⌘, and the screen's own gear opened B's Settings by its name.
  - This head (1.2.11-main.0d8aae85), both apps: closing `일 1` showed `일 2`; closing the last tab showed the one before it; closing the only tab left showed B's `hide / main` Workspace; B's list went 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 and no refusal was logged. With B's screen in front the rail's gear, ⌘, and the screen's gear each opened `Mac mini 설정` with the machine group `Mac mini`, and the screen's title read `Mac mini`; with A's own tile in front the gear opened `이 Mac 설정`.
  - A computer's screen after that computer updates: B updated first while A kept B's page loaded; A's tile then said `이 컴퓨터 업데이트 필요` and the screen stayed aside (the old page kept in memory). Once A updated too, B's screen showed B's new page (`main-O2cyZVvY.js` in place of `main-CW25Gi5p.js`), and A's work on B survived B's update. A page already loaded is never reloaded in place; a new one is read each time the view is made.

![After: closing the only tab left shows the project it stood in](https://github.com/yansfil/pr-assets/blob/main/hide/m75-remote-screen-fixes/0d8aae8/new-c1-5-after.png?raw=true)

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- **Layer**: unit for the access class (`event_class.rs`) and the page (`web/src/guestClose.test.ts`, `desktop/src/preload/remote.test.ts`); integration for the daemon's answer (`hided/tests/it/pairing/guest_work.rs`, two real daemons).
- **Catches**: a remote screen refused the close again (`a_remote_screen_works_but_lets_nothing_in`); a close claimed for a node that never heard it, after the node's end of the connection went and after the node ended (`guests::tap` test); an earlier page's `{pane_id}` close no longer read (`a_guest_pane_close_is_answered_in_the_shape_it_was_asked`, and the earlier form in `pairing::guest_work`); the page moving before the answer, to the Overview, or away after a failure (`guestClose.test.ts`, six cases, `node_unavailable` among the failures); the rail's gear opening this window's Settings over a computer's screen; a viewer told before the page listens being lost: the preload test fails on the previous preload, run before the change.
- **Repeat**: not run in the repeat lane yet.
- **Waits**: none new; the daemon test reads the answer frame with the suite's existing frame wait.

</details>

<details><summary>Risky files</summary>

- `hided/src/server/event_class.rs` - security: who may send which event; one kind moves from `OwnWindow` to `Window`.
- `hided/src/server.rs` - failure path: the close now answers the window instead of an error frame, and still takes the earlier `{pane_id}` form from a page loaded before an update.
- `hided/src/guests/tap.rs` - fail

author: a-kbv
body:
## What

A terminal on the phone had no way to copy a part of what it shows — only **More → Copy what is on the screen** or **Copy the last 200 lines**. xterm selects with a mouse only, the page is `user-select: none`, and every touch on the terminal is already a scroll, a zoom or a tap.

Now text is selected with a finger, the way the phone itself does it:

- **A finger held still** (450 ms) selects the word under it, with a short buzz. A word is a run of cells with something in them, so a path or an address is taken whole.
- **Dragged on without lifting**, the selection grows from that word, in either direction and across lines. Near an edge of the view the terminal scrolls under the finger (the view first, then xterm's history).
- **Lifted**, the selection stays: a handle under each end to move it, and a bar over the terminal — **Copy**, **Whole lines**, cancel.
- While a selection is shown a drag scrolls as before and a pinch zooms; **a tap beside it puts it away** (and does not bring the keyboard up).
- Copy goes through the same `copyText` as the menu's two entries, so the "copy by hand" sheet is still the fallback where the WebView refuses the clipboard.

## How

- The selection is xterm's own (`term.select`, `term.getSelection`), set from the touch handlers that were already there; the colour was in the theme (`--term-selection`). No native code, the same on Android and iOS.
- `mobile/src/select.js` holds the arithmetic — the cell under a point, the word, growing it, a handle past the other end, whole lines, the length xterm is given, where a handle is drawn. `terminal.js` calls it with the view as it is.
- What a browser makes of a touch for a mouse (`mousedown`, the `contextmenu` of a long press) no longer reaches xterm within a second of a touch: it would start a selection of its own or move its textarea under the finger. A real mouse in the browser preview is untouched.
- The handles are kept inside the terminal's box and `.term-pan` clips (`overflow: clip`): a handle at the first or last column would otherwise be cut off, or widen what the view scrolls over.
- A resize of the terminal, a reset of the link and xterm dropping the selection itself (another screen buffer) all end the selection.

## Verified

- **On an Android phone**, with the debug APK of this branch's CI: selecting and Copy work. (That build is `3b4e6ac`, before the last commit, which moves the arithmetic into `select.js` without changing what it does.)
- **In the browser preview** against `scripts/mobile-rig.js`, with synthetic touch events, before and after that last commit: a long press takes the word; a drag forwards over three lines and backwards over two copies exactly that text; a handle moved along a line; Whole lines; a tap cancels; a plain drag still scrolls and starts no selection; the view's scroll width is the same with and without a selection.
- `npm run test:mobile-select` (new, in CI with the other phone tests): a scrolled view and the history, cells of a fraction of a pixel, wide characters, blank cells and line ends, selections across lines in both directions, the length checked against a model of how xterm counts it, handles that never leave the box.
- `test:mobile-i18n` and `test:mobile-text` pass; both languages have the two new strings.

## Not verified

- **No iPhone.** Nothing here is platform code, but a long press in WKWebView was never tried; `-webkit-touch-callout: none` and `user-select: none` are already on the page.
- The scroll at an edge while selecting is not in the synthetic run, and was not checked on its own on the phone.
- A program in the alternate screen (Claude Code, Codex) redraws its screen: the selection keeps its cells, not its text. At an edge such a screen does not scroll while selecting — only xterm's own history does.
- No magnifier over the finger: at the whole-width zoom the text under it is hard to see; the handles and a pinch are the way to be exact.

author: abdumannopp
body:
## Summary
- **Migration 0014** adds two columns to `tenants`: `retention_settings` and `retention_last_run`. It is reversible.
- `lib/retention.js` defines the categories and their minimum days. Everything is off (kept for ever) until a company administrator sets a number of days:
  - positions of finished loads: at least 30 days;
  - messages of finished loads: at least 30 days;
  - files of finished loads: at least 90 days;
  - done NEXUS tasks: at least 30 days;
  - activity log: at least 365 days.
- What a run removes: the detail above, older than the days. Positions, messages and files go only for loads that are Delivered or Cancelled, so an open load keeps everything. Files in Cloudflare R2 are deleted too.
- What is never removed: loads, money, status history, legs and trips. Dismissed NEXUS tasks are also kept, so their warning does not come back.
- API (administrators only, `settings:write`):
  - `GET /api/settings/retention` returns the settings plus a preview of what a run would remove now.
  - `PUT /api/settings/retention` saves the settings. Saving never removes anything.
  - `POST /api/settings/retention/run` requires `{ "confirm": true }`. Every run is written to the activity log.
- An optional daily run is part of the NEXUS sweep, once a day per company, and is also logged.
- A "Keeping old data" panel in Team & settings shows a live preview per category, a Save button, and a "Remove now" button that asks for confirmation first.
- Docs updated: API_V2, DEPLOYMENT (including the reminder to keep backups) and the roadmap (6.2 done).

## Tests
- New `test/retention.test.js` covers:
  - the rules and minimum days;
  - that an operator is refused and another company has its own settings;
  - that saving removes nothing and the preview is correct;
  - that a run needs `confirm`, removes only old detail of finished loads, leaves open loads and the loads themselves, and is logged;
  - the daily run happening once a day.
- `migrations.test.js` updated for 0014.
- SQLite: 265 pass, 9 skipped. PostgreSQL: every test file passes.
- Checked in a browser: a value below the minimum is refused, a valid value saves with the message "Nothing was removed", and the preview shows.

author: ajccarlson
body:
A package install that hangs now ends at its own step's limit instead of holding its job until the job's limit.

apt has hung on a package mirror that stopped answering. In one merge-queue run, the browser job's `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` printed its last index fetch and then nothing for 39 minutes, until the job's 40-minute limit cancelled it. apt's own download timeouts do not bound such a hang: the hosted image already sets them stricter than apt's defaults (one retry, 15 seconds), and the hang happened anyway, inside apt's download queue.

- The browser install step has a limit of 15 minutes. A slow install takes a few minutes.
- The step that waits for the background ffmpeg install has a limit of 20 minutes. Without it, a hung background install held the Ubuntu compatibility job until its 85-minute limit.
- The workflow policy pins both limits, and a test checks that each is at most half its job's.

A hung install still fails its job, but now within minutes of the hang rather than at the job's limit.

author: jezoock
body:
## Où j'en suis

**Fait**
- Lecture des contributions `pages` par le cœur (`src/main/plugins/pages.ts`, `pageDefinitions()` du service, `pages.setBuiltin` du moteur des pages). Le cœur n'a plus aucune page intégrée (`builtin.ts` supprimé).
- Sept plugins inclus de données `plugins/mire.page.{movies,series,music,images,streaming,tv,games}/` (page, `i18n/fr` + `en`).
- Règles de continuité `P5-03-*` (mode `bundled`) + test ; fixtures `config-v*.migrated.json` mises à jour (avec P5-20).
- Tests `node:test` (lecture, données invalides ignorées, plugin désactivé, pages de l'utilisateur inchangées, continuité, plugins inclus lus par le cœur) ; test de fumée : les sept plugins sont actifs et leurs pages sont celles du cœur.
- Inventaire, `docs/architecture.md`, `BACKLOG.md` (P5-03 « faite »).
- Plugins vérifiés dans un clone de mire-addons (`npm run validate` 11/11, `npm test` 97/97, `npm run index:test`) et publiés par **jezoock/mire-addons#5** (fusionnée).
- `addons/` retiré ; `main` fusionné (P5-20 comprise, règles de continuité des deux gardées) ; lint, format, types et `npm test` (1730) passent en local ; test de fumée complet passé avant la fusion (93/93, ~121 s).

**Reste à faire**
- CI verte puis fusion.

## Ce qui a été fait

Une page prête à l'emploi devient un plugin de données (un par page, comme l'inventaire). Le cœur lit les contributions `pages` des plugins actifs : une page de plugin actif apparaît comme une page du cœur ; désactivé, elle disparaît (menu, Accueil, événement `pages:changed`). `pages.json` de l'utilisateur ne change pas : copies modifiées gardées, suppressions retenues (même plugin désactivé puis réactivé). Les identifiants de page (`movies`, `series`…) sont inchangés ; les clés `pages.*` du cœur restent pour les copies modifiées.

## Plugins (pour mire-addons)

Source dans `plugins/<id>/` (manifeste, `i18n/{fr,en}.json`, `pages/<page>.json`) ; publiés par jezoock/mire-addons#5.

| Plugin | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `mire.page.movies` | `movies` |
| `mire.page.series` | `series` |
| `mire.page.music` | `music` |
| `mire.page.images` | `images` |
| `mire.page.streaming` | `streaming` |
| `mire.page.tv` | `tv` |
| `mire.page.games` | `games` |

Tous : version `1.0.0`, niveau `data`, aucune permission, `engines.mire ^1.0.0`.

## Sécurité
- Niveau le plus bas (données), aucune permission, aucun code.
- Définition vérifiée par `validatePage` (champs connus, tailles bornées, valeurs permises) ; identifiant égal à celui de la contribution ; nom uniquement en clé de texte du plugin (nom en clair ou clé mal formée refusés) ; aucun texte interprété comme du HTML. Doublon d'identifiant : le premier plugin l'emporte. Aucune nouvelle méthode IPC.

## À vérifier à la main
- Menu et Accueil après désactivation/réactivation d'un plugin de page dans les Réglages.

## Ordre de fusion
1. jezoock/mire-addons#5 (déjà fusionnée) ; 2. cette PR.

## Mesures
`npm run test:e2e` : ~121 s après la PR (93 tests OK, seuil 3 min ; avant : non mesuré). Captures : aucune versionnée (remises comme sur `main`, elles ne variaient qu'avec l'environnement).

author: thewisp
body:
A recording shows where the robot moved, but replaying those same joint positions does not account for an object that has moved. FLASH needs to express selected demonstration frames relative to that object, turn them into robot commands, and save what was commanded during the run.

**FLASH stack: 3 of 5. Review base: [#281](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/281). Next: [#283](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/283).**

`main` (includes [#280](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/280)) → [#281 tracking](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/281) → **[#282 execution](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/282) (this PR)** → [#283 GUI](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/283) → [#284 research tools](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/284)

#280 is merged. #281 is next against `main`; #282–#284 depend on the preceding PR. The remaining PRs are drafts. Review and land them in order, restacking after each merge.

### What this adds

| When you… | This PR supplies… |
| --- | --- |
| Prepare a recorded demonstration | Saved keyframes tied to the selected object or to the world, with the recorded gripper actions |
| Execute the prepared demonstration | Return to the saved rest position, plan from measured joints within motor-calibration bounds, update commands still waiting to be sent, and stop execution when cancelled |
| Inspect the result | A saved rollout with robot observations and issued commands; local recordings open without downloading missing files from the Hub |

This is the execution backend. The **Demo editor**, **Apply to robot** and **Stop** controls are introduced by [#283](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/283). Both the older skill/Run path and the newer demonstration executor are included here.

Offline reset, cancellation, command-update and recording/reopen checks pass. The recording-rate defect [#277](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/issues/277) and recovery/experimental-fitting failures remain; this is draft and has not demonstrated a successful physical task.

### Appendix: from demonstration to saved rollout

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D["Recorded demonstration"] --> P["Select keyframes and object references — new"]
  L["Live object tracking from #281"] --> P
  P --> K["Plan using robot calibration — new"]
  K --> Q["Commands waiting to be sent — new"]
  Q --> R["Robot"]
  R --> S["Save observations and issued commands — new"]
```

### Appendix: proof and guardrails

These observations come from offline regression runs with synthetic recordings and simulated or stand-in robots. They do not measure physical movement.

| Input / action | Observed result | Guardrail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start from joints away from the saved rest position | Reset finishes before demonstration planning, and planning starts from the measured readback | [test_demo_execution.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_demo_execution.py) |
| Stop during reset, fail a motor read/write, or supply an invalid rest position | No demonstration commands are dispatched; the run records `stopped` or `failed` | [test_demo_execution.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_demo_execution.py) |
| Give either FLASH reset caller an unknown joint or an unreadable saved joint | Validation fails before any rest waypoint; ordinary robot reset behavior stays in the shared helper | [test_demo_rest.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_demo_rest.py) |
| Rebuild a hardware planner with a constrained wrist | Missing controlled-joint bounds are rejected; the reconstructed solver honors the supplied bounds | [test_flash_kinematics.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_flash_kinematics.py) |
| Move the tracked reference after part of the command sequence has been sent | Pending commands change; the already-issued command index stays unchanged | [test_demo_execution.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_demo_execution.py) |
| Record RGB values `30, 60, 90` and depth values `400, 500, 600` mm, then reopen locally | Pixels match the ordinary reader; the stored RGB mean is `60/255`, and the depth mean is `500` mm | [test_local_dataset.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_local_dataset.py) |
| Open a recording with missing metadata, data or video | A local file error is raised; the checks prohibit Hub access | [test_local_dataset.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_local_dataset.py) |

[test_dataset_export.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_dataset_export.py) also records through the rollout writer and reopens every depth pixel unchanged after the FLASH-only Parquet workaround. [test_flash_core.py](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/blob/24a532dd36fa022ba3071e441c451f5edc42dfbe/tests/policies/flash/test_flash_core.py) covers the older skill execution path. Commit/push hooks passed.

### Appendix: scope and known limits

The GitHub Fork Tests job inherits the missing RealSense test dependency described in [#280](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/280). Passing local checks do not establish green CI.

The local reader and its replacement TODO stay inside FLASH. The shared dataset constructor, metadata loader and statistics parser match `main`; the closed [#278](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/278) is not required. The Parquet helper/TODO arrive with [#281](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/pull/281), and this PR adds the recording caller and regression together.

The recording-rate bug is still present: a path that plans at 30 Hz loses the source recording rate. In the reproduced 10 fps case, a recorded 0.2-second interval becomes about 0.067 seconds. The passing timing test bypasses the editor conversion where that rate is lost, so it does not cover [#277](https://github.com/TheWisp/lerobot/issues/277).

Failures also remain in `test_native_acceleration_candidates.py`, `test_recorded_recovery_integration.py`, `test_recovery_acceptance_integration.py`, `test_combined_recovery.py`, `test_visible_surface_matcher.py` and `test_velocity_filter.py`. They need resolution before this execution layer is ready to land. Completing a command queue does not establish tool-position accuracy or manipulation success; no physical robot/camera run was performed for this split.

body:
**Problem:** a format the model doesn't offer is silently dropped when the model lists no formats (GW-414). `options.format: "webm"` on Seedance or Wan video gets 202 and an mp4; the ByteDance and Alibaba video adapters never look at the field. Kling, MiniMax and Agnes reject it, but only as "media options are not supported" with param null.

**Why it matters:** the docs say unsupported controls "are rejected, not silently discarded". The caller pays for a generation and gets a different format with no warning. Admission already rejects quality, background, image size and video ratio when the model lists no choices; format was the one control without that rule.

**Fix:** one line in `normalizeModelOptions`: a non-empty format must be one the model lists. The error is 400 with param `options.format` (or `output_format` / `response_format` on the OpenAI routes) and "is not supported by this model; omit it". Models that list formats behave as before.

**What changes for callers:** video `options.format` on Seedance and Alibaba Wan/HappyHorse, and image `output_format` on image models without a format list, now get 400 instead of 202. Speech is unchanged: every speech/music model either lists its formats (OpenAI, Alibaba Qwen/CosyVoice, Sonilo, mock) or already rejected the field (Kling TTS/audio, Sonilo ducking). A model with one fixed output format could advertise it later so that value is accepted again.

**Tests:** new `TestFormatWithoutAdvertisedFormatsIsRejected` for video, image, speech and music (fails on main with `video accepted an unadvertised format: <nil>`, passes here). `./internal/core`, `./internal/templates` and all `./plugins/provider/...` pass with `-race`; gofmt, go vet, `git diff --check` clean. `./internal/providers` and `./internal/worker` not run.

author: sky9662
body:
Game: [Turing Complete — Steam App ID 1444480](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1444480/Turing_Complete/)

Turing Complete hit a `NoExec` failure even though Wine's `VirtualQuery` reported the target mapping as committed and executable. In the captured failing case, that mapping was missing from FEX's executable-range tracker.

This proposal pairs an iOS ARM64EC executable-page recheck with a recommended preset for this game. On a tracker miss, the recheck records only the requested 4 KiB guest page after confirming that it is committed, executable, unguarded `MEM_MAPPED` memory.

Tested configuration:

```ini
env.MADEIRA_EC_HOOK_TRACE = 0
env.MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE = 4.1
env.MESA_GLSL_VERSION_OVERRIDE = 410
env.FEX_SMCCHECKS = full
env.MADEIRA_FEX_EXEC_RECHECK = 1
env.MADEIRA_X64_IMAGE_NOCOPY = 1
gl-backend = zink
```

The preset uses BCD's existing recommendation flow so new or untouched Steam entries receive the tested setup automatically. Existing customized configurations retain the normal Reset to Recommended workflow.

The recheck remains disabled globally and is enabled by this game's preset. Recommendation validation accepts the tested environment keys and OpenGL/GLSL values.

Testing: I built an unsigned IPA with the engine fix and tested it on my device using the configuration above. Turing Complete now runs. Both FEX DLL variants were rebuilt and the source check passes. I have not tested the individual settings separately. The new recommendation tests pass for the complete preset, App ID matching, build filtering and allowed/invalid values.

Release note: `minBuild: 713` is proposed as the first build after 0.1.712. Please align it with the actual first release containing the fix and policy changes, and re-sign the recommendation list through the existing publishing process.

author: edgarmesquita
body:
Closes #1544

## What

A component whose `Build` returns itself, or a box around itself, is contained by its error boundary when
a `MarkupHost` draws it, as it already was without one. It used to take the server's process down with a
stack overflow, and the server draws every write-once page through such a host. The browser, which lowers
the same frame since #1501, hung in a loop and froze the tab.

- The web's `ElementFrame` and its browser twin (`element-frame.ts`) index a component's position by its
  instance and by the component position whose build it stands in, and find a component inside the
  position whose build is being lowered.
- `WebLoweringVisitor` and `lowering.ts` enter a position for what it built: through a component's own
  lowering, a stack's child (which a stack reads through to what its component built), and, in the
  browser, a record lowered again (#1455).

Nothing changes for a developer except that a component that never stops building now costs its own
subtree on every target, as one that throws does. No public surface moves.

## Why

The owner was never the problem: it builds each position through the boundary at the depth the tree
reads, and contains the chain at the bound. The lowering was. It found a component by its instance alone,
and an instance that builds itself holds every position of the chain, so each lookup answered the
outermost one again, whose build is the same instance again.

Photon's layout already walks positions (it carries the element it measures down to the child) and never
had the defect: `Native.Engine.Tests/ComponentBoundaryTests` lay out such a component through an owner,
unchanged. Flutter never finds an element by the configuration it was built from either.

The issue suggested counting the lowering's walk with the boundary's counter. That would still read the
outermost position at every step, contain the chain a second time and report it twice; the lowering now
follows the tree, and the guard stays the boundary's alone.

## OpenSpec

author: rhaist
body:
Three additions on how language models handle pictures, sound and video, and on how benchmark answers are marked.

## What is new

**Tokens chapter: "Pictures and sound become pieces too"**
- How a photo or a recording gets into a language model: cut into pieces, each placed on the same map as text.
- Two consequences for readers: images use tokens, and a model that describes a picture fluently can still get simple visual facts wrong. Two current sources: Stanford's 2026 AI Index on reading analogue clocks (best model 50.6% in March 2026, people about 90%), and an ICLR 2026 paper on counting in pictures of familiar things with one detail changed (17%).
- The security note now says that text inside an image is read too, with a 2025 case where the instructions were invisible at full size.
- One paragraph for engineers (patches, paired image and text training, spectrograms), a fourth takeaway, and a glossary entry for "multimodal".

**Generating chapter: "Pictures, video and voice are made differently"**
- The two ways a chat app makes a picture: diffusion (start from noise, remove it step by step), and generation inside the chat model itself, with OpenAI's March 2025 switch as the dated example.
- What carries over from text: it is generated and not looked up, asking again gives a different result, and looking right is not being right. For the last point, the 2026 AI Index on where video models still fail.
- Sora as the video example: a diffusion model on space-time patches by OpenAI's own 2024 technical report, and discontinued by OpenAI in 2026 (app in April, developer interface in September). No reason is given, because OpenAI's notice gives none.
- One sentence on spoken answers, a paragraph for engineers, a fourth takeaway and a glossary entry for "diffusion".
- The tokens chapter links here.

**Judging claims: "Who marks the answers?"**
- Some scores are assigned by another model. A 2023 study found such markers agree with people about as often as people agree with each other, and lean towards answers by position, length and their own style.
- Until now only the engineers' box mentioned this.

**Reading list**
- Stanford's CME 295 course, as the pick for readers who want the maths. Linked to the course home page, because the syllabus address changes each term.

## Sources

Eight new claims, each with an excerpt from the source. The point that seeing is not measuring rests on Stanford's AI Index (independent, data from March 2026) and a peer-reviewed paper (ICLR 2026). Vision Transformer, CLIP and the two diffusion papers join the canon list. The guide does not say how OpenAI's image model works internally: OpenAI's page states only that it is built into the chat model.

## Left for the monthly update

A preprint from October 2026 reports the same gap for the newest models (best of 25 at 53.6%, people at 93.1%). It is not peer reviewed yet, so it is a lead and not a source.

author: gregunik
body:
## Problem

On 23 Nov 2026, 5 of the 17 Pages runs failed in "Deploy to GitHub Pages" with `No artifacts named "github-pages" were found for this workflow run`. The re-run of one of them failed with `Multiple artifacts named "github-pages" ... Artifact count is 2`. Each failure left the newest report 404 until a later deploy went through. Toks needed two fresh dispatches. Before that day, 0 of 55 runs (2 Sep–20 Nov) had failed. The action SHAs and the artifact size (35–38 MB) were the same.

## Cause

`actions/deploy-pages@v5` looks the artifact up **once, with no retry**: one `listArtifacts()` call, filtered to name `github-pages`, and it throws unless exactly one match comes back (`src/internal/api-client.js` at the pinned SHA `368f825`). In our single-job workflow that call ran 0.4–0.8 s after `upload-pages-artifact` finished. Sometimes the artifact list did not show the new artifact yet:

| Run | Trigger | Upload finished (artifact ID, size) | Lookup | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [45198742929](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45198742929) | push, rentalready | 14:52:13.13 (14831250061, 36.8 MB) | 14:52:13.62 | Found 0 |
| [45208739410](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45208739410) | push, vertbaudet | 15:45:53.76 (14833993848, 37.7 MB) | 15:45:54.51 | Found 0 |
| [45211397854](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45211397854) | push, true-born | 16:00:11.77 (14836966207, 38.1 MB) | 16:00:12.57 | Found 0 |
| [45213746138](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45213746138) attempt 1 | push, toks | 16:12:32.91 (14837765853, 38.4 MB) | 16:12:33.71 | Found 0 |
| 45213746138 attempt 2 | re-run failed jobs | 16:23:34.62 (14837607552, 38.4 MB) | 16:23:35.38 | **Found 2**, so "count is 2" |
| [45217845956](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45217845956) | dispatch | 16:34:02.57 (14838463430, 38.4 MB) | 16:34:03.08 | Found 0 |
| [45219912518](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45219912518) (success) | dispatch | 16:45:09.11 | 16:45:09.54 | Found 1 |

The gap was the same in passing and failing runs, so nothing in our workflow got slower. The upload itself always succeeded: attempt 2 of the Toks run listed attempt 1's artifact (that's the second of the two). It just wasn't listed yet 0.8 s after upload. Why the list lagged on 23 Nov is on GitHub's side. Our workflow had no tolerance for it.

The "count is 2" failure comes from the single job. "Re-run failed jobs" re-ran upload + deploy together, so a second `github-pages` artifact landed in the same run next to the first, and deploy-pages refuses more than one.

**What the artifact contains** (checked in the upload log): `upload-pages-artifact` runs `tar … --exclude=.git --exclude=.github .`, so `.git` (272 MB locally) and `.github` don't ship. It ships the 166 `<slug>/index.html` files plus `.nojekyll`: 218 MB raw, 38.4 MB uploaded. Nothing to trim, and size isn't the cause.

## Fix

`pages.yml` now has two jobs:

- **build**: checkout, configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact (same inputs, `include-hidden-files: true` kept, so `.nojekyll` still ships).
- **deploy** (`needs: build`, `environment: github-pages`): deploy-pages runs on a fresh runner, well after the upload has finished. If it fails, it waits 30 s and tries once more. The environment URL comes from whichever attempt succeeded.

With the split, "Re-run failed jobs" re-runs only the deploy job, against the build job's one artifact. Avoid "Re-run all jobs": that uploads a second artifact again. With the in-job retry, a re-run should rarely be needed.

Triggers, permissions and the `pages` concurrency group are unchanged.

## Verification

- [x] First dispatch of this branch: [run 45222724011](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45222724011). The **build** job passed. The **deploy** job was refused because the `github-pages` environment only allows `main`, `gh-pages` and `None`.
- [x] **Full deploy from the branch: [run 45228213115](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45228213115), green.** The branch was first rebased on `main` (`3151a1b report(siva)`), after the last report of the afternoon was live. With Greg's go, the branch was allowed in the `github-pages` environment for this one run, and the rule was removed as soon as the run finished. The environment is back to `None`, `gh-pages`, `main`.
  - build: upload finished 17:29:53.84 (artifact 14845077619, 39.4 MB).
  - deploy: started on its own runner. The artifact lookup ran at 17:30:04.56, **10.7 s after the upload** (it was 0.4–0.8 s before), and returned `Found 1 artifact(s)` on the first try. `Reported success!` at 17:30:11. The wait and retry steps were skipped.
  - Afterwards all 172 `/<slug>/` URLs in the tree returned 200, and so did `/.nojekyll`. `main` hadn't moved (`3151a1b`), so the deployed files match `main`. The artifact leaves out `.github`, so the workflow change itself doesn't ship.
- The retry path (deploy fails, wait 30 s, deploy again) didn't run here, because the first attempt passed. It's plain `continue-on-error` plus `if: steps.deployment.outcome == 'failure'`, and GitHub accepted the workflow.

Two more `main` deploys failed the old way while this PR was open: [45222545971](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45222545971) (talenter) and [45224622095](https://github.com/GregUniK/sales/actions/runs/45224622095) (store-cloud). That makes 7 on 23 Nov. Both reports were 404 until the next successful deploy.

author: nbl-ahmd
body:
Found by re-testing production after #108: the admin live streams were ending at exactly 15 s.

## Cause
`backend/server.js` destroys any socket idle for 15 s, but the event-stream keep-alive comment was sent every 25 s. Every stream (direct and relay) was cut 15 s after its first message and every browser reconnected, each time minting a ticket and doing session/database lookups. That is exactly the per-tab idle traffic the event-driven work was meant to remove.

## Fix
- Heartbeat is 10 s (about 5 KB/hour per open tab). Both constants live in `live.ts` and the server and routes read them, with a unit test requiring a safety margin.
- The e2e API now applies the same 15 s idle-socket rule, and a new spec holds a stream open for 22 s. Verified it fails with the old 25 s heartbeat and passes with 10 s.

## Verification
Typecheck, lint, API tests, order-live unit tests and the three stream specs pass locally. Will re-verify on production after deploy (streams should last minutes, not 15 s).

author: trkgod
body:
## Summary

### Remove cumulative request quota
- Remove max_requests_per_engagement validation, approval-time persistence, plan reservation checks and broker rejection after N requests.
- Keep request IDs unique and non-replayable.
- Keep rate limiting (hard maximum 5 requests/second), single concurrency, active authorization, exact engagement/task scope, testing windows, method restrictions, response limits, redirect checks, evidence capture and audit logging.
- Retain explicit per-run crawl page/depth bounds to prevent accidental unbounded crawling.
- Add regression coverage proving legacy max_requests_per_engagement values are ignored.

### Make enumeration useful for vulnerability discovery
- Expand the Enumeration Skill and agent contract with concrete Web/API techniques: routes/forms, robots/sitemap, OpenAPI/Swagger, OIDC discovery, API operation/parameter inventory, JavaScript/source maps, authorized role context and business-function/trust-boundary mapping.
- Add fixed-path same-origin metadata discovery for robots.txt, sitemap.xml, OpenAPI/Swagger and OIDC discovery.
- Parse documented API operations and OIDC metadata without executing documented methods.
- Increase configurable crawl bounds to 100 pages / depth 4; default active enumeration to 50 pages / depth 3.
- Hand off prioritized vulnerability leads rather than asking the Vulnerability Agent to test every category against every endpoint.

## Safety
No scope, authorization, method, rate-limit, concurrency, response-size, evidence or request-replay protections are weakened. No live targets were contacted.

## Validation
CI will run the complete regression suite, configuration/schema checks, compile check and secret scan.

Auditoria independente do TH-006/TH-009 (plano local do usuário). Relatório completo em `docs/audit/TH006_TH009_AUDIT.md` e resultados em `docs/audit/TH006_TH009_TEST_RESULTS.json`.

## Defeitos confirmados (teste falha antes, passa depois)

- **D1 (Android, P0):** o writer entregava ao mixer um pacote por bloco tocado. Com pacotes reais de 1024 quadros, a leitura adiantada ficava no tempo real e a região de mescla ficava com 0 quadros, ou seja, troca sem efeito. Agora o writer entrega tudo o que o mixer aceitar a cada ciclo.
- **D2 (Android, P0):** armar incrementava `mixEpoch` e descartava a fila (A pulava segundos) a partir da segunda transição. Agora armar não muda a geração.
- **D3 (Android, P1):** a fila ficava fora de `transitionLatencyMs()`: 6.004 ms guardados contra 0 ms informados. Agora a fila tem 16 entradas e entra na conta (2.877 contra 2.877 ms).
- **D4 (Windows, P1):** o evento tipado esvaziava o pipe com o começo da nova posição: 115.473 de 132.300 quadros lidos. Agora 132.300 de 132.300.
- **D5 (ambos, P1):** o fim natural da fila emitia `UserStop` e descartava o fim já lido. Agora ele é `NaturalStop`. O vigia do Windows foi ajustado para não reiniciar o motor; o teste `natural-end` falhava antes.
- **Menores:**
  - trace preso em "Armed" com região vazia;
  - geração conferida dentro do `trackLock`;
  - ordem preservada na drenagem;
  - produtores serializados;
  - falha do writer invalida a fila;
  - write curto na pausa retomado.

## Validação

- **CTest:** 12/12 (84,24 s).
- **JVM:** 20.084 checagens, incluindo 1M itens, cancelamento com fila cheia, interrupção e dois produtores.
- **AVD com AudioTrack real e PCM sintético:**
  - Suíte nova com pacotes de 1024 quadros: 2/2 mesclas de 4 s, 2,5 s de B guardados, 0 quadros perdidos e 0 underruns durante as transições (1 no fim do fluxo).
  - Suíte antiga: aprovada.
- **Spotify real no Windows (OpenAL nulo):** 3/3 transições naturais com A+B, 0 B faltando e 0 underruns.

## Não testado

- Spotify real no Android e aparelho físico.
- Bluetooth/carro e teste acústico.
- CPU, GC e p99.
- Ciclos de AudioTrack, rota e taxa de amostragem.
- Fim natural da fila com o motor real.

Sem mudança de versão nem release neste PR.

author: mhardingjones-lupa
body:
## Problem
Mid-week, weekly totals always look low next to full weeks. Users, and the AI summary, read that as a decline. Users shouldn't be penalised for looking on a Wednesday.

## Change
- **`compute_pace()`**: for each tracked kind, plus a weighted overall score, compares this week so far with last week and the 4-week average. Each comparison window runs from that week's Monday 00:00 UTC for as long as the current week has run.
- **Status**: within ±15% of the 4-week pace is on track. So is any difference within a small absolute floor (2 items, or 5 points overall), so one PR early in the week isn't a swing. Otherwise ahead or behind.
- **Pace card** on Trends: "This week's pace · Wednesday (day 3 of 7)", with So far / Last week by now / 4-wk avg by now / status. "Behind" uses muted amber, not red.
- **AI prompt**: includes the pace figures and leads with like-for-like progress vs last week. It's told a mid-week total being lower than a full week is expected.

## Tests
- `test_pace.rs` checks same-point windows (later-in-week activity from last week is excluded), the 4-week mean, the noise floor, and weighted overall.
- `pace.spec.js` covers card rendering.

author: hygef-v4
body:
## Why

A review of the MCP code found no critical hole, but four medium risks, one misleading error and some unbounded growth. While checking, MCP on the local machine refused every call with "more than 60 calls per minute". The cause was Docker Desktop port forwarding for Redis and RabbitMQ breaking after a container restart, not the code. The code made it hard to see: it reported a Redis outage as a rate limit and never logged the cause. No test called `/mcp` over HTTP, so the Redis-backed limiter had never run against a real Redis.

## What changes

**System tests**
- Five MockMvc tests on `/mcp` in `PlatformWorkflowIntegrationTest`: 401 without a token, 403 with an `Origin` header, a read-only token cannot see or call write tools, the 61st call in a minute gets `-32029`, an oversized body is refused.
- The suite's Redis now requires a password, like deployed environments.

**Fixes**
- Redis unreachable: still refused (BR-U06-53), now with its own code `-32030`, an ERROR log with the cause and the audit reason `RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `McpController` authenticates first, then reads at most 1 MB from the stream. It used to buffer the whole body first.
- `read_authorized_submission` marks the student's text `untrustedContent: true`.

**Token reveal removed (breaking)**
- `GET /api/v1/me/mcp-credentials/{id}/token`, the stored ciphertext and the `revealable` field are gone. Migration `V20261123_1200` drops the three ciphertext columns. Existing tokens keep working because authentication uses the hash.
- Editing an agent can lower its access but no longer raise READ_ONLY to READ_WRITE (`MCP_ACCESS_UPGRADE_NOT_ALLOWED`). The dialog locks that option.
- BR-U06-30/31, decision D05, the MCP guide and the U06 docs are updated.

**Cleanup**
- Delete the unreachable Admin MCP tools (decision D03).
- Move write-request SQL into `McpWriteRequestRepository`.
- `McpWriteRequestCleanupScanner` deletes retry records older than 7 days. Migration `V20261123_1210` grants delete to the runtime role.
- `last_used_at` is written at most once a minute per token instead of on every call.

## Checks

- Backend, after merging the latest staging: 282 tests pass. They cover MCP, AI, notifications, `ArchitectureTest` and `PlatformWorkflowIntegrationTest`.
- Frontend: 54 AI and i18n tests pass, and the typecheck is clean.
- Local backend restarted: both migrations applied, an existing token still calls MCP, and the cleanup scanner removed 6 retry records from October.
- Not run: the full backend and frontend suites. CI will run them.

## Not in this PR

- Per-IP rate limits for unauthenticated calls are left to the reverse proxy.
- `GradingProposalTransactions.java`, `useGradingWorkspace.ts` and `GradingWorkspacePage.tsx` have local edits that are not part of this work and are not included.

author: srod
body:
Related to FRA-345. Follow-up to #513, from the Atelier review's F1.

## Summary

`bun run try:merchant` opens a live store page with the local `cdn/` build in place of the published SDK. Since #513, merchant pages also preload `sdk.frak.id/loader.js`, and the harness didn't route that URL. The preload went to production, which returns `403` until the redirect is deployed and the released loader after that.

```diff
 serveLocal(route)
-  file = url.match(/\/cdn\/<file>.js/)       # sdk.frak.id/loader.js → components.js
+  file = url.match(/\/<file>.js/)            # sdk.frak.id/loader.js → loader.js

 context.route("https://sdk.frak.id/components.js*", serveLocal)
+context.route("https://sdk.frak.id/loader.js*", serveLocal)
 context.route("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@frak-labs/components**", serveLocal)
```

The other URLs resolve to the same files as before: `components.js` exists in `cdn/`, and a jsDelivr path whose file isn't in `cdn/` still falls back to `components.js`.

## Evidence

A Playwright page that only carries `<link rel="modulepreload" href="https://sdk.frak.id/loader.js">`, with `serveLocal` and the `sdk.frak.id` routes copied verbatim from the script:

- **Before:** the preload response is not the local loader (body empty, request reached production).
- **After:** the preload response is byte-identical to `cdn/loader.js` (105 782 bytes).

Biome, `lint:comments` and the `sdk/components` typecheck pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. A dev script only, nothing ships.

**Blast Radius:** `try:merchant`.

author: ross0x01
body:
## Production evidence

Seven Agent runs on Trigger worker `20261123.15` failed in one chat. Two representative runs show both routed models returning a generic PDF parser 400, then the existing sandbox fallback declining with `no_staged_attachments`. One exact same-run Desktop staging receipt confirms one successful transfer and zero staging failures. The staging writer uses `/tmp/hackerai-upload/`, while the recovery matcher recognized only `/home/user/upload/`. [HAC-154](https://linear.app/hackerai/issue/HAC-154#comment-8810a80f-db67-441e-9ea1-e1e0e9fd5698)

## Change

Recognize the canonical Desktop/local staging marker for a matched PDF in the same user message. Preserve cloud annotations, strict filename matching, privacy and authorization, and the existing request retry limit. Local non-PDF files and the request-size fallback retain existing behavior.

## Preview / demo

[Vercel Preview](https://hackerai-4s24gtymo-hackerai.vercel.app) is READY at `2e8a2e30eec302c6fbc29e0cf87e630f4507b114). [Trigger Preview](https://cloud.trigger.dev/projects/v3/proj_fixirhycbcnfdpicejfb/deployments/wspluc4v) passed its branch deployment check. Native acceptance was exercised separately on the exact commit with a macOS arm64 QA build, WorkOS Staging, its own loopback Convex/relay, and verified Development worker `20261123.1`.

## Recovery tested

PASS. The native app uploaded a harmless 119-byte malformed PDF in Development, then submitted it in a fresh `This computer` Agent task. The exact worker run `run_06h0ipt1bafmvhnqk5qgav4aa2` recorded the failure from Mistral OCR, the second parser failure, and the sandbox fallback. The native sandbox inspected only the staged fixture. The task completed and the attachment and invalid-PDF verdict remained available when reopened. Earlier checks verified the native terminal transport and a local-only fixture on the same source and native build.

An isolated Linux arm64 regression saw one provider request on the base, then a recovery request on the fix. All 179 focused provider/staging tests passed. The configured hook passed lint, formatting, typecheck, 4,059 related Jest tests and 32 tooling tests.

## Expected cost / customer impact

This affects Desktop/local Agent users only when a provider parser rejects a staged, uniquely matched PDF. The existing bounded recovery can now make one follow-up model request in that path and complete instead of returning the original parser error. No volume- or dollar-level estimate is available. The overall provider retry limit and normal request path remain unchanged.

## Rollback

If current-version failures materially increase, open a reviewed revert of this PR's merge commit and deploy through the existing web and Trigger pipelines. There are no data migrations. Keep the existing customer attachment records and failed historical tasks. Verify exact web and Trigger revisions and the first eligible live parser rejection/recovery separately from the Development result.

author: pingolee
body:
Part of #1599. Part of #1614.

**How a PormG application starts, in a trimmed binary (#1599 layers 1–3).** This PR answers two questions:

1. Can a trimmed binary read `connection.yml`? **No.**
2. Do models loaded with `@import_models` in a package's module body work? **Yes**, once the connection is registered in code.

It adds fixture steps for four boot and run shapes an application has under the JIT: models from `@import_models`, a second read-only key, a nested transaction, and a read on a spawned task. All four run trimmed on SQLite, MySQL 8.4 and Postgres.jl with **no walls**. No `src/` change.

## What runs now

| Step | Exit | Entries | What it checks |
|---|--:|---|---|
| `imported` | 34 | SQLite full | `TrimF1.Imported` reads `db/connection.yml` with `load_many` and loads `db/models.jl` with `@import_models` in its module body, at precompile time. At run time the binary registers the key the models kept (`db`) in code and reads through them with no `set_models` call. It reads again through `Base.invokelatest`. |
| `keys` | 33 | all write entries | A second key `f1_ro` on the same database, with writes off. Reads through both keys return the same race; a create through `f1_ro` is refused with `WritesDisabledError`. |
| `nested_transaction` | 35 | all write entries | `run_in_transaction` inside `run_in_transaction` on one key (a savepoint): both races commit. Then an inner block raises and is caught by the outer: only the savepoint rolls back. |
| `spawned` | 36 | all write entries | A typed read on `Threads.@spawn`, then on `@async`. |

### Why the `@import_models` form works

A package's module body runs at precompile time, under the JIT, so YAML is parsed there. The package image keeps each model with its `connect_key` (`db`) and none of the configuration. Once `db` is registered at run time, `ensure_model_initialized` takes its fast path; there is no rebind and no by-name lookup of `MODEL_SET` (#1606). I checked under the JIT that `connect_key == "db"` survives in the image while `config` is empty.

## Findings, and where they are recorded

- **YAML, on 1.13.4 (#1679).** The first parse now prints the runtime's `Internal error during type inference of string(::Encoding{:UTF-8})`, then throws a **catchable** `Core.MissingCodeError`. Under 1.13.3 it was a `MethodError`. Upstream is still JuliaData/YAML.jl#260.
- **No YAML refusal is possible.** `Base.JLOptions().trim` reads `0` inside a trimmed binary, and so does `jl_generating_output`, so PormG cannot tell at run time that it is trimmed. The docs say so instead.
- **`@__DIR__` in a package names juliac's temporary copy.** A probe app that computes its root from `@__DIR__` sees `/tmp/jl_XXXX/` at run time, a folder that is gone. Its `__init__`'s `load_many` fails with `MissingConfigurationError` before any YAML.
- **`register_connection` refuses a key that names a folder in the working directory** (`isdir(key)`, `src/Configuration.jl:2476`). An application whose keys are its `connection.yml` folder names cannot register them in code while it runs from its own root. The docs give the workaround: other keys plus `set_models(MODEL_SET; key)`. **Decision for you** below.
- **Threads.** A trimmed binary takes its thread count from `JULIA_NUM_THREADS`. In a probe, `@spawn` reads ran on threads 2–5 with 4 threads. The fixture binaries, run by hand with `JULIA_NUM_THREADS=2`, print the same lines. CI runs them with one thread.
- **Scale (report only, a probe outside the repo).** Generated F1-shaped model sets of 52, 200 and 700 models, each bound with `set_models(MODEL_SET; key)`, with one typed read:

  | Models | Unresolved calls | Binary | `set_models` (trimmed) |
  |--:|--:|--:|--:|
  | 52 | 2,325 | 31.45 MB | 0 ms |
  | 200 | 2,325 | 31.80 MB | ≤1 ms |
  | 700 | 2,325 | 32.98 MB | 3 ms |

  The rows by layer are identical: what the build compiles does not depend on the number of models. Build times (~180 s for the first two, run concurrently; 115 s for 700, run alone) are not comparable.

## Rows by layer (Julia 1.13.4, JuliaC 0.3.12)

Base: Trim on main [45196612069](https://github.com/PingoLee/PormG.jl/actions/runs/45196612069), green 4/4. Its rows equal my local base build exactly.

| Entry | Base (main) | Branch | Δ | L1 | L2 | L3 | L4 | L5 | L6 | L7 | upstream | other |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SQLite read-only | 2,559 | 2,559 | +0 | 130 | 178 | 50 | 100 | 1,893 | 160 | — | 30 | 18 |
| SQLite full | 3,852 | 3,858 | +6 | 134 | 377 → 383 | 50 | 102 | 1,952 | 245 | 916 | 46 | 30 |
| MySQL 8.4 | 4,092 | 4,098 | +6 | 134 | 564 → 570 | 52 | 102 | 1,956 | 177 | 1,036 | 41 | 30 |
| PostgreSQL 18 (Postgres.jl) | 3,993 | 3,999 | +6 | 134 | 420 → 426 | 52 | 102 | 1,958 | 183 | 1,063 | 41 | 40 |

(Where the row sits; local builds, binaries embed `julia-1.13.4`.)

The +6 on each write entry is **reach**. All six are in layer 2: the `_with_unlisted_pool(::_InTransaction{…})` open arm (#1784's `with_pool` walk), 2 rows for each of the three new transaction closures. The existing `transaction_step` closures have the same rows on base. The binaries never reach them.

## Where each binary stops

Nowhere. Each binary ran 3×, the servers through `tools/runner.jl`, and every step line equals its JIT control's.

| Binary | Runs | Step lines | Exit |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| SQLite read-only | 3× SAME | 52 (unchanged) | 0 |
| SQLite full | 3× SAME | 99 → 103 | 0 |
| MySQL 8.4 | 3× SAME | 101 → 104 | 0 |
| PostgreSQL 18 (Postgres.jl) | 3× SAME | 101 → 104 | 0 |

The new lines, identical on every engine (`imported` on SQLite only):

```
step	imported	@import_models 1 rows: 2008 Monaco Grand Prix; invokelatest 1 rows
step	keys	1 rows on f1, 1 on f1_ro; a create on f1_ro refused with WritesDisabledError
step	nested_transaction	committed 2 seen inside, 2 after; inner rolled back on TrimRollback, kept 2020; removed 3
step	spawned	@spawn 2 rows: Monaco Grand Prix, Brazilian Grand Prix; @async 2 rows: Monaco Grand Prix, Brazilian Grand Prix
```

With `JULIA_NUM_THREADS=2`: SQLite full 3× SAME; MySQL and Postgres.jl 2× SAME each.

## Verification

- JIT controls on the three engines: every existing line unchanged, the new lines added.
- Every line `trim.yml` expects, checked against the local binaries' output. The two Postgres.jl `no password` shapes are skipped locally (no `PORMG_TRIM_TRUST_USER` here), as on base.
- Full unit suite at `-O0` (1.13.4): 204,076 pass, 1 broken, 0 failed (60 min).
- Integration, `test_transactions.jl` and `test_connection_pool.jl`: db_sl (`-t 1`) green; db_2 green under LibPQ and under Postgres.jl. db_my: full `runtests.jl` 12,105 pass / 98 broken / 0 failed; `test_mysql_backend` 108, `_reads` 498, `_writes` 96, `_bulk` 60, `_migrations` 75, `_alters` 136, `_inspectdb` 28, all passing.
- Docs build: green locally (its one interpolation warning is in `read/custom_joins.md`, untouched).
- `alloc_baseline.jl` and JIT first calls: not applicable, since `src/` is unchanged.
- An independent review of the diff. Nothing blocking. I fixed its seven points: a spawned task's error is unwrapped from `TaskFailedException`; the docs claim about threads now names how it was measured; the scale numbers moved out of the docs into this body; the cwd requirement of `imported` is documented; `close_pool!` is skipped when the registration failed; `include_dependency` covers `db/connection.yml`; the README's per-job line listings now include the new lines.

## Workflow runs

- CI: [45223021254](https://github.com/PingoLee/PormG.jl/actions/runs/45223021254), green 3/3
- Trim: [45223020943](https://github.com/PingoLee/PormG.jl/actions/runs/45223020943), green 4/4. Its rows by layer equal the local builds above, and its step lines are 52 / 103 / 104 / 105 (Postgres.jl with the two `no password` shapes CI runs)
- Docs: [45223020993](https://github.com/PingoLee/PormG.jl/actions/runs/45223020993), green

## Residue

- `connection.yml` in a trimmed binary: upstream (JuliaData/YAML.jl#260)

author: khaliqgant
body:
## What and why

> **D5 recorded:** Khaliq confirmed option (b) (#owner-decisions 250887862744305664, Nov 23 2026 11:38 PM PT). relay-control reads no CODEOWNERS, so here it means org owners or admins only. That is implemented: only an org owner or admin may register a gate, and a gate serves only while its owner still is one.

This PR adds release gates on owner delegation to relay-control: AgentWorkforce/relay#2246, §11a, Khaliq's instruction of 2026-11-23. **It is stacked on #277** (`feat/owner-trusted-delegates`); review and merge that first.

The job that publishes redeems the approval itself, under its own short-lived workflow OIDC token, right before its first publish step. Whatever starts the job therefore cannot skip the check, and no stored secret is involved.

**Matches Cloud's PR AgentWorkforce/cloud#6507** (branch `feat/delegation-release-gates`). Routes, bodies, responses, reason codes, check order and audit events follow it; see "Alignment with cloud#6507".

**The relay-app workflow and permit-script cutover is owned by relay-app's lead** and waits for Khaliq's direct yes to them (§11a.4). Nothing in this PR changes relay-app.

## Surface (§11a.3, §16.3)

**`GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/delegates/gates`**, for the owner by browser session or verified Desktop sign-in (§4.1: no step-up).
- A gate is `{gate_id, owner_id, repo, workflow_ref, job_workflow_ref?, ref | ref_pattern, event, target_prefix, repository_id?, repository_owner_id?, allow_source_sha_mismatch?, created_at}`.
- Only one of `ref` and `ref_pattern` is present; the other is omitted.
- `ref_pattern` is limited to `refs/tags/<literal prefix>*`.
- `workflow_ref` must be a workflow in the gate's repo at the gate's `ref` (a tag gate: at its `ref_pattern`). `job_workflow_ref` (a reusable workflow, any repo) is at a full ref, the gate's `ref_pattern`, or a 40-hex lowercase commit SHA, matched exactly.
- `target_prefix` must start with `<repo>:`, end with `:` and contain no wildcard.
- `allow_source_sha_mismatch` (optional, default false; shown only when true) is accepted only when `ref` is `refs/heads/<the repository's default branch>`. See the sha binding below.
- A duplicate live gate, in any letter case, is 409 `gate_exists`.
- `DELETE` takes `?gate_id=` or `{gate_id}` and answers `{gate_id, deleted:true}`.

**`POST /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/delegates/gates/redeem`** takes `Authorization: Bearer <workflow OIDC token>` and `{approval_id, action:{class, target}, dry_run?}`.
- **Checks, in order (as cloud#6507 at b2d58bd2f):**
  1. The token verifies (see below), before anything about the workspace is read.
  2. The token's repository has a gate (`gate_unknown`).
  3. `repository`, `workflow_ref`, `job_workflow_ref` (when set), `ref` (or `ref_pattern`) and `event_name` all match a gate, and the gate is pinned to the token's GitHub repository ids (`gate_mismatch`; a token without the ids never pins). Until here nothing is written to the workspace's audit log.
  4. Delegation is on.
  5. The action's target starts with that gate's `target_prefix` (`target_prefix`).
  6. The approval and action are found. A `release` is then bound to the run's commit (`sha_mismatch`, below).
  7. The normal redeem checks pass: revocation, the tier D grant and delegate binding, scope, policy, tier O, expiry, the gate owner's standing, and conditions.
  8. A fresh re-read of that authority (a dry run answers from it). Then consumption under locks: `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on the approval, and `gate.redeemed` in the consuming transaction, so a failed audit write rolls the consumption back.
- **The token check:**
  - signature against the issuer's JWKS, found by OpenID discovery, cached and refetched for an unknown `kid`;
  - the issuer: GitHub Actions, or one listed in the new `SELFHOST_DELEGATION_OIDC_ISSUERS`;
  - the audience: this deployment's origin;
  - `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`, with 60 seconds of skew;
  - the required claims, including `sha` (40 or 64 hex, any case, kept lower-cased).

  A failure is `oidc_invalid`. If the issuer's keys can't be read and none are cached, the answer is `unavailable`. A failed key fetch backs off for 30 s.
- **Single use per run.** The first redeem consumes the approval and binds it to the token's `run_id`. Any later redeem in the same run (another job, such as promote then bridge, or a later attempt) answers `{ok:true, consumed:true, same_run:true}`. Any other run gets `consumed`.
- **`dry_run: true`** runs every check and never consumes. It answers `{ok:true, consumed:false, dry_run:true}` or `{ok:false, reason, dry_run:true}`.
- **HTTP status (as Cloud):** a redeem (`ok:true`) or any dry run is 200. A refusal is 401 (`oidc_invalid`), 503 (`unavailable`, `condition_unavailable`: retry) or 403 (every other reason: final). The body is the same either way, so a plain `curl -f` step fails closed.
- **Release targets (§11a.2)** are validated as part of action validity everywhere. A `release` action that names no single release makes the approval malformed. The accepted forms are:
  - `<repo>:<channel>:v<version>:<source sha>:<candidate run id>[:<profile id>]`
  - `<repo>:land:<branch>:<head sha>`
  - `<repo>:ios:<distribution>:<build number>:<sha>`
- **Owner-minted (tier O) approvals** redeem through a gate the same way.
- **Audit:** `gate.registered`, `gate.deleted`, `gate.redeemed` and `gate.refused`, with the run, workflow and action, and auth method `github_oidc`. A dry run carries `dry_run: true` in the event data.

## Alignment with cloud#6507

- **Same as Cloud:**
  - check order and reason codes, including `target_prefix` before the approval lookup;
  - the standing rule (the gate's owner stands where a recipient's owner would);
  - a consumed approval answers only its own run, ahead of expiry and condition checks;
  - the gate JSON, the DELETE form, the dry-run answer, and the audit event names and `dry_run` data flag;
  - the gate request validation;
  - the release grammar regexes;
  - the OIDC claim requirements, including `sub`.
- **Differences, on purpose:**
  1. relay-control also accepts the self-host's configured OIDC issuers (§11a.3: "accepts OIDC from the self-host's configured issuers"). So the same-run binding also compares the issuer, along with run id and repository.
  2. The redemption row keeps the issuer and the first attempt. Cloud keeps first and last attempt. These are internal and do not change any answer.
  3. A gate-only install, or a workspace without a Relaycast binding, answers `unavailable` (delegation is not available there).
- **Cloud has neither:** a per-gate path or a duplicate-gate refusal, so I removed mine.
- **Design wording:** the design lists the redeem result as `{ok:true, consumed, same_run?, dry_run?}`. Cloud's passing dry run, and this PR's, have no `consumed` field, as you instructed.

## Decisions folded in (Khaliq, 2026-11-23)

These apply to #277 and this PR:
- **No step-up (7:41):** a session or a verified Desktop sign-in is enough for every owner action, gate registration included.
- **No class needs tier O by default (8:24, design 1d098775).** `secret_change`, `destructive` and `spend` are delegable and single-use, like releases. An explicit `require_tier_o` still applies.
- **`config_change` is delegable**; this lands on #277.
- **No approval prompts** and no admin co-approval. Anomalies are audit-flag only.

## Migration

`0089_delegation_release_gates.sql` adds two tables, registered in `CONTROL_TABLES`:
- `delegation_gates`, with exactly one of `ref` and `ref_pattern`;
- `delegation_gate_redemptions`.

`schema-manifest.json` was regenerated on a fresh PostgreSQL 16, which first reproduced the base branch's committed manifest exactly.

## Tests

`test/delegation-release-gates.test.ts` has 10 tests, with an in-process GitHub-shaped OIDC issuer and a second, configured issuer:
- release target grammar, and the issuer config loader;
- **Gate registry:**
  - validation, including a workflow from another

author: ishantswami13-crypto
body:
Stacked on #90. Draft: not for merging until reviewed. Frontend counterpart: ishantswami13-crypto/vantro-flow-frontend#100.

This PR has two commits.

## 1. Timezone fix (88e92e2)
- node-pg returns a Postgres `DATE` at *local* midnight. Reading it with `toISOString()` moved promised and receipt dates one day earlier on servers east of UTC (for example IST).
- `dates.pgDateDay()` now reads the calendar day at the four DATE reads.
- Report-delay stores the new expected date at UTC midnight.
- Regression test: `tests/decisions.timezone.test.js`.

## 2. Live decision reconciliation (e27e1b7)

**Root cause.**
- Once a supplier-delay decision was chosen, approved or run (`SELECTED`/`APPROVED`/`EXECUTING`/`SHADOWED`/`EXECUTED`), discovery only appended a `REOBSERVED` event. `resolveVanished` only resolved `OPEN` decisions.
- So after a receipt, the page still said "5 days late, ₹2.63L", and the customer-update drafts stayed pending in Approvals.
- The pre-run re-check compared only order ids, so new dates on the same orders went through. It ran outside any lock, and the final status write was unconditional.

**Lifecycle now (supplier delay only; other kinds are unchanged and covered by a test).**
- **Fingerprint.** A decision's fingerprint is its shipment date plus, for each late order line, the promised date, ready date, quantity and value.
- **Facts change after a decision is chosen, approved or run:**
  - the decision becomes `SUPERSEDED` and is kept as history, with its exposure at the time;
  - a new `OPEN` decision carries the current numbers and `analysis.reconciliation` (`supersedes`, `previousExposure`, line-by-line `changes`, withdrawn-draft counts);
  - nothing is auto-approved.
- **The delay no longer applies:** the decision becomes `RESOLVED` with a specific reason: received in full, back on the original date, no order at risk, expected date missing (review manually), or line closed or removed.
- **Customer-update drafts of a retired decision:**
  - `pending` and `approved` drafts are set to `expired`, with a `block_reason` saying what changed;
  - `done`, `executing` and `execution_unknown` drafts are never touched. They are counted as "cannot withdraw", because a sent message cannot be recalled.
- **Audit trail.** `SUPERSEDED` / `RESOLVED_BY_REALITY` events are appended (the trail stays append-only) with `supersededBy`, the exposure then and now, and the notice ids.
- **Identical data** re-observes as before: no duplicate decisions or drafts.
- **Execution:**
  - the re-check compares the fingerprint, and on a change runs discovery and returns 409 with `supersededBy`;
  - the run lock reports a decision retired meanwhile;
  - the final status write is a compare-and-set on `EXECUTING`. If a receipt retired the decision mid-run, what the run prepared is withdrawn and the response is 409;
  - the failure path no longer resurrects a retired decision.
- **Last safe point for each draft.** `lib/domain/decisions/noticeFreshness.js` runs before every approve or send of a `COMMITMENT_DELAY_NOTICE`:
  - covered paths: `PATCH /api/ai-actions/:id`, the signed approval link, `/api/client/actions/:id/decision`, approve-and-execute, and `EXECUTE_RECEIVABLES_ACTION` (send);
  - it recalculates now and compares the draft's order line, promised date and revised date;
  - a stale draft is withdrawn and the request gets 409 `NOTICE_STALE` with `newerDecisionId`. If the check itself fails, the request gets 503 and nothing is approved.
- **Honest state.** Approving a delay notice via the link or client path leaves it `approved` ("not sent"). Before, it became `done`, which reads as delivered.
- **API.** `GET /api/decisions/:id` adds `lineage` and `notices` (with a state per draft). Discovery results add a `superseded` count.

No migration: this uses existing statuses (`SUPERSEDED`, `RESOLVED`, ai_actions `expired`) and columns.

## Tests
- `tests/decisions.delayReconcile.test.js`: 8 tests over HTTP plus a real Postgres, using the hand-worked Meridian fixture (`tests/fixtures/meridianTrading.js`):
  - LIVE and SHADOW flows;
  - a correction and a second slip;
  - idempotent re-discovery;
  - data changing between approval and run;
  - a stale draft caught at approval and at send;
  - a receipt racing a run (3 rounds);
  - tenant isolation;
  - receivables decisions unaffected;
  - a pure year-boundary check.
- **Against the previous code: 5 of the 7 DB tests fail.** Isolation and other-kinds are guards and pass either way.
- The new suite is added to `tests/decisions.timezone.test.js`, which runs it under Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles. All pass.
- Full suite (`npm test`, local Postgres 16, Node 22): **91 / 91 files pass**, 0 skipped files.

## Rollback
Revert this commit. Rows already set to `SUPERSEDED`, `RESOLVED` or `expired` stay as history. Nothing is deleted.
