author: hjung3113
body:
Closes #2792

Round cap: lead — fix (리뷰 2차 C2·C3·C4·C6을 고치고 3차 리뷰 대신 팀장이 수정 diff를 직접 확인)

#2792를 셋으로 나눈 마지막 PR(팀장 승인). PR1a(#2805, 공용 부품)·PR1b(#2824, `LaneTimeline`)에 이어 `OrderedIntervalTrack`이 같은 «표로 보기»·«내보내기»를 쓴다.

## 범위
- `OrderedIntervalTrack`이 `ChartTableToggle`·`ChartExportMenu`·`IntervalTable`을 씀.
  - «항목 목록» 토글 → «표로 보기»(`toggle`). 표는 플롯 자리를 대신해 현재 가로 범위의 항목, 열은 줄·항목(선택 버튼)·시작·끝·상태·길이, 20행씩.
  - 길이는 소비자 순서 단위의 수. 양수 길이는 0으로 보이지 않음(소수 여섯째 자리 아래는 지수 표기).
  - «내보내기 CSV»: 플랫폼 안이면 메뉴 manifest `features.export`, 밖이면 새 선택 `exportActions.exportAllowed`(기본 꺼짐). 현재 범위 항목을 순서 값 그대로(열린 구간·점 이벤트의 끝·길이는 빈칸), 파일 이름이 비면 `track`.
  - 범위 요청(`onRangeRequest`)을 쓰면 현재 요청(범위·재시도 회차·제한 상태)의 성공 응답이 있을 때만 «내보내기». 불러오는 중·실패·이전 요청의 응답에는 없음.
  - 플랫폼 밖 결과 줄은 항목·범위·제목·허용·제한 상태가 바뀌면 지우고, 제한 상태에서는 숨김.
- 차트 카탈로그 순서 트랙 지원 표: 내보내기 지원(0.6.11).
- 계약 `docs/contract/chart.md` §16(«캔버스 차트의 표로 보기·내보내기», 순서 트랙 문단), 조각 `packages/sdk/changes/2792.md`.

## Decisions
- 실서버 캡처: 없음, mock 증빙(PR1b와 같은 팀장 결정을 따름). 순서 트랙의 실서버 소비자는 로그 탐색뿐이고, 기본 서버 조립은 Source가 꺼져 있으며 켜도 `getPeriods`가 `unsupported`라 트랙이 그려지지 않음(`source-assembly.ts:9–12`, `provider-source.ts:59–65`). 로그 메뉴 manifest는 `features: NO_FEATURES`라 플랫폼 안에서는 내보내기가 안 보임. 권한·기능 작업이 아닌 SDK 차트 부품. CSV는 mock에서 실제로 내려받아 확인(«순서 트랙.csv», 맥락 줄·머리 줄·3067행).
- 버튼 이름 «항목 목록» → «표로 보기»: 이미 확정된 Frame 도구 줄 모양을 옮김(릴리스 범위 문서 #2792 줄). E2E에 옛 이름 참조 없음, 소비자 테스트는 SDK 테스트만.

## 리뷰 1차 (R-2792-P2) 반영
- C1 캡처: 아래 링크(mock 전후·팝오버), 실서버는 Decisions.
- C2 요청 세대를 렌더에서 정함: 같은 범위에서 `forbidden` → `ready`가 되어도 새 응답 전에는 이전 답으로 CSV를 열지 않음. 회귀 테스트는 effect 전 커밋을 `useLayoutEffect`로 단언(수정 전 실패).
- C3 결과 줄 세대(`useImageActionGate` generation) + 제한 상태에서 숨김(수정 전 실패).
- C4 계약의 선택 행을 `TableRow current`(강조·`aria-current`)+`aria-selected`로, 순서 트랙 CSV·재시도 조건, 영어 이름 이전(`Item list` → `Show as table`).
- C5 순서 트랙의 manifest 우선(양방향), `forbidden`·`unsupported`·`empty` 전환이 열린 표·팝오버를 내리고 파일을 쓰지 않음.

## 리뷰 2차 (R-2792-P2-b) 반영 — 커밋 9f26e1537
- C2 요청 세대가 effect와 같은 입력(`view` 참조 + 회차·제한·kind·로더)을 씀: 도메인만 넓어져 같은 범위를 재요청해도 첫 커밋부터 이전 CSV 없음. 테스트 «a wider domain re-requests the same range and offers no CSV until the new answer (PR2 round 2 C2)».

author: mugar123
body:
## Change

The feed has no signal of quality for a paper too recent to have citations. This change starts storing two: the highest h-index among a paper's first author and last three authors, and its Hugging Face upvotes. It only stores them. Feed ranking is untouched (`worker/paper-store.ts` is identical to main), so no reader sees a difference yet.

- Migration 0014 adds `openalex_author_impact` (an author's h-index, asked again after 30 days while the author is on an eligible byline, deleted a year after its last fetch) and `work_quality` (one row per paper with a positive score: each signal and the capped total).
- The nightly harvest gains three phases after enrichment: prune, author impact and paper quality (`worker/paper-quality.ts`). They cover papers of the last 90 days with fewer than 5 citations, or an unknown count, and at most 30 authors.
- Author lookups ask OpenAlex for 100 authors a call, newest papers first, and stop for the night when their part, the nightly share or the feed ceiling is spent. A provider outage, a malformed list or a discovery batch of 20 or more authors with no valid record stops the phase without caching the answer; an author OpenAlex leaves out of a refresh keeps the cached h-index. A 401 or 403 fails the phase after one call, and a short 429 is waited out at most three times a night.
- A missing value adds nothing: an author OpenAlex does not know, or one not yet loaded, gives no score, and a paper with no positive signal has no row.

## Authorized decisions

- Up to 2,500 billed OpenAlex author lookups a night, inside the harvest's existing nightly share of 3,700 units. Authorized by Nicolás on 2026-11-23; it replaces the 600 he authorized earlier that day. OpenAlex's daily allowance is not raised, and since #578 the harvest's share is kept apart from the readers' budget.

## Documentation

Updated: worker/README.md describes the two tables, the three phases, the author part in the OpenAlex budget table, and the longest run's subrequest and Workflow step estimates. ARCHITECTURE.md adds the phases to the harvest. The subrequest comment in wrangler.toml states the new estimate; no setting changes.

## Verification

- `VITE_PAPER_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 npm run check` on d23c3e12, rebased on main 26dc5359: exit 0, 5,441 tests, 5,440 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped; build and Worker dry-run passed. ESLint reports 3 warnings in files this change does not touch. Without the variable knip fails on main as well.
- Focused Worker tests (`worker/index.test.ts`, `paper-quality.test.ts`, `paper-harvest.test.ts`, `request-quota-ledger.test.ts`, `paper-enrichment.test.ts`): 337 of 337 passed on bfd92c5d.
- Sizes measured on the production paper store on 2026-11-23, read-only: 262,587 papers in the 90-day window; the papers published since 2026-11-16 are 30,771 eligible ones with 89,699 distinct authors (897 lookups). The first load is about 6,900 lookups, about three nights at 2,500.
- `/health/openalex/budget` on 2026-11-23 after the harvest: 870 of the nightly 3,700 units used.
- Estimates for the longest run with the whole cap spent: about 86,455 subrequests of the configured 100,000, and about 5,849 Workflow steps of Cloudflare's 10,000 per instance. One step makes at most 21 lookups of at most 8 s each, against its 10-minute timeout.
- Not verified: the phases in a production harvest, the migration against the production database, and the real duration of a night with 2,500 lookups. The first run is the harvest of 02:30 UTC after deployment.

## Review

- The `reviewer` subagent reviewed the rebased branch at bfd92c5d against main 26dc5359, with attention to the conflict with #578 in the OpenAlex relay. No blocking finding. It confirmed by mutation that author lookups charge the harvest's share and their own part, never the readers' share or minute limits, and that reader paths through the relay are unchanged.
- Its three non-blocking findings were left as they are: a reader asking the exact URL of an author batch while the harvest's call is in flight gets the upstream failure instead of the stored copy (no screen builds that URL); one new relay test depends on microtask order between two calls; and one of the three cache checks can only be reached by a scripted caller.
- Earlier rounds of the same subagent reviewed the branch before the rebase, up to 597923cc; their findings (provider failures cached as "no h-index", unbounded retries, refused calls repeated by step retries) were fixed in the second to fourth commits.
- The last commit, which raises the cap, was written by a Codex agent and reviewed by the orchestrating Claude session, which read the diff and checked its arithmetic. No separate reviewer subagent read it.

## Scope and risk

Worker only. Apply migration 0014 before deploying the Worker (`npx wrangler d1 migrations apply PAPER_STORE --remote`); without the tables the three phases fail and the rest of the harvest continues. Nothing reads the new tables yet. The relay change is confined to harvest requests that pass `canCacheList`. Verification read about 1.2 million rows of the production paper store for the counts above and made no OpenAlex call with the project's key; an earlier reviewer round made about 27 anonymous OpenAlex requests. No temporary edit was kept.

author: davefatkin
body:
better-sqlite3 bundles prebuilt binaries for eight platforms (linux, linuxmusl, darwin and win32, each x64 and arm64), plus the SQLite C source in `deps/` and `src/` that it would compile from. The image only ever loads `prebuilds/linuxmusl-<arch>.node`. The rest was about 26 MB of dead weight, already present in 1.12.0.

The builder stage now deletes the other prebuilds and the source after the native-addon guard, then opens an in-memory database so a missing binary fails the build instead of the container. Building better-sqlite3 from source still works if a future version needs it, since the toolchain stays in the deps stage. sharp already ships only its musl packages, so it is left alone.

## Testing

- amd64: `node_modules` drops from 197 MB to 173 MB and the image from 721 MB to 685 MB (both built with a fresh `APK_CACHE_BUST`). The container boots, `/setup` returns 200, and the database file is created.
- arm64 (built under QEMU): only `linuxmusl-arm64.node` remains and SQLite 3.54.1 loads.
- PR CI doesn't build the Dockerfile, so the Release run after merge is the first native build on both arches.

author: weside-agent[bot]
body:
## What

Findings from the event poller's first live hours, and the open panel notes of #328, #329 and #330.

**Live findings**
1. `main_red` had no silent first round: three older red runs (one already green again) became events at the start. The first round per repo and branch now records red runs silently; a forge error leaves the repo unseeded.
2. `run_queued_long` trusted the `status=queued` list, which returns stale runs. Each candidate past its limit is re-read once (`actions/runs/<id>`, at most `recheck_max`, default 5, per round); a run no longer queued is dropped silently, an unreadable one is retried next round.
3. Waiting `pull_request`/`pull_request_target` runs are noise when the queue is full: new kind `pr_run_queued_long`, which without its own route takes `run_queued_long`'s targets as a digest. Push, schedule and dispatch runs stay single lines.
4. The fork guard hid name and branch of every `pull_request` run. It now applies only when `head_repository` differs from the repo; a branch of the repo itself shows its workflow name and branch (through the cleaners).

5. Ghost runs: a run queued for more than a day whose jobs list is empty (the forge can neither start nor cancel it) is skipped and logged once (`events: ghost run …`); the jobs read happens only for such a candidate. The repo's own runs spend the re-read budget before pull request runs (panel note).

**Panel notes**: the watcher's merge path calls `board.py news merged` (tested, also its two skips); a repeated yes after the question left the board posts no second comment; the machinery tail delivers an escalated `permission_prompt`; a pending call past one 256 KiB transcript chunk is found; `startup_failure` and `timed_out` prod tag runs are damage events; duplicated tests dropped; one comment on the nine-case table.

**Docs**: `/we:setup` step 3 names the optional `events` block with `push` and `sessions`; `board.md` § Event lines says how a running session starts its tail without a restart.

## Tests

New tests per item above; touched suites with plain pytest: 1387 passed; `claude plugin test` 150/150; consistency, structure, frontmatter, budget green. Full run: CI.

Not proven: the ghost rule on the live run that triggered it (read after the merge in the poller log). A re-run that keeps its run id and hangs again after a dropped stale entry stays unreported (panel note; the dedupe key has no attempt number).

Compat repo checked: no, a setup paragraph and an optional route fallback; a project without `events` is unchanged.

Eight AppContainer integration tests failed on the GitHub-hosted Windows runner with exit code 1 and empty output/error; the same unit suite has previously passed real-app flows on the owner's PC. Cause is not yet proven and must **not** be hidden by skipping security tests.

body:
## 요약

비밀처럼 보이는 이름의 환경 변수 값을 파일에 쓰는 Bash 명령을 PreToolUse에서 막습니다(exit 2). 예: heredoc, `echo` 리다이렉트. #497을 고칩니다.

- 차단 여부는 owner가 결정했습니다. `printenv`와 같은 규칙으로 막습니다.
- 비밀 이름 판정은 `printenv_requests_secretish_name`과 같은 키 규칙(`secretish_env_values`)을 `env_names_include_secretish`로 빼서 함께 씁니다.

## 재현 (수정 전)

합성 변수 이름과 합성 값만 썼습니다. 명령은 훅 입력으로만 넣었고 실행하지 않았습니다.

| 형태 | origin/main (e12600dc) | v3.13.4 (plugin cache) | 이 Mac 적용판 (brew 3.13.4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cat > f <<EOF` + `$EXAMPLE_SECRET_TOKEN` 본문 | 통과(0) | 통과(0) | 통과(0) |
| `echo "$EXAMPLE_SECRET_TOKEN" > f` | 통과(0) | 통과(0) | 통과(0) |
| `${...}` · `>>` · `printf` · heredoc `${...}` 변형 | 통과(0) | 통과(0) | 통과(0) |
| 대조군 `printenv EXAMPLE_SECRET_TOKEN` | 차단(2) | 차단(2) | 차단(2) |

적용판 버전은 `agent-guard version` → 3.13.4로 확인했습니다. 플러그인 레지스트리는 코디네이터가 같은 날 3.13.4로 확인했습니다.

## 규칙

- 막는 것: 비밀 이름 변수의 `$NAME`/`${NAME}` 확장이 표준 출력이 파일로 끝나는 명령에 있는 경우입니다. 파이프라인 전체와 `( )`·`{ }`·`$( )`·if/for/case 묶음, `sh -c`·`eval` 프로그램까지 따라갑니다. 따옴표 없는 heredoc 본문에 있는 경우도 막습니다.
- 통과시키는 것:
  - 따옴표 heredoc, 작은따옴표나 이스케이프로 감싼 이름
  - `${#NAME}`, `${NAME:+word}`
  - `test`/`[` 조건 검사, 명령 앞의 환경 변수 할당
  - 비밀이 아닌 변수, 리터럴
  - `/dev/null`·장치·다른 fd로 가는 출력(리다이렉트 순서 반영)
- 탐지기가 실패하면 차단합니다(fail closed).

## 테스트

- `tests/secret-env-file-write.sh`를 추가했습니다(새 실패 테스트를 먼저 작성).
  - 모든 사례를 bash로 실제 실행합니다. 비밀 이름 변수에 무작위 canary를 넣고, 작업 디렉터리의 파일에 canary가 남았는지를 정답으로 씁니다.
  - 게이트 판정이 이 정답과 같아야 하며, Claude·Codex 두 호스트에서 모두 확인합니다.
  - 차단 39건, 통과 이웃 34건, 146 checks입니다(비밀이 아닌 변수와 리터럴 쓰기 포함).
- `tests/run.sh` diff는 0입니다. `tests/env-lookup-allowlist.sh`에서 새 테스트를 호출합니다.
- `tests/mutations.json`에 새 규칙의 mutant 20개를 넣고, `.github/workflows/mutation-check.yml` paths에 새 테스트를 추가했습니다. 로컬 `sh tests/mutation-check.sh <20 ids>` 결과: all 20 caught.
- 로컬에서 돌린 suite는 모두 exit 0입니다.
  - `heredoc-body-text`(107), `bash-path-text-data`(226), `path-operands-only`(222)
  - `literal-substitution-text`(143), `env-lookup-allowlist`(141), `hook-outcome-contract`(144)
  - `printenv-argument-contract`, `message-value-prose`
- shellcheck 0.10.0 `--severity=error`: 0건입니다.
- 전체 매트릭스는 CI에 맡깁니다.

## 오탐 측정

코디네이터가 replay로 측정했습니다. worker 안에서는 측정하지 않았습니다.

- 방법: 이 Mac의 최근 48시간 transcript에서 고유한 Bash 명령을 모두 모았습니다(봇·worker 전체). 그중 변수와 함께 `>` 또는 `<<`가 있는 명령을 3.13.4와 이 브랜치 head 9da4bc0b에 각각 돌렸습니다. 3.13.4는 통과시키고 이 브랜치는 막는 명령을 "새로 막힘"으로 셉니다.
- 후보: 고유 명령 55,513개(봇 2,624, worker 52,889).
- 새로 막힘: 5개. 모두 worker 쪽이고, 모두 `bash_secret_env_value_file_write`입니다.
- 5개에 나온 변수 이름: KIND_DB_PASSWORD (5), SECRETS (5), S (4), C (1), VERSION (1). 데이터베이스 비밀번호 변수를 파일에 쓰는 명령으로, owner가 printenv와 같은 규칙으로 막기로 한 경우입니다. 따라서 오탐이 아니라 의도한 차단입니다.
- 봇 세션에서는 새로 막힌 명령이 없습니다.
- 결론: 규칙을 좁힐 필요가 없습니다. 9da4bc0b 이후 head 변경은 main merge뿐이며 쓰기 규칙에는 영향이 없습니다.

## Codex 리뷰 (`codex review --base origin/main`)

리뷰를 6번 돌렸습니다. 매번 지적된 우회와 오탐을 실패 테스트(실행으로 얻은 정답)로 먼저 고정한 뒤 고쳤습니다.

| 회차 | 지적 | 처리 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 ×2, P2 ×2 (파이프 뒤 줄바꿈, 셸 프로그램, fd 2 오탐, 따옴표 파일 이름) | fixed |
| 2 | P1 ×2, P2 ×1 (바깥 리다이렉트, 명령 묶음, /dev/null heredoc) | fixed |
| 3 | P1 ×1, P2 ×3 (큰따옴표 안 명령 치환, 리다이렉트 순서, 셸 프로그램 범위, heredoc 대상) | fixed |
| 4 | P1 ×2, P2 ×2 (단어 안 확장 회귀, eval, 추가 fd, 버린 출력 전파) | fixed |
| 5 | P1 ×1, P2 ×3 (case 패턴, `:+`, 앞 할당, 3단 파이프) | fixed |
| 6 | P1 ×1, P2 ×2 (묶음이 물려받은 stderr, /dev/null heredoc 이름, 조건 검사) | fixed |

열린 Codex 항목은 없습니다. 6회 리뷰의 모든 지적이 **fixed**이고, follow-up으로 넘긴 항목은 없습니다. 이 규칙은 셸 문법을 근사하므로 7회차 리뷰는 돌리지 않기로 했습니다(#507과 같은 판단).

알려진 한계가 남아 있습니다.

Closes #497

author: tannevaled
body:
DRAFT, fork only, NOT for upstream merge: prototype of Raft replication of SQLite WAL pages in pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite, CGO_ENABLED=0).

## Review history

- Rounds 1 and 2: adversarial reviews by Opus 5.5 (correctness) and Fable 5.2 (security).
- Round 3: run with Fable 5.2 for both correctness and security, unlike rounds 1 and 2.

Each probe of a round is ported to a regression test; for round 3 each new test was also run against the round-2 head (47b0c296) and fails there.

## Round 3: findings and status (head 47b0c29)

| ID | Severity | Finding | Status | Test (red on 47b0c296) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-R3-1 | HIGH | `ATTACH` with a computed file name (`'p' \|\| ''`, a `file:...?vfs=unix` URI, a bound `?`) reaches the authorizer as NULL, which the guard read as VACUUM's `''`: a client could create and write files outside the engine directory | FIXED: a NULL name is always refused; only the literal `''` of VACUUM passes | `TestAttachWithAComputedNameIsRefused` (5 spellings, file absence checked), `TestGuardDeniesNullAttach` |
| R3-2 | MEDIUM | `Node.Query` on a new Leader read before the per-term barrier | FIXED: a Leader's read runs the barrier first | `TestQueryOnANewLeaderWaitsForTheBarrier` |
| F-R3-2 | MEDIUM | Snapshot `dbPages`, `seq`, `head` installed unvalidated | FIXED: `dbPages` must equal the size the files hold (last commit frame of the WAL, else file size / page size); `head` must be set | `TestSnapshotHeaderFieldsAreValidated` |
| R3-1, F-R3-3 | MEDIUM | `onStop` fired once, so a stopped node elected again stayed Leader | FIXED: a Raft state observer steps the node down on every election while stopped; a failed transfer is retried 5 times | `TestStoppedNodeElectedAgainStepsDownAgain`, `TestStoppedFollowerElectedStepsDown` |
| R3-3 | LOW | The barrier ignored the request context (50 ms context waited 791 ms) | FIXED: the wait is bounded by the context (Execute and Query) | `TestBarrierHonoursTheContext` |
| F-R3-4 | LOW | `Node.fatal` grew through `errors.Join` on every applied entry | FIXED: the first error only | `TestFatalKeepsOnlyTheFirstError` |
| T1 | LOW | `TestTempWritesAreRefused` stayed green when either half of the fix was removed alone | PARTLY: see below | `TestEachHalfOfTheTempFixHasItsOwnCase` |

T1: removing the schema half alone turns the new test red (its ATTACH '' case). Removing the CREATE TEMP half alone leaves every end-to-end statement refused, because SQLite also reports the write to `sqlite_temp_master` (schema `temp`) to the authorizer, which the schema half refuses: that half is defence in depth, held by the unit test `TestGuardDeniesTempAndForeignSchemas`, and no statement can separate it end to end.

## Gates
- Fix head 3009f22b. `go test ./db ./walframe`, `gofmt -l .` and `go vet` clean; mutsweep with no skip on every changed refusal as committed: db/guard.go 3 of 3 caught, walframe engine.go and node.go 98 of 98 caught, 0 survived, 0 hung. The fork reports no CI, so these are local runs.

## Left open
- `ATTACH ''` by a user (a literal, private, per-connection database) remains: it cannot reach a file, but data put there exists on the Leader only.
- `stepDown` cannot help a single-node cluster.
- Requests waiting for `reqMu` do not observe their context; only the barrier wait does.
- The applied index is not recorded in `Node.Apply`; a per-term Barrier is used instead.
- Round 1 items still open: no dedicated `scanTail` test, no snapshot fuzz target, read starvation bounded only by the query timeout, 15.6 MB/op remaining for a 1 MB entry.

author: wstein-agents
body:
## In plain words

With notebook sync on, when the agents chat showed a notebook and the agent rewrote that whole notebook (`workspace_write`), the write failed after a wait with "couldn't confirm the write … a tab of this browser has it open". The notebook page already took such writes; the chat's notebook pane didn't. Now the pane takes the write as the notebook page does: it is saved, the pane shows it at once, and what the person typed there first is kept (a write made from an older read is a conflict).

## What changed

- `web/agents/notebook-artifact.ts`: the pane's focus takeover (`writerHandover`) gets `shownDoc` and `replaceDoc`, as the notebook page's has. While the pane can't save the notebook (closing, let go, frozen, or no longer bound to it), `shownDoc` gives null.
- `web/page/handover.ts`: a null shown document answers the write "lost", with nothing changed, at both the prepare and the commit step. The asking page then asks again, and the write goes to whichever tab writes the notebook next (or is made with no holder). Before, a page with nothing to show would have answered a conflict.
- Size: `cli/pyjs.cjs` +116 bytes (measured with the exact local gate on base 32b08bda). No growth marker: those are retired.

### Checks run

- `test-agents-artifacts.mjs`, two new cases in the journal section. Both are whole writes through another page of the same browser while the pane writes the notebook and no notebook tab is open:
  - J13: saved, the pane shows it and is still the writer, and the journal has it.
  - J14: the person typed in the pane after the agent read the notebook. The write is a conflict, and the person's text is kept in the pane and in the journal.
  - Control: with the two pane lines removed, J13 and J14 both fail with "couldn't confirm the write".
  - J15 and J16: the pane still holds the notebook's writer lock but can't save it, frozen as a close's first step leaves it (a loopback-only test hook, `__sbTestPaneFreeze`). The freeze comes while the write is held at the pane's prepare (J15), or after its ready, at the commit (J16). In both, the pane answers "lost": it replaces, shows and saves nothing, the record keeps its revision, and the write ends "couldn't confirm", with no ok. Once the pane is closed and its lock let go, the same write is saved directly.
  - Mutations: with the pane's whole can-save condition removed from `shownDoc`, J15 and J16 fail (the frozen pane takes the write). With the handover's null → "lost" answer removed, they fail too (a conflict instead). Removing `!frozen` alone can't be caught, because a frozen pane's `guard` is never "open" again, so the other half of the condition already refuses it.
- `test-agents-artifacts.mjs`, all passed (on today's master, default build: 257 ok).
- `test-focus-takeover.mjs`: 46 checks.
- `test-notebook-write-journal.mjs`: 22/22.
- `test-workspace-journal.mjs`: 86 checks.
- The LaTeX group's budget: 35 checks.
- tsc (web and project).

author: patrickballard
body:
Closes #632

### What this changes

The first step from the issue: say it. No status changes.

pip reads index options on a line of their own in a requirements file and installs from what they name. wheelgap checks PyPI only, and before this the report gave no sign of it. Now stderr has one note per input:

```
$ cat requirements.txt
--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
torch==2.9.0
```

Before (0.13.0):

```
$ wheelgap requirements.txt -p 3.13 -t win-arm64,linux-x86_64 --all
wheelgap 0.13.0 · requirements.txt · 1 package · Python 3.13

package  version  win-arm64  linux-x86_64
torch    2.9.0    ✗ missing  ✓
...
```

After:

```
$ wheelgap requirements.txt -p 3.13 -t win-arm64,linux-x86_64 --all
wheelgap: note: requirements.txt sets --extra-index-url, which wheelgap doesn't read: its packages were checked on PyPI only, so a package pip finds elsewhere may install differently
wheelgap 0.13.0 · requirements.txt · 1 package · Python 3.13

package  version  win-arm64  linux-x86_64
torch    2.9.0    ✗ missing  ✓
...
```

- The note covers `-i` / `--index-url`, `--pypi-url`, `--extra-index-url`, `-f` / `--find-links` and `--no-index`, in any spelling pip's parser reads (`-iURL`, `--index-url=URL`, `--extra URL`), in the file or a file it includes. Options are read against the table of pip's line options that `_requirement_options` already uses. So a value (`--trusted-host -ifoo`) and an abbreviation pip refuses as ambiguous (`--no`) name nothing.
- It names the option and never its value, because the URL may hold credentials. Several options give one note (`sets --index-url, --extra-index-url and --find-links`).
- An index option after a requirement isn't counted, since pip ignores it there. #661's `pip ignores -f after a requirement` note already covers that case.
- An index option on a line with `-r` or `-c` (`--find-links wheels -r base.txt`) isn't counted either. pip 26.3 reads the included file and never applies the line's other options: `_parse_and_recurse` doesn't yield the line to `handle_option_line`. The file still doesn't count as PyPI-only, as before.
- `-q` drops the note, like the unpinned-package note. A run with `--index-url` (or `index-url` in `[tool.wheelgap]`) or a `WHEELGAP_INDEX_URL` mirror doesn't print it, because that run doesn't check PyPI.
- MCP: the note shows up in `check_lockfile`'s `notes` unchanged. The wording avoids `(--index-url)`, which the MCP translation table rewrites.
- One more fix: `--pypi-url` is pip's other name for `--index-url` (`pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py`), and `_names_index_option` didn't know it. So a file with a `--pypi-url` line counted as PyPI-only, and `--conda-forge`, `--notes` and `--fix` could send its package names out. It now counts as naming an index. The new `tests/test_origin.py` case fails on main.

- From review: `PIP_PYPI_URL` is now in `origin.INDEX_ENV`. pip maps `PIP_<NAME>` to `--<name>`, and with `PIP_PYPI_URL=file://…/simple` pip 26.3 prints `Looking in indexes: …/simple`. So a plain requirements file under that variable no longer counts as PyPI-only.

### How pip's behaviour was checked

- Source: pip 26.3 `pip/_internal/req/req_file.py`, `handle_option_line`. `--index-url` replaces the finder's index URLs, `--extra-index-url` adds to them, `--find-links` is appended, and `--no-index` drops the indexes. The line parser's options were listed with `build_parser()`; `--pypi-url` is one of them.
- Real pip, offline, against a scratch folder of tiny wheels with `uvx --from pip pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --no-deps -r req.txt`:
  - `--find-links wheels` in the file, with `--no-index` on the command line: `Would install demo-1.0`.
  - `--extra-index-url file://…/simple` in the file, with `--index-url file://…/nowhere`: `Looking in indexes: …/nowhere, …/simple`, `Would install demo-1.0`.
  - `-i file://…/simple` and `--pypi-url file://…/simple`: both replace the command line's index.
  - `--no file://x`: `pip: error: ambiguous option: --no (--no-binary, --no-index, --no-require-hashes?)`.
  - `--find-links wheels -r inc.txt` (and `-r inc.txt --find-links wheels`), with `--no-index`: `No matching distribution found for demo`. `-i file://…/simple -r inc.txt`: `Looking in indexes: …/nowhere`. For comparison, `--no-binary :all: -r inc.txt` does apply, because its parser callback sets it.

### Tests

- `tests/test_cli.py`: the note appears for `--extra-index-url URL`, `-i URL`, `-iURL`, `--index-url=URL`, `--extra URL`, `--find-links DIR`, `-f URL`, `--no-index` with `--find-links=`, several options in one note, a repeated option, `--pre --extra-index-url URL` and `--pypi-url`. It also appears for an option in an included file. There's no note for a file without one, or for an option after a requirement or on a `-r`/`-c` line, or with `--index-url` or `WHEELGAP_INDEX_URL`. In every case, `user:secret@` never reaches stderr.
- `tests/test_mcp.py`: the note is in `check_lockfile`'s `notes`, and the secret appears nowhere in the reply.
- `tests/test_origin.py`: a `--pypi-url` file isn't PyPI-only.
- The new tests fail on main (13 of them; the negative cases pass on main too). Full suite: 7145 passed, 3 skipped. Ruff, `ruff format --check`, mypy and `mkdocs build --strict` pass.

Docs: `docs/inputs.md` (the "Skipped" paragraph and the `environment.yml` `pip:` line), the first `docs/faq.md` entry, and `docs/differences.md` ("Additional index URLs"). Unreleased behaviour is marked "after 0.13.0". CHANGELOG has a line at the top of `## Unreleased`.

Not in this PR (later steps from the issue): a `--json` key for the unread options, and reading the other index.

author: tunnelbliick
body:
## Problem

The frontend names a character card "<character> [<skin>]", using the skin names in `character_names.json`, as in "Super Creek [Halloween]". Those come from a hand-kept list in the store. That list has no skin name for 19 JP-only outfits and calls 2 more only "Alt Version". So card 110802, Duramente's Halloween outfit "[Claret Nosferatu]", shows as plain "Duramente" in the planner, the timeline and the inheritance search.

JP's master can't name the theme. Outfit descriptions only say "〇〇の特別衣装" ("special outfit"). It does give the outfit title and the debut date.

## Change

- **Translation run:** it also has Claude write a short outfit label for each of those outfits. Labels are stored as `outfit_theme`, by card id, in `name_translations.json`.
  - A label names a season or event theme such as Halloween when the outfit clearly has one. Otherwise it is the outfit's English title.
  - The model reads the character, the JP and English outfit title, and the card's JP debut date. The 117 existing hand-kept labels are its examples.
  - A label is kept while its JP outfit title is unchanged.
  - A failed label request only logs a warning, so that run's name translations are still saved.
- **Generation:** the Global `character_names.json` fills the missing and "Alt Version" skins with these labels. Hand-kept skin names always win.
- **Corrections:** `name_overrides.json` accepts `outfit_theme` to correct a label.
- **Unchanged:** `outfit_theme` is in no master, so it stays out of the text categories. The JP set's `character_names.json` is unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo test` passes: 445 tests. The new ones cover which outfits are asked about, the debut date in Japan, overrides beating translations, and the skin fill.
- **What a real run would ask about today:** 21 outfits, including 110802 with debut 2026-10-13. No API calls were made.
- **End-to-end:** generate with a hand-added `outfit_theme` for 110802 and 109302 changed only those two skins in `character_names.json`. 1108's "02" became "Halloween" and 109302 lost its "Alt Version".
- **Not seen yet:** the model's actual labels. They come on the publisher's first translation run after deploy.

author: mboisvertdupras
body:
## Why

Agents spend most of their shell time on checks that another agent already ran on the same code. #29 added the rule that stopped this. The upstream port in #31 removed it, and the reruns came back in the next session. No other pstack text gives a check a cost, so a slow check suite can run for days before anyone times it.

## What changed

- `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` gets the **One owner per check per commit** paragraph back. The rule now says to rerun after the code changes, so it also covers work that is not committed yet.
- `autopilot-full.md`, `interrogate/SKILL.md`, and `principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md` get their matching sentences back. One gates lane runs the full checks, and reviewers run only the commands that prove a finding.
- `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` gains **Time every check**. Whoever builds or first runs a check suite reports seconds per check. A check over a minute is profiled before it runs again. Each brief names a scoped check per edit, and the full suite runs once per milestone.
- `worker.md` tells a worker to run the checks its change touches, and to run the full checks only as their named owner.
- `benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md` gains a rule for a subject that takes minutes per run. Save one baseline, rerun only the changed part, and run the whole new side once at the end.
- `test/fork-rules.test.mjs` lists one phrase per fork-only rule and fails when a port drops one.

## Scope

The test covers only the rules in this PR. Other fork-only rules need their own entries.

## Tradeoffs

Inline markers in the skill text were rejected. A deleted marker cannot report its own deletion, and the markers would sit in text that agents read.

## Blast Radius

Every poteto-mode root and every worker reads the new text. Roots stop rerunning a delegate's suite on unchanged code. A phrase edit in a listed file now fails `npm test` until the table is updated.

## Verification

author: wegastudios
body:
## Cosa cambia (H19, sessioni)

- **Area soci e moduli pubblici (donazione, adesione)**: la sessione sta in un cookie cifrato invece che nella tabella `core.sessions`. Prima ogni visita, anche di un robot sulla pagina delle donazioni, scriveva una riga (lettura + aggiornamento a ogni pagina). Ora non scrive nulla nel database.
- **Operatori e amministrazione: invariati**, restano nel database (servono a «Dispositivi collegati», alla revoca da tutte le sessioni, ai limiti di durata, alla 2FA).
- **Tabella `core.sessions`**: tolto l'indice su `last_activity` (serviva solo alla pulizia, su una tabella ormai piccola) e `fillfactor` 60 per gli aggiornamenti sul posto. L'autovacuum stretto c'era già (H29, #1190).
- A schermo cambia: niente. Un socio già dentro mantiene l'accesso (sta in `as_socio`, non nella sessione); perde al massimo la scheda scelta (figlio) una volta sola.

## Come funziona
Middleware `UseCookieSession` in testa al gruppo `web`: si attiva solo sulle rotte con il marchio `cookie-session` e solo se il driver impostato è `database` (con `array` o altri non cambia nulla, quindi le prove esistenti restano quelle di prima). Cambia driver, nome del cookie (`__Host-as_pubblico` in produzione, diverso da quello del gestionale), rifà `session.store` e il reindirizzatore (altrimenti i messaggi `->with()` finiscono in un'altra sessione) e a risposta fatta rimette tutto com'era. Il marchio è su: area soci (host dei soci e domini personalizzati), `/dona/*`, `/adesione/*`. Mai sulle rotte con `auth`, `two-factor` o `operator` (c'è una prova che lo controlla).

## Sicurezza: perché non peggiora
- Nella sessione dei soci non c'è nessuna credenziale: l'accesso è il cookie `as_socio` risolto su `app.member_sessions` (revoca, «esci da tutti i dispositivi», sospensione, uscita dall'associazione: tutto ancora lato server, provato nei test esistenti). Dentro il cookie di sessione ci sono solo messaggi, token CSRF, scheda scelta (la scheda scelta è comunque riconvalidata a ogni richiesta contro le schede del socio).
- Il cookie è cifrato e firmato dal middleware dei cookie; uno alterato viene scartato e si riparte da sessione vuota (provato).
- Nome diverso dal cookie del gestionale: una pagina pubblica sullo stesso indirizzo non tocca la sessione dell'operatore.
- Limite noto del cookie: ~4 KB; nelle pagine servite non si riporta input nei campi (nessun `withInput`), quindi i messaggi stanno largamente sotto. Se un domani si aggiungesse un modulo con molto input flashato, lo si vedrebbe come messaggio perso, non come buco.

## Prove
Test prima della correzione su branch `-prova` (rosso, 6 prove rosse): run 45255927699. File: `tests/Feature/Auth/CookieSessionsTest.php` (marchio sulle rotte giuste e mai su quelle con accesso; nessuna riga in `core.sessions` da area soci e moduli pubblici; il gestionale scrive ancora nel database con il suo cookie; messaggio tra due pagine; scheda scelta che persiste, uscita che la azzera e chiude l'accesso; cookie alterato; indice tolto e fillfactor).

## Misure
Nessuna ancora (la misura dall'interno è in H1): atteso 0 scritture su `core.sessions` per visita anonima/soci invece di 2 (SELECT + UPDATE/INSERT).

## Rischi / da decidere
- Tocca le sessioni: rilettura di Audit richiesta.
- Dopo il rilascio i soci con la sessione vecchia (cookie `as_gestionale` sull'host dei soci) la ignorano e le righe scadono da sole con la pulizia a sorte.

author: sergio222-dev
body:
## Problem

- Hyprland requests are made from the update loop on a blocking socket with no timeout. A stuck compositor would freeze the bar.
- The snip selector kept each monitor's frame twice: once as an `RgbaImage` and once as a copy for the image `Handle`. That is about 33 MB extra per 4K monitor while the selector is open.
- `meetings_fired` remembered every alert ever raised, with no bound.

## Change

- `hyprland::request_at` sets 500 ms read and write timeouts. Replies normally take well under 1 ms.
- The snip keeps only the `Handle`, built from the frame's own buffer (`into_raw`, with no clone). `snip::dimensions` and `cropped` read the handle's pixels for the crop.
- `meetings::Fired` maps each alert to its meeting's start, and `due_alerts` forgets the alerts past the late window, which can no longer fire.
- `odd/tasks/caches-and-streams.md` logs the whole chain.

Deleting a chat could leave some of it behind, or keep some of its work going.

- A chat deleted while it is busy stays deleted: a message waiting in its queue goes with it, and nothing that finishes for it afterwards brings it back.

author: shenxianpeng
body:
Second of two steps that split the action's code by area (the first was #354, tests only). This PR moves main.py's code into an `action/` package. Nothing changes in what the action does.

## Before vs after

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `main.py`: 3,037 lines, all the code | `main.py`: 69 lines, `main()` and the two helpers it calls; action.yml still runs it |
| | `action/`: 8 modules, the largest 1,212 lines |

| Module | Lines | What it holds |
|---|---:|---|
| `action/escape.py` | 46 | escaping text for the step log and workflow commands (`_log_safe`, `_annotation_escape`) |
| `action/inputs.py` | 114 | the inputs, read from the environment action.yml sets; their validation |
| `action/model.py` | 135 | `ScopeResult`, `Commit`, the run's overall status and exit code |
| `action/context.py` | 360 | the event, the pull request and its commits (git or API) |
| `action/base_config.py` | 225 | `config-source: base` |
| `action/cli.py` | 610 | running commit-check and turning its JSON into scopes |
| `action/render.py` | 1,212 | the step log and the Markdown report (incl. the output specification comment) |
| `action/publish.py` | 353 | job summary, `result` output, PR comment, AI label |

Dependencies only point down the list: nothing imports a module below it, so there are no import cycles. The report and the step log stay in one module because the step log uses about 20 of the report's helpers.

## Nothing in the code changed

- All 186 top-level functions, classes and constants are moved as is. A name used from another module is now written `module.name`. With that prefix removed, every definition parses to the same AST as before.
- `module.name` rather than `from module import name`: each name is looked up in the one module that defines it, so a test that patches it patches it everywhere.
- The action's output (step log, job summary, `result` output, exit code) is byte for byte the same as main's in 6 local runs: message + branch, dry run, an invalid boolean input, author + files, message-ai-attribution, and an invalid config-source.
- action.yml, the release flow and the `v2` tag are untouched. `python main.py` puts the action's own directory on `sys.path`, so `action/` imports from there. The caller's checkout is not on the path, so nothing in it can shadow the package.

## Tests

- They change only where they reach the code: `main.X` becomes `module.X`, and `patch("main.X")` becomes `patch("action.module.X")`. `patch("main.subprocess.run")` becomes `patch("subprocess.run")`, which patches the same object.
- `TestReconfigureIo` and `TestLogErrorAndExit` move to tests/main_test.py, next to the code they test.
- The same 412 tests pass. CI coverage now measures `main` and `action`, and both are at 100%.

author: superhussain
body:
The hourly cron now writes `spend-nudges.json` only after at least one device accepts the spend push. Before this change, it recorded the threshold first. A failed subscription list or a refused send then marked that week's nudge as sent, and it never arrived.

## What changed

- `worker/push.js`: `sendPushes` resolves to the number of subscriptions that answered 2xx. It returns 0 when there are no events or no key.
- `worker/spend.js`: `spendNudgePass` returns `{ events, state }` and writes nothing. The new `recordSpendNudges(env, state)` is now the only place that writes `NUDGE_KEY`.
- `worker/index.js`: `pushHourly` sends first. It records the spend state only when there were spend events and the push reached at least one device.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the Spend rollup row now says the nudge is recorded after a device accepts the push.

If the record write fails after a push goes out, the next hour sends the same nudge again. A duplicate nudge is better than a lost one. Board-commit pushes ignore the new return value, so they work as before.

## Testing

- Two new tests in `tests/worker/push.test.mjs` cover the failures. In the first, the push service answers 500, then 201, and the 80% nudge is recorded only after the 201. In the second, the `push/` list fails and nothing is sent or recorded. Both fail against the old worker.
- `push.test.mjs` passed 19 of 19, and `test:protocol` passed 503 of 503. Lint and `format:check` are clean.
- Remaining uncertainty: the local pre-review `cli` check failed on `tests/cli/test_bench.py` `test_claude_call`. On macOS, the expected temp path is under `/private/var` and the actual path is under `/var`. This diff changes no Python, and the test fails the same way on main's code. The fix is queued as its own follow-up.

Nothing visible changed, so there are no screenshots or device checks.

Follow-up of 2140-expected-weekly-token ([superhussain/factory#632](https://github.com/superhussain/factory/pull/632)).

author: pietrodags
body:
An email the outbox sends again carries the same `Message-ID`: after a failed attempt, and after the API stopped between the email server taking it and its row being recorded sent. Delivery stays at least once (a lost notice is worse than a rare copy), now tested and documented; a copy is the same message to mail clients, and some show it once.

Example: the outbox hands Ana's "La votación se ha cerrado" to the email server and a deploy restarts the API a moment later. On restart the email goes again, as before, but with the same `Message-ID`, so Ana's mail client can tell it is the one it already has.

## Design

- **The email's identity is a column of its row** (`notifications.message_id`, a random UUID): drawn when the email is queued and drawn again each time `scheduleEmail` queues it again as a new one (each closing's "voting closed"); kept while the outbox tries it again after a failure, while the organizer retries it, and when it is sent again after a stop (the stopped transaction never changed it). The outbox reads it with the row and hands it to `SendEmail` as the email's `id`; the migration gives every email already queued one of its own.
- **`OutgoingEmail` gains an optional `id`** (`email.ts`): the same each time the email is sent again. `smtpEmail` writes it as the `Message-ID` at the sender's domain (`<id@qando.app>`); without one (the sign-in codes) each send gets its own, as before. The port stays the one edge to the email server; nothing else learns about `Message-ID`.
- *Discarded:* a `Message-ID` derived from the event and the email's type (`<event.voting_closed@qando.app>`), without a column. Some mail clients drop a message whose `Message-ID` they already hold, so after the deadline is extended the second closing's "voting closed" would never show. A `Message-ID` derived from the row's ID and its attempts was discarded too: queuing it again resets the attempts, so a second closing would reuse the first one's.
- *Not done:* closing the window itself (recording the email sent before handing it over would lose it when the server refuses it or the API stops first); with SMTP it cannot be closed.

The code guide's rows of `OutgoingEmail`, `smtpEmail`, `scheduleEmail` and `emailOutbox`, and the data model and email flow in `docs/diagrams.md`, say the same.

## Test plan

- [x] Integration (`outbox.integration.test.ts`, PostgreSQL): the API stopped after the server took an email and before recording it (its connections ended, as a stopped process's are): `sendDue` rejects, the email is left pending with no attempt, and the next start sends it again once, as the same message (same `id`), and records it sent; a failed email tried again carries the same `id`; each closing's "voting closed" carries a new one; every email handed over carries one.
- [x] Unit (`email.test.ts`, against a local SMTP server): an email with an `id` arrives with `Message-ID: <id@qando.app>` each time it is sent; emails without one get a `Message-ID` each, at the sender's domain, never the same.
- [x] API tests: unit (587) and integration (278).
- [x] Mutation (local, `email.ts` and `outbox.ts`, 134 mutants): 96.27 % (`email.ts` 100 %, `outbox.ts` 95.37 %); the five survivors are older, in lines this branch did not change (`skipLocked` of the row lock, the pattern and test of `failureOf`'s plain code).
- [x] Full acceptance suite (local, three screens): 827 passed, 85 skipped, none failed.
- [x] `npm run check`; build.
- [ ] CI green.

## Codex review

**Codex + Codex.** Pass A: no finding ("No actionable regressions were identified") · Pass B: approve, no finding (it could not run the tests in its read-only sandbox; they run locally, above, and in CI).

closes #347

author: ymjacky
body:
## Summary

Client options that are Two Byte Integers in MQTT were not checked, and a value that does not fit reached the broker as another value:

- **`keepAlive`** (#117): only the low 16 bits were sent in CONNECT. `70000` was sent as `4464`, `1.5` as `1`, and `-1`, `NaN` and `Infinity` as `0`
  (keep alive disabled).
- **Topic alias maximums** (#118): `topicAliasMaximumAboutReceive: -1` was sent as the Topic Alias Maximum `65535`, `70000` made `connect()` reject with
  `MqttPacketSerializeError`, and `topicAliasMaximumAboutSend: 1.5` made `connect()` reject with a `RangeError` of the topic alias cache.

## Changes

- `lib/client/validation.ts`: new `validateClientOptions()`. `keepAlive`, and with MQTT 5.0 `topicAliasMaximumAboutSend` and
  `topicAliasMaximumAboutReceive`, must be integers from 0 to 65,535. The topic alias maximums are not checked with MQTT 3.1.1, which does not use them, as the
  properties are not checked there. The range check is shared with the check of the properties (`isIntegerIn()`).
- `lib/client/base_mqtt_client.ts`: the constructor calls `validateClientOptions()` first, before the `outgoingStore` is given the `clientId`. `keepAlive` is
  used as it is given; `Math.max(options.keepAlive, 0)` is removed.
- JSDoc of the options, of `InvalidArgumentError` and of the constructors of `MqttClient` and `WebSocketMqttClient`, and `readme.md` (the table of the client
  options and the table of errors): the range of the options, and that the constructors throw `InvalidArgumentError`.

## Behavior changes

- The constructors of `MqttClient` and `WebSocketMqttClient` throw `InvalidArgumentError` when `keepAlive`, `topicAliasMaximumAboutSend` or
  `topicAliasMaximumAboutReceive` is not an integer from 0 to 65,535, e.g. `70000`, `1.5`, `NaN` or a string. The message names the option and the value.
- **A negative `keepAlive` throws too.** Before, it disabled keep alive, like `0`. Use `0` to disable keep alive.
- Not changed: `0` to `65535` are sent as before, and the options that are not given use their defaults.

## Tests

- `test/deno/client/validation_test.ts`: `validateClientOptions()` accepts 0, 1 and 65535, and rejects 65536, 70000, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and a
  string, with MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1; the topic alias maximums are not checked with MQTT 3.1.1.
- `test/deno/client/connect_test.ts`: the constructor of `MqttClient` throws for these values; `keepAlive: 65535` and `topicAliasMaximumAboutReceive: 65535`
  are sent in CONNECT as they are.
- `test/deno/client/connect_ws_test.ts`: the constructor of `WebSocketMqttClient` throws.
- `test/deno/client/kv_session_test.ts`: a client that cannot be created does not give its `clientId` to the `KvOutgoingStore`, so another client can use the
  store.
- `test/deno/client/manipulation_test.ts`, `manipulation_ws_test.ts`: the tests that check that no PINGREQ is sent use `keepAlive: 0` instead of `-1`.

All the new tests fail on `main`, except the one that checks that 65535 is still sent as it is.

`deno task check`: 469 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #117
Fixes #118

body:
#### Reference issue

Closes gh-26803.

#### What does this implement/fix?

With two observations, `pearsonr` returned `1.0` for every alternative. Under the default method, the null distribution assigns equal probability to correlations of `+1` and `-1`. The one-sided p-value is therefore `0.5` for `greater` when `r = +1` and for `less` when `r = -1`. The opposite tail and the two-sided p-value remain `1.0`. Constant inputs still return `NaN`.

The regression tests cover both correlation signs and constant inputs for all three alternatives.

## Summary for non-engineers

A chat now carries its own finished, green pull request to merge instead of asking you for a "ship" yes.

**What went wrong:** on 23 Nov a chat held `valentinyeo/multiprompt-android` PR #524, finished and green, waiting for your yes. The board drain saw the ticket as "waiting" and passed. The reply check had nothing to say when a chat handed you the merge.

**What changes:**
1. The board drain fails its tick, with the fix named, when a ticket in this chat's view waits on you (marked waiting on you, or parked in Valentin Review) while its linked PR is open, mergeable and green.
2. It also fails when the ticket's newest comment from the chat asks you to merge, ship or approve the PR.
3. The Stop reply check adds the same fix to the chat's context when a final reply hands you a merge, ship, approve or review. It never blocks the turn.
4. One owner, `skills/hypertask-work/merge-ask`, holds the matcher and the fix line; both checks read it.
5. A real product question still passes. So does a red or conflicting PR, and a ticket that does not wait on you.

**What you will see:** a drain tick or a chat reply that asks you to merge now names the fix: "merge it yourself per pstack shipping; ask him only a product question". Chats still ask you "should the button be blue or green?".

**Watch out for:** the drain trusts the board's waiting mark and the Valentin Review column, so a chat that parks a green PR there gets a finding until it merges. Merge state from saved board facts is unknown, so an open green PR still counts; a PR GitHub reports as conflicting does not.

author: harishdarko
body:
## What

PR B of the CaseLens redesign (Neon PR 1): the API the redesigned review page needs, ahead of the recorded results in PR C.

### Migrations V11 to V14 (expand only, `lock_timeout` 5 s in each; V11 and V12 split by table in fix round 2, below)
- `triage_result.recorded BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`. `event_id` becomes nullable, because recorded results (PR C) have no outbox event. A new check `chk_triage_result_live_event (recorded OR event_id IS NOT NULL)` keeps it required for every live result.
- `triage_feedback.decision VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CORRECTED'`, and `note` becomes nullable. The new `chk_feedback_decision` replaces `chk_feedback_has_correction`:
  - ACCEPTED must change no field.
  - CORRECTED must change at least one field, so every row the old check accepted still passes.
  - Both new checks are added `NOT VALID`, and validated in their own later migrations (V13, V14).
- Deploy gap, tested on Postgres 16 with Testcontainers:
  - Rows written before V11 read back as live results and CORRECTED feedback.
  - The previous application version's inserts (which leave out the new columns) still succeed after V11.
  - Nothing in V11 rewrites a table.

### Feedback decision
- `POST /api/tickets/{id}/feedback` takes `decision` (`ACCEPTED` or `CORRECTED`). CORRECTED is the default when `decision` is left out, so older clients behave as before.
- ACCEPTED needs no urgency or note. An ACCEPTED that also changes a field is a 400.
- CORRECTED needs at least one change, as before. A no-op correction is still a 409. The note is now optional, and a blank note is stored as no note.
- Feedback is still append-only: a changed review adds an entry, and results are never edited.
- `requestId` stays idempotent. A resend returns the same entry. The same id with a different decision or body is a 409.
- The result can be named `triageResultId` (older clients) or `originalResultId` (#32). Both are accepted. Two different ids in one request is a 400.
- Responses and `GET .../feedback` entries now include `decision`.

### Enriched result
- `GET /api/tickets/{id}/processing` is the only endpoint that returns a result today. Its result now also carries:
  - `recorded`
  - `categoryLabel` and `categoryDescription`
  - `policyVersion`
  - `policies: [{id, label, guidance}]`, in `policyIds` order (`policyIds` is kept)
  - `fallbackReason` (from #31)
- All of these come from the workspace's own industry pack.
- `TriageResultView` is a public mapper, so PR C's `latestResult` on the tickets list uses the same shape.
- Each pack's `pack.json` now has `categoryLabels` and a `label` on each policy, and `PackRules` refuses to load a pack without them. SaaS labels match the approved prototype. The prompt text is unchanged, because it reads only descriptions and guidance.
- A ticket that has only a recorded result answers `/processing` with `job: null` plus that result. A ticket with neither a job nor a result is still a 404.

### Retry demo no longer seeded
- New workspaces and resets get 8 tickets per industry. The session industry list no longer lists `provider-retry-demo`.
- It can still be created with `POST /api/demo/scenarios/provider-retry-demo` in every industry.
- `frontend/src/industries.json` was regenerated with the sync test's write mode (`-Dcaselens.industries.write=true`).

## Tests (written first)
- New `FeedbackDecisionApiIntegrationTest` (7): accept with no urgency or note; accept with a change gives 400; CORRECTED is the default and needs no note, and a blank note means none; no-op and empty corrections give 409; both result id names, and mismatched ids give 400; an idempotent accept resend, and a different decision under the same requestId gives 409; append-only history.
- New `ResultViewApiIntegrationTest` (5): EV labels, description, policy version and guidance; SaaS labels come from the SaaS pack; recorded-only ticket gives `job: null` plus the result; no job and no result gives 404; another workspace's recorded result gives 404.
- New `RecordedResultsMigrationIntegrationTest` (Testcontainers, 2): V10 rows, then V11 defaults; old-version inserts after V11; recorded results without an event; a live result without an event is rejected; the decision check; `lock_timeout` is present.
- `PackCatalogTest` (+2): every bundled pack labels every category and policy, and a pack missing a label is rejected.
- Local `./mvnw -B -ntp -Plambda verify`: Tests run: 339, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0; LambdaJarBootIT 1 of 1; BUILD SUCCESS (Testcontainers Postgres included). The first full run caught a real bug: the corrections-only `FeedbackService.submit` overload called the new method as a self-invocation, so it ran without a transaction and `PostgresClientIdAndResetIntegrationTest` saw no workspace lock wait. The overload is now `@Transactional` itself.
- `npx vitest run src/App.test.tsx`: 50 passed.

## Changed assertions
- `FeedbackEvaluationApiIntegrationTest`: a correction with no note was a 400 and is now a 201 (`decision: CORRECTED`, no note), as the brief asks. The 400 is now checked with a 501-character note instead.
- Seeded counts went from 9 to 8 in `DemoIndustryApiTest`, `DemoWorkspaceOpenApiTest` and `DemoApiIntegrationTest`. The SaaS seed check now expects no retry ticket, and asserts the retry ticket can still be created on demand.
- `frontend/src/App.test.tsx`: "9 demo tickets" became "8 demo tickets" (the bundled list). #32 rewrites this file; if it merges first, this one-line change disappears in the rebase.
- `PostgresMigrationIntegrationTest` and `RecordedResultsMigrationIntegrationTest`: the version pin went from 10 to 14.
- `RecordedResultsMigrationIntegrationTest`: the single `lock_timeout` check on V11 became a check on every step (4 migrations).
- `FeedbackServiceTest`, `PostgresClientIdAndResetIntegrationTest`: now call the 9-argument `submit`.
- `TestPacks.SAAS_JSON` gets labels, which the loader now requires.

## Contract
The brief's contract is unchanged, with one addition: the feedback request also accepts `triageResultId`, since #32 sends both names.

## Gaps
- No recorded results are seeded yet (that is PR C). `TriageResult.recorded(...)` and the recorded-only `/processing` path are exercised by tests only.
- While a live re-run of a recorded ticket is queued, `/processing` shows that job with no result until it completes, not the recorded result. PR C decides whether the page keeps showing the recorded one meanwhile.

## Fix round 2 (review of this PR)
- **Feedback only on the latest result.** The latest-result query now orders by `created_at desc, id desc` (`findFirstByTicketIdAndWorkspaceIdOrderByCreatedAtDescIdDesc`, also used by `/processing`). In `FeedbackService.submit`, after the `requestId` idempotency check, an explicit result id that is not the ticket's latest gives 409. A resend of an already saved requestId still gives 201 with the same row.
- **Migration split.** V11 changes only `triage_result`, V12 only `triage_feedback`, so no transaction locks both tables. Each has `lock_timeout` 5s. The CHECKs are added `NOT VALID` and validated in V13 and V14 (each its own transaction, `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` only).
- **Unused overload removed.** The 8-argument `submit` had no production caller; tests use the 9-argument method.
- New tests (written first): `feedbackOnASupersededResultIsAConflictButAResendOfAnEarlierSaveIsIdempotent`, `feedbackWithoutAResultIdGoesToTheLatestResult`, `resultsCreatedAtTheSameInstantHaveOneDeterministicLatestByIdDescending` (two fail against the previous service and repository: 409 expected, 201 returned), `eachTableIsChangedInItsOwnMigration...`, `oldRowsAndOldVersionInsertsWorkBeforeTheConstraintsAreValidatedAndAfter` (Postgres 16: old rows and old-version inserts work with the constraints present but not validated, and after validation). The migration test class now cleans the shared container's schema before e

body:
## Summary Three changes in `a11y-rules`: 1. **New rule id `images/role-img-name-missing`** (Tier 2, WCAG 1.1.1, severity high, `FAIL`, ACT 23a2a8). An element that is an image only through `role="img"` (`
`, ``, ``, …) without an accessible name was reported by `names/required-missing`, whose declared criteria are 1.1.1 and 4.1.2. Consumers that map one criterion per rule id (auditmysite) filed it under 4.1.2, although ACT 23a2a8 maps it to 1.1.1 only. `names/required-missing` no longer checks `img`; no element is reported by both. `` and SVG keep `images/alt-missing` and `svg/name-missing`. A host with Chrome roles (`image`, also for `role="image"`, the WAI-ARIA 1.3 synonym) is covered as well. Outcome and severity are unchanged. 3. **`media/video-captions-missing`: `` without `kind` counts as subtitles.** HTML: the `kind` attribute's missing value default is the subtitles state, its invalid value default is the metadata state. A `` without `kind` therefore counts as a caption track; an invalid value (including empty or with surrounding whitespace, since enumerated values are matched ASCII case-insensitively without trimming) is `metadata` and does not count, nor do `descriptions` and `chapters`. 2. **New rule id `names/indicator-name-missing`** (Tier 2, WCAG 1.1.1, severity high, `FAIL`) for `meter` and `progressbar`, native (``, ``) or ARIA, without an accessible name. WAI-ARIA 1.2 requires a name for both ("Accessible Name Required"); they are not operable, so they are non-text content (1.1.1) rather than user interface components in the sense of 4.1.2. axe files `aria-meter-name` and `aria-progressbar-name` under 1.1.1 as well; there is no ACT rule. `names/required-missing` no longer checks these roles and now carries 4.1.2 only (`Meta.wcag = ["4.1.2"]`); no element is reported by both. ## Changes - `crates/a11y-rules/src/names.rs`, `semantics.rs` (Meta + registration), `media.rs` - Corpus cases (fail/negative/N/A and variants) in `tests/korpus/faelle/gruppen/namen.rs`, unit tests in `tests/names.rs` (incl. the Chrome `image` role), mutation catalogue entries in `tests/mutations/{namen,sonden}.toml` - ACT mapping `23a2a8` → `images/alt-missing`, `images/role-img-name-missing` (`xtask/act/src/main.rs`, `results.json`, `docs/testing/act.md`); the ACT run stays consistent, 0 of 18 wrong - Regenerated rule reference and examples (`cargo run --manifest-path examples/a11y/Cargo.toml`), doctest count of not-run rules 67 → 69 - `docs/packages/a11y-rules.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]` No version bump; release follows separately. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check -p a11y-rules --no-default-features`, `cargo check -p a11y-static --no-default-features`, `cargo clippy -p a11y-wasm --all-targets --no-default-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test -p a11y-wasm --no-default-features` - `xtask/mutate.py crates/a11y-rules --only images/role-img-name-missing,media/video-captions-missing,names/required-missing,names/indicator-name-missing` (all killed) - W3C ACT run (`xtask/act`): only change in the summary is the 23a2a8 mapping - `node packages/a11y-wasm/build.mjs` + `peakmark check`: brotli 167.4 kB (budget 171000 B), gzip 201.3 KiB (budget 205 KB)

author: emanuelmetal
body:
Follow-up to the Phase 4 security review of the separate `torre3_ask` database (no critical/high findings; this fixes the medium ones).

## Changes
- **Isolation check (`web/server/ask.ts`)**: "Preguntale al portal" is off (503, `available: false`) when `ASK_DB` holds any table besides the `ask_*` copies, e.g. a `wrangler.toml` that points it at the main database. Checked once per isolate, re-checked after a failure; no rate-limit count or model call is spent.
- **Never serve stale rows (`pipeline/alas3/ask_sync.py`)**: if the copy fails, every ask table is emptied and the publish fails loudly, so rows withdrawn by that publish are never answered from.
- **D1 statement limit**: INSERTs are split by size (≤ 90 KB, D1 caps at 100 KB) instead of 200 rows; a single oversized row fails with a clear error.
- **Dropped views**: an ask table with no source view is emptied, with a warning.
- **Publish order (`publish.py`)**: the ask copy runs last, after the R2 cleanup, so a failed copy no longer skips deleting unpublished files.
- CLAUDE.md rule updated.

Accepted trade-off (unchanged): one shared-link holder can use the 300/day global cap by re-opening the link (same as comments).

## Testing
- `make test`: ruff clean, 162 pytest, 140 vitest, tsc.
- New tests: misconfigured `ASK_DB` → 503; extra table in ask DB → 503; size-based splitting; failure and mismatch empty every ask table; orphan tables emptied.
- `make publish-local` through real wrangler: 24 statements, largest 89.8 KB, 2177 rows; the real local `torre3_ask` passes the isolation check.

body:
## Summary

The fleet consistency drift audit gets a new check, `boot-disk`. The check compares the boot-disk type and size of node pools. Each Linux node pool of the Standard clusters in a cohort has one vote. The audit files a pool that differs from the majority as a finding on `NodePool/<pool>`, at base severity `major`.

## Why This Change

A customer found the cause of a production incident when they compared two clusters by hand. The primary cluster used 100 GB boot disks and the disaster-recovery cluster used 500 GB. The drift audit exists to find this type of difference, but it did not read the boot disk. A cohort of clusters that differed only in boot disk showed as consistent.

## What Changed

- `fleet_drift.py` adds the `boot-disk` facet. It is the first facet whose voters are node pools. The cohort stays the cluster cohort.
- A pool baseline has two conditions more than a cluster baseline. A minimum of three clusters must vote. The pools that hold the baseline must be in two-thirds of those clusters, or more.
- Windows pools do not vote. A pool that GKE returns without a disk type or size does not vote.
- The procedure (`fleet_consistency_drift_sop.md`) gets section 4.15. The counts change from nineteen facets to twenty, and from eleven node-level facets to twelve.
- `audit_report.py` adds the check to the roster and adds its chat summary phrase.
- The new eval case `consistency-boot-disk-pool-outlier` reads the seeded fleet's `drift-pool-outlier` role. The case is in `hack/eval/nightly-cases.txt`. `hack/ci-eval-pr.sh` gives it the cost hint and the delegation timeout of `consistency-drift-outlier`.

Why pools vote and clusters do not: the seeded fleet has four Standard clusters. Three of four is an agreement of 0.75. At 0.75 the severity ladder drops each facet below base `critical`. Nine of ten pools is 0.90, and the finding stays at `major`.

## Context

Part of #2800. Part of #2599.

This pull request does not close #2800. These items stay open:

- The `kubelet-config` facet. It needs the fixture change in #6957.
- The throughput ceiling for each disk shape in the finding text.
- A finding for a cohort of two clusters. The audit needs three voters and a two-thirds majority, so a primary and disaster-recovery pair gets no finding.

Related open pull request: #6957 changes the kubelet half of the same fixture role. It changes some of the same lines in the fixture documents. The pull request that merges second must rebase.

## Bug Fix: Preventing Recurrence

Not a bug fix.

## Testing

- `python3 -m pytest agents/platform/skills/fleet-audit/scripts/test_fleet_drift.py`: 244 passed. 23 tests are new, in `BootDiskPoolVoteTest`.
- `python3 -m pytest scripts/test_ci_eval_nightly.py`: 87 passed. The audit-band test fails for the new case without its entry in `hack/ci-eval-pr.sh`.
- `10 of 10 passed under load (4 cores, 12 busy loops): python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider agents/platform/skills/fleet-audit/scripts/test_fleet_drift.py`
- `test_audit_report.py`: no failure that is only on this branch. 30 tests fail on this machine on `main` also.
- `test_collect.py`, `test_kcc_health.py`, `test_fleet_health.py`: 1359 passed.
- `make docs-check`, `make shellcheck`, `make bench-case-check`, `scripts/test_eval_rosters.py`, `scripts/check_prompt_assets.py`: passed.
- `prettier@3.9.6 --check` on the changed Markdown and YAML files: passed.

### Live validation

This change is an agent-behaviour change. The eval loop is the live validation.

- **Case:** `consistency-boot-disk-pool-outlier`, new.
- **Install:** a dev install (Autopilot, Terraform and Helm, GitHub forge), with one seeded fleet in scope. The runs went through the agent API, because the install does not have the inject door.
- **Red:** `main` at ffcd48087. The checks `a-boot-disk-finding-was-filed` and `the-boot-disk-finding-names-the-planted-pool` failed. Run directory: `run_20261123_201302_red-main-ffcd4808`.
- **Green:** the branch build at b8a1c26db, three runs. Run directories: `run_20261123_214052_green-b8a1c26-1`, `run_20261123_214804_green-b8a1c26-2`, `run_20261123_215547_green-b8a1c26-3`.
- **Registered:** `hack/eval/nightly-cases.txt`.

The branch head is b8a1c26db rebased on `main`, plus one commit for the eval runner and one test. No commit after b8a1c26db changes `fleet_drift.py`, `audit_report.py`, the procedure, or the cron prompt.

Not covered:

- The red ran on an older `main` commit than the branch base. No `main` commit has the facet.
- The inject lane. The CI lanes use it, and this install does not have it.
- Pool projects where the kubelet half of `drift-pool-outlier` shows drift. The lanes record the case there as infrastructure until #6957 merges and the fleet reconciles.

Cleanup: the install is back on `main` at ffcd48087. The drift ledger issue of the install's GitOps repository keeps the `boot-disk` finding until the next drift audit runs.

The run directories are on the author's machine. Ask the author for them.

### UX change

The chat summary of a run that has no ledger issue gets one new row for each `boot-disk` finding. No screenshot: no dev install has chat on without a ledger repository. This is the row from `render_no_forge_summary`, as text:

```
`major` seeded-c: default-pool node pool has a different boot disk from its peers
```

- [ ] No user-visible change

## Self-Review

Passes: `review-adversarial` two times, `review-docs-drift` one time, `review-chat-ux` one time. Each pass ran in a subagent that did not write the change. The second adversarial pass read the range after the first fixes. The context that wrote the change made the fixes for the second pass, and no pass read those fixes.

Fixed:

- **MEDIUM, adversarial:** section 4.15 said that the audit does not flag a disk shape that three or more pools share. The collector files it one level down. The section now says so, and a test shows the two cases.
- **MEDIUM, adversarial:** one cluster with many pools set the baseline for the cohort. The baseline must now be in two-thirds of the clusters that voted.
- **MEDIUM, adversarial:** that condition had no minimum number of clusters. One cluster with unreadable peers was compared with itself. A minimum of three clusters must now vote.

Those are fixed in `governance-sops.md`, `bench/tf/fleet/README.md`, `fixtures.json`, `main.tf`, `bench-fleet-catalog.md` and `fleet-fixtures.yaml`.

author: ajthom90
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ajthom90"} -->
_Requested by **Andrew** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01R3MHV4E7W4kUUr53s9CJX8?thread=cmsg_01R3MHV4E7W4kUUr53s9CJX8DEbfSE9CQWV6EVKoMht6GB)_

## What this adds

A second copy of every backup, kept somewhere else: a bucket in S3-compatible storage (Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO) or a folder on another disk or share. This is the replacement for the appliance's offsite vault.

- `internal/offsite`: `Sync` uploads the pack files and snapshot records the copy lacks and removes the ones the repository dropped; `Fetch` downloads a copy into a folder that then opens as a repository. Targets: a folder, and S3 through a small Signature Version 4 client (no new dependencies).
- Server: an `offsite` job, run daily at a set time or on demand. It runs beside backups and restores, and takes turns with garbage collection. Failures use the existing email alerts.
- Web UI: an "Offsite copy" dialog (where, credentials, schedule, "Save and test", "Save and copy now"), its state in the Repository panel, and the job's progress and result in the job dialog.
- CLI: `bb offsite [set|test|run|off]`, and `bb-server fetch` to download a copy when the server and repository are gone.
- API: `GET/PUT /api/v1/offsite`, `POST /api/v1/offsite/test`, `POST /api/v1/offsite/run`. The S3 secret key is write-only, like the SMTP password.

## Safety choices

- Snapshots are listed before packs and uploaded after them, so the copy never holds a snapshot whose data is missing, even while backups run.
- If more than half of the copy's files would be removed, nothing is removed and the job fails: that pattern is a dead or unmounted repository disk, not a clean-up.
- A folder target must already exist, so a disconnected disk fails the job instead of filling the server's own disk.
- A place that already holds a different repository's copy is refused.
- The copy is encrypted with the repository key, which is not part of it. The README says to keep `repo.key` somewhere other than the server.

## Not in this PR

Keeping forgotten snapshots longer offsite than locally (the copy mirrors the repository), multipart uploads (packs are about 32 MiB, well under the single-request limit), and using S3 as the primary repository.

## Testing

- The signer is checked against the three worked examples in Amazon's Signature Version 4 documentation.
- Sync, incremental sync, deletion, fetch, verify of the fetched copy, the wrong-repository guard and the lost-repository guard, against both a folder and an in-process S3 server that recomputes every signature and pages listings.
- Server API test: settings validation, write-only secret, test endpoint, manual run, alternation with garbage collection, the daily schedule not firing early.
- By hand: back up, copy to a folder, `bb-server fetch`, restore from the fetched copy and compare files; start a new server on a fetched copy; the dialog driven in a browser.
- **Not tested against a real S3 service.** I meant to run MinIO in CI, but its images are no longer public on Docker Hub or quay.io, so that step is gone. `TestRealS3` does the full round trip against any real endpoint when `BB_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT`, `BB_TEST_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `BB_TEST_S3_SECRET_KEY` are set, and "Save and test" in the UI checks a real bucket in a few seconds.

author: timmurphy
body:
Closes #870.

An app that follows association croquet can now ask the site for the players the world rankings know, at `/api/v0/ac/world-ranking-players`, in the order of their names. Each player is told with the id the site gave it, the number the rankings give it, its name, where its games will be told of, when it was archived and when it last changed. The id is what an app keeps, since the rankings can change a player's number. A player the rankings stop listing is still listed, with the moment it was archived.

It is read as the tournaments' list is: pages of at most 100, `changedSince`, a mark of the answer and of each player, and not modified where the app already has it. No key is needed, and a key that does not work is refused.

The `games` address is only named, not served. That is a separate piece of work.

The site's test control can now seed an association croquet player with a number, archive one, give one another number, and tell each player's number, id and moments. A player given two numbers or another's number is refused, and archiving twice keeps the first moment, as the import does.

Checked: typecheck, lint and prettier are clean. The changed features pass against Postgres (109 in-process and 35 web scenarios), and breaking the changed-since comparison, the ordering, the page cap, the games link, the page checks and each test control check turned the matching scenarios red. The rest of the suite and the browser scenarios were not run, which is left to CI. A review was run before this pull request and its nits are fixed.

body:
**Summary:** The shared list of commands that the assistant's safety filter must block (and must allow) has grown, and this project's copy was out of date, which kept a nightly check in the image-builder project red. This brings the copy up to date and closes two gaps the new entries exposed, so the assistant can no longer read a protected file through an obscure git option or point git at planted settings by changing its home folder or search path first. Normal git and gh use is unchanged.

---

**Why**

The nightly "copies of the shared safety files are current" step in Danathar/atomic-image-builder (#878) fails until every repository's copy of `tests/fixtures/gate-refusal-corpus.json` matches the master. The master on atomic-image-builder main hashes to `64246cb4d92cf1226a9eb07d3f1381942850fb090cfa59fcf50e23eb5c212558`, the same hash the issue names; it is copied byte for byte and `CANONICAL_SHA256` moves to it.

**Gate changes (`.claude/hooks/gate-git-diff.sh`)**

Read against the gate, these new refuse rows would have been allowed:

- `named-repo-after-shallow-file`, `shallow-file-reads-env`: `--shallow-file` was stepped over as a flag, so its separated value was read as the subcommand and a later `--git-dir` was never seen; and the option itself makes git quote the first line of the file it names. It is now refused between `git` and the subcommand alongside `-c`, `-C`, `--git-dir` and the rest (GIT_GLOBAL_MSG updated).
- `home-standalone`, `home-standalone-log`, `path-standalone`, `home-read`, `home-printf-v`, `home-for-loop`, `path-mapfile`: HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and PATH are already exported, so assigning one in a statement of its own (`NAME=value;`, `read`, `printf -v`, `mapfile`/`readarray`, `for`/`select`) reaches the git after it. A new pass records the first such assignment and refuses (REACH_ENV_MSG) when git or a gated command runs after it, the same ordering the export-family rule uses. Reading the variable (`cd "$HOME"`) and assigning other names (`TZ=UTC;`, `read -r line`) are unaffected.

The `--attr-source` rows, the `env -S`/`env -a` rows and the stand-alone `GIT_CONFIG_*` rows were already refused by existing rules. Per AGENTS.md section 9 ("Adding or widening a check"), these only widen existing checks.

**Corpus test (`tests/test_gate_refusal_corpus.py`)**

- `GIT_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUE` gains `--attr-source` and `--shallow-file`, matching the master's test, so the shape test can see that `git --attr-source HEAD ... log -p` names `git log`.
- `config-removal-allow-env-split-other-u` (`env -S -u FOO git log -1`) is an allow row this gate refuses on purpose: `env -S` is refused outright (CMD_MSG). It is listed in a new `OVER_REFUSED` map and asserted to still be refused, as decided on Danathar/goodreads-mcp#467 and Danathar/aurora-zfs-simple#523. No refuse row is skipped or listed.

**Not verified**

I did not run any tests, linters or the hook locally (scanner lane rule). I worked out which rows fail by reading the gate code against the corpus diff, so CI is the check. In particular CI decides whether: every new refuse row is now refused; the new allow rows (`allow-attr-source-separated`, `config-reach-allow-*`) still pass; the existing `tests/test_git_diff_gate.py` rows and its mutation strings (each must still match exactly one line) are unchanged; and ruff/shellcheck accept the new code.

Closes #345

Fixes several safety, edge-case, and QML warning issues:

- **Filesystem safety (`src/mediautils.cpp`, `src/translator.cpp`, `src/thumbprovider.h`)**:
  - `media::copyAtomically()`: check `!canonicalSource.isEmpty()` before comparing canonical paths so a missing source and missing destination report the file-open error instead of a false same-file conflict.
  - `media::moveIntoPlace()`: mask copied permissions with `0777` (and `0700` on failed `chown`) instead of `07777`/`07700` so setuid/setgid/sticky bits on an existing file are never copied onto a saved MP4.
  - `Translator::formatLocale()`: skip probing `/default/i18n/locales.json` when `OMARCHY_PATH` is unset.
  - `ThumbProvider::requestImage()`: validate `toInt(&ok)` instead of mapping malformed IDs to thumbnail index `0`.
- **QML edge cases & deprecation warning (`src/Main.qml`, `src/EditBar.qml`)**:
  - Declare the formal `pos` parameter in `MediaPlayer.onPositionChanged` to eliminate the Qt 6.12 implicit parameter injection deprecation warning.
