author: ervamahmutovic
body:
## What I changed
- Added Report 3 (`03_launch_results_by_pair.csv`) to `ReportWriter`: one row for every potato-launcher pair that appears in the attempts, with its attempt count and total points. Over-limit attempts are included.
- Rows are sorted by potato ID, then launcher ID.
- `Main` now also runs Report 3, and the generated file is added to `output/`.

## How I checked it
Ran `Main` and compared the file with a separate recalculation from the raw CSVs. All rows matched. I also checked that repeated attempts for the same pair are merged into one row: the 12 attempts produce 9 rows, the attempt counts in those rows add up to 12, and no pair appears twice. For example, `P01,L01` has 2 attempts in a single row (`P01,L01,2,36`), `P03,L02` has 2 attempts in a single row, and `P05,L03` has 2 attempts in a single row. The first two rows are `P01,L01,2,36` and `P01,L02,1,8`, as in the sample check.

## Design decision
I used a `TreeMap` of potato ID to a `TreeMap` of launcher ID to a list of attempts. A pair's attempts are added to the same list, so a repeated pair can only ever produce one row. The two nested `TreeMap`s also give the required potato-then-launcher ordering automatically.

author: profalfailakawi
body:
## Summary
Native iOS push (APNs) for personal notifications, modeled on schedule-kw #631.

**Server**
- `server/apns-push.ts`: HTTP/2 APNs sender with an ES256 provider JWT (cached for 40 min) and a 10 s timeout. Configured from env only: `APNS_KEY_P8`, `APNS_KEY_ID`, `APNS_TEAM_ID`, `APNS_TOPIC` (`com.dralfailakawi.mizan`), plus optional `APNS_ENV=sandbox`. If any is missing, sending is a silent no-op.
- `server/native-push.ts`: per-user token store (`native-push-tokens.json` next to the notification center, mode 0600, at most 10 tokens per user). Every new, non-deduplicated notification-center item whose target is `user` or `users` is also pushed to those users' devices. Tokens that come back as 410, `BadDeviceToken`, `Unregistered` or `DeviceTokenNotForTopic` are dropped. Logs show only a hash prefix of a token, never the token itself.
- `NotificationCenterRepository.onPublished()` hook. A listener error never fails a publish.
- Routes `POST /api/push/subscribe-native` and `POST /api/push/unsubscribe-native` use the same auth as `/api/notifications`. Account deletion also purges the user's tokens.
- The payload `url` is the notification's `actionHref`, limited to `#…` or a same-site `/…` path. Anything else becomes `#`.

**Web (native only)**
- An «فعّل التنبيهات» switch sits at the top of the notification center modal. It renders only in the iOS app. One tap shows the iOS permission prompt, registers the device and saves the token. Tapping again turns it off.
- `installNativePushNavigation()` at app start: on `pushNotificationActionPerformed`, the payload url is opened inside the app. External URLs are ignored.

**Apple shell**
- `@capacitor/push-notifications` added via `npx cap sync ios` (Package.swift updated).
- AppDelegate forwards the device token and errors to Capacitor.
- `App.entitlements` with `aps-environment=production`, wired into the project with `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS`.
- `UIBackgroundModes` now includes `remote-notification`. Added `PushNotifications.presentationOptions`.
- `xcodebuild -sdk iphonesimulator CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.

## Tests
- `tests/native-apns-push.test.ts` (9 tests, mocked HTTP/2 client, key generated at runtime): no-env no-op; headers and JWT signature check; sandbox origin; dead-token classification; timeout; notification center → push only for personal targets and not for duplicates, with the dead token removed; routes; tap navigation; the switch is native-only; shell plumbing.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Apple / Google / iPhone Duo
- **Apple:** native project changed as listed above. The simulator build compiles. No build number bump and no upload (owner instruction). The provisioning profile must include Push Notifications for the App ID `com.dralfailakawi.mizan` before the next signed build. End-to-end delivery is not tested until the APNs key is configured on the server.
- **Google:** not implemented. Android push needs FCM (google-services.json and a Firebase sender), which is out of scope here. The switch is hidden on Android because it is iOS-only, so web behaviour on Android is unchanged.
- **iPhone Duo:** the switch is one full-width row in the existing notifications modal, with no fixed widths. No Duo screenshots taken, because it renders only in a signed native build with push.

author: kanikabreed
body:
Closes #4210

## What it is for

Opening History from the Now playing window made the Recently played window stretch downward on its own, every frame, until it reached the bottom of the screen; it could then no longer be resized. The history now keeps the size it opens at, or the size the user gives it, with Clear, Copy and Max. entries inside it.

## Legacy Viewer origin

Yes for the window (floater_fs_streamtitlehistory.xml, FSFloaterStreamTitleHistory in indra/newview/fsfloaterstreamtitle.cpp), which has a fixed size there and never grows. The fix itself is Aurora's layout: Aurora's history is resizable.

## What changes

- **Interface:** the history's bottom row (Clear, Copy, Max. entries) measured a fraction of a point more than the room its bottom-up layout gave it, so the window grew to fit it at every frame. The history now lays its body out in the window's exact rect (`Floater::steady_size`, as the People, Chat and Buy Land windows do; `ui/stream_title.rs`). No option added.

## Screenshots

Demo `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM_TITLE=history` with `AURORA_TEXT_SIZE=1.4`, frame 900. Before, the Recently played window has stretched to the bottom of the screen; after, it keeps its size.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KanikaBreed/Aurora-Viewer/captures-issues/fix-4210/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KanikaBreed/Aurora-Viewer/captures-issues/fix-4210/after.png) |

## Tests

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead-code` (the Linux job's flags) clean; `scripts/check.ps1` not run (no PowerShell on this PC)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace stream_title`: 10 passed, including the new `the_history_keeps_its_size` (fails without the fix: the window grew 6 px a frame at text size 1.4, from 286 to 460 px in 30 frames) and `the_title_window_keeps_its_size` (a regression guard for the small Now playing window, which passes with or without the fix)
- [x] Demo scenarios: `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM_TITLE=history` with `AURORA_TEXT_SIZE=1.4`, before (the history stretched to the bottom of the screen) and after (its size kept), captured at frame 900
- [x] Validated by the human on 2026-11-23 in demo (in a build combining this fix with nine other pending fixes): the Recently played window keeps its size, its buttons inside

## Limits and follow-up

- On Linux the growth reproduced only with enlarged text; the reporter saw it at 100 % on Windows, where the fonts measure differently. The fix does not depend on the text size.
- No ⬜ line added to TASKS.md.

author: kayleewilliams
body:
## What and why

In Vue and Nuxt, `bannerLegalLinks` and `dialogLegalLinks` did nothing. The banner always linked both the privacy and cookie policies, and the dialog's footer link could not be removed. Both options are still typed and documented, and they worked before the consent UI was replaced.

- The banner and the dialog read the options again. A list shows only the links it names, and an empty list shows none.
- **Changed default:** with the option unset, each surface shows its stock links, as the React components do. Before the consent UI was replaced, unset showed none.
- Astro with `ui: 'vue'`: `<ConsentDialog legalLinks={null}>` hides the footer link.

`null` cannot mean "none" in Vue, because the plugin's config defaults fill it in. Use `[]`. The docs and the option's type comment now say so.

author: bondiano
body:
Closes #678

## Summary

Adds fixed-width integer types and IEEE 754 binary32 floating-point across the full Flick stack:

### Type Set, Aliases & Literal Syntax
- Added `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int64`, `UInt8`, `UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64`, and `Float32` as `@lang` types in `packages/core/src/Prelude.fl`, plus Prelude aliases `type alias Int32 = Int` (signed 32-bit wrapping) and `type alias Byte = UInt8`.
- Added literal suffixes `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `f32` in `flick-syntax` (supporting radix prefixes `0x`/`0o`/`0b`, underscores, and negative minimum boundaries like `-128i8`, `-32768i16`, `-2147483648i32`, `-9223372036854775808i64`; preserving hex `0x1f32` without suffix ambiguity; rejecting out-of-range literals with `FLICK-T003` and invalid suffix combinations with `FLICK-S006`).
- Numeric defaulting remains restricted to `[Int, Float, BigInt]` (unsuffixed literals never silently default to fixed-width types).
- Updated formatter checks and both editor grammars (`editors/tree-sitter-flick` + `editors/vscode/syntaxes/flick.tmLanguage.json`).

### Semantics, Classes, Standard Library & Conversions
- Fixed-width integer semantics follow `docs/backends/numeric-policy.md`: modular two's-complement wrapping `+`/`-`/`*`/unary `-` (including modular unsigned negation `-(1u8) == 255u8`), total `/` and `%` (`x / 0 == 0`, `x % 0 == 0`, `min / -1 == min`, `min % -1 == 0`), full-width `**`, shift count masking mod bit-width, bitwise ops, checked arithmetic returning `Result`, and `unsafe_div`/`unsafe_rem` defecting on zero.
- `Float32` follows IEEE 754 binary32 with `SameValueZero` `==`, total `Ord` with `NaN` greatest (`Float32.min`/`max`/`between`/`clamp` implemented via `compare`), and single-rounded `Float32.from_bigint` (avoiding binary64 double-rounding).
- Added `Eq`, `Ord`, `Hash`, `Show`, `Display`, `Numeric`, `Integer`, `Floating`, and lossless widening `Into` instances in `packages/core/src/{Numeric,Instances}.fl`, with zero implicit conversions.
- Added stdlib modules `packages/std/src/{Int8,Int16,Int32,Int64,UInt8,Byte,UInt16,UInt32,UInt64,Float32}.fl` with bounds, checked/wrapping/saturating/truncating conversions, bitwise ops, and parsing/formatting.

### IR, Optimizer, Backends, Runtimes & Pinned Components
- Bumped shared IR from `0.15.0` to `0.16.0` (`flick-ir`) with fixed-width `Num`/`Lit`/`Lang` variants, fallback `TypeIndex::lang_con` mappings, and `FixedWidthIntrinsic` (20 minimal `flick:rt` primitives).
- Updated `flick-core` (type inference/settling, lowering, consteval, Perceus intrinsic lowering, TS facade) and `flick-backend-support` (portable arithmetic, consteval, constant folding, specialization, bounded evaluator, layout catalog).
- Updated JS backend (`backends/js`), JS runtime (`runtime/src/core/fixed_width.ts`), and `@flick-lang/effect-ts`: `Int8`/`Int16`/`Int32`/`UInt8`/`UInt16`/`UInt32`/`Float32` as JS `number` (bit-masked / `Math.fround`), `Int64`/`UInt64` as JS `BigInt` (`BigInt.asIntN(64, ...)` / `BigInt.asUintN(64, ...)`).
- Updated Go backend (`backends/go`) and Go runtime (`runtime-go/flickrt/fixed_width.go`) using native `int8`/`int16`/`int32`/`int64`/`uint8`/`uint16`/`uint32`/`uint64`/`float32` with division/overflow/NaN guards, unboxed constructor field helpers (`FieldInt8`..`FieldFloat32`), struct alignment ranking, `EqualConstructed`, and special-float pattern unboxing.
- Rebuilt and pinned official WASM backend components (`flick/js@0.1.0#05c26603...` and `flick/go@0.1.0#1b39d02f...`).

### Reference Model, Lean Proofs, Tests & Documentation
- Extended both small-step λFlick and the counted memory VM in `flick-model` (including host-bridge wire encoding with BigInt tag `"n"` for `Int64`/`UInt64`) to check, translate, and execute all fixed-width types and boundary cases with zero leaks.
- Added `formal/Formal/FixedWidth.lean` proving modular wrapping, total/checked division and remainder, shift-count masking, checked/saturating conversions, lossless widening, interval preorder, and total `Ord` with `NaN` greatest, pinned in `formal/Formal/Axioms.lean` with zero `sorry` and only standard Lean axioms.
- Added independent check/fail/pass, language (`Language.FixedWidth`, 14 tests), Go runtime, wire-encoding, IR-validation, and cross-target e2e (`tests/run/codegen/fixed_width.fl`) boundary test suites.
- Documented the accepted design and JS/Go/C/WASM/Lua representation strategy in `docs/backends/numeric-policy.md`, updated `docs/backends/{contract,baseline}.md`, and updated paired EN & RU reference docs with stamped parity hashes.

## Validation

| Check | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `just lint` (`fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `feature-check`, `flick-wasm` clippy, `cargo machete`, `no-iife.mjs`) | Passed |
| `cargo test -p flick-ir --all-features` | Passed (74/74) |
| `cargo test -p flick-backend` & `cargo test -p flick --test backend_assets` | Passed |
| `cargo test -p flick-core --test check check_fixtures` & `scalar_fields_tests` | Passed |
| `cargo test -p flick-core --test corpus fl_sources_are_formatted` & `docs_examples_check` | Passed |
| `just go-test` (`go vet ./... && go test ./...`) | Passed |
| `just wasm-backends` (`check-component js/go`, `component_host`, `flick --test backends`, `default_backend`, `backend-conformance` 497/497 across effect/rt × debug/release) | Passed |
| `just language` & `just language-go` | Passed (497/497 identical across JS, Go, and RT) |
| `FLICK_E2E_ONLY=tests/run/codegen/fixed_width cargo test --profile e2e -p flick --test e2e -- --ignored run_cases rt_cases` | Passed (JS, TS, Go, RT × debug/release) |
| `cargo test -p flick-model --lib host_bridge::wire::encode` & `cargo test -p flick-model --test run model_prints_what_the_builds_print` | Passed |
| `node docs/scripts/parity.mjs` | Passed |

### Earlier pre-rebase checks on unchanged areas
- `pnpm -C runtime typecheck/lint/test`, `pnpm -C packages/effect-ts typecheck/test` (491/491), `just formal-schemes`, `just lean` (388 jobs, zero `sorry`), `just tree-sitter` (31/31), `just bundle-size`, `just ratchet`, `just feature-test`, full `just model` (212 lib + 656 model + 14 run + 5 doctests), and `consteval_node::folding_matches_node`.

### Not run locally (deferred to CI)
- `just e2e-js` (requires `wasm-opt`/binaryen + Playwright browser)
- Full `just e2e-tests` / `just e2e-cases` shards (requires `cargo-nextest`), `e2e-postgres`, `wasm-plugins`, and multi-OS Go jobs (`arm64`, `macos`, `windows`)

## 何を
- `__tests__/blogTenchusatsuLuckyDirectionsClaims.test.ts`（新規・14 件）
  - 1985-10-12 生まれ → 本命星 六白（立春前の 1985-01-15 は七赤）、1985-10-10 も六白
  - 日柱: 2000-01-07 から −5,200 日 → 番号 20 の甲申 → 午未天中殺。年天中殺は 2026・2027 年
  - 1985-10-10 → 番号 18 の壬午 → 申酉天中殺（2028・2029 年）
  - 2026・2027 年の年盤: 中宮の星、吉方位の並び、凶方位の顔ぶれと名前（`getYearDirections` と、盤から組み立てた重なりの**集合一致**）
  - 「2026 年に北西へ移る計画」が「方位は吉・期間は天中殺」に当たること
- `content/blog/tenchusatsu-and-lucky-directions.md`: 2026 年の「南（五黄殺）」を「南（五黄殺・本命的殺）」に。`updatedAt` を 2026-11-23 に

author: iced-cream
body:
## What and why

Plugin API 3's effect budget (core/user/um.cpp `fx_run`) now covers the built-in effects as well (decided 2026-11-23). CPU admission (#39) stays the first layer and predicts each effect's cost. This guard is the second layer: it measures what actually runs, which catches cases such as a Pi without a fan throttled to 600 MHz, or the L2 cache shared under load. Stacked on #39 (`rebalance-core2`).

- **What's timed:** each INSERT slot of every chain (voices, buses, master), which includes AMP and the master's send TYPEs, plus each send FX slot's built-in TYPE (STUTTER included). The timing runs on the core that runs the slot. A slot that is OFF, refused or shed is never timed. User effects keep their own guard and add their time to their core's total.
- **Rules:**
  - Built-ins are muted only while their core is hot: render cores at 80 % of a block or more, core 3 when slot 0's master chain uses what its limit leaves after its own control work.
  - A slot is muted after 16 hot blocks in a row over its budget (120 us per 12-frame block).
  - A core that is hot for 16 blocks in a row mutes its most expensive effect, built-in or user. A user effect goes through um.cpp's mute.
  - A single call of 2 ms or more mutes at once.
- **Muted state:**
  - The slot fades out over 5 ms and plays dry. A send slot's return goes silent.
  - INSERT slots show NO CPU on the box.
  - The mute holds until the slot is set again or its box attaches again. Regrant never readmits a muted slot.
- **Reporting:** /status gets `fxMuted` (built-in and user mutes in the same shape) and `fxGuard`. The web page gets an "Effects muted for CPU" section, and the log gets `fxguard:` lines.
- **Controls:** the console command `fxguard` (state, `on|off|report`, `budget:`, plus `slow:` and `mute:` for tests and gates) and a cmdline option `fxguard=`.
- **Docs:** docs/fx-measured-mute.md.

## How it was tested

- **Host tests:** cloud g++. The new `test_fx_guard` passes. It covers the hot-only slot rule, the most-expensive-effect pick, the 2 ms rule, the fade to dry, NO CPU, the hold, release on a new TYPE, release on set_type and on attach, a user effect sent to um's hook, report and off modes, and a send FX slot going silent and being released. test_insert, test_send_fx, test_admit, test_master, test_device, test_amp and test_engine also pass.
- **Kernel build:** the Pi 4 kernel builds with no new warnings (14,992 of 16,384 KB).
- **QEMU two-box gate:** passes with bench=0 (25/25) and bench=1 (25/25). /status `fxMuted` was empty at every step.
- **QEMU forced check:** `fxguard=slow:0:V1:A:2100` muted V1 A DRIVE at once, and /status and the log showed the reason. A new TYPE released it. An OFF send slot was never timed.
- **QEMU timing finding:** in report mode, a DRIVE slot with no forced slowdown had two single blocks over 2 ms within 20 s. This comes from QEMU's timing, so QEMU load gates that set FX should boot with `fxguard=report`.
- **Not tested:** this has not run on a unit. It changes sound (effects can be muted), so it stays a draft until a unit run and a listening check.

## Checklist

- [x] The tests pass locally (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] No Elektron firmware or anything derived from it.
- [x] No personal data in code, docs or commit messages.
- [x] Third-party code keeps its licence notice (none added).

author: kaczordodgers
body:
The three tests that run a skills command beside an unreachable pack now start from a seeded manifest. They no longer run `t3chad skills install` as their setup.

## Why

These three tests were one test, which ran past its 10 s budget on a busy macOS runner. It never waited on anything:

- The unreachable pack is refused in about 14 ms. The test's git config allows only the `file` transport, so git never opens a connection.
- There is no sleep, no retry and no timeout on its path.

The time is process starts. Every skills command starts 35 to 48 git children, and git's own helpers come on top. A git child costs about 7 ms on macOS on a quiet machine and several times that on a busy one; Linux starts one in a fraction of that, which is why the same test stayed fast there.

## Change

- `beside_an_unreachable_pack` writes the manifest that `install` publishes, taken from `skills-install.txt`, with the one `git fast-import` it already ran.
- `install` keeps its own tests (`skills_install_pack_and_copy` and the refusals around it).
- The assertions of the three tests are unchanged.

## Red first

Git processes one test starts, counted with git's own trace (a `trace2.perfTarget` line added to the test's git config for the count, not committed):

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `an_unreachable_pack_does_not_block_update` | 179 | 127 |
| `an_unreachable_pack_does_not_block_pin_undo_or_unpin` | 191 | 139 |
| `a_new_skill_name_is_refused_while_a_pack_is_unreachable` | 173 | 121 |

Run alone, each test takes about a fifth to a quarter less time.

## Not covered

- The other heavy tests in this file still install two or three packs through the CLI and start as many processes as before.
- A test's time still grows with the load on the machine, because it is a chain of process starts. Cutting that further means fewer git children per command in the program, which is a design change, not a test change.

Touches outside the repo: none

author: natalliabukhtsik
body:
## Summary

Overwriting a contact's primary email address used to fail with "Changing primary email requires promote an additional email first," forcing a four-step promote-then-delete dance to fix a simple typo. `ContactModel.updateContact` now treats a primary-email change with no promotion as a replace: the new address becomes primary, the old one is dropped unless it's re-sent in `additional_email_addresses`, and promoting one of the contact's own stored additional addresses still works and now correctly preserves the contact's other stored addresses instead of wiping them. The contact edit form surfaces a "keep the old address as an additional email" checkbox so users aren't forced to lose the old address when it wasn't a typo.

## Changes

**Model (`shared/models/contactModel.ts`)**
- Replace the hard error on a bare primary-email change with a replace path: new address becomes primary, old address is dropped unless re-sent, primary label only changes when the caller states one.
- Fix the promotion arm so it reconciles against the contact's stored rows instead of an empty array when `additional_email_addresses` is omitted, so a bare promotion no longer silently deletes the contact's other stored addresses.
- Stop re-appending the old primary when the caller explicitly sent rows without it (the editor's "uncheck keep old email" case), since sent rows are now treated as the caller's full intent.
- Renumber remaining additional rows by index after a swap so no two rows share a `display_order`.
- Run the pre-swap clear of additional rows on any primary-email change (not just promotions) so uniqueness triggers never see both addresses at once.

**UI (`packages/clients/src/components/contacts/ContactEmailAddressesEditor.tsx`, `ContactDetailsEdit.tsx`)**
- Add `savedPrimaryEmail` prop so the editor knows a contact's previously stored primary address.
- Show an inline checkbox under the primary email input, offering to keep the old address as an additional row once the primary is changed on a saved contact; unchecked by default, hidden on create and when the input is typed back to the saved value.
- Add `shouldOfferKeepOldPrimaryEmail` / `appendKeptOldPrimaryEmail` helpers and wire the checkbox state into the emitted `additional_email_addresses`.
- Add the checkbox label to all locale files (`server/public/locales/*/msp/contacts.json`) plus pseudo-locales.

**API docs**
- Update the `PUT /api/v1/contacts/{id}` OpenAPI description (`server/src/lib/api/openapi/routes/clientsContacts.ts`) to state that a different email replaces the primary and drops the old one unless re-sent, that sending one of the contact's own additional addresses with no `additional_email_addresses` in the body promotes it and leaves the contact's other addresses alone, and that another contact's address is refused.
- Regenerate the OpenAPI artifacts (`sdk/docs/openapi/*`) and the chat/MCP registries (`ee/server/.../apiRegistry.generated.ts`, `server/src/lib/mcp/registry.generated.ts`) so the drift gate stays quiet.

**Chore**
- Sync `package-lock.json` with already-committed `package.json` version bumps (no dependency added or removed).

## Testing

- Added integration coverage in `server/src/test/integration/contactModelEmailAddresses.integration.test.ts` for: bare primary replacement (dropping the old address), bare replacement refusing an address already owned by another contact, promotion via the contact's own additional address with and without the caller resending other rows, and keeping the old primary when the caller sends it back.
- Added/extended unit coverage in `packages/clients/src/components/contacts/ContactEmailAddressesEditor.test.ts` and `server/src/test/unit/contacts/ContactEmailAddressesEditor.test.tsx` for the new keep-old-email checkbox: visibility only on a changed saved primary, hiding when the input is typed back to the saved value, never showing on create, and correct emission of the kept row only while checked.

Raises the declared `@roarkanalytics/sdk` floor to 9.9.0, by [app-agent-codegen](https://github.com/roarkhq/app-agent-codegen).

Spec: https://api.roark.ai/doc

## Not a regeneration

No generated file is in this diff. This run found every one of them already byte-correct against
the spec, and only the declared `@roarkanalytics/sdk` range wrong - so what moved is that range and the
lockfile that has to agree with it, the two files in this package the generator does not write.

That is the state a generated table leaves behind when it merges before the SDK release carrying
its newest entries is published: the floor could not be raised on the run that wrote the table,
and nothing came back to it afterwards.

## What the old floor could not serve

`@roarkanalytics/sdk@9.4.0` is the oldest version the declared range admitted, and so the one a
consumer with an existing lockfile can resolve. It does not carry:

- `customerFlowFolder.update`

## Public surface

Unchanged. This package gained no tools; it stopped declaring an SDK that cannot
serve the tools it already had. That is why the commit is a `fix(deps)` rather than
the `feat` a regeneration carries.

### SDK floor

bump @roarkanalytics/sdk floor 9.4.0 -> 9.9.0 (1 entry the old floor cannot serve: customerFlowFolder.update)

pnpm-lock.yaml refreshed from the new range; the manifest and the lockfile move together.

author: amibamae
body:
## Staging recovery and durability groundwork
- Conservative same-instance recovery plan: two matching fresh health observations; Velocity backend draining; protocol `game.save.request` then `execution.unit.restart` for running Paper or stopped-runtime start for failed units; new runtime ID and fresh invocation-local Paper `Done (...)` before routing.
- Read-only local Paper probe bundled into new VM bootstrap. No raw player chat, credentials, or monitoring dependency sent to controller.
- `StoredBackupResolver` verifies the successful durable offline `server.backup` operation, exact backup-policy ID, current data generation, source instance, final stopped lifecycle boundary and fresh remote object readbacks before it can attest backup validity.
- Scoped, bounded Wasabi S3 full-object SHA-256 and immutable version comparison; missing, short, wrong-version or mismatched objects fail closed.
- Fixed invalid manifest construction by stripping planner-only `data_set_id` after validating its binding.
- Dedicated Go/Velocity/Python staging safety CI, documentation and isolated Vultr test runbook.
- Updated `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for current Go 1.26, SDK, bbolt and tooling versions. No new third-party dependency.
- Branch merged latest upstream main via a normal two-parent merge, with no overlapping file changes.

## Safety / not finished
**DRAFT; DO NOT MERGE OR DEPLOY as automatic recovery.** The currently shipping controller registers only `server.define`. These policies, Wasabi reader and resolver have not been wired into a real production game/execution adapter or authenticated lifecycle workflow. **No real Vultr fault-injection test or isolated restore has been run.** Work required to achieve that is tracked in [#425](https://github.com/amibamae/gameserver-controller/issues/425). There is no active direct SSH restart daemon, production changes, automatic VM create, or auto-destroy behavior.

## Merge gate
- [ ] Final branch Go build, gofmt, full tests, race and vet green
- [ ] Focused recovery staging Go/Python/Velocity tests green
- [ ] Protocol, Rust and supervised pilot checks green
- [ ] Security review of full readback and last-write fencing
- [ ] Complete runtime implementation and real isolated Vultr+Wasabi staging rehearsal in #425, or explicitly carve this PR down to staging-only policy with no claim of production readiness

VictoriaLogs and Homelable remain optional. Wasabi's 11-nines **object durability** is not a guarantee of application-level save/restore consistency.

author: msaad00
body:
## Summary
0.115.6 shipped to PyPI, Docker Hub, Helm and GitHub, but the MCP image and the MCP Registry entry stayed on 0.115.5. Both MCP workflows run on `workflow_run` of Release and required the whole run to succeed. Two jobs that run after every artifact is published, the docs build and the post-release pins sync, failed and marked the run failed, so both MCP workflows were skipped.

- `scripts/resolve_published_mcp_release.py` accepts a failed Release run when every failed job is post-publish (`Docs build (deploy on main)`, `Sync post-release pins`). Any other failed job skips publishing with a notice instead of an error. Cancelled or timed-out runs are still rejected, and an incomplete job list fails closed.
- `publish-mcp.yml` and `publish-mcp-registry.yml` run on a `success` or `failure` Release and let the resolver decide.
- The registry job now runs the resolver too, and publishes the `server.json` from the release commit; it previously published whatever `server.json` main held at that moment.

## Evidence
Replaying the resolver against the real 0.115.6 Release run (45096236085, conclusion `failure`) finds no blocking failures and resolves `v0.115.6` at `3c9f79add`, so both MCP workflows would have published.

## Guards
- A test pins the 0.115.6 shape (artifacts green, docs and pins red → publishes) and the opposite (PyPI failed → skipped, no git calls).
- `POST_PUBLISH_JOBS` must name real Release jobs, and no Release job may `need` one of them, so a job that gates publishing cannot be added to the list.
- The registry job must resolve before validating and must validate the released `server.json`.

## Also: merge-queue flake
`tests/api/test_push_async_ingest.py::test_lasting_store_read_failure_leaves_the_push_pending_and_a_retry_completes_it` dropped #6395 from the merge queue (`assert 201 == 202`). Its wait helper looked up a bare job id in `scan_queue._local_dispatches`, which is keyed by `(tenant_id, job_id)`, so the wait never waited; the first worker could finish the job after the store was restored, and the retry replayed a completed job (201). The helper now matches the key's job id. 25/25 isolated runs pass.

## Not in this PR
Republishing 0.115.6's MCP image and registry entry is a manual dispatch of `publish-mcp` and `publish-mcp-registry` (`publish=true`), waiting on the owner's go-ahead.

## Test plan
- `tests/test_mcp_container_release.py` (29 pass), plus 874 tests across files referencing the release and publish workflows
- `actionlint` on both workflows

suffixing
body:
From the agent report (F3, and the cause of F4): installing a split bundle meant unzipping it, picking the splits by hand, remembering `--abi`, and reading `dumpsys` to find out what happened.

`apkscope install app.xapk [-D serial] [--abi ABI]` (MCP `install_apk`, viewer **Tools → Install on device**):
- Reads the device's `ro.product.cpu.abilist` and the ABIs the app ships code for (ABI splits by name, plus `lib/<abi>/` inside any APK).
- Picks the first device ABI the app has. An arm64-only app on an x86_64 emulator with ARM translation therefore gets `arm64-v8a`, which is what the agent had to find out by hand. If no device ABI matches, it says the app can't run there and why, before installing anything.
- Installs base + that one ABI split + every density and language split, with `adb install-multiple -r --abi <abi>`. A plain `.apk` uses `adb install`.
- Prints `primaryCpuAbi` from `dumpsys package`, and a note when the chosen ABI isn't the device's own (the app runs through translation).

The emulator-side causes (wrong image, translation off, preview builds) are explained in the README limits and on the frida-server PR; apkscope doesn't patch devices.

### Checked
- Tests for reading split ABIs and choosing the ABI: an x86_64 emulator with translation, both ABIs shipped, no native code, and no translation (error mentions translation).
- With no device: a clear adb error.
- fmt, CI clippy, tests (130 + 47), and the viewer build.

### Not checked
**Not run against a device**: none was available.

author: grahammmm
body:
## What
`web/map/ssh-cells.ts` now checks each cell's computed polygon extents against legal lon/lat bounds (±180 / ±90) **before** building the color key or the GeoJSON. A cell whose polygon would cross the domain (e.g. center lat 89.75 with a 1-degree cell gives a 90.25 vertex) is rejected, not clipped or wrapped. Valid neighbours, exact legal boundaries (vertex exactly 90 / 180) and grid order/missing-cell gaps are preserved; if every cell is refused the result is the existing no-cells outcome. This also stops an extreme rejected value from widening the color-key endpoints for cells that still draw.

No source, projection or scale-threshold changes. Owned files only: `web/map/ssh-cells.ts`, `tests/test_ssh_cells.mjs`. No changelog, pin or generated artifact touched.

## Test contract (CI-ARTICLE-1)
Extends the existing regression owner `tests/test_ssh_cells.mjs` (no new file). Protects: out-of-domain cells are rejected and do not distort the scale. Believable bug that fails it: validating bounds after building the scale (or clipping instead of rejecting), so a 90.25 vertex draws or its value widens the key (synthetic baseline `{"bad":90.25,"good":35.75}`).

## Acceptance (exact head)
- `node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/test_ssh_cells.mjs`: 8 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped
- `git diff --check`: clean
- prepush: PREPUSH-TESTS PASS (core); web tests skipped locally (node_modules missing), CI runs them

Offline synthetic fixtures only; no live, release or data-publication effect.

body:
I thoroughly tested these changes locally and spent some time reviewing them via models.

More explanation is written in each commit.

Some examples worth noting:

## string-format and array safety

<details>
<summary>Code</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash

normal=$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null || true)
red=$(tput setaf 1 2>/dev/null || true)
green=$(tput setaf 2 2>/dev/null || true)
cyan=$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null || true)

_status_unsafe() {
    local type="${1}"
    local status="${package:+${package}: }${2}"
    local items=("${@:3}")
    case "${type}" in
        failure) local -n nameref_color='red';   title='[MSYS2 CI] FAILURE:' ;;
        success) local -n nameref_color='green'; title='[MSYS2 CI] SUCCESS:' ;;
        message) local -n nameref_color='cyan';  title='[MSYS2 CI]'
    esac
    printf "\n${nameref_color}${title}${normal} ${status}\n\n"
    printf "${items:+\t%s\n}" "${items:+${items[@]}}"
}

_status_safe() {
    local type="${1}"
    local status="${package:+${package}: }${2}"
    local items=("${@:3}")
    case "${type}" in
        failure) local -n nameref_color='red';   title='[MSYS2 CI] FAILURE:' ;;
        success) local -n nameref_color='green'; title='[MSYS2 CI] SUCCESS:' ;;
        message) local -n nameref_color='cyan';  title='[MSYS2 CI]'
    esac
    printf '\n%s%s%s %s\n\n' "${nameref_color}" "${title}" "${normal}" "${status}"
    if [ "${#items[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        printf '\t%s\n' "${items[@]}"
    fi
}

echo "=== 1. Format-string injection (% and Windows backslashes) ==="
package="mingw-w64-test"
echo "[UNSAFE]"
_status_unsafe message '100% done in C:\new\temp'
echo "[SAFE]"
_status_safe   message '100% done in C:\new\temp'

echo "=== 2. Trailing % causing printf error (aborts script under set -e) ==="
echo "[UNSAFE]"
_status_unsafe failure 'Build stopped at 50%' 2>&1 || echo "(exited with status $?)"
echo "[SAFE]"
_status_safe   failure 'Build stopped at 50%'

echo "=== 3. Array with an empty first element ==="
unset package
echo "[UNSAFE]"
_status_unsafe message 'Changed packages' '' 'mingw-w64-zlib'
echo "[SAFE]"
_status_safe   message 'Changed packages' '' 'mingw-w64-zlib'

## pkgver fixes

<details>
<summary>Code</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -eo pipefail

# --- Environment detection (MSYS vs MINGW) ---

msystem="${MSYSTEM:-MSYS}"
prefix_abs="${MINGW_PREFIX:-/usr}"
prefix_rel="${prefix_abs#/}"
pkg_prefix="${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX:+${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-}"

# --- Functions under test (fixed versions) ---

pkgver_from_metadata_old() {
    local version
    version="$(sed -n 's/^Version[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*//p')"
    version="${version%-*}"
    printf '%s\n' "${version#*~}" | sed 's/\./\\./g'
}

pkgver_from_metadata_fixed() {
    local version
    version="$(sed -n 's/^Version[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*//p')"
    version="${version%-*}"
    printf '%s\n' "${version#*~}" | sed 's/[][\.^$*|]/\\&/g'
}

execute_fixed() {
    local status="${1}"
    local command="${2}"
    local arguments=("${@:3}")
    if [[ "${command}" != *:* ]]
        then "${command}" "${arguments[@]}"
        else "${command%%:*}" | "${command#*:}" "${arguments[@]}"
    fi
}

# --- 1. Resolve locally installed target package ---

pkgname="${1:-}"
if [ -z "${pkgname}" ]; then
    if [ -n "${pkg_prefix}" ] && pacman -Qq "${pkg_prefix}gcc" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pkgname="${pkg_prefix}gcc"
    elif pacman -Qq gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pkgname="gcc"
    elif pacman -Qq "${pkg_prefix}gcc" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pkgname="${pkg_prefix}gcc"
    elif pacman -Qq bash >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pkgname="bash"
    else
        echo "No default local package found. Pass an installed package name as \$1."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Detect sync repo (defaults to ${msystem,,}, falls back to repo owning $pkgname)
repo="${msystem,,}"
if ! pacman -Si "${repo}/${pkgname}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    repo="$(pacman -Si "${pkgname}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^Repository[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*//p' | head -n 1 || true)"
fi

echo "============================================================"
echo "1. Live test [${msystem}] on package: ${pkgname} (repo: ${repo:-none})"
echo "============================================================"

old_pkgver="$(pacman -Si "${repo}/${pkgname}" 2>/dev/null | pkgver_from_metadata_fixed || true)"
new_pkgver="$(pacman -Qi "${pkgname}" | pkgver_from_metadata_fixed || true)"

echo "Sync pkgver (escaped)     : ${old_pkgver:-<empty>}"
echo "Installed pkgver (escaped): ${new_pkgver:-<empty>}"

# Test binary detection regex used by [runtime-dependencies] in both scripts
readarray -t binaries < <(pacman -Ql "${pkgname}" | sed -e 's|^[^ ]* ||' | grep -E "${MINGW_PREFIX:-}/.+\.(dll|exe|pyd)$" || true)
echo "Detected binaries count   : ${#binaries[@]} (sample: ${binaries[0]:-none})"

# Check if pacman -Fl database is populated; run [file-diff] against installed files
if [ -n "${repo}" ] && pacman -Fl "${repo}/${pkgname}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Running [file-diff] (sync DB vs installed DB)..."
    file_diff="$(diff -Nur \
        <(pacman -Fl "${repo}/${pkgname}" | sed -e 's|^[^ ]* |/|' ${old_pkgver:+-e "s|${old_pkgver}|PKGVER|g"} | sort) \
        <(pacman -Ql "${pkgname}" | sed -e 's|^[^/]*||' ${new_pkgver:+-e "s|${new_pkgver}|PKGVER|g"} | sort) || true)"
    diff_count="$(printf '%s' "${file_diff}" | wc -l)"
    echo "Diff line count           : ${diff_count}"
    if [ "${diff_count}" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "Sample diff (run 'pacman -Fy' if local files DB is out of date):"
        printf '%s\n' "${file_diff}" | head -n 6 || true
    fi
else
    echo "Skipping pacman -Fl comparison (run 'pacman -Fy' first if you want sync file lists)."
fi

# If a cached .pkg.tar.* archive exists, test Case 3 (-Qip / -Qlp without installing)
cached_pkg="$(compgen -G "/var/cache/pacman/pkg/${pkgname}-[0-9]*.pkg.tar.*" | grep -v '\.sig$' | tail -n 1 || true)"
if [ -n "${cached_pkg}" ]; then
    pkg_ver_archive="$(pacman -Qip "${cached_pkg}" | pkgver_from_metadata_fixed || true)"
    first_archive_file="$(pacman -Qlp "${cached_pkg}" | sed -e 's|^[^ ]* ||' ${pkg_ver_archive:+-e "s|${pkg_ver_archive}|PKGVER|g"} | head -n 1 || true)"
    echo "Cached archive tested     : ${cached_pkg}"
    echo "Archive pkgver (escaped)  : ${pkg_ver_archive}"
    echo "Sample normalized path    : ${first_archive_file}"
else
    echo "No cached .pkg.tar.* found in /var/cache/pacman/pkg/ (skipping -Qip/-Qlp archive check)."
fi

echo ""
echo "============================================================"
echo "2. pkgver & [file-diff] edge cases [${msystem}] (Old vs. Fixed)"
echo "============================================================"

# Case A: Brand-new package (old_pkgver is empty) with space in file path
empty_ver="$(printf '' | pkgver_from_metadata_fixed || true)"
sample_fl="${pkgname} ${prefix_rel}/share/doc/test/my helper.txt"
buggy_empty="$(printf '%s\n' "${sample_fl}" | sed -e 's|^[^ ]* |/|' -e "s|${empty_ver}|PKGVER|g")"
fixed_empty="$(printf '%s\n' "${sample_fl}" | sed -e 's|^[^ ]* |/|' ${empty_ver:+-e "s|${empty_ver}|PKGVER|g"})"

echo "[Case A: New package (empty old_pkgver) + space in path]"
echo "  Old (corrupts path) : ${buggy_empty}"
echo "  Fixed               : ${fixed_empty}"

# Case B: Regex metacharacters in pkgver (e.g., 1.0+r5[1]-1)

body: Preview only. Do not merge. This does not change production, Vercel env vars, or the live Supabase project. ## What changed Searchers on the Texas and Florida calculators now see a teaser after a search, then have to enter an email before the full breakdown. The homepage no longer says "No signup required." - After a search, the page shows the county, an eligibility headline, and a savings band (for example `$3,000–$3,500/yr`). The detailed breakdown underneath is blurred until the form is submitted. - Name is optional. Email is required and checked on the server (`/api/leads`, `intent: results_unlock`). - A new email is inserted into `bee_exemption_leads`. The same email later is updated, not inserted again. One `new_lead_captured` alert goes to chris@beekings.com through the existing Resend path in `lib/notify.ts`, with an `Idempotency-Key` of `bee-lead-{sha256(email)}`. Repeat searches do not send another lead alert. Address-search alerts are unchanged. - The lead is linked to the recent `address_searches` row by writing `email` on that row (existing follow-up). When the migration below is applied, the lead also stores `address_search_id`. - The browser remembers the unlock for 30 days (`localStorage` key `bee_results_unlock_v1` plus a `bee_results_unlock` cookie), so the same visitor is not asked again on the next search. - The $14.99 Unlock Full Report path collects an email before Stripe Checkout. `customer_email` is prefilled from that address, and the checkout route upserts the lead. Checkout without a valid email returns `400 email_required`. - The Florida "Get Your Free Guide" form now calls `/api/send-guide`, the same way Texas does. The guide email says Florida instead of Texas when that form sends it. Arkansas and Louisiana calculators are unchanged and still show full results without an email. The gate is visual. The calculator still runs in the browser, and the existing parcel lookup response is what fills the blurred section. Someone reading the page source can see those numbers. Stopping that would mean moving the calculation behind the email API. ## Gated UX Homepage copy now says the check is free and that an email is required for the full results. Florida (Marion County): county, "looks eligible", savings band, optional name, required email, blurred breakdown. Texas (Henderson County, a parcel that is too small): county and "looks short of the acreage", then the same form. author: d4rkeagle65
body:
## Problem

After the oCIS deploy merged, the `ocis-init` initContainer hung and the pod never left `Init:0/1`. Its log was looping:

```
Do you want to configure Infinite Scale with certificate checking disabled? [yes | no = default]
```

`ocis init` prompts for this interactively unless `OCIS_INSECURE` is set in the environment, which I'd left unset — so init blocked forever, and nothing downstream (auto-provision, admin bootstrap) could happen.

## Fix

Set `OCIS_INSECURE=true` in both the init and server containers. `true` also makes oCIS skip TLS verification on its internal service-to-service calls, which fits the single-binary-behind-Traefik setup — Traefik holds the only real cert, and this is LAN-only.

## Verified

In a throwaway pod (no volumes, cleaned up) with `OCIS_INSECURE=true`:

```
INIT_EXIT_OK
OCIS_YAML_WRITTEN
```

`ocis init` exits 0 and writes `/etc/ocis/ocis.yaml` with no prompt; the pod reached `Succeeded`.

## Check against the live cluster

On merge, Flux rolls the Deployment; the new pod's `ocis-init` should complete and the main container start. Then the originally-planned steps resume: add your user to `oCIS Users`, grab the admin password from the `ocis-init` log, log in, promote the first admin.

The Authentik side is already confirmed good (groups, provider, application, and the two policy bindings all applied).

`scripts/` unchanged.

author: kanikabreed
body:
Refs #4325

## What it is for

Right after sending a group notice, its new row in Group › Notices opened on "Loading…" and never showed the notice. It now reads at once, as it was sent. Refresh then brings the grid's copy, and a notice being read stays selected while the list comes back.

## Legacy Viewer origin

Yes: LLPanelGroupNotices (indra/newview/llpanelgroupnotices.cpp): onClickSendMessage, which adds the sent notice's row at once under an id the viewer makes up and leaves it unselected; onSelectNotice; updateSelected, which re-selects the previous notice by id once the list is in, otherwise the first one (called from LLPanelGroup::draw).

Two deliberate differences, noted in the code and TASKS.md:
- **The sent notice's text is shown locally.** Chosen, the new row shows its subject, message, our name and the attachment's name as they were sent. In the Legacy Viewer a click on that row shows nothing new and keeps the previous notice.
- **No GroupNoticeRequest for the made-up id.** The Legacy Viewer's onSelectNotice sends it even for that id, and the grid never answers. Aurora skips it on purpose.

## What changes

- **Interface (Group › Notices, Home tab's latest notices):**
  - the row added after sending is never opened by the tab on its own; when nothing is chosen, the grid's newest notice is read first;
  - chosen by hand, it reads as it was sent, without "Loading…" and without a Save button for its attachment (nothing is offered to us);
  - after Refresh, a choice that cannot come back (that row, replaced by the grid's copy under its own id) falls back to the newest notice; a notice still to come in a later packet of the list stays chosen.
- **Network:** no GroupNoticeRequest for the sent row; the rest of the notices traffic is unchanged.
- **Data (`world/group_data.rs`):** `add_sent_notice` takes a `SentNotice` (subject, message, sender, attachment name and type) and keeps it with its row until the list is asked again (`GroupData::sent_notice`).
- **Demo:** new mode `AURORA_DEMO_GROUP_PROFILE=<scenario>:sent` (for example `officer:sent`): a new notice is sent at frame 640 and its row clicked (docs/TESTING.md).

## Screenshots

Demo `AURORA_DEMO_GROUP_PROFILE=officer:sent`, frame 700: a notice sent from the window, then its row clicked. Before, the reading pane stays on "Loading…"; after, the notice reads at once.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KanikaBreed/Aurora-Viewer/captures-issues/fix-4325/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KanikaBreed/Aurora-Viewer/captures-issues/fix-4325/after.png) |

## Tests

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead-code` (the Linux job's flags) clean; `scripts/check.ps1` not run (no PowerShell on this PC)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace -- notice group_profile demo_group`: 132 passed (6 + 126), including the new `a_notice_sent_from_here_is_read_from_what_was_sent_never_asked`, `a_notice_just_sent_is_not_asked_for_and_reads_as_sent` and `a_chosen_notice_survives_a_list_arriving_in_packets`; theme-guard and i18n filters: 10 passed
- [x] Demo scenarios: `AURORA_DEMO_GROUP_PROFILE=officer:sent`, before (fix disabled: the reading pane stays on "Loading…") and after (the notice shows at once), captured at frame 700; `officer:compose` for a manual send
- [x] Validated by the human on 2026-11-23 in demo (in a build combining this fix with nine other pending fixes): a sent notice shows at once, no "Loading…"; an older notice stays selected after Refresh

## Limits and follow-up

- Grid check still to do (hence `Refs`): send a notice to a group, click its new row, press Refresh: the grid's copy is listed under its own id and opens normally, and an older notice chosen before Refresh stays chosen. ⬜ line added under the task in TASKS.md.

author: arynbht
body:
M4's CI-budget and judge-check items, in one PR (both touch the profile's new `ci` block).

## What changes

- **Profile:** an optional `ci: { budget_minutes_per_month?, trust_judge? }` block (`packages/catalog/src/profile.ts`), documented in the schema's comments. A budget is a positive whole number; unknown keys are rejected.
- **Minutes per PR:** close asks the Actions API for every completed run on each of the PR's commits and records `ci_minutes` and `ci_runs` in the task's history.jsonl row. Minutes are per job, rounded up to the minute, skipped jobs free (how GitHub bills). A token without `actions: read` leaves the fields out; nothing fails.
- **Status issue:** with a budget set, `rivetari ci` appends `CI minutes this month: X of Y (Z%) over N run(s).` (marked at 75% and 100%). The ci.ts hunk is one import and one line; the logic is `ciBudgetSection` in `packages/engine/src/github/actions.ts`, so it sits apart from F5's ci.ts work.
- **Doctor:** a `ci` warning line once the month reaches 75% of the budget. No line below 75%, without a budget, without a token, or when the API can't be read. It caches the minutes of runs it has already counted in `.rivetari/cache/ci-minutes.json` (gitignored), so later runs only look up new runs.
- **`rivetari/judge` check run:** when a task ships with a `passed` judge verdict and CI may trust the judge, ship posts a completed `rivetari/judge` check run with conclusion success on the judged head. Its output carries the judge record's sha256 and the ledger hash (the chain head's MAC), and the post is logged in the ledger. A head a person let through on `needs a human` gets no check, so CI runs in full. A failed post is logged and ship goes on. The check is posted once per head and task (`external_id` is the task id).

## Decisions (reversible)

- **The gate is on posting, not on what CI trusts.** With trust off, Rivetari never posts the check, so no workflow anywhere has anything to skip on, and nothing in a client's repo needs to know about the setting. ci-next's hook already trusts only the App named in `RIVETARI_JUDGE_APP`. A second gate in each workflow would just be another thing to keep in step.
- **`trust_judge` default:** true when the repo's owner is the account Rivetari's App is registered to (`app.json`'s owner), false otherwise or with no App. A profile that doesn't load grants nothing.
- **Posted on ship, not in the judge:** `runtime/src/judge/**` is being changed in another PR, and ship already holds the App client it uses for the review. Only an App can create check runs, so no check is attempted when the token is a person's `gh` login.
- **Month-to-date comes from the Actions API, not history.jsonl.** history.jsonl isn't committed, so CI never sees it, and the budget covers every run (pushes to main, nightly runs, plain PRs), not only task PRs. The month is the UTC calendar month. A filtered listing stops at 1,000 runs, and the status issue caps job lookups at 500 per run to stay under the token's rate limit. Past either limit the line says "at least".
- **No OS multiplier** (Windows ×2, macOS ×10 on private repos): the count is runner minutes. The run timing endpoint's `billable` is 0 on public repos and that endpoint is being retired, so it isn't used.
- **One PR instead of two:** both halves add to the same profile block.

## What the owner must set

- **App permission:** `checks: write` is added to `APP_PERMISSIONS`. The already registered App needs it added in its settings, and each installation has to accept the new permission. Until then the post is refused and logged, and ship goes on.
- **Repo variable `RIVETARI_JUDGE_APP`:** the App's slug (the `slug` in `~/.config/rivetari/app.json`), so ci-next's skip hook trusts the check.
- **Workflow (protected, not touched here):** `rivetari.yml`'s `audit-status` job has `permissions: contents: read, issues: write`. It needs `actions: read` before the status issue can count minutes. Until then the line says the minutes couldn't be read.

## Tests

New tests only: the schema accepts and rejects `ci` values; job rounding, PR minutes and month minutes from a stubbed Actions API (msw), including the cache and the partial count; the status issue line and section; doctor warns at 75% and over, and stays quiet below 75%, without a budget, without a token, or on an API error; close records `ci_minutes` and `ci_runs`, and leaves them out without them; postJudgeCheck sends the right name, sha, conclusion and hashes, and skips an existing check; ship posts the check with the right head, record sha256 and ledger hash when `trust_judge` is true, posts nothing when it's false, and ships anyway when the post fails; and `trustsJudge` defaults by App owner and follows the profile.

author: chiragagg5k
body:
Part of #5640. Follows #5642 (the output queue).

`SocketOutput.close_wait` and `send_wait` were `pub`, and 16 places in `hooks`, `phpclients`, `clients` and `server` read or wrote them directly to ask two things: is this socket waiting to close, and why did the send loop stop. The socket now answers those questions, and both fields are `pub(super)`, visible only inside `corebase::reactor` (`output.rs` sets them from a send's result, and `flush.rs`'s tests build the struct).

## Operations added (on `SocketFields`, in `reactor/write.rs`)

| Operation | Intent it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `defer_close()` | "close this once whatever still uses it lets go" (`close_wait = true`): hooks' close with a bound coroutine, the HTTP client closing from inside a callback, test setup |
| `close_deferred()` | "is it waiting to close": the client's package loop, hooks' descriptor state, wait snapshot and network release, the HTTP client's read loop |
| `send_stall() -> Option<SendStall>` | "why did this failed send stop the loop": `Close` (`close_wait`), `Wait` for writability (`send_wait`), or `None` to go on. Corebase's flush and the server's `ReactorThread_onWrite` made the same decision |

## Behaviour

Unchanged. Tests that set `close_wait = cond` on a fresh record (`co_io`, `socket_wait`) now call `defer_close()` when `cond` holds; the field starts out false.

## Not in this PR

The remaining `SocketOutput` fields reached from outside the reactor, about 50 places, are for later PRs under #5640:
- `buffer_size`: 15 places, for the output limit and watermarks
- `nonblock`: 11 places, for nonblocking mode
- `send_timer`: 6 places
- `ssl_send`: 3 places

The `.deslop-please.allow` `field-leak ... SocketFields::output` line is recorded by #5638, which is still open, so this PR can't remove it.

## Checked

- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --locked -p swoole-rs-corebase -p swoole-rs-server -p swoole-rs-clients -p swoole-rs-hooks -p swoole-rs-phpclients`: 1089 passed, 0 failed.

author: octaviobr
body:
## Summary

Closes #116. Every PR from a branch in this repo gets a **PR Preview**. All PR Previews share the `card-duel-preview` D1 database (ADR-0010). Also adds a root `pnpm clean`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PR
    participant WF as pr-preview.yml
    participant D1 as card-duel-preview
    participant CF as Worker Preview pr-<n>
    PR->>WF: opened / synchronize / reopened
    WF->>WF: build client (dev Clerk key, SITE_URL = PR Preview URL)
    WF->>D1: apply this PR's migrations
    WF->>CF: wrangler preview --name pr-<n> --var APP_ORIGIN:<own URL>
    WF->>WF: fail unless Cloudflare reports that exact URL, then GET /api/health
    WF->>PR: post or edit the one marked comment
    PR->>WF: closed
    WF->>CF: wrangler preview delete
```

**Change from the issue: the URL is `pr-<n>.cardduel.ooctav.io`, not workers.dev.** In Wrangler 4.162 a Preview only gets a workers.dev URL when the Worker's top-level `preview_urls` is true. That flag also puts every production version on a public workers.dev URL. So `preview_urls` stays `false`, and the Custom Domain route gets `previews_enabled: true` instead. ADR-0010 records this.

```diff
 .github/
+├── scripts/pr-preview-comment.sh   # posts or edits the one PR Preview comment
 └── workflows/
+    ├── pr-preview.yml              # deploy on push, delete on close, skip forks
+    └── preview-db-reset.yml        # manual: drop all tables, apply main's migrations
 apps/worker/
+├── scripts/preview-db.ts           # runs `d1 migrations apply` / reset against card-duel-preview
 └── wrangler.jsonc                  # previews block: DO bindings, card-duel-preview DB, vars
 docs/
+├── adr/0010-pr-previews-share-one-preview-database.md
 └── authentication.md               # PR Preview setup; the origin-pinning exception
+tools/clean.ts                      # `pnpm clean`
```

`wrangler d1` only reads top-level `d1_databases`. So `preview-db.ts` writes an ignored `wrangler.preview-db.json` that binds `DB` to the database from the `previews` block.

`pnpm clean` deletes `node_modules`, `dist`, `dist-e2e`, `.wrangler`, `coverage`, Playwright output, `*.tsbuildinfo` and the generated Wrangler files. It keeps `.env.local` and `.dev.vars`. **This includes the local `pnpm dev` D1 database in `.wrangler`.**

## Evidence

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (263 tests) and `pnpm e2e` (62 tests) pass. I ran Biome on the changed files: my local `.claude/worktrees/alpha` breaks a repo-wide `biome check .`.
- `wrangler types` accepts the new config.
- With the placeholder database ID, `pnpm preview:db:migrate` stops: "Set previews.d1_databases[DB].database_id in wrangler.jsonc…"
- I ran the reset SQL against a local D1: it dropped all 11 tables and `d1_migrations`, then all 4 migrations applied again.
- `pnpm clean` followed by `pnpm install` and `pnpm check` gives a working tree.
- Not run end to end: no PR Preview has been deployed yet. It needs the setup below first.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** CI

Production is untouched until the next manual **Deploy**. That deploy publishes `previews_enabled` on the Custom Domain, and production keeps serving as before. Until setup is done, the PR Preview job fails on every PR (this one included) with a clear error.

Setup before or after merging:

- [x] `pnpm --filter @card-duel/worker exec wrangler d1 create card-duel-preview`, then put the ID in place of `<REPLACE_ME>` in `wrangler.jsonc`.
- [x] Repo variable `gh variable set PREVIEW_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and repo secret `gh secret set PREVIEW_CLERK_SECRET_KEY` from the development Clerk instance.
- [x] Run **Deploy** once so PR Previews get a URL.
- [x] On the first PR Preview, check for `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. It's only confirmed for workers.dev Previews.

author: xmiksay
body:
Closes #104.

## Problem
In the `pdf`/`pdf-presentation` targets, a `;` directly after inline code was dropped (`Use \`foo\`; then \`bar\`.` → "Use foo then bar."). The md→Typst converter emits inline code as `#raw(...)`; in Typst markup a `;` right after an embedded expression is consumed as its terminator. `(`, `[` and `.ident` after the call were likewise parsed as call arguments, a trailing content block, or field access.

## Fix
`push_call()` in `src/backends/typst/markdown/mod.rs` writes every inline call the converter emits (`#raw`, `#link(..)[..]`, `#footnote[..]`, `#image`) followed by an explicit `;`, which Typst consumes, so the following character is plain markup again. Block-level calls (`#quote(block: true)`, `#table`) are always followed by a newline and are unaffected.

## Tests
- Unit tests on the emitted Typst.
- `punctuation_after_inline_constructs_survives_typst_compile` compiles through the in-process typst engine and checks the laid-out text for `;`, `(x)`, `.len`, `[y]` after inline code in paragraphs, headings, list items, blockquotes, emphasis, link text, table cells and footnote bodies, plus a call at end of line. Verified it fails without the fix.

`make lint` and `make test` pass. One test fails locally both on this branch and on clean `master`: `no_pandoc_target_embeds_a_host_file` in `tests/pandoc_local_files.rs`. It is host-specific (the dev machine's hostname matches the canary check) and unrelated to this change.

- **iOS Secure Enclave `ML_DSA_65_ES256` support (iOS 26+)**: Implemented internal composite key generation and signing for `Algorithm.ML_DSA_65_ES256` (`draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-07` / RFC 10073) directly inside `SecureEnclaveSecureArea`, dropping the need for a separate `CompositeSecureArea`.

author: hjlauener
body:
Phase 6 nach Umsetzungsplan v1.1 mit den Entscheidungen 8.4 bis 8.12. Nach dem Merge ist **Meilenstein M3 (KI)** erreicht.

## Was neu ist
- **Fragen auf der Suchseite** (8.8): Ein Umschalter wechselt zwischen „Suchen“ und „Fragen“, für Mitglieder bleibt die Wahl gespeichert. Gäste sehen einen Anmeldehinweis. Wer noch keinen Schlüssel hinterlegt hat, bekommt eine Anleitung.
- **Antworten nur aus Hub-Inhalten** (8.7): Jede Aussage trägt einen Verweis [n]. Darunter stehen die Quellen mit Link auf den passenden Abschnitt und der Tokenverbrauch.
- **Wenn nichts passt**, wird der KI-Anbieter gar nicht angefragt, es entstehen also keine Kosten. Stattdessen erscheinen:
  - der Hinweis „Im Teaching Hub habe ich dazu nichts gefunden“
  - ähnliche Seiten
  - ein Link zur Volltextsuche
  - der Knopf „Inhalt fehlt – der Redaktion melden“, der den Feedback-Dialog mit der Art „Idee“ und vorausgefülltem Text öffnet
- **KI-Index** (8.6, 8.9):
  - Er enthält Abschnitte aus publizierten Inhalten: Deutsch sowie von Menschen übersetzte englische und französische Fassungen. Nicht aufgenommen werden Themen mit Status „folgt“ und News, die älter als 2 Jahre sind.
  - Die Embeddings entstehen lokal über Ollama mit `bge-m3`; dafür verlässt kein Text den Server.
  - Den Index baut `npm run ai:reindex` auf. Danach führt ihn ein Hook nach jeder Änderung im CMS nach, ohne das Speichern zu blockieren.
- **Eigener Schlüssel** (8.4): unter „Mein Hub → KI-Einstellungen“.
  - Vor dem Speichern prüft ein kurzer Aufruf beim Anbieter den Schlüssel.
  - Gespeichert wird er mit AES-GCM verschlüsselt und an das Mitglied gebunden. Der Geheimschlüssel dafür liegt in `AI_KEY_SECRET`, also nicht in der Datenbank.
  - Sichtbar ist nur „…abcd“. Der Schlüssel lässt sich jederzeit löschen.
- **Anbieter** (8.5):
  - **Anthropic** über das offizielle SDK, mit Streaming, `effort: medium` und serverseitigem Refusal-Fallback für die Claude-Modelle der 5er-Generation.
  - **OpenAI**.
  - **OpenAI-kompatibel** mit eigener Adresse. Erlaubt sind nur öffentliche https-Adressen; eine DNS-Prüfung blockiert interne Netze, damit der Server nicht im Auftrag eines Mitglieds interne Dienste anfragt.
  - Die Modellliste pflegt der Admin unter „KI-Einstellungen“. Voreingestellt sind Claude Opus 5.5 und Claude Sonnet 5.5.
- **Verlauf** (8.12): unter „Mein Hub → Fragen an den Hub“, ohne automatisches Löschen.
  - Jede Antwort hat eine eigene Detailseite.
  - Antworten lassen sich mit Mitgliedern teilen und erscheinen dort unter „Mit mir geteilt“.
  - Man kann einzelne Einträge oder den ganzen Verlauf löschen.
  - Der Daten-Export enthält Verlauf und Schlüsselkennung, nie den Schlüssel selbst.
- Keine Datenschutz-Rückfrage (8.10) und kein Monatslimit (8.11), wie entschieden. Als Missbrauchsschutz gilt höchstens 60 Fragen pro Stunde und Mitglied.

## Betrieb
- Neuer Docker-Dienst `ollama` (`ollama/ollama:0.40.16`). `npm run ai:reindex` lädt beim ersten Mal `bge-m3` herunter (etwa 1,2 GB).
- Neue Variablen in `.env`: `AI_KEY_SECRET` (mindestens 32 Zeichen, später nie ändern), `OLLAMA_URL`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, optional `AI_MIN_SCORE`.
- Das Datenbankschema `ai` braucht pgvector; das Docker-Image `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` bringt es mit. Die Payload-Migration `20261123_220534_ai_settings` legt die Modellliste an.
- Die CI läuft ohne externe Dienste: `AI_EMBEDDER=fake` liefert Ersatz-Embeddings, `AI_TEST_PROVIDER=1` einen Testanbieter mit festen Antworten.

## Tests (im Cloud-Container mit Postgres 16, pgvector und Mailpit)
- Lint und Typprüfung: ohne Fehler
- Unit: 115 grün; neu sind Tests für Abschnitte, Auswahl der Quellen, Prompt-Maskierung, Verweise, SSRF-Schutz, Verschlüsselung und Ersatz-Embeddings
- Integration: 51 grün; neu sind Tests für Index aus Payload-Inhalten, Übersetzungen, Entwürfe, Schlüssel, Verlauf, Teilen, Cascade, Suchmodus und Modellliste
- E2E mit axe: 31 grün; neu sind Anmeldehinweis für Gäste, Schlüssel speichern, Frage mit Quellen, gemerkter Modus, „nichts gefunden“ mit Meldung an die Redaktion, Verlauf, Export und Löschen

## Offen
- Die Antwortqualität mit echten Inhalten und `bge-m3` ist noch nicht gemessen; danach `AI_MIN_SCORE` einstellen (Standard 0.45).
- Die echten Anbieter (Anthropic, OpenAI) habe ich ohne gültige Schlüssel nicht live aufgerufen; die Tests decken sie über den Testanbieter ab.
- OpenAI-Modelle sind nicht voreingestellt: Der Admin trägt sie ein, bis dahin geben Mitglieder den Modellnamen frei ein.

author: tomaszjanusz
body:
## What and why

Echo reduction lowered every band of every sound once it decayed. On `dev`, music with no voice in it loses 2.8 dB at Light and 8.7 dB at Strong, inside the speech bands and outside them. The goal is narrower: clean the room echo that trails speech, where speech is, and leave the rest alone.

This is step 1, in the current DSP and without ML. The gain stays at exactly 1 unless all four of these hold:

- **Speech bands.** 80 Hz to 4.8 kHz (bins 2 to 102 at 48 kHz, 70 to 4805 Hz). Bins outside are never computed.
- **After speech.** The cue is a syllable, read from the level of the speech bands: the level rises over the gap and then holds instead of falling at once. The gain is free while a syllable sounds (up to 2 s) and for 0.8 s after, and returns to 1 over 0.4 s.
- **Only what falls.** The gain is free only while the level of the speech bands is falling, and 0.1 s after. Music under a voice holds its level and passes; so does a held vowel.
- **As far as the cue is sure.** One syllable that hardly stands out from the sound around it may be a chord accent and gets two fifths of the depth. One that lasts, or stands 15 dB clear, gets all of it. A run of syllables adds up only where each has another spectral shape than the one before, as vowels do and a chord struck again does not.

All of the syllable's rules are in seconds, so they hold at any sample rate. The comment at the top of `assembly/echo-reduction.ts` documents the cue and every constant.

### Round 3 after Sol's re-review (DSP as of 6213e4b4)

All four findings reproduced. Light / Strong, dB.

| Finding | `dev` | da07912f | This head | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Accents every 0.5 s, accompaniment: largest 50 ms dip | 5.89 / 9.96 | 5.70 / 9.21 | 3.24 / 6.39 | Reduced |
| 1. Same, accompaniment level over the clip | −2.93 / −6.59 | −1.35 / −1.91 | −0.47 / −0.93 | Reduced |
| 1. Accents every 1.6 s: largest dip | 6.02 / 9.94 | 5.21 / 6.74 | 3.24 / 6.39 | Reduced |
| 1. Cut from voice to music 12 dB under it: largest dip of the music | 5.36 / 9.96 | 5.38 / 9.33 | 5.38 / 9.33 | Not fixed: known limit |
| 2. Vowel held 1.2 s at 96 kHz, tail (lab fixture) | −6.67 / −9.46 | −2.48 / −2.71 | −6.65 / −9.43 | Fixed |
| 2. Same at 44.1 / 48 kHz | −6.70 / −9.54, −6.69 / −9.53 | −6.69 / −9.53, −6.68 / −9.51 | −6.69 / −9.53, −6.68 / −9.51 | Unchanged |
| 2. Steady mono noise at 96 kHz, lowest frame after 4 s | | | 0.00 (4 seeds, 30 s) | No retriggering after startup |
| 3. `largestDip` on long input | | RangeError near 12 min (Sol's figure) | 30 min of frames in 60 ms | Fixed |
| 4. Claims | | | | Corrected below |

**Finding 1, what I chose.** Repetition alone no longer builds the cue up. A syllable adds its two fifths only when the levels of the five bands (each against its own peak) differ from the syllable counted before it: repeated accents differ by 0.15 to 0.45, the built-in voice in the 1.5 s room by 0.5 to 1.4, and the threshold runs from 0.4 to 0.6. A syllable that stands 9 to 15 dB clear of what sounded before still counts whatever its shape, because then there is nothing else to protect. Against Sol's cap (4.41 dB at Strong, 1.5 s room tail 7.34 → 5.30 dB) this keeps the rooms: 1.5 s room −4.12 / −7.36, rt080 −6.72 / −9.72, 0.8 s room −5.78 / −9.47. The worst dip stays at 6.39 dB at Strong because the first one or two accents after the music starts are new by any measure; after them the accompaniment is at −0.9 dB over the clip instead of −1.9.

Three cheaper-looking variants were measured and rejected:

- Restart the hold count on any clear rise: accents 2.3 / 3.2 dB, but rt080 tail −2.66 / −4.35 and 1.5 s room −3.29 / −5.40.
- End a syllable on the smoothed fall: accents every 0.5 s back to 5.56 / 9.13.
- End a syllable relative to its loudest moment: 96 kHz vowel −5.27 / −7.06, accents every 0.5 s 4.66 / 8.83.

**The cut to music is not only overlap.** At the Strong minimum, about 0.17 s after the cut, the music already carries 3.32 dB more power in the speech bands than what is left of the voice and its room (Sol's measurement), and it is still 9.33 dB down (5.38 at Light). The level of the speech bands is still falling and the window is open, so the gain is free for everything in those bands, the new music included. The music is back at a gain of 1 in the later music-only part (0.00 from 1.5 s on, against −2.8 / −9.0 on `dev`), and over the pauses it loses 0.24 / 0.32 dB against 3.0 / 8.9. The gate holds both cases by their largest dip, and the transition is in the listening check.

**Finding 2.** The hold count, the syllable's end, the once-per-rise count and the smoothing all acted per frame, and a frame is 256 samples at any rate. They are in seconds now. A syllable also ends on a real loss of power (half over the gap) instead of on one frame that dips, so a held vowel may waver: with its pitch swinging by 4 Hz the unit test gives −4.83 / −6.92, −4.92 / −6.86 and −3.98 / −6.04 dB at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz (`dev` −4.9 / −6.9 at all three; da07912f −1.59 / −2.03 at 96 kHz).

**Finding 4, corrected claims.**

- The voice is not "left alone". It keeps its level while it sounds (−0.1 to −1.2 dB at Strong across the rooms, `dev` −0.4 to −3.1). The fading ends of words fall, so they go down with the echo: `room-rt080` word endings −5.66 / −8.09 dB (`dev` −6.04 / −8.89). The changelog now says that it usually preserves sustained speech, that word endings fade with the echo, and that music can still duck at accents and at cuts from speech to music (745 characters with the bullet marker).
- Tones beside a voice, Strong, 48 kHz, over the clip and at the worst 50 ms: 40 Hz −0.11 / −0.24, 55 Hz −0.59 / −1.30, 65 Hz −1.17 / −2.68, 4825 Hz −0.30 / −0.61, 4900 Hz and up 0.00 dB. The −1.47 dB I gave for 65 Hz came from another fixture; these are from the committed test, which now asserts both figures. At 96 kHz a bin is twice as wide and the bands start at 47 Hz, so 65 Hz is inside them there (Sol measured −5.55 dB at its worst 50 ms; I did not re-measure that).

body:
## What
The retry ladder in `forge-bool` (research/decide-once/old-path-statements.md §G, G2–G5) no longer talks through thread-locals. Each try is now a function of its inputs and its rung alone:
- `Rung` holds `careful`, `chords`, `no_run_on`, `fences` and `absorb`. It is passed down to `plan_once_in`, `trim`, `crossings_near` and `meet_region`.
- `Tried` holds `rung`, `retried`, `odd` and `undecided`. The caller keeps it across the tries and reads it in the checks after them (`undecided_touch`, the RETRIED result check).
- forge-geom's `ABSORB_HAIR_ROOTS` is the one flag that stays thread-local, because forge-geom reads it there. It is set for one try only by the `Absorbing` guard, which is cleared on unwind and tested.
- `FORGE_IMPRINT` is read only under a feature.
- Under `--features decisions` there are structural-site counters (G4, G5, G6, G7, D3, D9).

## Speed fix (new in this round)
The earlier version (0d7b91f) was over band. On this VM: patterns seq +0.31%, coplanar seq +0.28%, torture/plate seq +0.18%, nary1 lines +0.05–0.07%.

Callgrind put `trim_in`'s own cost at +674k on patterns seq. A line-level profile and an asm diff showed why: the 15th argument (`tried`) spilled `body` out of a register in the edge-box prefilter loop of `trim_in`. That cost several reloads per edge.

Variants that did not fix it:
- Reading `tried.rung.X` at each use: worse.
- `#[inline(never)]` on `trim_in`: no change.
- `rung` passed by value: no change.
- The edge-box scan in its own non-inlined iterator: mixed (patterns +0.94%).

The fix: `ts` and `Tried` share one `Trimming` struct behind one pointer, so `trim_in` has main's argument count again. `Tried` is copied back on Ok and on Err alike, so ODD still survives a failed try.

## Band (tools/speed/band.py; exact callgrind gate `GATE_COUNTER=callgrind`, main db5c0759 and this head 2f7a881 counted on the same VM with the same /usr/bin/valgrind 3.22)
- Strict total: **−0.0054%** (20,199,486,636 vs 20,200,568,268).
- Worst strict line: **+0.0034%** (torture nary1). plate/shaft nary1 are also +0.0033–0.0034%, mixed nary1 +0.0011%, patterns nary1 +0.0003%. Every other strict line is ≤ 0.
- Former over-band lines: patterns seq −0.040%, coplanar seq −0.049%, torture/plate seq −0.055%.
- Diagnostic seq/nary1 lines: none over 0.5%. The largest is jack nary1 at +0.0045%.
- **bits: identical** (tools/speed/bits.txt unchanged).

## Tests (on this VM, at head 2f7a881, which contains main db5c0759)
- `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`: debug build with debug assertions on, debuginfo off for disk. Exit 0: 285 test binaries, 2202 passed, 0 failed, 45 ignored.
- `cargo test -p forge-bool --features decisions`: ok.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p forge-bool --all-targets`, with and without `decisions`: clean.
- wasm: left to CI.

## Why

The backend and its operational tools carried descriptions of individual steps alongside the reasons for compatibility and recovery decisions. This pass removes that narration and records one follow-up for pricing data that fails to load silently.

## What changes

The comment baseline falls from 4,272 lines to 2,332. Every remaining line belongs to the frontend, browser tests, Playwright configuration, test sources or workflows. The pricing backlog entry requests a diagnostic that identifies a skipped provider while other providers continue to load.

## Evidence

- Compared TypeScript compiler trees, literal tokens and directives across 129 JS and TS sources. The comparator detected a changed literal and a removed directive in controls.
- Compared all three Python syntax trees and directives, seven shell scripts’ active lines and here-documents, and both configuration files.
- The full local gate passed, including 1,888 backend tests, 290 frontend tests, 49 parity and contract tests, 73 Chromium end-to-end cases and 24 verifier tests. The built-runtime skill checks passed.

## Flags

The edits in verification and test helpers change their explanatory comments. Their executable source comparisons passed. Workflow definitions and test assertions are unchanged.
